> # Arithmetic declaration plugin: proposed concrete runtime packet
>
> Read-only proposal, held for coordinator review. No Go implementation or test has been written for this packet. The target remains the complete `src/ast/arith_decl_plugin.h` and `.cpp`, including their actual rational, algebraic, recognizer, utility, and owning `app_ref` specializations. Installing only the rational declarations must not be reported as completing this source unit.
>
> ## Existing prerequisites and integration boundary
>
> The real AST owner, all five node kinds, parameter/info copying, scalar handles, AST interner, reference owners, symbol service, rational service, sexpr owner, charged IDs, MPBQ/MPBQI, and resource-limit utility now exist. They are usable prerequisites rather than substitute AST or numeric implementations.
>
> Current AST storage has `plugins [5]astPluginBinding`; dispatch in `ast_core_plugin_dispatch.go` and value operations in `ast_builtin_plugins_values.go` reject `fid >= 5`. The constructor interns the `arith` family but deliberately does not install its plugin. It has no arithmetic plugin cold-state field. Source `ast_manager::register_plugin` (`ast.cpp:1635`) publishes registry membership before calling `set_manager`. These existing owner/dispatch fields require coordinated changes; a new-file-only implementation cannot honestly provide integration through a global side table.
>
> The source lazy wrapper (`arith_decl_plugin.cpp:25–113`) requires an independent unsynchronized MPQ manager, a real algebraic-number manager borrowing the manager's resource limit, a charged ID generator, and a concrete owning algebraic numeral vector. There is no current algebraic-number, upolynomial, or sexpr-to-upolynomial Go implementation. The AST owner also does not yet embed/expose its source resource limit. Those are genuine prerequisites for `am`, `aw`, irrational numerals, root parsing, algebraic comparison, deletion, and translation. No stub algebraic token or unsupported callback may stand in for them.
>
> ## Proposed public API and private layout
>
> All methods remain on the real `ASTManager` and acquire its lock; private helpers run under that lock. Proposed names are explicit and concrete:
>
> - `InstallArithmeticPlugin() error`, `ArithmeticPluginInstalled() (bool,error)`, `ArithmeticFamilyID() (int32,error)`.
> - `ArithmeticIntSort()/ArithmeticRealSort() (ASTHandle,error)`; `ArithmeticNumeral(mpnum.OwnedRational,bool) (ASTHandle,error)`; `ArithmeticPi()/ArithmeticE() (ASTHandle,error)`.
> - Existing `MkFamilySort`, both family function-declaration routes, `MkFamilyApp`, value/unique/equal/distinct/some-value routes dispatch to the actual installed arithmetic state. Explicit selector overloads may be exposed as `ArithmeticFuncDecl` and `ArithmeticFuncDeclFromArgs` for source branch tests, using the existing concrete parameter owner and borrowed handle arrays.
> - `ArithmeticNumeralValue(h, *mpnum.OwnedRational, *bool) (bool,error)` copies the source rational output before publishing the integer flag. A failed recognition leaves both outputs unchanged; failed copying preserves its actual source prefix.
> - Concrete expression/sort/decl kind predicates and unary/binary matching methods cover every actually declared recognizer overload. Matching uses caller outputs, preserving false-output behavior. `ArithmeticIsZero`, `ArithmeticIsMinusOne`, and `ArithmeticTimesMinusOne` use real temporary rational actions.
> - `ArithmeticApp(kind,args)`, explicit unary/binary/three-argument convenience wrappers, `ArithmeticEq`, `ArithmeticAddSimplify`, and `ArithmeticMulSimplify` cover the real utility routes. Owning simplify results use real `ASTRef`; owning arithmetic operator counterparts use a concrete checked app-reference specialization, with constructor/return/destructor actions rather than raw borrowed-handle substitution.
> - `ArithmeticGetSortNames(output,logic)` and `ArithmeticGetOpNames(output,logic)` append into a concrete charged builtin-name owner. Each element contains actual `Symbol`, signed family ID, and declaration kind; no strings, interfaces, or record pointers. The output vector's source growth/copy/header arithmetic is audited independently of actual Go stride.
> - Once the real backend exists: `ArithmeticAlgebraicNumeral(OwnedAlgebraicNumber,bool)`, `ArithmeticRootNumeral(SexprHandle,uint32)`, algebraic copy/accessor methods, and concrete external-parameter translation between two actual owners. The algebraic type is a prerequisite contract to design in its own source packet, not a proposed opaque placeholder here.
>
> Private `astArithmeticPlugin` is a single charged cold object bound to its real AST owner/family ID. It contains three actual Symbol fields (`Int`, `Real`, `RootObject`), named scalar node fields for every source cached sort/declaration/app, two concrete scalar small-numeral vectors, the sticky conversion flag, lifecycle/continuation metadata, and an optional pointer to the one real cold algebraic wrapper. Hot cache entries contain only actual scalar `astNodeRef`; no per-entry pointer or boxed value. A coordinator-owned field holds the cold plugin. Header reservation occurs before escaping owner allocation. Manager stats account that header, every full backing capacity, old/new growth overlap, and the real lazy numeric graph separately.
>
> Use all named cached declaration fields from the source, not an enum array whose convenient traversal silently changes constructor/finalizer order. Cache vectors use the actual `ptr_vector<app>` source allocation schedule and bounds; source `inc_ref` precedes `setx` growth. Failed growth retains the unlisted increment in the manager's real graph. Finalize releases only actual cached entries, then manager forced teardown reclaims retained nodes. No invented failed-push rollback.
>
> The optional algebraic wrapper owns its independent rational manager, real algebraic manager, embedded charged IDs, and typed algebraic records/vector. Its members destroy in reverse declaration order. Source `mk_id` publishes the ID action before numeral-vector reserve/copy; `recycle_id` recycles before deleting the numeral. External parameters retain their source integer IDs, distinct from allocator slots/generations; actual algebraic values live in the wrapper. Closed/foreign scalar handles are checked at API boundaries.
>
> ## Complete source-method inventory
>
> | Source surface | Concrete implementation/actions required |
> | --- | --- |
> | Constructor, `set_manager`, `finalize`, destructor, `mk_fresh` | Real symbols, exact eager cached nodes/pins/flags, source field order; fresh plugin starts empty and does not clone caches; lazy wrapper destruction plus reverse member cleanup. |
> | `aw`, `am`, wrapper ctor/dtor, `mk_id`, `recycle_id`, `idx2anum`, `to_anum` | Real algebraic backend and source ID/vector actions; scalar private access checked at borrowed lifetime boundaries. |
> | `del`, `translate` | Actual external-parameter recycle and cross-owner deep algebraic copy; source callback availability follows registry lifetime. |
> | `mk_sort` | Real/Int cached sorts; parameters ignored; unknown kind returns null. |
> | Private declaration selector, `fix_kind`, `check_arity`, `mk_num_decl` | Full switch, unary SUB becomes UMINUS; retain unused `check_arity` body without inventing calls; exact NUM parameter-kind/arity checks. |
> | Both `mk_func_decl` overloads | NUM first, then zero-arity error except PI/E; coercion selector scans any Real only for its exact operation set, otherwise first domain/argument; ignore range/non-NUM parameters as source does. |
> | Three numeral overloads, `mk_pi`, `mk_e` | Rational cache/general construction, real algebraic branch/conversion, actual sexpr polynomial root parsing, cached constants. |
> | `get_sort_names`, `get_op_names` | Append order, symbol construction before output growth, sticky NRA conversion state, no fabricated underspecified names. |
> | `is_value`, `is_unique_value`, `are_equal`, `are_distinct`, `get_some_value`, `is_considered_uninterpreted` | All base short circuits and algebraic branches, four ordered ADD/nonzero checks, exact sorts, three underspecified kinds. |
> | Recognizer constructor/family accessor and all header predicates/matches | Explicit concrete expr/sort/decl routes, actual owned numeric copies, unary/binary arity tests and false-output behavior. |
> | Utility ctor, manager/plugin access, `init_plugin`, arithmetic manager/accessors | Borrow the installed real plugin lazily; utility construction does not install one. Missing source plugin is a checked Go domain adapter. |
> | All utility constructors and simplify overloads | Actual generic AST dispatch, exact singleton-app shortcut versus singleton-variable route, owning simplify returns, equality orientation by numeral and AST ID. |
> | All inline `app_ref` numeral/arithmetic/comparison operators | Concrete owning app specialization; real numeric temporaries and full-expression references, copies, and cleanup. No generic dispatcher. |
>
> ## Source quirks and exact failure actions
>
> 1. `set_manager` eagerly builds Real then Int and every predicate/arithmetic/conversion/power/abs/trigonometric/constant/underspecified cached declaration. Domains/ranges/chainability/associativity/commutativity are real AST info, not recognizer metadata. Constructor and finalizer order differ: finalize releases MOD before REM, Int power before Real power, and cached small Int entries before Real entries.
> 2. Public declaration selection does not validate the selected declaration's expected arity or require every domain to be numeric. Source application checking/coercion performs later checks. Generic irrational kind is not a constant operation: zero arguments produce the ordinary no-arguments error; nonzero unknown selector returns null.
> 3. Direct NUM declarations accept any rational parameter when the second parameter is any nonzero signed integer. Unlike rational numeral construction, this route does not reject a nonintegral value tagged as integer.
> 4. Small cache includes unsigned values below 16. With sticky NRA conversion, an integer 15 becomes cached Real with flag 0; integer 16 becomes Real with the original flag 1. Recognition can therefore report integer despite a Real sort. `get_some_value(Int)` also follows the sticky conversion route. Do not canonicalize these quirks.
> 5. `get_sort_names` for NRA/QF_NRA/QF_UFNRA sets the conversion flag before append and never clears it for later logics. Normal sort append is Int then Real. Op names have their exact baseline and ALL/null extension; no underspecified names are exported.
> 6. Source plugin registration publishes membership before initialization. Failures retain completed source initialization prefixes with an owned continuation, so cleanup releases only completed pins once. Cache INC-before-growth prefixes remain until actual explicit balancing or manager forced teardown.
> 7. Real app coercion is necessary. `ast.cpp:2038–2098` allocates candidate app storage before determining/coercing arguments, uses actual TO_REAL/TO_INT apps and source inline16 owning buffer callbacks, and then checks/publishes. A plugin-local sort rewrite is not equivalent.
> 8. Source numeric parameters own real rational copies; temporary parameter arrays and info copies retain their lexical destruction and fault prefixes. Expression results never borrow a numeric handle past its owning statement.
> 9. Source debug checks occur at actual sites (external kinds, algebraic IDs/nonzero values, some-value sort, recognizer accessor kind, lazy utility plugin). Trace/SMT2 printer actions remain open until actual printers exist; g3checked alone does not claim these source actions.
>
> ## Required coordinated owner edits
>
> The coordinator must approve/own existing AST field and plugin-binding integration, generic dispatch routes, manager graph stats, finalize/deallocate ordering, external-parameter callbacks, actual resource-limit field/accessor, and app coercion. This proposal does not authorize this agent to mutate those files. Constructor defaults remain the actual five eager plugins; installation is explicit. Format-manager/plugin-copy behavior follows real source registration, not automatic arithmetic installation.
>
> A private concrete registered-plugin record may extend the current binding mechanism; it must preserve source registry growth/publication and permit later plugin families. Merely increasing a hard-coded bound to six and calling that the complete generic plugin registry would be a false scope claim. Exact selected arithmetic binding and full general registry coverage must be distinguished.
>
> ## Source assertions and tests-first plan
>
> There is no dedicated registered arithmetic declaration-plugin test found. `src/test/main.cpp:176,196` registers arithmetic simplifier and rewriter consumers. `arith_rewriter.cpp` invokes actual parser/rewriter/normalization paths: its parser VERIFY and nonempty-assertion ENSURE execute per parsed example and cannot be claimed ported by standalone plugin fixtures. `var_subst.cpp` and algebraic/nlarith/QE consumers similarly require their real algorithms. Existing AST registered assertion totals remain unchanged.
>
> After API/integration approval, observe missing-API RED before production for the following additional finite fixtures:
>
> - Real installation and every cached declaration/sort/app flag, owner pin and exact finalize sequence; fresh-state and installation failure prefixes.
> - Rational numerals 0/15/16/negative/large/fractional; cache reuse, warm allocation-free hits, INC-before-cache-growth faults; direct fractional NUM with nonzero flag; sticky NRA/normal logic sequence and recognizer output flags.
> - Both declaration overloads, unknown/zero-arity/NUM branch order, ignored range/parameters, unary SUB, any-Real versus first-domain selection, and actual mixed-argument casts with candidate-before-coercion failure accounting.
> - Every recognizer/matcher false-output route and copied rational failure; all utilities including singleton VAR versus APP, equality ID orientation, simplify owning results and explicit app-reference operators.
> - Names append order and symbol-before-vector failure prefixes, three uninterpreted kinds, base unique-value shortcuts, all four ADD-distinct cases.
> - Actual algebraic rational/irrational/root creation, ID recycle and reserve/copy failures, equality/distinctness, cross-manager external translation, deleting parameters while plugin live versus registry gone. These tests await the real backend, not invented stand-ins.
> - Immediate whole graph/root/Words accounting before formatting/Close; synchronized temporary cleanup and retained source prefixes separately; budget/refusal/allocation tests, all source debug actions, warm plateau and no hidden owner allocations.
>
> Native/full checkeddebug, named race and actual checkeddebug JS RUN/PASS, vet, WASI builds, source audit and no-generics checks follow immutable selected-file snapshots. All artifacts remain below golang. Until reviewed dependencies and integration are implemented, the complete arithmetic plugin and its registered consumer tests remain OPEN.
>
> ## Backend prerequisite audit and proposed next actual algorithm packet
>
> The declaration plugin depends on `algebraic_numbers::manager`, which is a real 3073-line implementation plus a492-line public header. Its implementation owns rational and algebraic cells (polynomial coefficient array, MPBQI isolating interval, minimal/sign/not-rational/index flags), cached intervals, temporary numerals and vectors, actual polynomial/upolynomial managers, source allocator and borrowed resource limit. It requires more than the currently implemented raw MPZ/MPQ and MPBQ/MPBQI arithmetic. Public methods include lifecycle/conversion, arithmetic/roots/powers, order/equality and sign/evaluation, isolation/refinement, integer selection, parameter updates and rendering. None can be replaced by an `OwnedRational` pretending to represent an irrational.
>
> The real dependency chain is:
>
> `IntegerManager` → `mpzzp_manager` → dense upolynomial core arithmetic/division/GCD → Sturm chains/root isolation and refinement → algebraic cells/operations → plugin external parameters/numerals. Factorization, polynomial arithmetic/resultants and conversion dependencies join this path; `sexpr2upolynomial` then enables the plugin's actual polynomial-root sexpr entry point. Current MPBQ/MPBQI cover dyadic interval numerals, not these polynomial/root algorithms.
>
> `upolynomial.h` is922lines and `.cpp`3127lines; the header also imports the actual multivariate polynomial header and source factor parameter definitions. Dense core owns a real `mpzzp_manager` plus basic/division/exact-division/GCD/CRA/six modular-GCD/square-free/power temporary vectors. Its ctor does not eagerly compute polynomials. Source reset/trim/set_size/set/neg/add/sub/mul have concrete owning coefficient actions and alias handling (`m_basic_tmp` then swap); this should be a later complete selected algorithm packet, not a copy-on-write Go slice substitute. GCD uses the real prime table, modular images and fallback; factorization lives in the additional upolynomial factorization source and uses its real RNG. Conversion from multivariate source `polynomial_ref` remains open until its actual owner is implemented.
>
> `sexpr2upolynomial.cpp` accepts exactly +, -, *, ^, integer coefficients and symbol x; it recursively checks depth, builds real scoped coefficient vectors, and executes exact add/sub/mul/power actions. Its errors carry source line/position. The existing sexpr owner is a prerequisite, but a standalone parser cannot advance root creation until these polynomial algorithms exist.
>
> The smallest coherent missing actual algorithm is **all defined operations of `src/util/mpzzp.h`**, the dynamically selected Z / GF(p) / composite Zp numeric manager used by upolynomial. It needs no fabricated polynomial object and can use current `IntegerManager` operations, including real ExtendedGCD, signed Rem, fused arithmetic, bit/log/root operations and owned formatting. Proposed independent ownership is new `mpnum/mpzzp.go`, `mpnum/mpzzp_test.go` and a separate status document, subject to coordinator approval.
>
> Concrete `IntegerModularManager` borrows one actual unsynchronized `IntegerManager` and owns the source seven real Int fields: modulus, lower bound, upper bound, three inverse temporaries and division temporary. Its actual cold header must reserve before object publication. Close deletes these fields in explicit source order and refunds only its own header; the borrowed numeric manager outlives it. All arithmetic uses pointers to actual concrete Int records; no arbitrary precision substitute, interface dispatch, boxed coefficient or generics. Source mode/configuration, alias/publication and cached scratch are retained.
>
> Proposed API maps every header-defined body: constructor(s), manager accessor, Precise/Field/Finite/Modular, modulus copy/read adapter, SetZ/SetZPInt/SetZPUint64/SetPSquare/SetZPSwap, IsPNormalized/PNormalize, Reset/Del/Neg/Abs, all sign/zero/one comparisons, Add/Sub/Inc/Dec/Mul/AddMul/SubMul, Inv/Div/Divides/Swap, both GCD forms and ExtendedGCD, every typed Set, mutable versus const machine-conversion routes, Hash/Power/PerfectSquare/Mul2k/PowerOfTwoMultiple/Log2/MLog2/MachineDiv2k/Root, formatting and destruction. Signatures remain explicit for mutable conversion operations, because those normalize their input while the const source overloads do not. A concrete manager's private helpers avoid duplicated numeric algorithms; normalization remains the actual Rem then upper comparison/Sub or lower comparison/Add, not canonical [0,p) modular arithmetic.
>
> Important source defects/domains discovered in the complete `mpzzp.h` read:
>
> - Bounds are centered: odd p has [-floor(p/2),floor(p/2)], even p has [1-p/2,p/2]. Normalization/Neg/Abs and ordering preserve this representation.
> - Both modulus-taking constructors accept `prime` but never initialize `m_p_prime`. After such construction, `field()` and division's debug prime assertion read an indeterminate bool. The Z constructor plus explicit `set_zp` is the defined source route (set_zp sets true), used by registered upolynomial tests. Do not silently initialize the buggy constructor from its unused argument and claim faithful behavior. A Go constructor may represent an explicit unknown-prime state and diagnose only the actual undefined bool read, allowing otherwise defined normalization/arithmetic; status must mark that adapter precisely.
> - `set_p_sq` sets prime=false before squaring modulus and recomputing bounds; `set_zp_swap` preserves the prior prime flag. `divides` short-circuits field/nonzero before raw IntegerManager.Divides.
> - Inverse normalizes the caller first, performs real ExtendedGCD into all three cached outputs, normalizes its first coefficient, swaps into the caller, and only then debug-asserts gcd==1. Composite/nonunit release results are not to be strengthened into a preemptive mathematical inverse check. Undefined inputs and enabled source assertion adapters are separate.
> - `power` uses a uint32 mask loop, initializes/copies its local power then writes output1, and squares the local on every iteration including the final one. For exponent>=2^31 the mask wraps0 and the source loop never terminates. Explicit typed nontermination handling must be documented rather than a replacement exponentiation algorithm; finite exponents preserve all source actions and aliases.
> - Modular perfect-square calls source NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET; modular roots have source debug !modular preconditions. These are explicit remaining unsupported/undefined conditional routes, not invented modular algorithms.
>
> No direct registered mpzzp test exists. `src/test/main.cpp:205–207` registers polynomial, upolynomial and algebraic. Upolynomial's active entry calls GCD, lower bound, factorization, remainder, exact division, root isolation5, root isolation (twice), Sturm2, rational-to-dyadic conversion, translation, refinement/refinability, Sturm, one-half removal, basic arithmetic, Zp cases, and two extended-GCD cases. GCD body has an unconditional early return; its later examples are inactive. The Zp and extended-GCD examples print polynomial outcomes rather than standalone mpzzp ENSUREs. Algebraic's active entry calls root, isolation, ex1, sign evaluation, select-small, Dejan, Wilkinson, basic and dyadic refinement. Their registered assertion loops cannot be counted without full call/conditional evaluation, and are not claimed ported by the modular-manager unit.
>
> Tests-FIRST for the modular packet should observe missing API RED, then independently freeze centered representatives for every residue in small odd/even moduli; source integer-mode delegation; prime/composite mode transitions; all inverse/division/fused aliases; exact ExtendedGCD cached coefficients and source output order; mutable versus const conversion; final unused power-square action failures; constructor unknown-prime adapter; immediate cells/Words/header accounting at every predictable allocation failure before formatting/Close; all real debug short circuits and warm cached zero-allocation paths. Test-only bounded integer arithmetic/math-big may provide independent numeric expectations. Full upolynomial/algebraic registered consumers remain open until their algorithms run.
>
> After that leaf packet, propose the actual dense coefficient owner plus full core basic arithmetic/reset/trim/set/neg/add/sub/mul/derivative/equality/evaluation needed by subsequent division and Sturm isolation. Its exact concrete storage and selected source test assertions must be reviewed separately; this proposal does not authorize that implementation or pretend it completes root isolation.
>
> ## Subsequent implemented backend prerequisite
>
> The approved mpzzp leaf proposal above has now been implemented and verified
> in PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-mpzzp-port-status-md: actual IntegerModularManager owns the seven source
> numerals and preserves every selected defined method and publication order,
> with constructor unknown-prime and raw-Power error-cleanup adaptations explicit.
> Thirteen tests-first groups and full native/debug/race/actual JS/vet/WASI/source
> gates passed. This does not install an arithmetic plugin or execute polynomial
> root isolation. Dense coefficient ownership and source arithmetic are the next
> proposal; GCD/Sturm/algebraic/external-parameter and real AST dispatch/coercion
> remain original complete-port requirements. No rational-only plugin replaces
> those missing algorithms.

### Historical evidence: AST_CORE_PACKET.md

Original text follows as historical evidence; its old completion claims do not

> # First real AST runtime packet
>
> The selected first runtime-core packet is implemented and frozen against
> HEAD9f8974d, and held for coordinator review and integration. The original
> design was approved against HEADd0ceaf5. Whole-manager completion remains OPEN,
> with the remaining source boundaries recorded below. This document
> supersedes the provisional dependency list in PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-ast-core-port-status-md,
> without changing that frozen document. The
> no-generics rule in AGENTS.md overrides generic sketches in GO_PORT_PLAN.md.
>
> ## Scope and source boundary
>
> The first runtime packet implements all five kinds, all six parameter kinds,
> sort/function information, the actual structural chaining table, registration
> and logical deletion, concrete owning references, expression persistent
> arrays, and the five plugins used by eager initialization. It must support a
> real normal manager and a real formatting manager. A Boolean-only manager,
> lazy placeholder plugins, or an integer array with dummy value callbacks does
> not meet this contract.
>
> Evidence: ast.h parameter/node definitions and plugin classes; ast.cpp
> parameter/decl_info sections, get_node_hash/compare_nodes, constructors and
> init at 1297–1398, registration at 1666–1780, deletion at 1781–1840, factory
> and quantifier sections; ast.h:1411–1497 and 1916–1930 for array ownership.
> The basic plugin is in these files, not a separate basic_decl_plugin file.
> Registered tests are src/test/ast.cpp and src/test/parray.cpp. Source vector
> parameter destruction is ascending, per vector.h::destroy_elements; it must
> not be replaced with reverse element cleanup by analogy to class members.
>
> The complete manager remains the goal. This packet does not claim the copy
> constructor, cross-manager AST translation, every proof builder, arithmetic
> plugin/coercion implementation, dependency operations/arrays, marks, source
> printers or resource-limit integration. Those have explicit follow-on gates
> below. Constructor-owned empty dependency headers are real initialization
> state, not callable stub dependency algorithms.
>
> ## Frozen external contracts to approve
>
> All operations return a typed error when validation or a predictable reserve
> fails. Zero ASTHandle represents source nullptr. Factories return non-owning
> handles with source RC initially zero; obtaining a handle does not implicitly
> pin it. Owned wrappers perform the source retain/release actions explicitly.
> Public calls serialize through the manager; private helpers do not reacquire
> the lock. Borrowed symbol/numeric owners must outlive both the normal manager
> and its nested formatting manager.
>
> ```go
> type ASTHandle struct { origin uint64; slot, generation uint32 } // private fields
> type ASTKind uint16 // App=0, Var=1, Quantifier=2, Sort=3, FuncDecl=4
> type ASTProofMode uint8 // Disabled=0, Enabled=1
> type ASTManagerConfig struct {
>     Symbols *SymbolManager
>     Numerals *mpnum.RationalService
>     Budget *arena.Budget
>     ProofMode ASTProofMode
>     OutOfMemory func() bool
> }
> func NewASTManager(ASTManagerConfig) (*ASTManager, error)
> func NewASTFormatManager(ASTManagerConfig) (*ASTManager, error)
> ```
>
> Normal construction creates a full nested format manager with proofs disabled
> before initializing its own families/plugins. Format construction initializes
> the same five real plugins and pins and has no nested manager. GetFormatManager
> returns self for the latter. Both share supplied symbols/numerals, but have
> different AST origins, IDs, interning, allocation and pins. The normal owner
> owns/charges the nested manager; no global numeric or symbol manager appears.
>
> The two source trace overloads need concrete adapters, not silent omission:
> NewASTManagerWithTrace(config, borrowed io.Writer) and
> NewASTManagerWithTraceFile(config, path string). io.Writer is a cold stream,
> never a hot record. The file overload owns its file and EOF/close action; the
> stream overload borrows it. Nested format construction borrows the same
> stream. Literal source trace events must work before declaring these overloads
> ported. Printer-backed error/diagnostic text stays an explicit printer gate;
> it is not a reason to substitute a fake stream. Test files remain under golang.
>
> Proposed methods needed by the first tests and five-kind audit:
>
> ```go
> func (m *ASTManager) MkBoolSort() (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkConst(name Symbol, sort ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkSort(name Symbol, info ASTSortInfo) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkFuncDecl(name Symbol, domain []ASTHandle,
>     rangeSort ASTHandle, info ASTFuncDeclInfo) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkApp(decl ASTHandle, args []ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkFamilySort(fid FamilyID, kind int32,
>     parameters []ASTParameter) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkFamilyFuncDecl(fid FamilyID, kind int32,
>     parameters []ASTParameter, domain []ASTHandle,
>     rangeSort ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkFamilyApp(fid FamilyID, kind int32,
>     parameters []ASTParameter, args []ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkVar(index uint32, sort ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) MkQuantifier(spec ASTQuantifierSpec) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) IncRef(ASTHandle) error
> func (m *ASTManager) DecRef(ASTHandle) error
> func (m *ASTManager) GetKind(ASTHandle) (ASTKind, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) GetASTID(ASTHandle) (uint32, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) GetHash(ASTHandle) (uint32, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) GetRefCount(ASTHandle) (uint32, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) GetSort(ASTHandle) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) GetArg(ASTHandle, uint32) (ASTHandle, error)
> func (m *ASTManager) Stats() ASTManagerStats
> func (m *ASTManager) Close() error
> ```
>
> Slice arguments are borrowed only for the duration of the call, never stored.
> Kind-specific getters cover every source scalar and indexed accessor; they
> return scalars/checked handles, not arena record pointers. ASTQuantifierSpec
> is a caller input containing forall, bound sorts/names, body, weight, qid,
> skid, patterns and no-patterns. It is not the stored record. It does not invent
> a simultaneous-pattern/no-pattern route rejected by the source constructor.
> Nullable info tokens represent the source null-info distinction.
>
> ASTParameter, ASTSortInfo and ASTFuncDeclInfo are scalar owner/slot/generation
> tokens into concrete manager-owned typed records. Parameter constructors cover
> int32, uint32-to-int32 source bit pattern, AST, symbol, rational, double and
> external uint32 ID. Copy/Assign/Move/Del and scalar typed accessors are explicit.
> Rational construction/copy uses the real RationalService; AST parameter
> construction does not retain. Info constructors copy parameters as source
> vectors do; unique node registration copies info again, then attaches its AST
> parameters. Deleting unattached caller info does not call attachment del_eh.
> Borrowed rational getters become explicitly named owned copies, with documented
> additional Go boundary copy, never an exposed mutable raw numeral.
>
> ASTRef and concrete ExprRef/SortRef/FuncDeclRef/AppRef/VarRef/QuantifierRef use
> manager-issued scalar ownership tokens and explicit New/Copy/Assign/Reset/Del.
> Copying a Go token is not acquiring another retain. Retire generations rather
> than making a stale token valid again. Preserve source self-assignment and
> retain-before-release ordering. No per-reference heap object is necessary.
> Ref vectors are concrete typed storage with source null callback adaptation
> explicitly recorded if required, not a generic ref_vector replacement.
>
> ## Storage, identity and charges
>
> Use a concrete common node directory with named scalar fields: generation,
> live state, kind, sourceID, hash, uint32 RC, mark1/mark2/shared flags, debug mark
> owner identities and kind-record index. Five concrete pointer-free record
> pages hold Sort, FuncDecl, App, Var and Quantifier fields. This avoids a boxed
> node union or a large union of all five bodies. A temporary local record borrow
> must be reacquired after any allocation or callback.
>
> Sort records store Symbol plus info token. FuncDecl records store Symbol,
> arity, range and domain payload descriptor. App records store declaration,
> argument count/descriptor and source depth/ground/quantifier/label flags. Var
> records store index/sort. Quantifier records store body, forall, weight, qid,
> skid, all counts/descriptors, depth, unused-vars flag and labels flag. Name
> payloads contain Symbol scalars; AST payloads contain compact internal refs.
>
> Parameter pages contain named kind, int, internal AST ref, Symbol,
> mpnum.OwnedRational, float64 and external-ID fields. OwnedRational is opaque to
> g3 and is stored as its actual pointer-free type; do not serialize its private
> fields into arbitrary byte offsets. Info pages contain family/kind, flags,
> parameter-vector descriptor and SortSize or function flags. Real typed page
> backings and source vector capacity storage must be charged, including any
> union-layout inflation. Page directories are cold and pointerful, one entry
> per page. No pointers, strings, slices, interfaces or functions appear in hot
> node/parameter/persistent-array/chaining entries. Recursively audit the actual
> imported record layouts on native and wasm targets.
>
> Node origin/slot/generation is distinct from source ID. Source expression IDs
> start at zero, declarations at 1<<31. Recycle/free-list behavior uses the
> committed charged utilIDGen, including OOM skip and uint32 behavior. CompressIDs
> later changes source IDs without moving public handles. Numeric ID caches in
> the basic plugin must follow the source and cannot silently become slot caches.
>
> Use actual arena.SmallBytes for variable scalar payloads with readable fixed
> encoding, or concrete typed payload pages where checked ref width warrants it.
> The implementation must state which layout it chooses before writing tests.
> Charge actual target sizeof via audited reflection/layout constants, whole
> allocated capacity, every owner/header/directory/free-list, retired ledger,
> format manager, plugin/cache, scratch buffer and old+new growth peak. Never
> charge fictitious C++ object bytes in addition to a Go record's actual storage.
> Constructor fault tests sum the complete graph rather than assuming fixed
> header bytes across architectures. Borrowed SymbolManager/RationalService
> headers are excluded; storage they acquire for copied numerals is included in
> the operation's full-service oracle.
>
> ## AST-specific source chaining table
>
> Implement a separate concrete AST table specialization, reusing the audited
> algorithm, not the int32 comparator. Entries contain only internal AST refs
> and next indices. Key hash is node.hash; equality first tests matching hashes,
> then source compare_nodes. Source pointer identity means equality of live
> internal AST identities, not source IDs or an address cast. AST erase must use
> identity even when structural equality would find another candidate.
>
> Preserve bucket/cellar layout, modulo, growth before duplicate detection,
> insert-at-head displacement, copy reversal, repeated cellar doubling, bucket
> ascending/chain traversal, collision counters and failed-copy UsedSlots prefix.
> Do not implement it as UintMap or Go map. Hashing is uint32 source arithmetic,
> not raw struct-byte hashing: range is omitted from function hash but checked
> by equality; quantifier hash uses declared-sort hash, pattern count and body.
> Array hash consumes triples backwards; its 0/1/2/3-element branches remain
> separate. Permanent expected vectors must cover every branch and overflow.
>
> Defined structural quirks are mandatory fixtures: sort cardinality and private
> parameters ignored; function idempotence ignored; null-info distinction;
> quantifier qid/skid ignored; range checked despite hash omission. decl_info
> compares using the LEFT parameter count without checking right count. Preserve
> finite left-prefix equality in a forced hash collision; a right-shorter read
> is undefined C++ and becomes a typed validation error, not a new symmetric
> length rule. NaN equality and finite double hash conversion follow source;
> out-of-range double-to-uint32 conversion is undefined and receives a typed
> domain adapter. Function is_null ignores flat-associativity, kind and params.
>
> ## Publication and destruction actions
>
> Registration allocates candidate/trailing payload, computes hash, inserts into
> the real interner, then allocates source ID. Duplicate candidates free their
> raw storage only: no info deep copy, child retains, or consumed ID. Unique
> sort/function info is copied after insertion/ID, then init_eh runs parameters
> ascending. Function retains domain ascending then range; app retains decl then
> args ascending; var retains sort; quantifier retains declared sorts ascending,
> body, patterns ascending, then no-patterns ascending. Derive app flags during
> that source traversal. Constant app flags are the shared constant defaults;
> nonconstant app depth saturates at 65535, quantifier depth does not use that cap.
>
> Source C++ allocation exceptions after interner publication can leave an
> incompletely constructed graph. The Go adapter must explicitly unwind only
> new candidate ownership, identity-erase that candidate, release completed
> attachments and clean copied info, without undoing source table growth,
> collision/failed-copy counters, ID consumption or legitimate numeral scratch.
> Tests must inspect these prefixes immediately. This adapter addresses an
> invalid source continuation; it is not an assertion of whole-operation
> transactionality. Parameter assignment deletes an old rational before copying
> the new one, so failure must not restore that old rational silently.
>
> Deletion uses source ptr_buffer inline16 and doubling overflow, lexical per
> delete invocation. Remove identity first, recycle source ID next, release info
> AST/external attachments ascending then destroy parameter vector ascending.
> Info releases may recursively invoke deletion independently of the outer
> worklist. Function queues domain ascending then range; app decl then args;
> var sort; quantifier sorts/body/patterns/no-patterns. The queue pops LIFO.
> Free node only after these actions. Do not replace this with a recursive child
> walk or an arbitrary retained vector capacity schedule. Preflight charged ID
> free-list cleanup capacity before a publication that requires it; document
> each physical preflight adapter. Worklist reserve failure must leave an owned
> continuation ledger or be prevented before destructive release, not abandon
> RC-zero nodes. Exact buffer/failure policy is a review gate before coding.
>
> Release IncRef wraps uint32; wrapping does not itself delete. DecRef at zero
> is a source assertion domain and returns a typed error. In g3debug, preserve
> the source preincrement UINT_MAX assertion and predecrement zero assertion;
> g3checked alone is handle validation, not Z3DEBUG. Null manager Inc/Dec is a
> source no-op. Debug contains/slow_not_contains/assertion routes need separate
> conditional tests and method inventory; no claim that value equality tests
> cover these actions.
>
> Runtime debug_ref_count is separate from g3debug: it suppresses ID recycling
> and info del_eh/deallocation, records free IDs in real UintMap, and frees node
> storage. Retained info must have a charged cold retirement ledger. Close may
> destroy retained numeric payloads as an explicit owner-teardown adapter, but
> must not replay skipped AST/external callbacks against freed nodes. Until
> these behaviors are implemented and fault-tested, that mode remains OPEN.
>
> ## Real eager plugins and constructor teardown
>
> Families initialize in order basic, label, pattern, model-value, user-sort,
> arith. Registering arith's family does NOT register an arithmetic plugin.
> Preserve int_real_coercions=true initially; missing plugin factory returns
> source nullptr. Unsupported arithmetic coercion continuations are a real
> dependency gate, never a fake conversion or forced disabled flag.
>
> Five concrete cold plugin objects implement real declaration/sort/value hooks.
> The plugin registry may use cold interfaces as GO_PORT_PLAN permits; no hot
> record stores one. Basic implements its complete header declaration dispatch,
> Boolean/proof sorts, pinned Boolean declarations, undef proof declaration,
> eq/oeq/ite caches by source sort ID, proof-arity caches and their real flags and
> finalization order. Actual proof declaration variants are included even though
> manager proof builders are a later packet. Label validates int/symbol params
> and real Boolean domains; pattern accepts source argument sorts and returns
> Boolean; model-value uses int+AST-sort parameters, private parameters and real
> value uniqueness; user-sort registers names in source vector/map order and
> copies them in mk_fresh. Base default no-op/false hooks are actual source
> defaults, not invented callbacks.
>
> Initialization order: nested format manager first; basic plugin pins Bool and
> Proof sorts and declarations; manager pins Bool, Proof, undef app; register
> remaining four plugins; manager pins true then false. Failure tests cover
> every successful reserve prefix in both managers and prove completed roots,
> numerals, pages, headers and owned streams are refunded.
>
> Close drops manager Bool, Proof, true, false, undef pins in that order; finalizes
> plugins in registry order, destroys plugins in that order, then resets registry.
> Remaining interner roots are found by actual source child marking and table
> traversal, forced to RC zero and deleted. Since registry is already reset,
> external del_eh on leaked roots cannot find a plugin: preserve that source
> fact. Close then destroys nested format manager and owned stream. Outstanding
> public AST handles become invalid. Escaped expression-array refs need an
> explicit teardown policy: proposed bulk invalidate/cleanup their physical
> graph after node teardown without calling AST DecRef on freed nodes, matching
> allocator teardown rather than inventing live arrays after manager Close.
> This differs from standalone Int32PArrayManager.Close's live-cell guard and
> requires an explicit integration test, not an implicit reuse of that Close.
>
> ## Concrete expression persistent arrays
>
> ASTExprArray is a scalar owner/cell-generation/updates record. Implement all
> manager array methods Mk/Del/Copy/Size/Empty/Get/Set/SetFrom/Push/PushFrom/
> Pop/PopFrom/Unshare/Unfold/Reroot. Algorithms are the actual parray ROOT/SET/
> PUSH_BACK/POP_BACK forward and reverse trails, with RC30, preserve_roots=true,
> factor=2, max_trail_sz=16 for ast_manager. The disabled parray.cpp tst4 has a
> separate max_trail_sz=8 specialization; do not claim it from the manager's 16.
> Stored values retain/release through actual locked AST helpers. ROOT payloads
> own all initialized expression refs; trails own values/links as source. The
> documented inverse-PUSH idx defect remains, with its dedicated regression;
> no copied-slice implementation can replace these actions. Warm updates must
> plateau in real AST nodes and array cells, not just heap bytes after Close.

> ## Current implementation evidence (not a freeze)
>
> The observed initial missing-API RED used an isolated committed HEAD archive

> # Concrete AST dependencies and persistent dependency arrays
>
> Selected configuration: `dependency_manager<ast_manager::expr_dependency_config>` and `parray_manager<ast_manager::expr_dependency_array_config>` from `src/util/dependency.h`, `src/util/parray.h`, and the actual AST manager wrappers in `src/ast/ast.h`/`ast.cpp`. These are real AST callbacks, not the region-backed `scoped_dependency_manager<void*>` used by old intervals/Grobner.
>
> ## Source methods and public contracts
>
> `ASTDependency` is a pointer-free, comparable owner-qualified allocator token. Fresh leaves and joins have source RC0; callers retain them explicitly with `DependencyInc` and release with `DependencyDec`. Null is source empty. Public methods are `DependencyEmpty`, `DependencyLeaf`, `DependencyJoin`, `DependencyJoinValues`, `DependencyInc`, `DependencyDec`, `DependencyRefCount`, `DependencyIsLeaf`, `DependencyContains`, `DependencyLinearizeRaw`, and `DependencyLinearize`. Leaf null is the AST wrapper fast path, rather than a generic null-valued leaf. Join null/equal fast paths do not increment. The 30-bit counter wraps exactly; zero DEC is a source debug assertion, with defined release unsigned underflow.
>
> The actual constructor, leaf/join allocator/callback order, iterative LIFO destructor, shared FIFO queue, root/child marking order, early-found unmarking, and raw linearization of dependency identities are implemented. Distinct leaves containing the same expression remain distinct dependencies. AST-level linearization then uses the real `ASTFastMark1` and source `remove_duplicates`: mark, optional in-place `set(j)`, advance j, final shrink. It deduplicates the entire preexisting output, preserving stable order and completed compaction prefixes on failure. No staging/replay/maps are used in production.
>
> `ASTDependencyJoinProgress{Completed, PendingLeaf}` exposes the actual loop prefix when constructing the next leaf succeeds but allocating its join refuses. Both returned nonnull RC0 roots remain owned by the caller; no silent DEC of the unjoined leaf occurs. Each nonnull input is checked at its actual iteration; a later foreign or stale token returns the preceding completed leaf/AST INC prefix. The borrowed input slice is never persisted.
>
> `ASTExprVector` is the actual non-owning expression-pointer output specialization: `NewExprVector`, `ExprVectorPush`, `ExprVectorGet`, `ExprVectorSize`, `ExprVectorReset`, and `DelExprVector`. Shared scalar codecs with the reference vector invoke no reference callbacks here. A caller must keep expressions alive separately; output tokens are not owning AST references. Output owners require explicit NewExprVector and must not be shallow-copied or coerced into an owning reference-vector token; the full generic ptr-vector copy API is not claimed. Persistent-array owners likewise use explicit Copy, not Go scalar assignment. ExprVectorGet checks actual AST lifetime. Additional generic vector methods are not claimed.
>
> `ASTDependencyArray` is an owner-qualified scalar with source update counter. The full selected persistent-array branches are implemented: `DependencyArrayMk`, `Del`, `Copy`, `Size`, `Empty`, `Get`, `Set`, `SetFrom`, `Push`, `PushFrom`, `Pop`, `PopFrom`, `Unshare`, `Unfold`, and `Reroot` (all names have the `DependencyArray` prefix). Internal ROOT/SET/PUSH/POP encoding, RC30, both scratch vectors, copy-values callbacks, source requested growth `0->2->(3c+1)/2`, ROOT preservation, update threshold `>size`, trail `>16`, and reroot split `size/2` follow the source. Its value manager is the actual ASTManager, whose callbacks route to its dependency manager. The source `manager()` accessor is represented by the existing containing manager; no borrowed raw callback owner is exported.
>
> The selected configuration is reference-counted with preserve_roots=true; false/reference-disabled/different value-manager configurations remain separate. Public logical Get/Set assertions are debug-only. Release can read a retained initialized pointer or construct a nonroot SET at an arbitrary uint32 index. Source empty nonroot POP can publish a POP with index0 and subsequent Size UINT32_MAX; debug rejects at !empty. Root/null empty-pop physical undefined behavior is guarded. Copy-only Get returns a retained scalar even if its dependency lifetime has ended; actual dependency queries/callbacks then diagnose an invalid handle rather than dereferencing a source dangling pointer. No universal logical bound replaces these distinctions. At an invalid retained old callback, rset preserves the incoming INC completed before the lifetime guard; tests recover it explicitly. Generation validation remains strict after a lifetime ends, even if storage is reused; raw source transparent pointer replacement/ABA is not emulated.
>
> ## Physical ownership and failure adaptations
>
> All hot records contain scalars, not Go pointers. The existing manager header charge automatically includes the two actual embedded owners and their source scratch-slice headers once. Both main and formatting managers bind them eagerly. No new allocation is invented by empty owner construction.
>
> Selected source 64-bit leaf/join sizes are16/24; charged Go encoded sizes are24/32. Each has an actual8-byte intrusive continuation link. Source flags/RC are encoded at0, value/children at8, continuation at16/24. This additional physical backing is an explicit allocation-exception cleanup adaptation. Ordinary deletion grows the source LIFO todo only at its real push, after decrement. On first reserve refusal, already queued entries and the failed entry are linked in exactly the same LIFO order; the same finite deletion completes without another reservation, freeing every dependency and performing every AST DEC. The first error is propagated after completion. AST emergency destructor errors similarly consume ownership while finishing the remaining dependency graph. No all-live scratch preflight, replay, ignored allocation refusal, or orphaned lexical node substitutes for this.
>
> The FIFO traversal queue is a real charged concrete slice, with complete old/new backing overlap and full-capacity scalar copying. Its source unsigned32 allocation-byte bound and actual host backing-byte bound are checked separately before reserve; arena.ErrBounds is the concrete checked overflow/memory-domain adapter, not a claim to the source default_exception class. An explicit unsafe source allocation-exception adapter clears the completed dependency marks (including a root marked before an initial push refusal); appended output remains a source completed prefix. This is distinct from FastMark1's source defect: when its mark-before-buffer-push refuses, the current unlisted AST mark remains dirty after lexical Close. It is not repaired by linearization. Tests demonstrate explicit caller recovery.
>
> Dependency-array cells retain the source selected24-byte scalar layout; value locators are8 bytes. Source backing has an8-byte capacity header; actual Go backing charges12 bytes including initialized high-water metadata. Growth copies all old capacity bytes without inventing initialization. Only actual writes/logical copy construction advance initialization. Logical copy-values increments only copied values. Physical/initialized/allocator uint32 bounds diagnose source invalid memory access; the actual12-byte limit differs from source8. Shared-root reversal publishes before the requested operation, preserving normal allocation/refcount prefixes. Reroot PUSH storage preparation before destructive union retagging is the existing explicit source-unsafe exception adapter, not a second algorithm. Temporary rematerialized blocks/cells are cleaned lexically on failure; consumed callback errors finish publication and clear consumed caller tokens. Owner/provenance checks guard Go raw-handle misuse before numeric/domain callbacks.
>
> Manager Close follows existing forced AST teardown before allocator/member reclamation. Escaped dependency/array/output records are bulk reclaimed without callbacks against freed ASTs; retained todo/get/reroot backing is then refunded exactly once. Constructor-prefix cleanup also handles unbound empty owners. Borrowed symbols/numerals/allocators are never separately closed by the embedded managers.
>
> ## Tests-first evidence and source attribution
>
> Initial complete actual API test produced isolated compilation RED (session24055, HEAD07a6182 plus new test, undefined dependency/array/output APIs). Six initial tests plus constructor binding passed after implementation (22351). Added source RC30 release regression produced behavioral RED50797, then native/checked-debug GREEN86342. Constructor-prefix test exposed a real nil-owner teardown panic (30215), fixed and GREEN97826. Empty nonroot POP release regression was RED14808, then full targeted release/checked-debug GREEN17998. Later-input prevalidation was caught RED26908 and corrected to preserve prior source prefixes (GREEN11382); invalid retained-old rollback was caught RED31080 and corrected (GREEN93275). Scalar source/host scratch-bound test was missing-helper RED before the concrete helper (GREEN62650). Full gates below supersede intermediate development runs.
>
> There are **zero registered direct AST-valued dependency or dependency-array source assertions**. Added tests cover actual AST callbacks, source FIFO/LIFO action order, duplicate values/shared DAGs, independent finite reachable-value sets, aliases, real failure prefixes, physical allocator live counts before Close, constructor teardown, and warm allocation-free raw traversal/output reuse. > # AST dependency owning alias packet
>
> Source: ast.h:2232–2234, complete obj_ref.h, ref_vector.h, ref_buffer.h, their concrete pointer vector/buffer algorithms, and actual AST dependency INC/DEC callbacks. This packet closes the selected dependency owning aliases, not the generic templates or their other configurations. Source Microsoft notices will be preserved in translated files. No generic Go, unsafe, per-entry Go pointers, hidden slices, or substitute callback owners.
>
> ## Concrete ownership and storage
>
> All public owners are distinct pointer-free scalar tokens qualified by the containing ASTManager. Explicit construction/copy/move/destruction is mandatory; Go shallow copy is prohibited. Manager methods use the existing lock and existing charged allocator services. No manager fields, existing core headers, constructor, storage files, or teardown methods need edits: actual owned records/backing live in the already budgeted allocator graphs, and force-close has the existing AST teardown/bulk-reclamation policy.
>
> `ASTDependencyRef` owns a16-byte encoded cold record containing dependency slot/generation plus record validation fields. It borrows the ASTManager by scalar provenance, not a heap owner pointer. A default/null obj_ref is a constructed record holding null, distinct from an invalid unconstructed Go token. Constructor allocation is an explicit Go locator adaptation before the source INC; copy allocates another real record then INC, move allocates a record and transfers without INC/DEC. Get/bool/equality copy the raw pointer token and do not invent a dependency dereference. Actual dereference/query remains on the dependency manager. Steal transfers one retained reference to the returned raw dependency without DEC; caller must eventually DEC it.
>
> `ASTDependencyRefVector` owns a24-byte encoded cold record, including actual cleanup target/cursor words, source-geometric backing0→2→3→5..., and8-byte slot/generation entries. Reuse existing fixed-width AST ref-vector geometry/byte codecs only, never its AST-node callbacks. Selected source header8 versus actual charged header12 includes initialized high-water. Growth preserves ALL old capacity bytes and initialization history; no INC/DEC during relocation. Copy constructor starts empty and appends geometrically, unlike raw vector exact-capacity copy. `set(other)` resets then appends, self no-op; public Go `Assign` denotes this source set method because ordinary copy assignment is private. Move transfers backing only. All pointer-returning Get/Back/element/iterator adapters copy retained raw dependency tokens; actual dependency dereference validates generation separately.
>
> `ASTDependencyRefBuffer` owns an actual160-byte encoded record:32 bytes of state/initialization metadata and the actual inline16×8-byte dependency entries. This is charged physical Go storage, distinct from the selected source LP64 wrapper/header plus128-byte inline area. No phantom separately allocated inline block or per-buffer Go slice/header. Overflow backing is in the borrowed vector allocator with actual12-byte metadata plus doubled pointer capacity16→32→64.... The source capacity doubles uint32, and selected actual byte/host/allocator guards diagnose unsafe wrapped allocation before writing. Source buffer growth copies ONLY logical m_pos entries, so overflow initialized extent becomes that logical prefix; it does not preserve inactive dynamic tail. The original inline area and its separately recorded initialization extent survive growth/finalize until the owner record is destroyed. Finalize restores inline16, size0, leaving actual retained inline bytes intact. Reset keeps the current backing. The intended copy constructor starts inline16 and appends, but the preserved ref_buffer constructor is uninstantiable under conforming dependent-base lookup (see diagnostic below). Source buffer assignment resets then appends. No buffer move constructor is invented (the source user copy constructor/destructor prevents one).
>
> Scalar element and iterator borrows bind to actual owner/physical backing and captured end; no cold pointer-return object or runtime heap allocation. Vector mutable element_ref assignment is INC-before-DEC and debug rejects null at its actual SASSERT. Buffer mutable back/c_ptr returns T*& rather than a smart proxy: expose a clearly named raw borrow-write route with NO callbacks, alongside ordinary callback-correct Set, without claiming that raw mutation retains ownership. A borrowed raw pointer write can create a source-invalid lifetime; later callbacks validate at actual dereference.
>
> ## Exact method/API inventory
>
> All methods below are on ASTManager. Source manager accessors return the existing containing manager after token checks. `DependencyRefGet` returns `(ASTDependency,error)`; size APIs return `(uint32,error)`; predicate APIs return `(bool,error)`; mutations return error. Constructor/copy/move return `(owningToken,error)`.
>
> - Object: `NewDependencyRef(value ASTDependency)`, `CopyDependencyRef(src)`, `MoveDependencyRef(src)`, `DependencyRefGet`, `DependencyRefPresent`, `DependencyRefEqual`, `DependencyRefManager`, `DependencyRefSet(dst,value)`, `DependencyRefAssign(dst,src)`, `DependencyRefReset`, `SwapDependencyRefs`, `DependencyRefSteal`, `DelDependencyRef(*owner)`. Null constructor takes a null dependency. No ordinary pointer dereference substitute is introduced.
> - Vector: `NewDependencyRefVector`, `NewDependencyRefVectorFrom([]ASTDependency)`, `CopyDependencyRefVector`, `MoveDependencyRefVector`, `DependencyRefVectorSize/Empty/Capacity/Manager`, `Get/GetDefault/Back`, `Set`, `Push/Pop`, `Resize/ResizeFill/Reserve/Shrink`, `Reset/Finalize`, `Erase/EraseValue/Contains`, `Append/AppendValues`, `Assign` (source set), `SwapElements/Reverse`, `SwapDependencyRefVectors`, `DelDependencyRefVector`. Method names have DependencyRefVector prefix except constructor/copy/move/swap/destructor.
> - Vector borrows: `DependencyRefVectorElement`, `DependencyRefElementGet/Set/Assign/Equal`; `DependencyRefVectorBegin`, `DependencyRefVectorNext`. Concrete element/iterator scalar types. Pointer-vector c_ptr iteration is represented by these checked captured-end borrows, not an escaped Go slice.
> - Buffer: `NewDependencyRefBuffer`, `DependencyRefBufferSize/Empty/Capacity/Manager`, `Get/Back`, `Set/SetX`, `Push/Pop`, `Resize/Shrink`, `Reset/Finalize`, `Append/AppendValues`, `Assign`, `DelDependencyRefBuffer`. No source-absent Reserve, ResizeFill, move/swap/erase helpers will be advertised for this alias.

Source raw back maps to DependencyRefBufferBackBorrow with its actual debug nonempty assertion; Element is a physical c_ptr offset without a logical-size assertion. Raw reference-return adapters do not INC/DEC.

> Vector pointer equality helper can compare sequence values. Source ref_vector_ptr_hash requires dependency::get_id, absent from dependency.h, so this specialization is uninstantiable; do not invent a hash. Other generic ref_util map/collection callback loops and alternate buffer sizes/configurations remain open unless a real consumer requires them.
>
> ## Arithmetic, aliases, failures, and publication
>
> INC precedes old DEC in obj_ref assignments and vector/buffer Set, including self-assignment. Incoming INC stays completed if an old-pointer lifetime/debug guard refuses. No rollback of a completed source callback. Source DEC0 debug refusal reports not consumed; a consumed deletion callback worklist refusal propagates after the real finite graph cleanup. Following a consumed DEC, publish replacement/reset/empty owner before returning its error. Destructor-range safety continuation must finish or preserve all actual roots; no lost unvisited references or ignored callback error. Clearly distinguish this Go cleanup continuation from source exceptions/assertions that abandon C++ control flow.
>
> Push does dependency INC BEFORE storage growth. Allocation refusal therefore leaves that INC completed and not stored in the container; tests expose it and recover it explicitly. Constructor unwinding cleans stored entries but cannot silently undo the last source failed-push INC. Dynamic growth allocations preserve source old+new peaks; physical retained allocator growth remains charged.
>
> Vector retained Get/Set/back use source debug logical assertions and actual physical/initialized guards only. Release increasing Shrink dec_range(begin+n,end) is empty; null backing is no-op, and initialized retained capacity can publish increased size without INC. Erase shifts and decrements size before DEC; it leaves raw trailing bytes. No DEC of inactive tail on reset/destruction. Nonempty vector self-Append is source growing-size nontermination, explicitly guarded before body. Empty self-Append is valid.
>
> Buffer Shrink calls Resize after its debug assertion: release increasing Shrink genuinely appends null values to the new size, unlike vector. SetX preserves idx+1 uint32 wrap, then actual source Set INC-before-read/write order and typed unsafe access guard. Buffer Append captures source size and c_ptr ONCE. Finite same-buffer append is valid while captured backing survives. Inline backing survives a switch to overflow storage; dynamic captured backing is freed on subsequent expansion and guarded only at the next actual captured read, retaining prior appended values/INC prefixes. No blanket self-append rejection and no rereading growing size.

> # Expression-array retained storage correction
>

> preserving release retained root reads/writes and arbitrary-index nonroot SET.
> Debug guards execute before allocation/copy and report ErrASTDomain.
>
> A popped root slot retains its raw handle. Get returns that token in release;
> later AST dereference rejects a freed generation. Root Set follows INC(new),
> DEC(old), write, including a retained value outside logical size. Root deletion
> decrements only logical elements. Nonroot SET stores its index/value without
> touching root backing; matching Get returns it before any root-array read.
> The test independently checks reference counts and unchanged logical sizes.

> field to the8-byte capacity prefix (12-byte total). Writes advance that marker;

> # Concrete expression substitution packet
>
> Sources independently read in full: `src/ast/expr_substitution.h/.cpp`, `util/obj_hashtable.h`, selected `core_hashtable` algorithms in `util/hashtable.h`, `ref_util.h` map callback loops, and the actual pointer/unsigned vector specializations. Microsoft notices are preserved. No Go generics, unsafe, production math/big, substituted callback manager, Go map, per-entry interface, or unaccounted heap backing.
>
> This selects all non-display methods of expr_substitution and scoped_expr_substitution. Both display methods remain OPEN: mk_pp delegates to actual mk_ismt2_pp/ast_smt2_pp, its formatting environment and plugins, none of which is replaced by a handle-number printer. The selected ref_util map key/value and map-value DEC loops are concretely translated through actual AST/dependency callbacks; other generic hashtable/ref utilities, compiler-generated unsafe copying of these owners, rewriters, tactics, SMT/proof consumers, and whole AST remain separate obligations.
>
> ## API and actual storage
>
> All methods are on the real ASTManager under its existing mutex. Public pointer-free ASTExprSubstitution/ASTScopedExprSubstitution tokens contain manager origin and an actual arena.SmallBytesRef. Shallow copying is prohibited. No existing manager header, field, allocator, constructor or teardown file changes. Existing charged allocator services own every record/backing; source manager borrows do not create fictitious extra manager charges.
>
> - Constructors: NewExprSubstitution(), NewExprSubstitutionCores(bool), NewExprSubstitutionPolicy(cores,proofs bool).
> - Inspectors: ExprSubstitutionManager/ProofsEnabled/UnsatCoreEnabled/Empty/Contains.
> - Mutations: ExprSubstitutionInsert/Erase/Reset/Cleanup and DelExprSubstitution(*token).
> - Finds: ExprSubstitutionFindProof(token,key,*def,*proof) and FindDependency(token,key,*def,*proof,*dependency), returning (bool,error). Required output pointers are nonnil. Misses and disabled policies preserve existing caller values. Go output aliases retain source sequential writes. Raw returned handles are borrowed, not INCed.
> - Scoped constructor/destructor: NewScopedExprSubstitution(token), DelScopedExprSubstitution(*token).
> - Scoped methods: ScopedExprSubstitutionInsert/Reset/Push/Pop/ScopeLevel/Empty/FindValue/FindProof/FindDependency/Contains/Cleanup. FindValue returns the original key only on a miss; a present NULL definition returns NULL.
>
> Primary owner charges **128 actual encoded bytes**, not a guessed C++ sizeof. Map descriptors occupy offsets0/32/64, each32 bytes: payload slot/gen0/4, capacity8, size12, deleted16, reset cursor20, reserved phase24, availability/finalize marker28. Policy96, magic100, pending mutation104, reserved cursor108 and reserved locator words112–124 finish the real allocation. Reserved words are physically initialized storage, not claimed extra callback roots. Map entries charge **24 actual bytes**: key slot/gen0/4, value slot/gen8/12, FREE/USED/DELETED state16, callback-ownership bits20. Source LP64 obj_map entries are two pointers/16 bytes; encoded generations/state/cleanup ownership are an explicit width adaptation. Table backing is exactly capacity×24, without an invented header.
>
> Scoped owner charges **48 bytes**: borrowed substitution locator0/4; actual ASTRefVector record locator8/12; unsigned-limit payload16/20; size24, capacity28, initialized32; operation36, callback cursor40, magic44. The real existing ASTRefVector cold record/backing is allocated separately and charged by its existing services. Limit backing charges actual12-byte header plus capacity×4; source header8 versus Go initialized-highwater metadata12 is explicit. All source limits geometry2→(3n+1)/2, uint32 byte-overflow checks, full-capacity trivial relocation and old/new allocation peaks are retained. Actual byte/host/uint32 arena guards are additional representational-domain boundaries.
>
> Constructors create primary capacity8 BEFORE the explicit proof-policy debug assertion, then optional proof map before dependency map. Policy snapshots the real manager proof mode; subsequent toggles do not change the substitution. The explicit proof=>manager-proof assertion is debug-only. Disabled optional inputs are ignored without provenance/lifetime checks; used inputs enforce manager provenance. Optional descriptors are embedded in the actual128-byte owner (physical-layout adaptation); only enabled table backings are constructed.
>
> ## Source algorithms and publication
>
> Three maps have distinct actual physical histories. Hashing reads real AST structural hashes; pointer equality compares encoded slot/generation. Exact pre-insert threshold `(size+deleted)<<2 > capacity*3`, expansion doubling, linear probing with wrap, last encountered tombstone before a FREE slot, and ascending source rehash order are translated. Rehash allocates/moves before deleting/publishing old storage. Stale-key hash guards diagnose source-undefined reads and free only the unpublished nonowning temporary; they do not undo callbacks.
>
> Removal marks FREE when the next bucket is FREE, otherwise DELETED. Rebuild occurs only when deleted>size and deleted>64, and is skipped on the actual bound source-memory OOM predicate `m.exprIDs.outOfMemory`. Reset counts preexisting FREE slots, marks entries FREE, and may delete/halve/reallocate a sparse table; that source half-capacity publication precedes allocation. Finalize instead deletes then allocates64 THEN publishes64: refusal preserves old capacity with nil backing and an explicit pending-finalize marker. Recovery allocation is a Go undefined-continuation adapter. Prior bindings remain retryable after primary expansion refusal before callbacks.
>
> Insert uses **definition==NULL**, not “new key”, to select its source new-entry branch. Source key INC precedes definition INC/publication. Optional new-map insertion publishes its raw pointer before INC. Replacement INCs new before DEC old, then publishes value; no staging/whole-substitution rollback. Disabled maps do nothing. Repeated NULL definitions retain the source repeated key INC, optional old-value overwrite without DEC, and exact debug contains assertion after primary publication. Extra unlisted INCs are not silently reclaimed as invented map multiplicity. Tests explicitly recover these source prefixes.
>
> Erase processes proof, dependency, then primary key and definition, with source erase/hash afterward. An unpinned primary key can be freed before that final source hash read; the typed lifetime guard retains completed DEC/entry prefixes instead of dereferencing ended storage. A separately pinned key (including the scoped trail) makes ordinary erase valid. Reset is primary key+value per ascending bucket, then proof values, then dependency values. Actual destructor executes source reset including sparse reallocation before reverse dependency/proof/primary member storage destruction.
>
> ## Callback errors and Go lifetime continuation
>
> Real AST INC/DEC and dependency INC/DEC are used. Per-entry ownership bits advance only when callbacks consume their references. A refused callback preserves the current and later roots; successful consumed callbacks are never replayed. Consumed deletion-worklist errors finish the **same entry**, then Reset stops before later entries/tables, preserving their roots. Retry starts at the next unconsumed action. Destructor can complete finite remaining lexical cleanup and refund the record before returning the first consumed error; on refusal it preserves the owning token. These are explicit Go continuations for source exceptions/undefined interrupted destruction, not C++ ordinary semantics or callback rollback.
>
> Partially published inconsistent mutations guard further mutation with ErrASTPending until Reset/Cleanup/Del recovers the real stored roots. Completed new INCs that the source has not stored remain observable caller-recoverable prefixes. A pure primary expansion refusal before callbacks does not set that guard and allows ordinary source retry.
>
> Scoped Insert first Contains, then base Insert, then actual trail Push. Duplicate keys ignore all unused incoming values. Failed trail growth leaves the installed binding and source unstored trail INC. Push saves current trail size. Pop computes unsigned size−n and reads the actual limit with source debug logical assertions plus real physical/initialized guards; it erases ascending keys, resizes the real trail, then resizes limits. Release retained-limit underflow can therefore grow the trail with NULLs and construct zero uint limits; it is not universally rejected. Debug rejects at the actual logical index assertion.
>
> Scoped Reset resets the borrowed substitution, then trail, then limits. Scoped Cleanup forwards only underlying Cleanup and leaves trail/limits unchanged. Destructor destroys limits then trail and **never resets the borrowed map**. Pending pop/deletion cursor is charged scalar metadata. After a refused tail DEC, destruction drains the still-unconsumed tail and then the still-owned prefix, without replay. Stage3 payload requires prefix<2^29; the actual pointer-vector maximum capacity floor((UINT32_MAX−12)/8) proves this, and simulated bounds plus actual refused Pop→refused Del→repaired Del test it. Pending growth owns only the real old logical prefix. No callback preflight or synthetic callback hook is used.
>
> ## Test evidence and source registration boundary
>
> `src/test/main.cpp` registers tst_expr_substitution. Its active body constructs the object but has **zero ENSURE/VERIFY assertions**; insertion and substitution-rewriter use are commented divergent code. The Go test ports the constructor/destructor action route and labels this boundary; the full BV rewrite/printed sequence remains OPEN. `src/test/substitution.cpp` exercises the different substitution/unifier classes and is not counted. Actual consumers include th_rewriter, SMT asserted_formulas, dom_simplify, solve_eqs and other tactics; their algorithms remain OPEN.
>
> Initial full API missing-implementation RED71072 preceded translation. Behavioral RED77946 covered consumed same-entry erase and the missing destructor sparse-reset allocation. RED85540 covered real-hash collisions/wrap/last-tombstone insertion, finalize capacity publication order, and preserving later entries on consumed Reset error. Disabled unused-argument RED45084 preceded correction. Retained-limit and caught-pop destructor RED6329, and primary growth-retry RED20211, preceded correction. Later tests use actual source callbacks/counters with explicit typed-domain counter seeds, never fabricated callback implementations.
>
> Current31 groups additionally cover a500-action independent bounded mapping/reference-count model, all four policies, raw output preservation, NULL quirks in both profiles, every constructor reservation prefix to observed completion, distinct map growth-refusal prefixes, immediate physical roots before Close, actual128/24/48 widths, simulated host bounds, scoped nesting/cleanup/NULL lookup, refused/consumed continuation and zero warm allocations under budget refusal. Final frozen full native/checkeddebug/race/actual JS/vet/WASI/no-generics evidence is recorded below.
