> # Concrete AST marks packet
>
> Selected declared mark APIs are complete and frozen for coordinator integration. This packet contains six Go files and sixteen additional finite test groups. It does not claim whole `ast.h`, `ast.cpp`, `obj_mark.h`, or `bit_vector` completion.
>
> ## Source and method map
>
> | Source surface | Concrete Go counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | `util/obj_mark.h`: default `obj_mark<expr>` constructor; reference/pointer `is_marked`; `mark(flag)` and `mark(true)` overloads; `reset` | `NewASTExprMark`, `IsMarked`, `Mark(h, flag)` (`true` selects the no-flag overload), `Reset`, `Close` |
> | `ast.h`: `ast::mark1/mark2`, `reset_mark1/reset_mark2`, `is_marked1/is_marked2`, including actual `Z3DEBUG` ownership assertions | `ASTManager.MarkNode1/2`, `ResetNodeMark1/2`, `IsNodeMarked1/2`; node constructor initialization is the existing real AST core |
> | `ast_fast_mark<1/2>` constructors/destructors, `is_marked`, `reset_mark`, both `mark` overloads, `reset`, `get_level`, `set_level`; expr typedef aliases | `NewASTFastMark1/2`, `Close`, `IsMarked`, `ResetMark`, `Mark`, `Reset`, `GetLevel`, `SetLevel` |
> | `ast_ref_fast_mark<1/2>` constructors/destructors and all declared methods; expr typedef aliases | `NewASTRefFastMark1/2`, `Close`, `IsMarked`, `ResetMark`, `Mark`, `Reset`; actual manager INC/DEC callbacks |
> | `ast.cpp:3232–3250`: `ast_mark::is_marked/mark/reset` plus virtual destructor | `NewASTMark`, `IsMarked`, `Mark`, `Reset`, `Close`; independent expr/declaration bitmaps |
> | `ast.cpp:3258–3294`: both `scoped_mark::mark` overloads, `reset`, `push_scope`, both `pop_scope` overloads; constructor and empty derived destructor | `NewASTScopedMark`, `Mark`, `Reset`, `PushScope`, `PopScope`, `PopScopes`, `Close` |
> | Instantiated `bit_vector` subset required by these `obj_mark`s | Private budgeted `astMarkBits`: default construction, exact resize(false)/get/set/reset/destruction |
> | Instantiated `ptr_buffer<ast,16>` and `ast_ref_buffer` operations | Actual cold-owner inline16 scalar array, heap doubling, ASC reset/destruction; no separate inline slice or per-entry object |
>
> The expression map uses actual Expr IDs. The AST declaration map uses unsigned `get_id() - (1u << 31)` and the expression map remains separate. Marks survive node deletion and ID recycling as explicitly warned by source `ast_mark`.
>
> ## Storage, ownership, and failure actions
>
> All owners bind a real borrowed ASTManager. Headers (including named inline16 arrays), complete bitmap word capacities, fast-buffer overflow, scope limits, and real scoped ASTRefVector metadata/payloads are charged to that manager's budget. Growth reserves the whole replacement while old storage remains charged, then refunds the old storage. Bitmap capacities follow source `((num_words(new_size)*3+1)>>1)`; fast buffers double 16→32→64; scope limits follow unsigned-vector 2→3→5 growth. Reset retains backing.
>
> Header reservation and owner-identity preparation now occur **before** the escaping Go cold object is allocated. The final allocation fixture proves all seven constructors refuse FailAfter(0) with zero Go allocations.
>
> Ordinary ID maps and nonref fast lists do not retain AST references. Ref-fast lists retain actual nodes. Fast marking sets the node bit before list insertion, and ref-fast increments before list growth. Failed unlisted mark/INC prefixes remain visible; Reset/Close cannot clear/decrement an entry that was never inserted. Explicit caller balancing remains possible. `reset_mark` and `mark(false)` clear a fast bit without decrementing its retained reference or removing a list entry.
>
> Ref-fast Reset clears **all** node marks ascending before the real ref-buffer decrements nodes ascending. Its completed release order is tested through actual recycled IDs. Scoped marking pushes an owning stack entry before growing/setting its bitmap; retries repeat source INC and push, retaining completed prefixes. Scoped pop clears bitmap entries ascending, pops the limit, then resizes/decrements the actual stack. PopScopes preserves completed scopes before a later underflow guard. Scoped Reset clears declaration/expr maps before resetting the owning stack and then limits. Scoped Close follows source reverse member destruction: limits, stack, base declaration bitmap, base expression bitmap. It does not invent a Reset call.
>
> ## Explicit Go adapters and remaining source scope
>
> * Checked origin/slot/generation handles replace source raw pointers. Foreign, null, or freed handles fail safely. Nonref fast lists retain checked borrowed generations; stale-borrow Reset/Close reports a typed error and leaves the owner open until forced manager teardown permits physical cleanup.
> * Cold owners are caller-confined. Operations that touch the manager hold its mutex. Private `newASTFastMark1Locked`, `markLocked`, `nodeMarkedLocked`, `resetMark`, and `closeLocked` permit real dependency traversal under an already-held lock, with the same algorithms and budgeted owner.
> * A unique scalar owner identity replaces the debug `this` pointer comparison. Assertions execute only with `g3debug` at the actual source mark/read/reset sites; release ignores owner assertions. Raw low-level APIs accept an opaque uint64 owner token.
> * Implicit owning C++ copy/assignment is not implemented in this selected packet. Go owner copies are explicitly rejected by self identity; declaration/bitmap ID semantics are not changed to generation keys.
> * Source uint32 resize arithmetic and completed publication are preserved even at unsigned wrap. Source-undefined physical accesses return typed errors. A behavioral RED showed a later physical read panic after retained resize publication; the final guard reports ErrBounds without erasing that prefix.
> * After forced ASTManager Close, marker Close refunds only its external cold/backing storage and avoids callbacks against the freed AST graph. Consumed deletion failures use the core's owned emergency continuation; these source unsafe-exception continuations are explicit adapters.
> * `expr_sparse_mark`, the shared-occurrence private mark/functor, other generic `obj_mark` BV/functor instantiations, implicit source copies, and whole AST/util units remain open. Bit-vector TRACE diagnostics remain part of the pending whole bit-vector surface.
>
> No registered mark-specific test was found in `src/test`. `src/test/bit_blaster.cpp` uses ast_mark during real traversal; that integration remains dependent on its actual BV plugin. The sixteen tests here are additional coverage, not invented registered source assertions. They include all five real node kinds, a bounded independent boolean oracle, source growth/ownership order, deletion/ID reuse, immediate physical accounting at constructor failure prefixes, partial scopes, stale/foreign owner guards, and warmed zero-Go-allocation operations under FailAfter(0).
>

>
> ## Source distinctions to test before translating
>
> - mk_proof returns null when disabled. Its three-expression overload creates
>   three local entries but passes count TWO. Preserve this finite legacy route.
>   It does not license changing the ordinary three-argument mk_app overload.
> - Disabled mode is checked per body. Reflexivity, hypothesis, symmetry, binary
>   transitivity, monotonicity, congruence, unit resolution and hyper-resolution
>   directly call mk_app; do not add one universal proof-disabled shortcut.
>   mk_true_proof builds true before calling the guarded helper. Assertions in
>   mk_asserted/mk_goal/def_intro precede that helper even when mode is disabled.
> - Null-parent early returns, reflexivity elimination, double-symmetry elimination
>   and OEQ/EQ selection in transitivity preserve exact identity and branch order.
>   Array transitivity folds left. The endpoint overload returns null at zero and
>   its sole input at one without constructing an endpoint fact.
> - PR_GOAL declaration is cached with TWO parents, while mk_goal supplies one
>   fact. This source inconsistency must follow real application validation rather
>   than an invented successful goal node. Fixed declaration caches and hyper-resolve
>   first-count caching are source contracts, not corrected dynamic signatures.
> - has_fact examines only the last argument sort; parent count follows that test.
>   A generic proof app can have no fact. get_parent converts the requested arg
>   to App; genuine out-of-bounds/type-undefined continuations get typed guards at
>   their actual access, separate from source debug assertions.
> - In inferred unit resolution, two complementary facts produce false directly.
>   Otherwise scan original OR literals in order against parents1..N-1. Retain
>   duplicate unmatched literals and choose false/singleton/or by remaining size.
>   Debug found.setx and continue run inside DEBUG_CODE, so all complementary
>   parents are marked in debug; release breaks on the first complement. Its
>   later debug parent-coverage loop is conditioned on proofs_enabled.
> - Explicit-fact unit resolution appends parents and fact before its debug-only
>   validation. It counts matches independently and accepts the source duplicate
>   literal cases; do not replace it with the inferred-fact algorithm.
> - check_nnf_proof_parents returns a bool that mk_nnf_pos/neg IGNORE. It still
>   executes. Preserve its short-circuit reads and any earlier invalid access,
>   but do not reject a well-formed non-OEQ parent solely for this ignored false.
> - Quant-inst parameters are actual owning AST parameters in binding order. Its
>   reader requires an empty output only in debug and appends in source order.
>   Rewrite inspection executes VERIFY of eq-or-iff extraction in all profiles;
>   OEQ is not added to this disjunction.
> - Theory lemma prepends the actual family-name Symbol parameter before copied
>   caller parameters, then appends parents and fact. Hyper-resolve flattens each
>   substitution then two integer position entries between adjacent substitutions.
>   It also builds the real temporary fact/Proof-sort vectors even where these
>   local arrays are not consumed by the final mk_app. No dead-operation elision
>   where allocations, budgets, assertions, references or failures are observable.
> - Hyper-resolve decoding appends premises, assigns conclusion, pushes the first
>   substitution vector, then reads parameter pairs/substitutions in order. An
>   exception keeps completed output/refcount prefixes. It does not reset caller
>   outputs or infer missing positions. Negative int parameters convert uint32.
>
> ## Ownership and test requirements
>
> Use actual ASTManager, eager/lazy basic plugin declarations, pointer-free nodes,
> source ID/hash interning, exact sorts and real RC; no fake proof graph. Temporary

> | `is_shared`, `num_shared`, begin/end iteration | `IsShared`, `NumShared`, `BeginShared`, `EndShared`, concrete iterator operations |
> | `reset`, `cleanup`, destructor | `Reset`, `Cleanup`, `Close` |
> | `display` | OPEN: requires real `mk_ismt2_pp` / AST SMT2 printer; no substitute rendering |
>
> Defaults are exactly TrackAtomic=false, VisitQuantifiers=true, VisitPatterns=false. Application children visit ascending; quantifier visits body, patterns, no-patterns. Parent frame cursor increments before processing each child, and frames are reread after growth. An atomic early return does not drain a preexisting release-mode stack. Source debug empty-stack/quantifier-visit assertions execute with g3debug, separately from handle checks. Reset does not clear the frame stack; Cleanup finalizes it.
>
> The actual `obj_hash_entry<expr>` / `core_hashtable` specialization uses zero FREE, scalar sentinel DELETED, current node hash on every USED hash read, pointer-identity equality adapted to checked slot/generation, strict >75% growth before duplicate lookup, ascending move-table scan, wrapped linear probing, last-tombstone insertion, immediate-next FREE erase, and cleanup only after the DELETED erase branch. Its resource OOM skip uses the manager's constructor-bound resource callback (also bound in the real ID owner). No cached hashes, AST ID bitset, Go maps, or alternative table algorithm occur. Constructor, actual used find/contains/insert/insert-if-absent/erase/reset/finalize/rehash and physical iteration paths are represented. General inherited copy/assignment/swap/union/intersection/find-pointer/dump, optional HASHTABLE_STATISTICS, and remaining generic diagnostics are not claimed complete by this private specialization. Default source statistics are disabled.
>
> ## Ownership, layout and failure actions
>
> All owners are confined to one real ASTManager. Sparse keys and visitation lists borrow nodes; they do not increment RC. Shared set publication precedes the unique real `incNode`. Reset invokes real DEC in ascending physical buckets, then table.reset through the collection helper equivalent, then the second source table.reset. Destruction resets first, then frees stack backing, then table backing. Visitation resets flags ascending and frees overflow after reset. The separate actual node `shared` flag never uses public mark1/mark2 or their debug owners. Failed visitation push leaves the already-published bit unlisted; Reset cannot silently clear it.
>
> Cold headers reserve before constructing escaping Go objects. Actual reflect-sized headers, every 8-byte scalar entry/list element, every target-sized frame including padding, and all unused array capacity are charged. Marker inline16 is physically in its charged owner; local default visited inline16 is lexical stack storage with no self-slice. Overflow doubles 16→32→64. Frame svector uses actual 2→3→5… capacities. Its scalar growth helper preserves source unsigned32 capacity arithmetic, independently checks the selected LP64 pair extent16 plus two unsigned32 header words, and checks actual Go frame stride12 against the host allocation extent. Boundary fixtures exercise the exact source extent endpoint without allocating a large array. Ordinary replacement reserves new while old remains charged. Generation handles are eight bytes on both targets, an explicit physical adaptation of source pointers, not a claimed source pointer ABI.
>
> Reset clears entries, refunds/deletes old backing, publishes halved capacity BEFORE allocation, then clears counts only after success. Finalize deletes old backing, allocates64, and publishes64 AFTER allocation. A scalar pending phase with nil backing preserves old count prefixes and these different capacity prefixes; reads reject the source undefined nil-entry access. Retry completes the physical replacement without repeating already-consumed DEC callbacks. A separate release cursor retains actual callback consumption when core deletion reports a failure after its owned emergency continuation. Its behavior is verified immediately using live node counts before retry/Close. No fake retained old backing is charged. Scalar epochs invalidate borrowed iterators only when the backing is replaced/freed. In-place insert, erase, and nonshrinking reset preserve the captured current position and endpoint, including at epoch exhaustion. A cleared current slot returns source null and an erased DELETED slot returns an explicit non-node sentinel scalar; dereferencing that token is an invalid AST domain. Actual relocation exhaustion returns typed bounds errors before old storage is touched, and a pending replacement can finish after its invalidation consumed the final epoch. Failed relocation reservation leaves the previous iterator alive.
>
> Checked origin/generation/self guards replace invalid raw-pointer / implicit owning-copy domains. Implicit copies of cold owners are rejected, rather than exposing double-destruction. Explicit Close is required. After forced manager Close, external owners refund only their own physical storage and skip callbacks against freed AST nodes; iterators reject that lifetime. Iterator and scalar count views are owner-confined. These are Go lifetime/failure adapters, not source extra ownership or cleanup actions.
>

>

> ## Ownership and failure adaptation
>
> The owner header is charged once using actual target layout. Every table cell
> is `{key int32, value int32, next uint32}`; physical bytes use actual layout on
> each target. The table-only owner retains an unused scalar value field because
> it shares concrete storage with the map. Link indices replace source pointers;
> reserved FREE/END indices impose checked capacity bounds. FREE/recycled payloads
> are retained, as in source. The Hash environment is borrowed and must outlive
> the owner; callers serialize operations and use a stable, non-reentrant hash.
>
> Growth charges both original and replacement arrays. Each insufficient-cellar
> trial is refunded before the next trial. Each attempted copy resets and updates
> `m_used_slots` by reference, preserving the source's observable failed-copy prefix
> even if the next reservation fails. The old physical table, entries and views
> remain unchanged, but UsedSlots can then differ from the old occupied-bucket
> count. The regression freezes eight old occupied buckets becoming prefix count
> one when an early merged chain overflows before later buckets are visited.
> `Finalize` allocates its initial table before
> destroying the current table, charging the overlap and preserving the current
> graph if allocation fails; source deletes before allocating. These are explicit
> predictable-allocation-failure adapters.
>
> Swap allocates no arrays. Same-budget and equal-byte cross-budget swaps reserve
> nothing. Across distinct budgets, the owner receiving the larger table reserves
> only its positive byte delta before the other owner refunds that delta and the
> fields swap. Header charges and hash functors stay with their original owners.
> Quota or epoch failure publishes no field changes. This transfers ownership
> charges rather than inventing an old/new physical allocation peak.
>
> References and iterators are caller-owned cold value wrappers. Their owner/epoch
> checks conservatively invalidate borrows on membership changes, expansion,
> finalize and swap. Non-growing value overwrite retains existing views. Default
> and cross-owner end iterators compare equal, preserving the source's null list
> pointer equality. Mutable keys are supported; as in source, callers can violate
> bucket placement by changing them. Close refunds storage at exhausted epoch
> without panicking and is idempotent. Structural epoch exhaustion is checked
> before mutation; existing non-growing overwrite and empty Reset still succeed.

> ## External source baseline
>
> Local g++13.3/libstdc++13 C-locale implementation inspected at
> /usr/include/c++/13/bits/locale_facets.tcc::_M_insert_float (near993-1120).
> It chooses precision6 if stored precision is negative, constructs a printf
> format from float/showpoint/showpos/uppercase flags, converts under its C locale,
> then applies the stream locale decimal point/grouping, padding, resets width0,
> and writes the fully formatted span to the output iterator. Normal profile
> precision is used for fixed/scientific/defaultfloat; combined fixed|scientific
> is hexfloat and ignores precision. Conversion initially tries45 chars for IEEE64
> (digits10*3), then alloca(requiredCount+1) if insufficient. Locales/custom num_put,
> streambuf failures, sentry/tie/unitbuf/exceptions are external runtime behavior,
> not repository algorithms silently transferable to ordinary Go strings.
>
> Go proposal explicitly selects narrow-byte C-locale and IEEE round-to-nearest,
> ties-to-even. It does not pretend to detect/replicate arbitrary caller locale,
> process fenv rounding, custom streambuf/facets or Windows CRT tokens. All concrete
> IEEE64 values, signs, default/fixed/scientific modes and requested precisions in
> that profile must work; no default-only, integer-only or finite-only fake closure.
> Full hexfloat/wide/localized/custom ostream surface stays inventoried open.

> ## Semantic adapters needed
>
> | Domain | Source C-locale baseline | Raw Go AppendFloat difference/required adapter |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | +0/-0 | 0/-0; fixed2 0.00/-0.00 | signbit preserved; no zero normalization |
> | positive Inf | inf; +inf only with showpos | Go emits +Inf: intercept/classify IEEE bits; explicit sign/case policy |
> | negative Inf | -inf | explicit lower/uppercase token |
> | signed NaN | nan/-nan, +nan with showpos if positive | Go emits NaN and loses sign; classify original IEEE sign bit, preserve signed token; payload not printed |
> | uppercase | E marker, NAN/INF | E/G for ordinary output; explicit token case; fixed finite digits unchanged |
> | showpos | positive finite/zero/Inf/NaN prefix+ | insert once from original sign bit; unsigned integer counters ignore showpos |
> | showpoint | decimal point even at precision0; defaultfloat retains significant zeros | Go g trims zeros: rebuild point/significant trailing zeros before exponent in charged scratch; f/e precision0 need point insertion |
> | defaultfloat | significant max(P,1), fixed if exponent>=-4 and exponent<P after rounding | g/G with effectiveP, NOT shortest; handle showpoint padding independently |
> | fixed/scientific | P digits after point; scientific signed exponent at least2 digits | f/e/E; enforce source negative precision=>6, not Go negative shortest mode |
> | exponent | e+06/e-05/e-324 | Go ordinary e/E matches minimum2 digit profile; no fabricated three-digit Windows exponent |
> | ties | nearest/even exact binary input | Go default integer conversion matches selected nearest profile; process directed fenv mode remains outside profile |
> | locale | C '.', no grouping in selected profile | reject/document other profiles; do not silently ignore selected non-C locale |

> Do not use math.IsNaN and lose sign before token rendering; inspect Math.Float64bits
> for classification/sign. Floating value2.675 rounds fixed2 to2.67 because actual
> binary64 is below decimal halfway; no decimal-string double rounding. Sign of

> ## Approved concrete API/storage
>
> NewNumericTextStream(NumericTextStreamConfig{Budget *arena.Budget}) owns cold
> header, nested actual StringBuffer64 owner and reusable byte numeric scratch.
> Private enum mode Default/Fixed/Scientific; state fields Precision int64 (source
> streamsize), Width int64, Fill byte, Alignment Right/Left/Internal, Uppercase,
> ShowPoint, ShowPos, integer base Dec/Oct/Hex and ShowBase. Fresh source default:
> defaultfloat, precision6, width0, fillspace, decimal, right adjustment.
> Concrete manipulators change state without emitting bytes; scalar Stats snapshots
> include exact persistent state and owned byte charges. Width<=0 emits no padding
> but still resets after the next valid formatted insertion. Preserve setters'
> source order; no boxed per-argument record or function callbacks.
>
> Methods proposed: SetFloatMode, SetPrecision, SetWidth, SetFill, SetAlignment,
> SetUppercase, SetShowPoint, SetShowPos, SetIntegerBase, SetShowBase;
> AppendFloat64, AppendUint32, AppendInt32, AppendUint64, AppendInt64,
> AppendCString, AppendByte; String, ResetText, Close. Destination is private owned
> buffer, not an externally lockable SymbolManager. String returns one final caller
> copy. ResetText only clears text and retains state/scratch/capacity, matching a
> stream's str(empty) behavior; it must not reset flags implicitly. No generic
> ostream object or fake CLI stream is invented. A future owned-byte adapter can
> accept this concrete stream in Statistics display methods.
>
> Formatted strings/chars consume Width, including the space inserted immediately
> before stats double manipulators. State Fixed/Precision2 changes persist before
> float conversion. For each numeric insertion, stage the entire formatted field
> successfully, apply width/align logically, reset Width0 BEFORE writing its bytes
> as num_put does. If byte-output growth later fails, already emitted prefix and
> Width0 remain. Scratch preparation failure is a predictable Go allocation adapter:
> retain prior width/output, while preceding explicit flag changes remain. Source
> fatal alloca/OOM has no recoverable same-prefix contract; document the Go one.
> Integer formatting must honor widths/base/prefix and actual signed type widths;
> negative int32 hex is its32-bit unsigned pattern, uint32 showpos ignored. This
> supports statistics codes/counters without assuming every stream is decimal.
>
> The numeric owner/header, nested buffer/header/inline, and actual retained scratch
> must all be charged once, with borrowed Budget never duplicated. Scratch growth
> charges full new physical capacity while old remains, then releases old after
> copy/staging. Output uses committed buffer growth; Close destroys nested storage
> and scratch/header exactly once. Returned final text is caller-owned, no other
> intermediate host string. State inspection is scalar, no escaping backing slice.

> ## Worst-case preflight before AppendFloat
>
> Let effectiveP=6 for negative stored precision; defaultfloat P=max(effectiveP,1).
> Check signed-to-host-int conversion, uint64 additions and physical allocation
> size before reservation. Derived IEEE64 finite bounds including sign and enabled
> showpoint (not C terminator; AppendFloat does not append one):
>
> - Fixed: at most309 integer digits. For P>0: P+311 bytes (sign+point+fraction).
>   At P0:310 bytes, or311 with showpoint. This covers negative MaxFloat64.
> - Scientific: P+8 bytes (sign+leadingdigit+point+fraction+e+exponentsign+3digits).
> - Defaultfloat: P+7 bytes; exponent -324..308, scientific form uses P significant
>   digits; non-scientific small values need at most four leading zero positions.
>   Showpoint can pad significant digits to requestedP; include this in the bound.
> - Specials:4 bytes with sign; no showpoint decimal added.
>
> Reserve/ensure actual scratch capacity>=bound BEFORE AppendFloat(rawdst[:0],f,
> mode,effectiveP,64). Sign/showpoint normalization must fit that same bound or a
> separately checked larger staging reservation. Never call AppendFloat first and
> charge a returned enlarged slice afterwards. Width may exceed numeric field
> length; padding length is checked max(width,fieldLength), then emitted as counts
> rather than requiring another uncharged padded string. Output budget failure can
> stop a huge width loop after a defined prefix; no arbitrary width cap. The signed
> C precision ABI boundary below is separately classified, not a convenience cap.
> Precisely document reusable scratch geometric/exact capacity policy as Go storage
> adaptation; warm conversions and slow high-precision paths need zero allocation
> checks and unchanged backing identity after conversion, not just budget counters.

> SetPrecision retains signed64 state. If stored state is negative, effective6;

> ## Exact description assignment order
>
> 1. `ackermannization`: solving UF via ackermannization
> 2. `nnf`: negation normal form
> 3. `pi`: pattern inference (heuristics) for universal formulas (without annotation)
> 4. `pp`: pretty printer
> 5. `rewriter`: new formula simplification module used in the tactic framework, and new solvers
> 6. `interp`: interpolation parameters
> 7. `algebraic`: real algebraic number package
> 8. `rcf`: real closed fields
> 9. `fixedpoint`: fixedpoint parameters
> 10. `nlsat`: nonlinear solver
> 11. `opt`: optimization parameters
> 12. `sat`: propositional SAT solver
> 13. `smt`: smt solver based on lazy smt
> 14. `combined_solver`: combines two solvers: non-incremental (solver1) and incremental (solver2)
> 15. `sls`: Experimental Stochastic Local Search Solver (for QFBV only).
> 16. `ackermannization`: tactics based on solving UF-theories via ackermannization (see also ackr module)

> ## Ownership, budgets, synchronization and failure
>
> One charged cold registry header owns its three real record arrays, global descriptor owner, successfully transferred module descriptor owners, real cold ParamsRef cells, root pointer directories, borrowed region-binding directory, and byte workspace. Every real retained backing/header is charged using the translated physical stride, host byte bounds, and old+new growth peaks. Nested descriptor graphs keep their own budget contracts; borrowed Symbol/Params/BytesRegion owners, caller-provided registration closure environment, and caller-returned immutable output/error strings are external boundaries. The source map's allocated initial capacity-eight backing and local C++ strings are implemented with fully charged Go backings; these reservations are **storage adaptations**, not alleged C malloc events. Global physical allocation hooks remain open.
>
> Cold directory preparation can precede source dictionary publication. A successful binding/directory growth remains owned if later map insertion fails; unpublished cells are released, and no failure-injection attempt counter is rewound. Module reset releases each real cell and reuses private directory slots on future creation, keeping retained metadata bounded. These slots are not user handles. Failed source shrink leaves native recovery undefined; the Go continuation exposes an absent guarded backing with released storage and safe Close, rather than reading freed source memory.
>
> Merge failure retains both the source destination's completed Copy prefix and the caller's incoming descriptor owner; incoming destruction occurs only after full success. Unknown-kind set preserves actual get_params publication. Validation failure occurs before module-cell creation. Constructor failure releases all successfully created owner roots. Tests compare complete retained budget graphs immediately after failures, before Close can hide leaks.
>
> The registry mutex is a source critical-section adaptation. Registrar methods are by-value cold capabilities valid only while the dispatcher executes under that lock; callbacks must not reenter public registry methods. Output helper lock order remains output→descriptor→Symbol. Registry operations acquire Symbol locks only while public output calls are not holding those locks, and private metadata writes use the existing descriptor helper ordering. Provided owners must outlive borrowers and be torn down only under caller coordination. Independent service locks do not make a shared external `Budget` globally thread-safe. Plain Go owner copies and shallow owning copies are forbidden; self-identity guards diagnose the supported cold misuse domain.
>
> `GetRef` is const-like by contract: callers must not mutate or Del the borrowed pointer. GetModule snapshots are genuine owning shared refs and must be Del'ed with the borrowed ParamsContext; they can outlive the registry while that context remains live. Closing the registry never closes borrowed services or description regions. NULL description is distinguished from present-empty and sets the byte-stream adapter's typed failure at its actual output action; stale/closed region errors occur at the actual byte read, preserving emitted prefixes.
>
> ## Explicit source/platform boundaries
>
> * Default selected C signed-long width is 64; `CLongBits:32` tests the alternate strtol saturation then uint32 narrowing. No host-width reinterpretation silently changes the selected profile.
> * The public double validator admits only digits, minus, dot and slash. Its actual strtod consumed-prefix behavior is adapted to C-locale nearest IEEE64. The exact nearest overflow threshold is checked before `strconv.ParseFloat`, avoiding escaping host error allocations. Other locales, fenv modes, general C strtod spellings and ABI behavior are not claimed. No production math/big is used; tests derive an independent exact threshold.

> # Source ID generator prerequisite
>
> `idgen/generator.go` translates `src/util/id_gen.h`: constructor, mk/recycle,
> reset/cleanup, show_hash, get_id_range, set_next_id, and free-ID display. IDs stay
> uint32 in both handle builds and are distinct from arena slots/generations.
> Source UINT_MAX wraparound and duplicate recycle behavior are preserved;
> this low-level generator does not invent globally unique/permanent IDs.
>
> The owner controls the source memory-service check through one cold callback;
> recycle skips enqueueing while that service reports out-of-memory. The full
> process/owner resource service remains unported. Free-ID backing arrays are owned,
> reset retains capacity and cleanup drops it. The generator must not be shallow
> copied. Budgeted construction now charges each actual free-list backing array;
> the embedded generator header is charged once by its enclosing owner. The
> standalone constructor retains a nil/unlimited budget.
>
> There is no dedicated source id_gen assertion suite. Finite added tests check
> known allocation/recycle sequences, resource skip, debug skip over free IDs,
> range, reset/cleanup, source wraparound, duplicate behavior, display and explicit
> little-endian byte representation of hash input. A 3,000-operation independent
> live-ID set tests uniqueness when the caller obeys source ownership. A warmed
> mk/recycle loop allocates zero Go objects. Hash ordering follows the established
> utilhash baseline; the empty-list hash avoids the source's invalid address-of-
> element-zero expression without changing the result. Oversized hash byte length
> is explicitly rejected instead of truncating to uint32.
>
> Tests first failed with undefined constructor, then passed after translation in
> release and checked builds. No test reads reference files or runs C++.
> Source AST register/delete/compress call sites were read for integration context
> but remain unported; this primitive does not implement an AST manager.
>
> ## Budgeted reclamation workspace
>
> Four new groups first failed to compile for the missing budgeted API, then passed
> after implementation. Source vector capacities are 2,3,5,8,12,...; each growth
> reserves the entire new uint32 array while the old array remains charged, copies
> logical free IDs, publishes the new array, then refunds the old one. The exact
> 8+12 byte overlap requires a limit of20;19 rejects it before logical mutation.
> Reset retains the charged capacity; repeated cleanup refunds it and leaves the
> helper reusable. The source OOM callback runs before reservation or enqueue.
>
> reserveFreeIDs is an explicit Go ownership adapter: the future AST owner can
> prepare fallible reclamation storage before publishing nodes. It changes no
> logical IDs and retains any successful physical growth prefix on failure.
> Recycle returns allocation errors; enclosing owners must handle them or preflight
> sufficient capacity. Source uint32 wrap, duplicate IDs, LIFO order and hashes
> retain their existing behavior. Physical array sizes are checked against both
> uint32 and host-int bounds before allocation. One hundred warmed batches of64
> live IDs recycle within preallocated capacity with zero host allocations and
> no budget reservation, even with the next reservation forced to fail.
>
> New tests: TestIDGeneratorBudgetSourceGrowthAndReset,
> TestIDGeneratorBudgetExactOverlapAndFailedPublication,
> TestIDGeneratorBudgetReservationPrefixesAndOOMSkip, and
> TestIDGeneratorBudgetWarmEmbeddedValueAndCapacityBounds. Together with the four
> existing suites these cover the helper, not actual AST registration/deletion or
> the complete resource service. Diagnostic free-ID rendering still uses host
> formatting and remains a cold unbudgeted diagnostic path; no claim is made that
> it is an AST-owned printer implementation.

> ## Preserved source behavior and actions
>
> Infinity is an exact rational coefficient, not a saturated sign/flag. Addition,
> subtraction, scaling, division and fused operations preserve its magnitude and
> allow infinity cancellation. Pair ordering is lexicographic infinity then nested
> first/epsilon, with separate source LT then structural EQ checks before descending.
> Greater reverses Less; <=/>= negate the correct reversed/nonreversed Less.
>
> **Mixed equality deliberately compares a rational against the infinity coefficient
> and requires the nested numeral to be zero.** Mixed Less instead uses the sign of
> infinity, and descends into the numeral only at zero infinity. Consequently an
> infinity coefficient one with zero numeral equals rational one, while rational
> one is simultaneously less than that value. Finite numeral five does not equal
> rational five under this source overload. These source defects are frozen tests.
> Floor/ceil ignore infinity because their source finite-domain assertions are
> commented out; the nested infinitesimal rounding rules remain unchanged.
>
> Assignment/arithmetic publish infinity before nested first before nested epsilon.
> Assignment from Numeral resets infinity before a fallible nested copy; that reset
> survives failure. Source compound-return expressions clone, mutate, then copy
>  the returned lvalue again. Named-result returns use explicit ownership transfer,
> matching the selected move/elision adaptation used elsewhere in the port. Every
> failed value expression deletes its partial local graph. All multiplication,
> fused accumulation and unit increment routes call existing faithful locked raw
> helpers; component coefficient aliases are reread after earlier publications.
>
> Destruction reverses declaration order: nested numeral first (epsilon then first
> rational), then infinity. A production InfEpsInfDel allocator-reuse test verifies
> actual release order; it does not run a mirrored test destructor. Static value
> constructors borrow existing private owner constants during construction and copy
> only the fields copied by the source. No new service fields/caches are needed.
> Borrowed public accessors become owning checked copies; typed conversion errors
> replace source assertions. Close invalidates all values; foreign owners are
> rejected before reservations or mutations.
>
> Numerical cells, word payloads, descriptor/directories and formatting scratch use
> the existing owner budget. This packet adds no independent cold owner/header or
> managed backing array; caller-provided hot records follow the existing value API.
> String construction stages all text in the existing accounted NaturalManager
> workspace and allocates exactly one final caller-owned host output. A tests-first
> regression observed six warmed allocations from intermediate strings before this
> correction. Absolute-value numeral temporaries survive their formatting expression
> and die before its following closing-parenthesis append. Growing text preserves
> completed prefixes and checked uint32 lengths; failures clean all numeric locals.
>

>

> ## Source action fidelity and ownership adaptations
>
> Arithmetic and assignment publish first component before second; failures retain
> already-published prefixes. Member destruction is the reverse: **second then
> first**, because the empty C++ destructor implicitly destroys members in reverse
> declaration order. Constants traverse zero, one, minus-one. Parent integration

> constants and manager. Constructor failure unwinds the same owned graph.

> Source free compound-expression results explicitly copy the input, mutate the
> copy, then copy the returned lvalue again. Named-result returns transfer ownership
> without inventing a further copy. Approximation rational binary expressions use
> that same clone/compound/return-copy path. Product temporaries coexist until the
> sum/assignment full expression completes; denominator/half/power expression

> copy(k), multiply, accumulate; they do not substitute manager fused arithmetic.

> considering epsilon. Greater reverses Less operands; <= and >= negate the correct
> reversed/nonreversed Less. Unnormalized raw numerals therefore retain source

> constructor fault regression caught fractional normalization replacing the
> source rational(int) temporary/copy route; InfSetInt32 now follows that route.

> zero lower roots, unchanged upper roots, exponent-zero behavior and dropped
> epsilon coefficients outside exponent one. These routines are not replaced by
> more precise mathematics. Hash retains numerator-only component hash behavior
> and uint32 addition/XOR wraparound.
>
> C++ borrowed const accessors/constants become owned copies, so callers cannot
> modify internal components or service constants through exported borrows. Every
> public operation validates service provenance, raw handles and closed lifetime.
> Copying across distinct service owners is rejected; numeric cross-owner copies
> remain a separate explicit service facility. Public numerator/denominator require
> zero epsilon; roots require nonnegative values; division approximation requires
> nonzero denominator first component. Source assertions become typed errors.
> The signed fraction constructor follows existing service widening for signed
> INT_MIN-negation undefined domains. `InfSetFraction` additionally exposes the
> existing int64/uint64 constructor adapter; source-int arguments use
> `InfSetFractionSigned`.
>

> # Concrete integer heap
>
> This packet translates src/util/heap.h into IntHeap and preserves every active
> assertion in src/test/heap.cpp. No Go generics, unsafe, interfaces or Go pointers
> appear in the int32 value/inverse-index arrays. Cold owner fields contain the
> Budget, borrowed Less callback, checked epoch and retained query workspace.
> An owning heap must not be copied as a Go value; use Clone or Assign. Callers
> serialize operations and shared budgets, and keep comparator environments alive.
> Comparators must be strict, nonreentrant and nonpanicking.
>
> ## Source method and storage audit
>
> - Constructor pushes sentinel -1 before resizing the inverse vector; destructor
>   maps to idempotent Close. empty/contains/get_bounds/min_value map to
>   Empty/Contains/Bounds/Min. Invalid keys/empty minima return typed preconditions.
> - move_up keeps strict comparator ordering; move_down chooses right only when
>   strictly less than left, retaining the source left-child tie rule.
> - insert/erase/erase_min/decreased/increased preserve source value and inverse
>   position assignments and comparator notification directions. No priority is
>   copied into a heap record. Source mutable-priority callers update the borrowed
>   priority environment then notify the appropriate direction.
> - reset/clear return immediately when empty, retaining any failed-insert inverse
>   entries. When nonempty they preserve both capacities and zero the complete
>   logical inverse vector. set_bounds/reserve retain source shrinking/resizing/no-op behavior;
>   unsafe live-key shrink is refused before mutation. Newly exposed indices are
>   zeroed, including regrowth of retained capacity. Negative Reserve is a no-op.
> - Source vector resize repeatedly expands 2,3,5,8,12,18,27,41,..., rather than
>   allocating the requested minimum directly. Each successful expansion remains
>   retained on later failure; logical bounds remain unchanged. Source unsigned32
>   vector allocation-size overflow (including two source header words) and host
>   int bounds are checked before allocation. Source vector header metadata is
>   represented by cold owner slice fields, already included in the header charge.
> - begin/end map to cold checked owner/epoch iterators; Next/Value/Equal and
>   AppendValues preserve heap-array order without returning an internal slice.
>   Raw mutable pointers become readonly checked values; callers may not corrupt
>   the source inverse-index invariant by changing a borrowed array element.
> - swap exchanges only values and inverse indices. Comparators, budgets, headers
>   and retained FindLE scratch stay with their owners; incoming comparators must
>   be compatible as required by source debug invariant checks. Cross-budget swap
>   reserves both complete incoming vector graphs while outgoing charges remain,
>   rolls back the first on second failure, then publishes infallibly.
> - Source implicit deep copying is explicit Clone/Assign. Clone copies comparator
>   and exact vector capacities, but not query scratch (source locals). Assign
>   stages a charged clone before publishing, preserving destination on predictable
>   failures rather than exposing source partially destroyed vectors. Its peak
>   includes a temporary cold owner header. Destination query scratch is retained.
> - find_le uses the source LIFO traversal: append node, push left then right;
>   output is right-first and unsorted. Source local todo and caller-result growth
>   become retained budgeted todo/found vectors followed by caller publication.
>   Source pushes of representable beyond-heap children are retained. Signed-shift
>   overflow children are discarded instead of invoking source undefined behavior.
>   Failed preparation leaves all caller output bytes/elements unchanged while
>   successful scratch capacity prefixes remain charged. Returned output belongs
>   to the caller; no internal backing escapes.
> - display preserves recursive preorder, indentation and decimal/newline spelling.
>   Its result is caller-owned diagnostic output. check_invariant visits live values
>   and checks their parent ordering and inverse mappings, as the source does.
>   Additional inverse entries after failed insertion do not fail this traversal.
>
> Every retained backing capacity and reflect-sized cold owner header is charged.
> Replacement allocation charges full old+new capacity. Close refunds the complete
> graph even after partial growth and at exhausted epoch; it drops comparator borrows
> without invoking callbacks. Structural/reordering mutations refuse epoch wrap
> before publication; readonly/no-op actions remain available.

> containing service must synchronize global access and confine explicit lanes.
> No generic code is used.

> Actual adapters must call TLS-malloc accounting AFTER physical success and
> TLS-realloc/non-TLS allocation accounting BEFORE their physical operations.
> They must retain each source completed counter/physical ownership prefix.
>
> Eight groups cover strict ±100000 thresholds, repeated local count contribution,
> no getter flush, memory-before-count failure, limit-failure prefixes, negative
> clamp, retained peak, watermark equality/zero, signed-overflow prefixes and the
> physical deallocation boundary. A 300-event independent three-lane model includes
> shrink-reallocation deltas. Signed synchronization/count overflow and ILP32-promoted LL64 overflow are
> undefined: Go stops at the actual failing addition, preserving prior mutations.
> LP64 size_t updates instead use unsigned64 modular arithmetic and the selected
> two's-complement signed conversion. ILP32 realloc subtraction occurs as uint32
> before LL64 promotion; a shrink can therefore add a large positive delta.
> A compiled GCC source-promotion probe confirmed both distinctions; the new
> size_t-width fixture observed missing-API RED before those helpers were added.

> ## Implemented public API
>
> Package path github.com/glycerine/g3/golang/memory. No generics, unsafe, cgo, per-record interface fields, payload slices escaping to callers, or duplicate runtime/allocator bodies.

>
> Runtime/SmallAllocator contain private self pointers, cold configuration, actual directories and accounting; neither can be copied as a Go owning value. Constructors validate before header allocation and preserve existing reserve/unwind behavior. Token accessors are zero-allocation scalar views, not raw pointer factories. RuntimeOwner returns the actual borrowed Runtime pointer (nil for nil/foreign-copied owner), without allocating another object; identity remains available after normal Close. All ordinary source operations retain closed/self/provenance/generation guards and existing source action positions.
>
> Default FailureKind mapping: Memout=>code101/message `out of memory`; AllocExceeded=>code113/message `number of configured allocations exceeded`; VectorOverflow=>code0/no-code/message `Overflow encountered when expanding vector`. Failures are cold caller-owned returned errors, not owned payloads. Transport is invoked at the existing actual failure site AFTER the appropriate counter/physical prefix. Domain/ownership/initialized/header guards retain existing typed errors and are not rerouted as fabricated vsnprintf/OOM. A nonnil transport must return a nonnil error; nil return is a typed invalid-transport error at that call, never successful allocation. Only static named functions are permitted; captured closure environments would need explicit independently owned/charged storage and are outside this API contract.
>
> Exported sentinel aliases correspond one-to-one to existing errors: ErrRuntimeOwner, ErrRuntimeLive, ErrRuntimeUninitialized; ErrAllocatorOwner, ErrAllocatorAssertion, ErrAllocatorUnreachable, ErrAllocatorPending, ErrAllocatorNonterminating. Main exports can alias those exact error identities. New ErrAllocatorIO diagnoses missing cold IO only when an actual enabled emission is reached, not at constructor. It does not claim source global stderr disappearance. Process-wide std::cerr/verbose binding, badbit/flush/exits remain OPEN.
>
> ReadUint32/WriteUint32 byte-word codecs and MPZ-specific descriptor preparation are phase B proposals, not required by this API-absence packet. Their bounds/initialization action order needs separate tests before implementation.
>
> ## Exact cold error and diagnostic bridge contracts
>
> A lower package cannot import main NumericTextStream, GlobalParamCString, or Z3Error. The dependency is deliberately one-way:
>
> - Main `memoryErrorTransport(f memory.Failure) error` is a static function, mapping101/113 to the existing actual Z3Error and VectorOverflow to existing NewDefaultException with its fixed source message. No fmt/serialization/closure. RuntimeConfig stores only its function value (actual reflected owner header charge includes that field). Existing main exception definitions remain in place and retain their nominal ErrorCode surface. Lower package's default Failure supports direct mpnum/library use; main source consumers use the real bridge.
> - Main `smallObjectIOBridge.Emit(a *memory.SmallAllocator, event memory.AllocatorIOEvent) error` is a static method on one cold receiver containing only borrowed Diagnostics/Verbose streams, static ID flags/string, BorrowedID region/scalar IDRef, and its owned charge/lifetime bookkeeping. It reuses current real CString and NumericTextStream insertion bodies unchanged. The interface lives ONCE in the allocator's cold config, never in ObjectRef, a numeral, location, or byte record. No per-emission/per-record closure or boxing environment is created.
> - The lower core dispatches Leak only after its debug requested>0 condition and actual chunk frees. Dispatch executes the existing warning prefix, then current ID read, then count/suffix. VerboseStart occurs before lexical pointer-vector construction; VerboseEnd occurs before reverse lexical destruction. The receiver queries actual source WastedSize and Runtime.AllocationSize at their original insertion positions. Reentrant mutations/Close are forbidden; read-only getters needed by the bridge remain valid at those stages.
> - Native source m_id borrowing is represented by the cold bridge's retained borrowed ID fields. Constructor stores them without reading. It normalizes the default static unknown spelling as the current main constructor does. Nullable, embedded-NUL, mutable/stale region ID behavior stays in the existing main byte emitter; lower core does not duplicate it. No owned string copy is substituted.
>
> The main wrapper owns one bridge receiver and one thin wrapper header. Both real Go allocations are charged with reflect.TypeOf(...).Size before make/new and refunded on unwind/final Close. Runtime core header/directories, allocator core header/location directory, and bitmaps are each charged once at their actual owning layer. Borrowed interface receiver, Budget, streams, source regions and literal/static spelling are NOT double-charged by lower owners. Pointer interface conversion is cold, not a boxed per-cell record. A caller-supplied receiver is externally owned; the test recorder is explicitly caller-owned instrumentation, not an implementation of ostream or a hidden allocator allocation.
>
> Thin wrapper Stats aggregate its actual owned header/bridge charges in OwnerBytes/TotalBytes while retaining core source counters separately. A pending lower owner retains wrapper and IO charges as well: final release waits for the same destructorDone/pending finalization contract. Completed diagnostics are never repeated. A diagnostic error without pending roots can still finalize exactly as the committed allocator does. Main Runtime aliases need no wrapper header unless an actual allocation is introduced.

> # Global memory runtime: source contract and next TDD packet
>
> Coordinator-owned prerequisite for the complete SAT/SMT runtime. This document
> records inspected source bodies. The scalar transition component is implemented;
> see PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-memory-accounting-port-status-md. Full memory manager/global runtime
> integration remains open. The proof builder prerequisite is committed at a18b6ce. Existing
> arena.Budget is owner-local predictable storage accounting and cannot replace
> memory::get_allocation_size. Go runtime.MemStats and process RSS cannot replace
> that getter either.
>
> ## Complete source body scope
>
> memory_manager.h/cpp declare and implement initialization/finalization,
> is_out_of_memory, exit_when_out_of_memory, set_high_watermark,
> above_high_watermark, set_max_size, set_max_alloc_count, get_allocation_size,
> get_max_used_memory, get_allocation_count, both display methods, allocate,
> reallocate and deallocate. Include debug allocation/deallocation wrappers,
> source out_of_memory_error and both limit failure transports. Concrete typed
> allocation/destruction adapters replace template wrappers; no Go generics.
> Generated mem_initialize/mem_finalize and PROFILE_MEMORY/TRACE dependencies
> remain separately required, rather than silently replaced by empty callbacks.
>
> ## Ordered source behavior to preserve
>
> - initialize updates the limit unless max_size equals UINT_MAX. Only the first
>   initializer clears OOM and runs mem_initialize; concurrent initialization
>   waits until full initialization. finalize runs actual mem_finalize while
>   finalizing=true, then clears initialized; it does not reset every counter or
>   fully_initialized. Do not invent a zero-counter reset.
> - get_allocation_size returns max(global signed allocation bytes, 0).
>   The getter does not flush thread-local counters. Maximum used memory records
>   the global peak; allocation count is cumulative and not a count of live blocks.
>   High watermark is disabled at zero and otherwise uses strict watermark < size.
> - Every raw allocation includes its actual size_t prefix. Deallocation reads
>   the original stored extent; shortening a logical consumer does not shrink it.
>   Raw byte payloads and typed backing storage need real ownership and physical
>   budget charges; no fake counter-only successful allocations.
> - The thread-local branch synchronizes only when local bytes > 100000 after
>   allocation/reallocation, or local bytes < -100000 after deallocation.
>   Synchronization adds BOTH local size and local count, updates peak, checks
>   limits, then resets ONLY local size. Local allocation count remains cumulative
>   and is added again at later synchronizations. Preserve this source behavior.
> - Thread-local allocate calls malloc and writes its size header BEFORE local
>   counter changes and synchronization. A synchronization limit failure thus
>   follows a real allocation prefix. Go must explicitly expose/own that prefix.
> - Thread-local realloc updates local size delta and count BEFORE synchronization
>   and BEFORE actual realloc. A limit failure leaves the old physical allocation
>   intact while the counter prefix is published. A later allocator failure also
>   preserves the prior counter mutation. Successful realloc updates the header.
> - Non-thread-local allocate/realloc update GLOBAL size/count/peak and check
>   memory then allocation-count limits BEFORE the physical allocator operation.
>   Limit or allocator refusal must not roll back those source counter prefixes.
>   Non-thread-local deallocate subtracts the stored extent before free.
> - Synchronization while deallocating never throws memory/count-limit failures.
>   Allocating checks memory before count. OOM transport sets the global OOM flag;
>   allocation-count transport does not silently set it. Exit policies and output
>   channels are distinct source contracts.
> - display_i_max_usage ignores its supplied stream and writes stdout. Debug
>   deallocate performs actual deallocation BEFORE conditional TRACE, including
>   the finalizing guard. Debug allocate traces only after successful allocation.
>
> CMake Linux x86_64 selects _USE_THREAD_LOCAL; scripts/mk_util.py selects it for
> 64-bit Linux. Both conditional bodies remain in scope for Go native/wasm builds;
> explicit runtime lanes replace implicit OS-thread-local ownership. Host word
> width, actual Go backing sizes and extra owner metadata must be documented
> separately from source ABI sizes. Invalid pointers, signed overflow and host
> unrecoverable OOM need typed/explicit boundaries without changing finite paths.
>
> ## Actual consumers and integration requirement
>
> SAT solver.h checkpoint checks global allocation bytes every tenth call against
> its configured maximum; probing.cpp checks actual accounting to clear/stop its
> cache. Solver diagnostics and statistics.cpp also read this service. Runtime
> ownership must therefore connect real allocations across participating owners
> and preserve synchronization/limit ordering. A getter covering only one budget,
> only a test raw-byte allocator, or only the solver clause directory is not full
> integration. Existing typed owners still need an audited allocation-hook plan;
> aggregate budget reservation must not be mislabeled as an exact C++ malloc call.
>
> Generated initialization uses component-sorted header traversal, stable numeric
> initializer-priority ordering, and collected finalizer order (not an invented
> reverse initializer order). Full registered modules are required eventually.
>
> ## Tests before implementation
>
> Write and observe missing-API RED for actual owned raw storage and source counters
> in both selected branches: strict threshold edges, no getter flush, repeated
> local-count contribution, negative global clamp, watermark equality, real
> realloc data/header preservation, counter-before-allocator refusal, old-block
> ownership after failed realloc, physical allocation publication after TLS limit
> refusal, deallocation without throwing limits, memory-before-count selection,

> ## Exact implemented surface
>
> Runtime.ReadUint32/WriteUint32 use the real initialized byte backing and SIZE_T header validation. Complete four-byte bounds use offset<=extent and extent-offset>=4, avoiding offset+4 wrap. Read checks every initialized byte; write checks the entire word before publishing its four bytes. Explicit little-endian shifts are the selected internal32-digit physical adapter, with no unsafe casts or slices escaping. Unaligned byte offsets work as explicit codec positions. No allocation/reservation/count/free events are emitted.
>
> SmallAllocator.ReadUint32/WriteUint32 preserve ordinary byte API requested-size bounds and actual owner/generation/closed guards. They resolve the one genuine raw Block+offset and use the same runtime codec. ObjectExtent returns real rounded pool-class block bytes or direct Runtime.Size, distinct from requested bounds. Future MPZ typed access must check its own word against this physical object extent, never the entire underlying chunk or the source claimed capacity. LP64 pooled request4 rounds8 and fits the actual capacity header at offset4; ILP32 pool/direct4 truly endanger that access. Existing byte Write(ref,4) still rejects request4.

> The helpers own no new header, backing, interface or closure. Actual Budget graph and source Runtime.State stay unchanged across warm reads/writes/extent queries. They do not interpret Budget reservations as malloc calls.

>

It represents **finite open intervals with two BinaryRational endpoints**. There are no infinity flags, per-endpoint open/closed flags, dependency objects, precision callbacks or arithmetic rounding-mode switches. Do not substitute the separate `math/interval/interval_manager` API or the same-named realclosure typedef. Preserve Microsoft source notices: basic_interval.h Copyright (c)2011 and mpbqi.h Copyright (c)2012, Leonardo de Moura.
>
> ## Scope and new-file ownership
>
> Approved new files:
>
> - `mpnum/mpbqi.go`: scalar interval, borrowed numerical owner, lifecycle/set/accessor/query methods, three retained multiplication scratch endpoints, source arithmetic.
> - `mpnum/mpbqi_format.go`: source open-interval display using existing budgeted numerical text workspace, caller-buffer/final-string boundaries.
> - `mpnum/scoped_binary_interval.go`: concrete lexical owning scoped_interval specialization, checked borrow/swap/reset/close methods.
> - `mpnum/mpbqi_test.go`: source shared-template assertions, finite independent interval expectations, source defects and alias/prefix fixtures.
> - `mpnum/scoped_binary_interval_test.go`: constructor/header/caller-root/fault/lifetime/borrow tests, actual whole-graph accounting.

>
> Implement all executable inherited/derived methods together, rather than publishing a partial Add-only interval. The full generic basic_interval.h source unit remains partial: other numeral specializations and closed=true branches, field-only Inv/Div, generic external algorithms, persistent ostream state and downstream polynomial/AST integration are separate scopes. No Go generics in production/tests/tools/generated files, unsafe, hot-record pointers/interfaces, or production math/big.
>
> ## Concrete representation and owner hierarchy
>
> ```go
> type BinaryInterval struct { lower, upper BinaryRational }
> func NewBinaryInterval() BinaryInterval
> func NewBinaryIntervalManager(bounds *BinaryRationalManager) (*BinaryIntervalManager,error)
> ```
>
> The default scalar has two source zero endpoints; for open configuration it is empty according to source representation equality. There is no ownership ID in each hot record; its numerical owner is implicit as in committed BinaryRational. Never shallow-copy owning intervals; Copy is two source Set operations, Swap is two source endpoint swaps. The manager borrows one live BinaryRationalManager, which in turn borrows its IntegerManager/diagnostic service. Caller intervals and scoped owners must die before the interval manager closes; close that manager before its borrowed bounds manager and underlying owners.
>
> The interval-manager cold header contains the borrowed pointer, self/closed guard and source `mulCurr`, `mulMax`, `mulMin` BinaryRational fields. The source constructor performs no numeral arithmetic or eager payload allocation. Reserve exactly the actual concrete header through bounds.z.budget; its three scalar scratch endpoints are charged once inside that header, and big payloads are ordinary owner-local cells/Words under the existing budget. No phantom per-endpoint heap-node charge, additional numerical owner, copied borrowed owner-header charge, or unaccounted four-product array. Destructor order is Del mulCurr, Del mulMax, Del mulMin, then release the Go header; it closes no borrowed owner. Stats report own header and live scratch numerator roots, with numerical owner stats remaining distinct.
>
> ScopedBinaryInterval is a concrete cold lexical owner with manager pointer, scalar BinaryInterval, self/closed guard, actual header charge and no per-endpoint Go pointer. New creates default scalar endpoints only; Close source-Dels lower then upper and refunds its own header. Repeated Close is idempotent; shallow copied owners, nil/copied/closed managers and mismatched scoped owner provenance receive existing typed guard errors. Manager operations remain owner-confined; a borrowed diagnostic mutex does not make interval arithmetic or a shared Budget concurrent.
>
> ## Proposed full executable API inventory
>
> All numerical mutable arguments use pointers and operations return explicit error; bool source queries return `(bool,error)`.
>
> | Source methods/accessors | Concrete Go mapping |
> | --- | --- |
> | interval constructor, lower()/upper() const/mutable | `NewBinaryInterval`; checked scoped Lower/Upper lexical borrows, and manager `Lower(a,out)` / `Upper(a,out)` owning copies |
> | manager constructor/destructor and m() | `NewBinaryIntervalManager`, `Close`, `Bounds() (*BinaryRationalManager,error)` explicit borrowed owner |
> | del/reset | `Del(a)`, `Reset(a)` lower then upper, retaining their distinct source Del/Reset actions |
> | set(interval,interval) | `Copy(dst,src)` routes through the bounds setter, retaining source ordered assertion and lower-before-upper publication |
> | set(interval,lower,upper) | `SetBounds(dst,lower,upper)` |
> | set(interval,bound) | `SetPoint(dst,n)` two Copy calls despite open configuration |
> | derived set(interval,mpz) | `SetInteger(dst,n *Int)` two bound SetInteger calls; implicit same-integer-owner contract |
> | set_lower/set_upper | `SetLower(dst,n)`, `SetUpper(dst,n)` with source build-aware ordering assertion before the Copy |
> | swap/neg | `Swap(a,b)` lower then upper; `Neg(a)` Neg lower, Neg upper, Swap endpoints |
> | is_empty/is_pos/is_neg/contains_zero | `IsEmpty`, `IsPos`, `IsNeg`, `ContainsZero` |
> | is_subset/disjoint | `IsSubset(a,b)`, `Disjoint(a,b)` with exact source short-circuit equations |
> | precedes(interval,interval) | `Precedes(a,b)` |
> | precedes(interval,bound), precedes(bound,interval) | `PrecedesBound(a,bound)`, `BoundPrecedes(bound,a)` |
> | add/sub/mul(interval,interval,interval) | `Add(a,b,out)`, `Sub(a,b,out)`, `Mul(a,b,out)` |
> | derived add(interval,mpz,interval) | `AddInteger(a,n *Int,out)` lower then upper mixed BQ/Int Add |
> | power(interval,n,interval) | `Power(a,n uint32,out)` exact source order including final sign rereads after output publication |
> | private init_mul_max_min/update_mul_max_min | concrete private helpers retaining Set-min/Swap-max and compare/Copy/Swap action order |
> | display and scoped ostream forwarding | `String`, `FormatInto`, scoped `String`/`FormatInto` using source `(lower, upper)` syntax; persistent stream-state integration stays open |

>
> Raw endpoint pointers from Get/Lower/Upper are borrows, not ownership transfers; they remain valid only within the live owner operation and may not be shallow-copied as owning numerals or retained past reset/swap/close. Do not provide an implicit scoped copy constructor/Assign/Clone: unlike scoped_numeral, this source scoped_interval declares no deep-copy constructor, and its implicit C++ copy would shallow-copy owning bounds. Explicit manager Copy is the legitimate value copy route. Existing `CopyFrom` may be used at a future owner boundary, but this packet will not accept foreign raw cell handles as same-owner Int/BQ inputs.
>
> Inv and Div are **not executable MPBQI specializations**: the generic source requires `numeral_manager::field()` plus m.inv/m.div, while mpbq_manager declares field=false and has neither member. Instantiating those generic functions for MPBQ cannot compile. Do not invent public interval Inv/Div, implement them with ApproxDiv, or claim an unsupported diagnostic is a field inverse algorithm. They remain explicitly uninstantiable here, pending a different field-backed interval specialization.
>
> ## Exact source algorithms, quirks and prefixes
>
> - Source open-set predicates: Empty is BQ structural Eq(lower,upper), Pos is NonNeg(lower), Neg is NonPos(upper), ContainsZero is Neg(lower) && Pos(upper). There is no hidden lower<upper validation, infinity support, empty flag or mixed openness. `(0,0)` therefore reports Empty, Pos and Neg true, ContainsZero false. Mathematically equal raw endpoint representations can report nonempty. Singleton setters are allowed even though the source comment says their manager must be closed: the body has no such guard and MPBQI explicitly exposes the Int singleton setter.
> - SetBounds checks source Le(lower,upper) in g3debug, then publishes lower Copy and upper Copy. SetLower/SetUpper likewise check only their source ordering assertion before publishing that endpoint. Go provenance and initialization guards precede arithmetic, but do not invent a global interval-order check: legitimate source error prefixes or raw endpoint borrows can leave unordered bounds that still need Del/Reset/query access. Release source ordered-precondition behavior versus g3debug typed invariant failures stays explicit.
> - IsSubset is Le(b.lower,a.lower) && Le(a.upper,b.upper). Precedes is Le(a.upper,b.lower), and scalar overloads use the corresponding upper/lower comparison. Preserve short-circuit evaluation so a false first comparison does not allocate scratch through the second.
> - **Open Disjoint source defect:** `Le(a.upper,b.upper) || Le(b.upper,a.lower)` (first term compares upper to upper, not upper to b.lower). Thus `(0,3)` / `(1,4)` reports true despite overlap; the reverse reports false; a nonempty interval can report disjoint from itself. Freeze these finite source results separately from mathematical interval oracles. Do not silently correct the comparator or call conventional geometric separation.
> - Add and derived AddInteger publish lower before upper. Sub is `a.lower-b.upper` then `a.upper-b.lower`; preserve output aliases and resulting rereads. With a=(2,4), b=(1,3), out=b, source publishes (-1,5), while a separate output is (-1,3). With a=b=out=(1,3), source yields (-2,5), not mathematical (-2,2). No new prohibition on source aliases and no whole-interval rollback.
> - Mul computes all four source corners in this order: lower*lower, lower*upper, upper*lower, upper*upper. After the first product, Copy current to min then Swap max/current. Each update compares current<min and conditionally Copies min; independently compares current>max and conditionally Swaps max/current. Finally Swap out.lower/min, then out.upper/max. Retained scratch now owns the old output endpoints; this is actual ownership, not a leak to wipe by generic Reset. Do not replace by four local exact products, generic min/max, sign-pattern shortcut, or rational multiplication. Inputs may alias output because products precede publication.
> - Power calls bound Power lower then upper before sign tests. Odd n finishes immediately. Even n rereads **a.lower** and **a.upper after those writes**, then returns unchanged for NonNeg(a.lower), swaps for Neg(a.upper), otherwise swaps if output lower>upper and Resets output lower to zero. Output=input aliases must retain this source defect: (-3,-1)^2 in-place produces (9,1), while separate output produces (1,9); (-2,3)^2 in-place produces (4,9), while separate output produces (0,9). For separate output and n=0 with nonzero straddling endpoints, source even branch produces (0,1), not (1,1). Keep inherited 0^0, exponent-product, PowerDomain and budget errors with their completed Copy/exponent/endpoint publication prefixes. Source n%2 assertion in its even branch remains build-aware, not an independent arithmetic substitute.
> - Neg negates lower then upper before swapping. If the upper operation fails, the completed lower mutation survives. Set/Copy/Power preserve completed lower publication when upper fails; Mul retains partial scratch/old outputs according to source ordering. Existing BQ/MPZ primitive staging remains inherited; no new whole-pair atomic transaction. All Go error paths still clean their actual lexical owned roots immediately.
>

> ## Complete proposed packet and file ownership
>
