> ## Representation, owner graph, and proposed constructor
>
> `BinaryRational` is a pointer-free scalar `{ num Int; k uint32 }`, denoting `num/2^k`. Raw Go zero is the valid source default 0/1. `NewBinaryRational()`, `NewBinaryInt(int32)`, and `NewBinaryIntPower(int32,uint32)` reproduce source constructors; the last **does not normalize**. Manager setters with a denominator power do normalize. Owning big numerators may not be shallow-copied; `Copy` deep-copies, `Swap` transfers ownership, and the lexical scoped owners reject copied owner headers. There is no invented denominator allocation.
>
> Proposed cold-owner constructor:
>
> ```go
> type BinaryRationalConfig struct { Diagnostics *RationalService }
> func NewBinaryRationalManager(z *IntegerManager, c BinaryRationalConfig) (*BinaryRationalManager, error)
> ```
>
> The manager borrows `z`; caller binary values and scoped/vector owners must be destroyed before this manager closes, and it must close before `z.Close`. It never closes `z`. Operations remain owner-confined, matching the source unsynchronized manager. A self pointer in the cold manager detects shallow copying; it does not make raw numeric handles detect foreign managers. `Close` is idempotent; nil/copied/closed owner and nil numerical arguments receive existing typed owner/storage errors before arithmetic.
>
> The source constructor initializes only default scalar scratch, with no integer arithmetic or eager limb allocations. Retain exactly its eight Int and three binary scratch fields (eleven owning numerators): `tmp`, `tmp2`, `addMulTmp`, `selectIntTmp1/2`, `selectSmallTmp`, `selectSmallTmp1/2`, and `divTmp1/2/3`. Charge the actual manager header through `z.budget`; inline scratch lives in that header. Big payloads use existing numeric cells/Words and the same Budget. Close reproduces source destructor order: addMulTmp; tmp; tmp2; selectIntTmp1; selectIntTmp2; selectSmallTmp; selectSmallTmp1; selectSmallTmp2; divTmp1; divTmp2; divTmp3. Report owned versus borrowed bytes and live numerator payloads separately; never double-charge the borrowed integer owner or numeral header fields.
>
> For `g3debug`, borrow the supplied `Diagnostics` service instead of inventing a global service. Require a valid service with the same Budget at constructor entry in that build; release can accept nil. The parent approved this explicit borrowed-diagnostic context adaptation. Diagnostic arithmetic follows source `to_rational` and wrapper actions, not a production mathematical oracle. Service locking is confined to its own actions; no service callback acquires a binary-manager lock. Both owners and their shared Budget are externally confined. Diagnostics contribute real additional scratch/cache/peak costs; no claim of release-equivalent allocation profile.
>
> ## Proposed concrete API mapping
>
> Names below represent ordinary methods on `*BinaryRationalManager`; numerical inputs/outputs are pointers. Errors are explicit even for source void/bool methods. Queries returning a bool use `(bool,error)`; magnitudes use `(int32,error)`; powers use uint32. Families are listed rather than replaced by a generic or interface dispatcher.
>
> | Source methods | Proposed Go names and shape |
> | --- | --- |
> | precise, field | `Precise() bool`, `Field() bool` (true, false) |
> | swap, del, reset scalar | `Swap(a,b) error`, `Del(a) error`, `Reset(a) error` |
> | reset(mpbq_vector&) | `ResetVector(v *ScopedBinaryVector) error`, ascending **Reset** then clear logical length, retaining backing capacity |
> | set(int), set(unsigned) | `SetInt32(dst,n)`, `SetUint32(dst,n)` |
> | set(int,k), set(int64,k), set(mpz,k) | `SetInt32Power(dst,n,k)`, `SetInt64Power(dst,n,k)`, `SetIntegerPower(dst,n,k)` |
> | set(mpz), set(mpbq) | `SetInteger(dst,n)`, `Copy(dst,src)` |
> | is_int, numerator, denominator power | `IsInteger(a)`, `Numerator(a,out *Int) error`, `DenominatorPower(a) (uint32,error)` |
> | zero/nonzero/one/pos/neg/nonpos/nonneg | `IsZero`, `IsNonzero`, `IsOne`, `IsPos`, `IsNeg`, `IsNonPos`, `IsNonNeg` |
> | add/sub/mul(BQ,BQ) | `Add(a,b,out)`, `Sub(a,b,out)`, `Mul(a,b,out)` |
> | add/sub/mul(BQ,Int) | `AddInteger(a,b,out)`, `SubInteger(a,b,out)`, `MulInteger(a,b,out)` |
> | addmul(a,b,c,r), mixed overload | `AddMul(a,b,c,out)`, `AddMulInteger(a,b *Int,c,out)` |
> | neg, div2/div2k, mul2/mul2k | `Neg(a)`, `Div2(a)`, `Div2k(a,k)`, `Mul2(a)`, `Mul2k(a,k)` |
> | power in-place and copy overload | `PowerInPlace(a,p)`, `Power(a,p,out)` |
> | root lower/upper in-place and copy overload | `RootLowerInPlace(a,n)`, `RootLower(a,n,out)`, `RootUpperInPlace(a,n)`, `RootUpper(a,n,out)` returning `(bool,error)` |
> | eq/neq/lt/gt/le/ge(BQ,BQ) | `Equal`, `NotEqual`, `Less`, `Greater`, `LessEqual`, `GreaterEqual` |
> | six comparisons(BQ,Int) | same six names with `Integer` suffix |
> | six comparisons(BQ,Rat) | same six names with `Rational` suffix, signature `(a *BinaryRational, qm *RationalManager, b *Rational)` |
> | magnitude_lb/ub, lt_1div2k | `MagnitudeLower`, `MagnitudeUpper`, `LessOneDiv2k(a,k)` |
> | to_mpbq | `FromRational(qm,q,dst) (bool,error)` |
> | template to_mpq, to_rational | `ToRational(qm,src,dst) error`, `ToOwnedRational(service,src) (OwnedRational,error)` |
> | floor/ceil with external integer manager | `Floor(a,out)`, `Ceil(a,out)` plus `FloorInto(a,zm,out)`, `CeilInto(a,zm,out)` |
> | select_small, closed select_small_core | `SelectSmall(lower,upper,out) (bool,error)`, `SelectSmallCore(lower,upper,out) error` |
> | three mixed select_small_core overloads | `SelectSmallRationalLower(qm,lower,upper,out)`, `SelectSmallRationalUpper(qm,lower,upper,out)`, `SelectSmallRationalBounds(qm,lower,upper,out)` |
> | refine_upper/lower | `RefineUpper(qm,q,lower,upper)`, `RefineLower(qm,q,lower,upper)` |
> | approx, approx_div | `Approx(a,k,toPlusInf)`, `ApproxDiv(a,b,out,k,toPlusInf)`; explicit-default forwarding method selects source k=32,false |
> | to_string/display | `String(a)`, `FormatInto(a,dst)` |
> | display_pp | `PrettyString(a)`, `FormatPrettyInto(a,dst)` |
> | display_smt2 | `SMT2String(a,decimal)`, `FormatSMT2Into(a,decimal,dst)` |
> | display_decimal(single and pair) | `DecimalString(a,precision)`, `FormatDecimalInto(a,precision,dst)`, `IntervalDecimalString(a,b,precision)`, `FormatIntervalDecimalInto(a,b,precision,dst)`; default forwarder selects source precision 8 |
>
> Direct Int arguments use the same implicit-owner contract as existing IntegerManager. Rational methods explicitly identify `qm`; if `qm.z==z`, read fields directly after checked initialization. Otherwise use budgeted lexical `z.CopyFrom` numerators/denominators, preserving raw shape; never interpret foreign cell handles through z. Mixed selection still executes the source qm Ceil/Floor/Mul actions using qm-owned lexical temporaries, then copies results into z as the source boundary requires. `ToRational` performs source **Power(2,k,target), Inv(target), MulInteger(numerator,target,target)** in that order, with a cross-owner numeral copy where necessary; it does not substitute SetParts. `ToOwnedRational` preserves source owning r(numerator), twok assignment from power(rational(2),k), and value-return division copy routes. Existing private service helpers can be used within new package files under the service lock, without new exported raw borrows.
>
> `FloorInto`/`CeilInto` use the requested output integer manager for actual arithmetic, with a checked lexical input copy only when owners differ. Foreign scoped bridges validate their self/owner first. Explicit cross-owner copies are storage adapters, not new source arithmetic algorithms.
>
> ## Exact arithmetic/control-flow obligations
>
> - Normalize: early return for k=0; set zero numerator's k=0; otherwise compute numerator's power-of-two multiplicity, cap by k, source MachineDiv2k, subtract k. Preserve the inherited small INT_MIN/shift31 sign defect. Del calls Int.Del only and **leaves k and source inline m_val intact**; Reset calls Int.Reset and sets k=0. Copy retains raw representation and source requested numerator capacity; it does not normalize.
> - Add/Sub align denominators into retained tmp and preserve operand order in all three k branches, then normalize. Mul multiplies numerators first, writes `r.k=a.k+b.k` at uint32 width, then **rereads** `a.k==0 || b.k==0` after publication. Output aliases can therefore suppress normalization; do not snapshot that condition or force normalization. Mixed Mul always normalizes. AddMul uses retained tmp and source order `Mul(b,c,tmp)` or `Mul(c,b,tmp)`, then Add(a,tmp,out).
> - Div2/Div2k increment/add exponent at uint32 width and normalize only if its old value was zero. Mul2 decrements nonzero k or shifts the integer numerator; Mul2k either subtracts k or shifts numerator by the excess. Magnitudes compute source unsigned-width log2-minus-k(+1), then explicitly convert to int32. Source equality is representation equality; a raw constructor 2/2 need not Equal normalized 1 although order comparisons consider their values equal. One likewise requires k=0.
> - Power multiplies exponent **before** integer Power. Preserve source copy-before-in-place overload. Source uint64 exponent-product assertion becomes a build-aware diagnostic; release multiplication wraps. Inherited typed PowerDomainError/0^0 errors remain distinct. Proposed failure policy is source statement-prefix publication, including exponent changes before failing inherited Power; do not silently add a whole-BQ rollback transaction.
> - RootLower uses integer root upper bound, Dec numerator when result is false, then rounds denominator exponent according to the resulting numerator sign. RootUpper does not Dec and uses the complementary exponent rounding. Both normalize and retain the source bool, including raw zero with nondivisible k reporting false. Degree zero is undefined in BQ `%n` even if integer-root zero returned true; classify before that undefined division. Negative-even root uses existing typed domain error. Copy overload publishes source Copy before in-place actions.
> - Floor/Ceil use MachineDiv2k and then unconditional Sub(1) for negative fractional representation / Add(1) for positive fractional representation. Raw unnormalized -2/2 thus floors to -2, and raw 2/2 ceils to 2. Do not apply conventional mathematical rounding to these source fixtures.
> - FromRational is exact for denominator1 or positive power2, otherwise stores numerator/2^(Log2(den)+1) and returns false. It is not a generic nearest approximation. Rational comparison cross products do not flip order for raw negative denominators; preserve reachable finite raw-shape results, document the normalized-denominator expectation of interval algorithms.
> - SelectInteger chooses source first applicable endpoint/integer bound; closed BQ/BQ, open Rat/BQ, open BQ/Rat, and open Rat/Rat variants have distinct ±1 endpoint adjustments. SelectSmallCore BQ/BQ first tries integer; then linear search when `min(kLower,kUpper)<=8`, otherwise source binary search with final VERIFY call. Mixed variants always use source linear doubled-interval loops and scoped qm temporaries. SelectSmall returns false without changing out for reversed closed bounds.
> - Refinement repeatedly Add endpoints into lexical mid, Div2, compare with q, Swap one endpoint, and only Del mid on the successful return (lexical cleanup also handles Go errors). Source preconditions require strict enclosure and a non-power-two denominator. No additional denominator-sign or reducedness guard was added: finite raw negative/unreduced examples retain the source action results. Source strict-enclosure/non-power2 preconditions have the approved typed adapters. Normalized positive-denominator nonbinary rationals and valid intervals terminate without an arbitrary iteration cap.
> - Approx retains input when k is already small enough; otherwise uses Abs, truncating MachineDiv2k, increment iff sign differs from direction, restore sign, publish k, Normalize. Increment is unconditional in that direction even for raw exact-divisible input. ApproxDiv has three exact source branches: positive power-two divisor numerator; divisor numerator divides numerator; otherwise scaled absolute numerator and truncating division plus directional increment. Preserve all k arithmetic widths, numerator aliases, exponent publication and inherited Div divisor-alias defects. Never replace by exact rational division plus generic rounding.
>
> Predictable errors in underlying integer operations retain their existing staged guarantees; the BQ compound method preserves previously completed source statements. Every error path still releases lexical numeral roots immediately. Source exceptions do not define safe ownership cleanup; cleanup is the explicit Go adaptation, not a claim of identical C++ throw behavior.
>
> ## Formatting, diagnostics, and scoped specialization
>
> Use z's existing budgeted NaturalManager text workspace and repeated-decimal-division helpers. Append offsets preserve existing prefixes through workspace growth. No per-call limb slices, digit slices, fmt intermediate strings, or decimal-power Go strings. Formatting prepares full owned text before caller-buffer publication; short buffers/budget failures leave caller bytes unchanged. Returned Go strings contain one final caller-owned allocation; do not claim that escaped lifetime is manager-budgeted. Length excludes NUL.
>
> Plain formatting distinguishes k=0, /2, /2^k. Pretty formatting uses `/2<sup>k</sup>` for k>1. SMT2 uses exact `(/ NUM (^ 2 K))`, decimal suffixes on NUM, 2 and K, and the existing negative integer SMT2 route. Single decimal follows source absolute numerator/Power(2,k)/Rem/Div; exact termination omits `?`, exhausted precision appends `?`. Integer fast path has no decimal point. Raw noninteger representation with zero remainder violates the source SASSERT; release still performs the source loop. Interval decimal emits `?` immediately for differing signs; for equal negative signs its leading `-` precedes a possible `?`; mismatched integer parts or digits end at their exact source prefix. If both remainders become zero, return precise text, otherwise append `?` at exhausted precision. All local numeral cleanup reproduces source sequence on success and lexical cleanup on error.
>
> `g3debug` reproduces source before/after rational conversions in Normalize, six Add/Sub/Mul bodies, and Approx strict-bound checks, plus ordinary source assertion sites (exponent product, interval conditions, division conditions, decimal remainder). Failed diagnostics use a typed invariant error and retain source publication prefix; real diagnostics are not replaced by empty tag handlers or test-only arithmetic. The VERIFY selection action executes in both builds. TRACE/STRACE logging is observational instrumentation and remains explicitly separate, not an invented logger prerequisite.
>
> Concrete `ScopedBinary` owns one numerator, borrows its manager, charges its actual cold header, and supplies checked Get/Manager/Set/Assign/Clone/Reset/Swap/Close, source predicate/Neg, comparisons and Add/Sub/Mul compound/value methods. Int32/Int overloads create scoped `_b`, call Set, then the BQ/BQ operation; clean `_b` at the source expression boundary. Generic source BQ/BQ value operators use copy-before-compound and returned-lvalue-copy semantics as existing scoped/facade translations do. Test expressions destroy every temporary at each source statement. Do not expose Div/Rem/Abs methods: those generic template functions cannot instantiate for this manager because it provides no div/rem/abs member.
>
> `ScopedBinaryVector` is a concrete cold owner with contiguous pointer-free BinaryRational payloads, exact source vector growth 2 then (3n+1)/2, actual-capacity byte charges, old/new allocation peak, checked size/host-length arithmetic, and explicit transfer/invalidation on growth. The one Go slice belongs to the vector owner, not each hot numeral. Push publishes a default element before Copy as source scoped_vector does; a failing Copy leaves its default/prefix slot logically present. Shrink/Pop/Reset destroy ascending numerators via Del; manager ResetVector instead uses Reset before retaining vector backing. Final Close frees backing/header and closes no borrowed manager. Source vector's raw scalar storage destruction never automatically owns/destroys big numerators; ownership routes must be tested separately.
>

>

> ## Implemented source methods
>
> FastFloat is a pointer-free fixed-precision significand handle/sign plus int32 exponent. This is source MPFF, not IEEE arithmetic. NewFastFloat/default scalar is zero; owning shallow copies are prohibited. FastFloatManager implements the complete selected executable manager families:
>
> - Construction/destruction, precision/capacity block initialization, source reserve-zero VERIFY, owned one, ensure_capacity/expand/allocate, recycle/del/reset, scalar swap, explicit Copy, exponent getter/setter and Precise/Field.
> - Both rounding modes and setter/query; sign/zero/positive/negative/nonpositive/nonnegative; integer/int64/uint64 predicates and getters; abs-one/one/minus-one/two; epsilon predicates; all six comparisons; neg/abs.
> - Signed/unsigned32 and64 setters with distinct source routes, both fraction setter overloads, source copy setter; MPZ/MPQ setters, significand extraction and integer/rational conversions with either actual manager temporary policy. No hardware float/double setter is invented: the source declares none.
> - Internal indexed buffer/shift/bit-test/normalization helpers, inc/dec significand, min/max significand and exponent saturation; epsilon/min/max/next/prev; source add_sub/Add/Sub/Inc/Dec, Algorithm M Mul, single Algorithm D Div, both Inv overloads, complete Power, both Floor/Ceil output forms, both power-of-two queries and previous-power query.
> - Raw, ordinary, pretty, decimal and SMT2 displays; to_string/to_rational_string. String variants return one caller-owned final Go string; FormatInto variants publish into caller buffers only after successful staging, exclude NUL, and leave buffers unchanged on error/short-buffer.
> - Concrete ScopedFastFloat: lifetime/copy/assignment/swap/neg/abs, every executable arithmetic compound and value operator, six comparisons, five scoped predicates and printing. Value arithmetic preserves source copy-before-compound followed by returned-lvalue-copy and statement cleanup. ScopedFastFloatVector: owning elements, 2→(3n+1)/2 growth, resize/push/pop/shrink/reset/back/at, ascending element destruction and idempotent Close. At/Get are borrowed views invalidated by the documented owner/vector lifetime; no claim that old Go pointers detect every invalidated vector borrow.

The whole source unit remains **partial**: persistent ostream flags/fail-state/custom ostream transport, all TRACE/STRACE (including trace-only Power copies), integration with the external z3_exception transport, and the real subpaving consumer/config/context/tactic remain open. > # MPQ additive and mixed-product publication packet
>
> Implemented and frozen, based on committed `facaeb4`. The selected public
> methods now write caller fields in source order. Eight Go files are frozen;
> Git, source metadata and integration commits remain parent-owned. No Go
> parameterized types/functions, unsafe operations, cgo or production
> `math/big` were introduced.
>
> ## Selected source and implementation
>
> Read complete `src/util/mpq.h:76–155` and `271–442`. The selected source methods
> are both `rat_add` overloads, `rat_sub`, public rational Add/Sub, mixed Add,
> both integer-product rational-result Mul overloads, Inc/Dec forwarding, and
> all four rational/mixed AddMul/SubMul overloads. SYNCH selects actual local
> numerals; the other profile retains the existing manager caches.
>
> Production edits are restricted to:
>
> * `mpnum/mpq.go`: Add/Sub's shared addSub implementation.
> * `mpnum/mpq_ops.go`: AddInt, MulInt and MulInts.
>
> Add/Sub's integer fastpath writes caller.num with the existing Integer
> Add/Sub, then destroys caller.den and publishes inline denominator1. General
> Add/Sub computes tmp1=a.num*b.den and tmp2=b.num*a.den, writes caller.den
> with a.den*b.den, writes caller.num using tmp1 +/- tmp2, and normalizes once.
> Ordinary SYNCH completion explicitly deletes tmp1 then tmp2, as the source
> statements require. Deferred per-local cleanup remains only for interrupted
> Go ownership; it does not claim C++ plain mpz locals are exception-safe.
>
> AddInt uses the integer fastpath or computes b*a.den into the actual single
> local/retained tmp, Copies a.den to caller.den, Adds a.num/tmp to caller.num,
> then normalizes. MulInts writes caller.num through the actual Integer Mul,
> then resets caller.den. MulInt selects whether b is integer-valued before
> any aliased output mutation, writes caller.num through Integer Mul(a,b.num),
> then either resets caller.den or Copies b.den and normalizes. There is no
> new pair staging, source algorithm replay or private fused-only substitute.
>
> The existing fused/fusedInt implementations are unchanged: select the actual
> b=+1/-1 shortcuts before mutation, or call public Mul/MulInt on the source
> local/retained rational temporary, then public Add/Sub exactly once. Their
> local deferred destruction already occurs after Add/Sub returns. Closing their
> public dependencies corrects their caller publication without duplicating
> arithmetic. Raw Inc/Dec still call AddInt with integer +1/-1; service prefix
> operators still construct source rational-one and use rational Add. The two
> routes are deliberately preserved.
>
> Public Rational Copy/Mul, normalize, Integer Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Mod/GCD, Natural
> algorithms, service implementations, allocator and coefficient store are
> unchanged. All existing method signatures and cold owner layouts remain
> unchanged. There is no selected raw sub(mpq,mpz,mpq) overload, so no invented
> SubInt or fabricated missing-API RED was added.
>
> ## Tests-first evidence and scope
>
> NEW `mpnum/mp_add_publication_test.go` contains nine groups:
>
> 1. TestAdditivePublicationBoundedModelsAndAliases: 504 independent signed
>    exact operation/mode/output-alias cases through all nine public routes.
> 2. TestAdditivePublicationCallerFailurePrefixes: actual reservation sweeps,
>    complete immediate named cells/Words audits, exact old/raw/normalized
>    component candidates and owned failedRef, unchanged inputs, finite success
>    detection and complete Close refund.
> 3. TestAdditivePublicationFusedUnitDispatch: 64 actual +/-1 dispatch cases with
>    every rational output alias and both policies.
> 4. TestAdditivePublicationIntegerFastpathOldDenominator: real cold integer

> 5. TestAdditivePublicationRawDenominatorsAndIdentity: unreduced, negative

> | InvInPlace | Debug !is_zero before numerics; if numerator negative, Neg num then Neg den; Swap num/den. No GCD, denominator repair or allocation work pair. |
> | Inv(a,out) | Copy caller numerator then denominator using already corrected public Copy; call actual InvInPlace. Thus debug zero assertion occurs AFTER Copy, not at method entry. Self output retains source Copy self no-action. |

> | Div, b==out | Actual local tmp: Mul(a.num,b.den,tmp); Mul(a.den,b.num,out.den); Copy(out.num,tmp); Del tmp at source statement before signs/normalize. Error cleanup is lexical Go adaptation. |

> | AccDiv | Mul(a.den,b,a.den); reread actual b sign, Neg a.num then a.den if negative; normalize a. No inserted numerator Copy. |

> ## Approved design history: zero-domain and owning-result contract
>
> Source inv(mpq&) has only SASSERT(!is_zero(a)). Release Inv(0/1) executes Swap
> and finitely leaves1/0. Output Inv must first Copy0/1 into destination; debug
> assertion then retains copied0/1. For source INT_MIN numeral Neg, actual
> promoting allocation can fail BEFORE denominator Neg/Swap. No whole-pair
> rollback or retry using destroyed/missing scratch is valid.
>
> Source rational Div/DivInt/AccDiv/RatDiv have no early zero-divisor guard.
> For nonzero numerator and zero divisor, real component operations can leave
> n/0; normalize computes gcd(n,0)=abs(n), then returns immediately if gcd1 or
> Divs numerator to±1 and denominator to0. These are finite raw results.
> For0/0, real fields become0/0 before gcd0 and the first Integer Div(num,0,num)
> reaches unsafe arithmetic; ErrDivideByZero belongs there. If an earlier
> Copy/Mul/GCD allocation fails, that failure and its completed prefixes precede
> any later domain condition. Do not blanket-reject all zero divisors at entry.
> Component aliases can change what zero/sign is subsequently read; derive
> fixtures from exact action routes, rather than original scalar values alone.
>
> Current RationalManager.check rejects denominator0 as ErrUninitializedRational;
> checkCleanup does too. These guards intentionally distinguish NewRational0/1
> from raw Go zero and prohibit ordinary invalid-numeral reads. They cannot be
> silently equated with a source arithmetic exception. Full owning cleanup is a
> prerequisite once caller fields can hold source-finite zero-denominator results.
> Proposed alternatives for parent review:
>
> 1. **Preferred raw action fidelity:** return nil from source-finite Inv/Div
>    actions and retain exact1/0 or±1/0; ordinary check/String/next arithmetic
>    still returns ErrUninitializedRational. Cleanup-only Del validation checks
>    actual integer field ownership but permits denominator0, so callers can
>    destroy all live/failed components. This also permits harmless cleanup of
>    raw Go0/0; it does NOT initialize, lazily normalize or allow reads of it.
> 2. **Explicit Go post-action domain boundary:** return ErrUninitializedRational
>    AFTER all source-finite actions/publications, with the same cleanup contract.
>    This is a Go adapter; source does not throw there. It can alter service
>    value-result behavior and must be documented/tested as such.
>
> Option1 was approved and implemented; Option2 remains historical and was
> not used. The distinctions below remain real ownership boundaries. Neither alternative
> claims true source wrapper equivalence for denominator0. Source rational value
> operators can copy raw1/0 through their ordinary field setters. Current service
> value-result Copy/Move/check routes reject it as an initialized-numeral boundary.
> Keeping service production unchanged would preserve a safe empty owning result
> on that Go boundary error with local drop cleanup, while compound assignment
> retains its actual invalid raw destination. Those differences must remain
> explicitly open; do not add an unreviewed private unchecked-copy surrogate or
> new initialized marker to pretend source equivalence. A later full owner-value
> representation/bridge contract could reconcile these transfers separately.

> ## Exact full grammar and action inventory to preserve
>
> | Phase / condition | Actual source actions and current faithful implementation |
> | --- | --- |
> | Entry | Reset actual numerator before any byte inspection; source inline ten10 and scoped tmp0. No denominator Copy or reset yet. |
> | Leading/sign | Skip only ASCII space0x20 for sign detection. Remember negative only if the first remaining byte is '-'; sign byte is subsequently ignored by digit scanning. Tabs/newlines/Unicode and later signs do not alter this flag. |
> | Integer bytes | Until NUL/end, '/', '.', 'e' or 'E': ignore nondigits, each ASCII digit calls integer Mul(num,10,tmp), then Add(tmp,digit,num). No strict whole-token grammar or strconv substitution. |
> | No suffix | reset_denominator caller only after integer bytes; final optional Neg(num), then normalize caller. Empty/junk parses0. |
> | '/' or '.' | Create scoped tmp2, set1; Reset actual den before suffix digit scanning. Every ASCII digit calls Mul(den,10,tmp), Add(tmp,digit,den). For decimal only, Mul(tmp2,10,tmp2) follows that denominator digit publication. Ignore all other bytes except e/E/NUL; '/' inside this scan is ignored. |
> | Scientific marker | Slash suffix plus e/E throws mixed-notation BEFORE exponent reading or zero-denominator check. Otherwise advance past marker; exponent negative only for immediately following '-'; all later nondigits ignored except '/' throws mixed-notation. |
> | Exponent digits | uint64 wrap on exp=10*exp+digit; do not replace with overflow rejection or signed conversion. Source<=9 SASSERTs are already implied by the ASCII digit condition, not a manufactured behavioral failure. |
> | Non-slash completion | If wrapped exp>UINT_MAX, throw exponent-too-big BEFORE creating scoped b. Then create scoped b; when decimal digits existed, SetParts(b,current den,tmp2), integer Set caller.den1 (not reset_denominator), then actual public Add(caller,b,caller). |
> | Nonzero exponent | Create scoped exp then scoped ten rational, Set ten10, call actual public Power(ten,exp,expTmp), then public Div or Mul on actual caller depending remembered exponent sign. Source first-growth failures before actual mask wrap retain precedence. No giant unbounded test or early power cap. |
> | Slash zero | After mixed-notation checks, if actual caller.den is zero throw division-by-zero parser category. This is a source exception, not normalize's later integer unsafe division. |
> | Final | Suffix scoped locals die before outer optional numerator Neg; then actual normalize caller; outer scoped tmp dies at function exit. No successful or exceptional final whole-rational rollback. |
>
> Embedded NUL ends every loop; bytes beyond it cannot create later markers,
> exceptions or digits. Go strings are borrowed only for the call, never retained
> in numeral storage. Empty Go string models an empty C string, not nullptr.
> The existing numeralByte helper provides the finite host buffer boundary.
> The selected source char comparisons use only ASCII digit/sign/marker values;
> signed high-byte behavior does not broaden their acceptance.

Close deletes seven fields in source order and refunds only its own header. Caller operands still obey the raw manager's documented implicit-owner contract.

Copying an owning manager is an explicit rejected unsafe domain, not a new source manager copy algorithm. Static `Precise` remains owner-independent. Borrowed manager lifetime normally exceeds wrapper lifetime; after forced borrowed-manager Close, wrapper Close refunds only its own external header and skips callbacks against already reclaimed cells.

> Centered representations preserve odd [-floor(p/2),floor(p/2)] and even [1-p/2,p/2]. Source constructor `prime` arguments are unused and `m_p_prime` uninitialized. >
> Power copies its real local then publishes output1, executes every selected multiplication and every local square (including final unused square), and advances the uint32 mask. On the actual 2^31→0 mask wrap, after all completed iteration actions, it returns the existing typed `PowerDomainError`/`ErrNonterminatingPower`; no earlier output rollback or alternate power algorithm. **Raw C++ mpz has no destructor:** source `del(power)` runs only at normal end. > # Actual MPZ allocator/backend integration proposal
>
> Phase B design and new missing-API tests only, following shared memory phase A commit6ffd717. No memory/mpnum/arena production, existing tests, metadata or Git changes are authorized in this phase. The objective is to replace the MPZ cell backing actually used by the numerical algorithms, not to install an unused second allocator or reinterpret Budget reservations as source malloc calls. Full solver/runtime integration remains required.
>
> ## Audited source and current boundaries
>
> Read allocation/layout/lifetime bodies in src/util/mpz.h:46–184, cpp:86–245,247–280,306–354,1185–1216,1555–1595; arithmetic scratch consumers and source mpn.h/.cpp/buffer.h allocation bodies; memory_manager.cpp global initialization/getters and both TLS/non-TLS allocation branches; committed standalone allocator bodies. Current IntegerManager/mpz_slab, limbView/NaturalManager/format storage, RationalManager, RationalService, and BinaryRationalManager ownership were inspected. Existing concurrent power/publication drafts remain parent-owned; integration must be rebased on their final committed results rather than silently restore an older action order.
>
> Current Go cells are numericCellSlab records containing a Words descriptor, size, and capacity. Allocate acquires a logical slab record and a separate geometric Words payload; free releases both. This is an audited storage adaptation, but it is not the source small-object-allocator topology. NaturalManager also obtains four Words allocations for source inline buffers. SourceCounters cannot be repaired by adding events to either operation: neither existing slab/page allocation equals a source cell allocation, and a per-cell malloc counter would count pooled objects incorrectly.
>
> The source manager owns one small_object_allocator, one mpn_manager, two temporary and two argument cell pointers, intMin and two64. MPQ inherits that same MPZ manager (mpq.h:43), so numerator and denominator must share one allocator. Binary rational managers borrow their MPZ manager (mpbq.h); RationalService owns a RationalManager and synchronizes its operations. No allocator per rational, coefficient, wrapper, or cached value is appropriate.
>
> ## Selected source profile and exact cell layout
>
> The current arithmetic is explicitly _MP_INTERNAL with unsigned32 digits. This is not the default Linux GMP backend: mpz.h:46–53 selects GMP when neither internal nor MSBIGNUM is specified on non-Windows. GMP's mpz_t and external GMP limb allocations, and MSBIGNUM's size_t digits, are separate OPEN source profiles; no cgo, unsafe, generic, or GMP substitute is proposed.
>
> For the selected internal profile, sizeof(mpz_cell)=8: size at byte0, capacity at byte4, and little-endian uint32 digits at byte8+4*i. Actual cell allocation is one object with those bytes. The selected pointer width changes allocator rounding and runtime SIZE_T prefix, not digit width or these header offsets. capacity6 requests32 bytes in both profiles. allocate writes capacity immediately after allocator.allocate; m_size is not initialized by that helper. Argument construction then writes size1. New/free-list storage must not be silently zeroed or presented as source-initialized digits. Freelist pointer writes really overwrite the first4/8 object bytes; LP64 therefore overwrites both source header fields. Reallocation of that free object rewrites capacity, not all digits or size.
>
> Important width: cell_size returns unsigned, even on LP64 (mpz.h:122). Compute the source expression then narrow to uint32: uint32(8+4*uint64(capacity)), not an unrestricted uint64 cell extent. Large capacities can wrap to a finite small allocation. Preserve that allocation/capacity publication and guard only the actual endangered header/digit access. A global capacity rejection would erase source prefixes. Any source capacity assertion remains debug-only at its actual site.
>
> Boundary fixtures: LP64 capacity59 =>244-byte pooled object, capacity60 =>248-byte direct object. ILP32 capacity60 =>248-byte pooled object, capacity61 =>252-byte direct object. Debug non-Windows directs every nonzero cell; debug Windows pools. Source initial capacity is6 for uint32 digits; the source64-digit capacity4 branch remains OPEN.
>
> ## Actual shared package boundary and phase B codecs
>
> Phase A now provides the sole real memory.Runtime/accounting/SmallAllocator implementation, with main error and real byte-stream bridges. RuntimeConfig carries Budget, SizeTBits32/64, ThreadLocal and one static borrowed ErrorTransport. SmallAllocatorConfig carries the actual Runtime, PointerBits/Debug/Windows profile, one cold borrowed AllocatorIO receiver and Verbosity. Main exported source errors alias lower identities where applicable. Block and ObjectRef are scalar owner/slot/generation locators; ObjectRef additionally retains the deterministic source-pointer-order address adapter. RuntimeOwner() on the allocator returns the actual borrowed runtime after Close. Phase A preserved all41 original groups plus12 new groups; source process-global/TLS and generated initialization remain honest separate dependencies.
>
> Phase B proposes exactly these missing concrete codecs, using actual byte initialization state and no slice borrows:
>
> ```go
> func (*memory.Runtime) ReadUint32(ref memory.Block, offset uint64) (uint32, error)
> func (*memory.Runtime) WriteUint32(ref memory.Block, offset uint64, value uint32) error
> func (*memory.SmallAllocator) ReadUint32(ref memory.ObjectRef, offset uint64) (uint32, error)
> func (*memory.SmallAllocator) WriteUint32(ref memory.ObjectRef, offset uint64, value uint32) error
> ```
>
> These are selected little-endian internal digit/header adapters, independent of host unsafe casts. Validate genuine owner/generation, then the actual endangered four-byte range using offset<=extent and extent-offset>=4 without offset+4 overflow; check initialized bytes for reads. A word write validates its physical range at the word access before publishing its four initialized bytes. It does not reject an earlier finite wrapped cell allocation or header publication elsewhere. Misaligned byte offsets remain representable by explicit codec; MPZ offsets0/4/8+4*i are aligned within their source objects. Codec operations never reserve storage or emit source allocate/free/count events. Allocator codecs resolve actual ObjectRef provenance/lifetime and use the same Runtime backing, never a second payload.
>
> Failure transport remains static/borrowed; direct lower default errors preserve101/113 and no-code vector overflow. The selected allocator diagnostic receiver may be caller-provided but must outlive the manager. No production main-package import is introduced into mpnum. Native process stderr/verbose/stdout binding and source SYNCH locking remain separately audited adapters, not fake sinks.
>
> ## MPZ record and physical access replacement
>
> Retain Int's current release uint32/check-mode uint64 numericCellRef layout and owner-local implicit-owner contract. Use a charged numeric descriptor ledger mapping that ID/generation to one memory.ObjectRef. The record is pointer-free. Keep the existing permanently dead failedRef as charged auxiliary identity metadata with no source cell allocation or counter event. Source size/capacity and digits are stored in the actual allocator object. > ## Selected source finalization and owning cleanup contract

>
> ```go

> func (*IntegerManager) CloseChecked() error
> func (*IntegerManager) Close() // existing signature; attempts CloseChecked, retains charged retry state on failure

> SourceFinalize releases two64, intMin, tmp0,arg0,tmp1,arg1 in source order, then Natural member overflow in reverse member order, then allocator pooled chunks/actual diagnostics. It never invents direct user-cell frees. Managed release cursor and flags record completed actions, preventing a transport/physical error from repeating requested-byte subtraction or diagnostics. Ordinary arithmetic is closed after source finalization begins; cleanup-only actions retain genuine owner/provenance validation. A source-finalized manager retains its charged descriptor directory and actual direct caller raw-location roots until explicit owning cleanup. Source-pooled caller refs are invalidated only when the underlying chunks really free. Already freed direct refs and failedRef remain distinguishable.

> CloseChecked is the explicit owning Go continuation: clean caller-owned live cells and completed unpublished pending cells once, perform any remaining source-member teardown, then release descriptor/dead-token/Natural/header metadata and close only an internally owned Runtime. Existing Close delegates to it; on a cleanup refusal it must fail visibly with a concrete cleanup-error panic while retaining all charged roots/cursors, since its existing void signature cannot return the error. CloseChecked returns the same error for explicit non-panicking continuation. This selected Go failure-surface adapter needs parent approval; it is not silent successful Close or C++ exception equivalence. This preserves existing caller expectation that normal Close invalidates/releases every numeral while marking additional direct free events as owning Go cleanup, not C++ destructor actions. SourceFinalize followed by CloseChecked must clean surviving direct refs without rerunning member frees or diagnostics. The direct allocator RawLocation token can outlive allocator context for real Runtime.Deallocate when source-finalized cleanup requires it; retain the actual capacity/extent and release phase before intrusive overwrite.

Numeric cleanup cannot infer all completed actions from the error or token alone. > ## Debug/release domain and nontermination contract
>
> The source negative checks are SASSERT, not universal release guards. Preserve:
>
> * Release small/small negative OR/AND/XOR is finite signed arithmetic, including
>   INT_MIN and output aliases. Debug refuses at its source assertion before any
>   numeric action. Existing ErrBitwiseDomain can remain the debug assertion
>   category; it must no longer reject all finite release cases.
> * Mixed-sign big binary operands have finite source paths: the nonnegative
>   quotient eventually reaches0, the loop ends, and OR/XOR execute their actual
>   negative tail while AND omits tails. Zero with a big negative can take the
>   no-loop tail/no-tail path. Compare finite results to independent test-only
>   two's-complement big.Int expectations, and freeze any source-specific
>   departure separately instead of changing the algorithm.
> * Two negative operands in the big branch eventually reach a1=b1=-1; source
>   while remains true forever. This is distinct from the finite small/small
>   negative fast path. Parent source review accepts a typed nontermination
>   boundary at the FIRST actual continuation where BOTH quotients are inline
>   -1, after all preceding copy/reset/mod/set/multiply/add/div actions.
>   Proposed `ErrNonterminatingBitwise` and concrete
>   `BitwiseNonterminationError{Operation BitwiseOperation}` distinguish this
>   from source debug assertions. The operation enum identifies OR/AND/XOR.
>   Earlier real allocation errors take precedence. This stops an infinite
>   domain whose multiplier/output can still grow; it does NOT claim equality
>   to a future source budget-refusal prefix. No entry sign rejection or arbitrary

> # MPZ public manager contract closure
>

> `IsMinusOne`; `Inc`, `Dec`; `Equal`, `NotEqual`, `Less`, `Greater`, `LessEqual`,
> `GreaterEqual`, `LessInt`; `SetInt32`, `SetUint32`; `Dup`; `Inv`.
>
> Sign retains the entire inline int32 value, not a normalized mathematical sign.
> Big values retain their existing -1/+1 sign representation. One/minus-one checks
> require inline representation. Comparisons use the already translated Compare
> algorithm; transposed/negated wrappers retain source operand order. LessInt
> retains its inline fast path and otherwise creates a scalar inline argument.

> Sub route. SetInt32 explicitly Del's the old payload before inline publication.

> threshold, and otherwise uses the signed int64 source constructor.

> preserving requested cell capacity and representation. A returned big Int owns
> its independent cell; the caller must Del it and may not shallow-copy it.
> Predictable failure destroys any unpublished output. No new persistent or
> unbudgeted scratch storage is introduced, and small Dup allocates no storage.

>
> Read-only existing production proposal. Base203486f includes the additive source correction. No consumer/destructor implementation edits have been made. Parent approved the listed lifecycle regions after source review; selected GCD bodies remain numeric-owner controlled. No race or WASM/WASI checks will be launched following the new user steering.

> ## Source versus Go assembly owner
>
> The source BIG integer display action is sign insertion BEFORE construction of its inline1024 char sbuffer, requested uint32 `11*size`, then mpn conversion, then C-string insertion, then char-sbuffer destruction. Source SMALL integer insertion directly uses out<<m_val, with NO source char buffer or three Natural limb locals. The three mpn limb locals exist only for >1 limb conversion and destruct in reverse order BEFORE source C-string insertion returns to integer display. Each integer displayed by rational/binary/infinitesimal composition gets its own logical char/local-limb lifetime, not an accumulated persistent manager formatting scratch.
>
> Propose NEW concrete `numeralOutputScope` in mp_format_output.go. One charged cold owner exists per public composed output operation, created before acquiring source formatting roots. It contains:
>
> - private owner/self identity, borrowed Budget/Runtime, headerBytes;
> - one [1024]byte Go assembly inline buffer and initialized/position metadata; optional actual []byte assembly overflow with its capacity charge;
> - one concrete sourceCharBuffer with actual [1024]byte inline/source initialized mask, source uint32 pos/capacity, raw/pending memory.Blocks;
> - three sourceLimbBuffer locals for the exact mpn conversion; scalar active/cleanup cursors;
> - cold original/cleanup errors, with no additional exception allocation on failure.
>
> The assembly bytes are a Go buffered-output adapter replacing the external ostream/ostringstream boundary, NOT source memory::allocate events. Actual assembly owner header/backing is charged by reflected physical size/capacity; old+new assembly growth peaks reserve before make, copy prior bytes, release old backing. Source char/limb overflow calls the actual shared Runtime and affects true source counters. No host intermediate text/string or fmt. Only `string(assembledBytes)` produces one final caller-owned string; FormatInto copies only after successful preparation, preserving the current documented buffered-destination adapter and ErrShortBuffer domain. No source-counter charge for that caller-owned string.
>
> A single cold output-scope heap allocation, if compiler escape requires it, is explicitly charged; it is not hidden per-record boxing. Arithmetic warmed Mul/Div must still allocate zero Go objects. Output allocation counts must be measured and reported honestly rather than assert that this Go owner is C++ stack storage. An optional stack-friendly output implementation may remove that allocation later only if actual root retention remains correct.

> ```

Existing reserveText/textRead/textWrite/reverseText/prepareInteger offset semantics can temporarily preserve signatures, but use this operation-owned assembly, never a persistent Natural SmallBytes owner. At success/failure endOutput clears that borrowed pointer exactly once. It cannot invoke public formatting while holding a service mutex; service helpers are private and use existing service->manager confinement.

> Every public non-alias formatting entrypoint brackets its entire preparation+final copy with begin/end, including errors before publishText/finalString. Public alias methods delegate without constructing a second scope. endOutput joins errors without a new wrapper allocation: preserve original operation cause; attempt exact pending/source-local cleanup and report a retained owning error only when cleanup actually refuses. Parent selects retention of the ALREADY charged output scope itself on any cleanup refusal: Natural owns one cold pendingOutput pointer after activeOutput is cleared. No eight-root transfer directory/fallback is needed. Its actual header, assembly and source raw roots stay charged until checked cleanup completes. The scope implements the cold error interface itself, with fixed Error label, original/cleanup causes and cleanup stage/cursor; no new exception allocation. A new operation rejects a pending owning context before replacement. Natural CloseChecked cleans that actual context before its Runtime/header, and borrowed Runtime never closes. Cleanup retry does not resume formatting, emit delayed text, refree physically completed blocks or repair a failed TLS synchronization. Scope/parent cause links must remain acyclic; ordinary formatting arithmetic returns leaf transport causes, and a self/ancestor owner must never be stored as its own unwrapping cause. Final caller string is produced ONLY after source-local cleanup succeeds; assembly charges are refunded after final copy.

> SourceCharBuffer growth is source uint32 doubling, actual profile size_t byte request, copy source POS bytes only, old overflow free before pointer/capacity publication. Char construction with `(11*size,0)` runs source resize/push zeroing; no premature UINT32 domain rejection. Source buffers remain separate from assembly. Per-integer conversion resets local logical lifetimes/initialization, and any overflow must actually free after that integer's source display; no retained capacity from one numeral to the next.

> # Mandatory MPZ backend: retained owning failure contract
>
> Read-only production proposal, based on committed tracked memory core facaeb4. This document authorizes no production edit. Existing production/test files, metadata and Git remain parent-owned. The selected source profile is non-GMP, uint32 digits, LP64 or ILP32 size_t, with actual selected allocator debug/platform branches. Source files/hashes are retained in PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-mpz-allocator-integration-packet-md. Other digit/GMP profiles remain open.
>
> ## Actual ownership and physical layout
>
> Default IntegerManager must use one actual memory.Runtime and memory.SmallAllocator for every numeric cell, not keep an optional idle backend beside Words. Supplied Runtime is borrowed; nil constructs an isolated owned Runtime (explicitly not a process-global runtime claim). Borrowed Runtime and Budget must outlive every related numerical/coefficient owner. Cells.Budget and Words.Descriptors.Budget remain equal for compatibility; the Words configuration no longer creates numeric payload owners. Runtime/Budget/profile compatibility is checked before source cell work.
>
> Each source cell is one actual allocator object: uint32 size at byte0, capacity at byte4, uint32 digits beginning byte8. Source requested bytes use uint32 `(8+4*capacity)` wrapping before widening even on LP64. Actual requested access uses codec bounds; source-defined accesses into rounded pooled slack may use actual ObjectExtent plus raw Runtime codec bounds, never the surrounding chunk extent. A wrapped allocation completes before the endangered header write reports a typed guard. Header initialization comes only from actual source stores.
>
> Numeric descriptor retains ObjectRef, request uint32, and a private scalar release phase/cursor, instead of owning a second digit array. Current Int scalar token shape and owner-specific permanently dead failedRef stay unchanged. Directory, ledger, failedRef and pending-state charges are Go safety metadata, never source malloc events. Physical source capacity is authoritative; cached safety copies are not substitute initialized bytes.
>
> IntegerManager embeds its Natural state, including four actual [16]uint32 buffers, initialized masks and scalar overflow/pending Blocks. An ephemeral pointer to the embedded state is permitted as cold owner metadata; it creates no separate Natural allocation/header charge. The four inline arrays are charged once through the real Integer header. Standalone NaturalManager needs its own charged owner and explicit borrowed/owned Runtime contract; its callers (notably FastFloatManager) require a separately coordinated compatibility change, not a second numeric algorithm.
>
> ## Retained owner fields and public error API
>
> Each of IntegerManager, RationalManager and RationalService embeds a concrete cold `numeralFailureState` containing `original error`, `cleanup error`, operation/stage uint8, root cursor uint32, component cursor uint8, active bool. These two interfaces are cold error transport only; no hot record contains an interface or closure. Reflected owner header charges these fields. Each owner has its own self-identity guard; shallow copied owner operations fail without freeing the true owner.
>
> Proposed common cold interface:
>
> ```go
> type ConstructionFailure interface {
>     error
>     Unwrap() error
>     Cleanup() error
>     RuntimeOwner() *memory.Runtime
>     OriginalCause() error
>     CleanupCause() error
> }
> ```
>
> The owners themselves implement it; there is no IntegerConstructionFailure/RationalConstructionFailure/Service wrapper allocation. Fixed-label Error does not format an allocated string. OriginalCause is the first operation failure and never changes on cleanup retry. CleanupCause is the most recent cleanup refusal (nil after completed cleanup). Unwrap returns original, or cleanup when there was no construction/operation cause. Neither cause may refer to that same owner: when a leaf returns self during cleanup, extract its stored underlying transport cause, never set original=self or cleanup=self. Child-owner errors may be retained by an outer owner only when that child cannot refer back to the outer owner; their ownership graph is strictly acyclic. errors.Is/As must terminate; tests inspect the bounded unwrap chain before calling them.
>
> `Cleanup()` delegates to that owner's checked owning teardown without changing the original classification. A successful cleanup can release all owner charges while the caller retains the Go error object, as with a caller retaining any closed Go owner; it no longer contains owning roots. Status/cursor fields are not caller-authorized flags and cannot skip any source action.
>
> Existing constructor return shape remains `(*Owner,error)`. Before header reserve succeeds, return nil plus static failure. Immediately after successful header reserve, allocate/initialize the actual owner (including self identity) before acquiring child roots. On an error, attempt exact cleanup. If completed, return nil plus original cause. If refused, return nil plus that same existing owner; never allocate a second error header after Budget refusal. A constructor error therefore retains every physical and cold root until caller Cleanup. Do not release a header containing still-owned roots.
>
> Integer/Rational expose `SourceFinalize() error`, `CloseChecked() error`, and retain existing void Close. Proposed void Close invokes CloseChecked and panics that SAME retained owner on refusal, rather than silently dropping a root; this compatibility adapter requires explicit parent approval. Service's existing Close returns checked error, and SourceFinalize remains separate. Ordinary arithmetic rejects once source finalization or owning teardown begins; cleanup operations remain available. Valid output reads after an unrelated scratch publication failure remain allowed before teardown begins.
>
> ## Constructor and lexical cleanup cursors
>
> Integer constructor: owner/descriptor/dead-token preparation (explicit Go metadata safety adapter), actual allocator header and embedded Natural state, then source tmp0,arg0,tmp1,arg1,intMin,two64 and final tmp0/two64 exchange. Cursor reflects actual completed roots, not a presumed six-cell baseline. Missing scratch remains absent. One pendingCell field captures a successfully allocated object before capacity write/descriptor preparation; another pending allocation cannot overwrite it. The allocator itself owns any partial raw/headerless or lexical scratch failure roots.
>
> Integer source finalization order follows mpz.cpp:142–161 and reverse member destruction: two64, intMin, tmp0,arg0,tmp1,arg1; source SYNCH lock destruction; Natural t_ab,t_ms,v,u; allocator chunk frees/diagnostics. Only completed release steps advance root cursor. Failed physical release retains the object and real memory.ReleaseProgress; after physical release an error is retained and retry acknowledges the same private authority rather than refreeing or repeating requested/global subtraction. Managed roots are cleared only when their cleanup step completes; separate physical-dead state rejects dangling normal reads while still allowing cleanup continuation.
>
> SourceFinalize never frees caller direct cells. Pooled caller locators become dangling only when actual chunks are freed. Direct live objects survive allocator source destruction; descriptor retains original request, raw Block/offset and release phase before allocator context closes. Owning CloseChecked cleans caller live cells/pending cells and any remaining source members; after SourceFinalize it uses those captured direct raw tokens through the same Runtime, never fabricates a SmallAllocator event on a closed allocator. Runtime.Deallocate retries persisted before-free authority; after-free pending acknowledgement is completed through retained genuine authority. If the current API cannot acknowledge a postfree error after allocator context is closed, preserve that context until completion; do not use exported flags to authorize skipping. The descriptor directory and header release only after actual roots and allocator pending roots are empty. Internally owned Runtime closes last; borrowed Runtime never closes.
>
> Rational constructor currently has only one child construction edge (mpq.go:49): IntegerManager. Proposed owner is charged/allocated first. If child construction fails, no other Rational root exists, so refund the Rational header and forward the child owner error unchanged. Otherwise retain child pointer immediately. Rational SourceFinalize destroys nTmp,addTmp1,addTmp2 then ltTmp1,ltTmp2,addMulTmp; each rational is NUMERATOR then DENOMINATOR (mpq.h:186–189). Cursor advances component by component; never clear the whole pair after only numerator cleanup. Then call child's SourceFinalize. Owning CloseChecked follows those same leaf actions, then child's owning CloseChecked, then releases Rational header. A child failure retains the Rational parent if it still owns child/other roots. `drop` cannot remain an error-ignoring helper for owning destruction.
>
> Service constructor currently has only one child edge (rational_service.go:76): RationalManager. Before constants, a failed child is forwarded unchanged after the unused Service header is refunded. Once manager exists, service owner retains it and any initialized constant prefix. Initialization order is zero,one,minusOne,inf-rational constants,inf-int constants. Per-constant initialized components must be recorded before copy calls. Partial construction must not pretend all constants exist or free uninitialized handles.
>
> Service teardown follows existing audited rational service ordering: inf-rational zero/one/minusOne, each SECOND then FIRST (wrapper lexical member destruction); inf-int zero/one/minusOne FIRST; ascending power-cache values, each NUM then DEN; free cache backing only after all entries clean; zero,one,minusOne NUM then DEN; manager checked teardown; service header last. Separate stage/cache-index/component cursors retain the exact current root. Parent/child locks follow existing service->manager order; Cleanup must not call a public service method recursively while holding its mutex. A late initialization error never calls Close and discards its result. Store both original and cleanup cause in the existing service, retaining its manager and partially initialized components.
>
> ## Physical initialized-header and span map
>
> | Source operation | Actual write/action order |
> | --- | --- |
> | mpz.h:124 allocate | actual object allocation, capacity store ONLY; no size/digit initialization |
> | h132 allocate_if_needed | small sign1 before allocation; growing old free before sign1/new allocation; capacity repeated only at its source statement |
> | h156 ensure_tmp | old free; then uint32 `(3*needed+1)>>1`; allocate/capacity only; actual endangered span guard after allocation |
> | cpp165/207 set_big_i64/ui64 | allocate/pointer publication if needed; sign; low AND high32 digit stores even when high0; size last |
> | cpp247 set scratch | inspect actual requested scratch digits; sign/ref swap; result size after swap; missing scratch allocation after result publication |
> | cpp306 limb set | trim input; sign; optional oldfree/allocate; size and capacity source stores before logical digit copy |
> | cpp1185 big_set | self early return; sign; optional oldfree/allocate; size/capacity stores, then logical digits copy |
> | cpp1555 ensure_capacity | new allocation while old live for big; new size before digit copy; oldfree then pointer publication; distinct from big_set |
> | cpp1596 normalize | scans existing size/digits; reset-small cleanup or final new size after scan |
> | cpp1630 div2k | digit shift first; new size; normalize |
> | cpp1700 mul2k | ensure_capacity; zero-fill new digit range BEFORE publishing new size; shift/copy; normalize |
> | cpp1472 power-of-two fast path | allocate_if_needed; size BEFORE zero-fill/final digit; sign last |
> | add/sub/mul/div scratch | capacity preparation/ephemeral span only; no physical scratch size store until source result-transfer statement |
>
> `prepareTmpSpan` and current resizeCell cannot simply become physical size writers. Separate ephemeral digit span extent from actual published header. Scratch access checks ObjectExtent and actual initialized words at that action, not an uninitialized size header. Every current store/resize/publishTmpAt caller must be mapped before backend changes; do not globally preflight or repair missing scratch. No setter synthesis of zeros to make undefined source scratch fields readable.
>
> ## Full Natural topology included, not deferred behind optional cells
>
> Four embedded source sbuffer<uint32,16> fields expand with source uint32 doubled capacity. Each actual raw allocation succeeds before copy of POS initialized words, old overflow deallocation, and new pointer/capacity publication. Old/new raw backing and bitmap/cold metadata peaks are charged honestly. Retained pending new and completed oldfree phases require scalar per-buffer root state on a failure. Reset retains capacity; finalization frees overflow in reverse field order and returns to inline16.
>
> mpn.cpp:308 div_n resizes ms(n+1) first; writes quotient q_hat, then if borrow decrements quotient and resizes ab(n+2) at THAT branch. Remove current universal preprepared ab: no-addback paths do not allocate it. Late ab failure preserves prior numerator subtraction/quotient decrement. Existing single AlgorithmD and direct paired quotient/remainder publication are retained, not restaged.
>

> # Remaining MPZ/MPQ publication and diagnostic audit
>
> Read-only proposal, 2026-10-03. This document is the only file written in this audit. The parent-owned selected source-publication packet and its seven dependent test corrections remain frozen. No production change, source assertion port, or new GREEN claim is made here. The audited profile is `_MP_INTERNAL`, 32-bit limbs, selected Lehmer GCD, both source SYNCH settings. GMP, 64-bit digit branches, TRACE and persistent C++ stream state remain separate obligations.
>
> ## Evidence and current boundaries
>
> Authoritative bodies read: `src/util/mpz.h/.cpp`, `src/util/mpq.h/.cpp`, current `mpnum/mpz.go`, `mpz_slab.go`, arithmetic/division/number-theory/bitwise/power/shift/root/parser/inspection files, rational arithmetic/mixed-operation/root/rounding/parser/number-theory/inspection files, and `mp_copy.go`. Source allocation topology was checked against `small_object_allocator.h/.cpp`. Source tests were searched in `src/test/mpz.cpp` and `src/test/mpq.cpp`; direct source assertions are not interchangeable with independent arithmetic properties or injected-failure expectations.
>
> The completed core now frees undersized temporary cells before replacement allocation; publishes transferred result cells before replacement scratch allocation; preserves sequential paired quotient/remainder output publication; publishes big-copy sign before destination free/allocation; preserves direct Div/Mod caller-output actions and divisor alias rereads. Missing scratch is guarded at its actual subsequent use. One charged, permanently retired failed allocation token per owner represents otherwise dangling replacement state. It is not a live numeral, a C++ cell or a source malloc event. Cleanup may clear that exact owner token; ordinary reads still reject it. These are explicit Go ownership continuations, not source exception recovery.
>
> The current `normalizeOwned` in `mpz_power_shift.go:83` implements `mpz.cpp:1597` normalization: scan leading zero limbs, Reset on all-zero, Del then signed inline publication when the sole limb fits INT_MAX, otherwise adjust size. Older prose saying standalone normalization is unimplemented is stale. This helper is already called by shift algorithms. It is not a missing arithmetic algorithm.
>
> ### Scalar setters and capacity helpers
>
> | Source action | Current Go route | Assessment / next evidence |
> |---|---|---|
> | `mpz.h:199 set_i64`, inline branch Del then inline value | `SetInt64` | Correct ordinary action order; no replacement allocation in inline branch. |
> | `mpz.cpp:165 set_big_i64`, allocate only when small, capacity assertion, sign, low/high digits, size | `setBig64` | Allocation precedes sign, as source. Existing sufficiently large cell reused. Go publishes scalar ref/sign after infallible indexed writes; no present allocation-failure distinction after allocate. Source capacity assertion is not reproduced at its exact site. Test ref/retained-capacity and both sign transitions rather than inventing sign-on-OOM debt. |
> | `mpz.cpp:215 set_big_ui64` | `setBig64` through `SetUint64` | Same conclusion. Source unsigned inline threshold is strict `< INT_MAX`, already preserved. Distinguish public SetUint32 threshold from uint64 route. |
> | signed `-v` when v is INT64_MIN | unsigned-magnitude expression in SetInt64 | Defined Go magnitude adapter for source signed-negation UB. Do not label that input universally defined C++ arithmetic. |
> | `mpz.h:132 allocate_if_needed` | Power base-two currently calls `ensureOwnedCapacity` | **Missing exact helper.** Source promotes small by publishing val=1 before allocate; insufficient big capacity frees old before val=1/allocation. No content copy. Current preserving replacement stages allocation/copies and frees old last. Successful result agrees after Power overwrites all limbs; failure prefix and physical peak differ. |
> | `mpz.cpp:1556 ensure_capacity` | `ensureOwnedCapacity` | Existing helper corresponds to preserving expansion, not allocate_if_needed. Big expansion allocates/copies before free, matching source. Small allocation-before-sign is correct. Exact source debug equality assertions remain absent. |
> | `mpz.cpp:1597 normalize` | `normalizeOwned` | Present. Needs direct source-route fixtures, not a duplicate implementation. |
>
> Public API proposal retains `SetInt64`, `SetUint64`, SetInt32/SetUint32 and existing scalar layouts. Add private concrete `allocateIfNeeded(a *Int, capacity uint32) error`; keep `ensureOwnedCapacity` distinct. Add private build-selected exact-site assertions using existing typed numeric invariant category or an explicitly agreed new category. No new numeral namespace, generics, escaped slices, or foreign-owner raw handles.
>
> `SetLimbs` and same-owner Copy are already direct source publication routes. Integer `CopyFrom` deliberately remains a cross-owner adapter: it allocates replacement before freeing the old destination; rational `CopyFrom` stages both fields. C++ same/global-owner set has no cross-owner API. Do not conflate that explicit bridge policy with a same-owner setter defect; same-owner CopyFrom forwards to actual Copy.

> # Selected integer/rational number-theory port
>
> Ownership: `mpnum/mpz_number_theory.go`, `mpnum/mpq_number_theory.go`,
> `mpnum/mp_number_theory_test.go`, and this status. Concrete APIs only; no Go
> generics, production `math/big`, unsafe storage, or global numeric manager.
>
> ## Source-method inventory
>
> | Source | Go counterpart | Coverage |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | `mpz.cpp:845` active array `gcd` | `IntegerManager.GCDMany` | Active sequential algorithm, empty/singleton, early one, destination/future-element aliases |
> | `mpz.cpp:915` extended `gcd` | `IntegerManager.ExtendedGCD` | Selected release algorithm, exact quotient/coefficient action order, input-sign rereads, final result copy, six-local destruction |
> | `mpz.cpp:985` `lcm` | `IntegerManager.LCM` | All signed shortcuts and division/product branch; destination/input aliases |
> | `mpz.cpp:2054` `divides` | `IntegerManager.Divides` | Zero branch (`0` divides `0`), scoped remainder branch |
> | `mpq.h:601` rational pair `gcd` | `RationalManager.GCD` | Integer inputs, numerator operation then denominator reset |
> | `mpq.cpp:102` rational array `gcd` | `RationalManager.GCDMany` | Sequential branches; fractional singleton is allowed; future operands skipped after one |
> | `mpq.h:609` rational extended `gcd` | `RationalManager.ExtendedGCD` | Output denominators reset before integer algorithm; selected release algorithm |
> | `mpq.h:619` rational `lcm` | `RationalManager.LCM` | Integer inputs, numerator operation then denominator reset |
> | `mpq.h:627` rational `divides` | `RationalManager.Divides` | Integer-input validation and integer delegation |
>
> The integer-valued `mpz` forwarding overloads in `mpq.h` are represented by the
> concrete IntegerManager API, not duplicate methods with ambiguous operand types.
> Previously ported pair integer GCD remains the implementation used by array GCD
> and LCM; this packet does not replace its algorithm.
>
> ## Source actions and adaptation
>
> Array lengths are bounded by source uint32 widths. Only visited array elements
> are validated: array output may overwrite a future element, and an early result
> of one avoids inspecting remaining operands. Rational singleton GCD copies and
> takes the absolute value without imposing pair-GCD's integer precondition.
>
> Extended GCD publishes each source coefficient action directly. Output/output
> and input/output aliases retain source release behavior, including surprising
> coefficient results when a modified input sign is reread. Failure preserves
> already published output prefixes; it does not impose a transaction around the
> whole algorithm. Rational extended GCD resets all three output denominators
> before allocating integer locals. The six integer locals are always deleted,
> including on budget failure. LCM and Divides similarly clean their scoped local.
> Numeric cells and Words payloads use the existing owner budget. Both rational
> scratch policies are tested; no extra cached manager fields were introduced.
>
> Source integer precondition assertions become `ErrRationalNotInteger`; stale
> handles use existing manager guards. Raw records require genuine caller-supplied
> owners; matching foreign slots/generations are not intrinsically detected. Signed LCM
> shortcuts are intentionally preserved: for example LCM(-6,-6) is -6 and
> LCM(-6,-3) is 6. Source debug tracing is not implemented.
>
> ## Tests and remaining conditional coverage
>
> Tests were written first; the initial RED was missing all nine selected APIs.
> Nine test groups cover the active `rational.cpp` tst1 gcd(12,8)=4 assertion and all
> nine tst6 signed calls (which have no source assertions), strengthened by fixed
> coefficients and independent `math/big` checks. The tst7 loop over 1..999 supplies
> the same odd modular-inverse property to the manager implementation (500
> assertion executions across999 cases). Source tst7
> uses the separate `ext_gcd.h` wrapper algorithm: that wrapper remains unported,
> so this property test does not claim its algorithm or wrapper API is ported.
> The commented-out registration of mpz's long `tst_gcd` run and the disabled
> `#if 0` sorted-array GCD optimization are not claimed as active coverage.
>
> Independent finite oracles check 1,925 signed pairs, signed LCM fixtures, zero
> cases, array ordering, fractional singleton/skipped-tail behavior, fixed release
> alias coefficients, large scaled coefficients, and Fibonacci coefficients.
> Injected allocation prefixes are exercised through first success for rational
> extended GCD, LCM, Divides, array GCD, and pair GCD. Immediately after each
> failure, before formatting, deletion, or Close, an independent live-root audit
> checks numeric cells and Words references, allowing only published caller roots
> and actual manager-owned scratch. Budget refunds after Close are checked too.
>
> **Conditional coverage update:** `mpz.cpp` Extended GCD's `#ifdef Z3DEBUG`
> mul/mul/add/equality sequence is now selected by the separate `g3debug` build
> tag. `g3checked` still selects Go handle validation independently. The diagnostic
> reuses the actual coefficient locals and rereads modified input aliases before
> the final gcd assignment; a failed source assertion becomes a classified error
> with source output prefixes intact. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-extended-gcd-debug-port-status-md.
> No blanket alias restriction suppresses finite release cases. The separate
> ext_gcd.h wrapper has also since been translated; see PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-ext-gcd-wrapper-port-status-md.

> # Explicit numerical owner copying
>
> GO_PORT_PLAN.md B12 requires rational values moving between owners to be copied
> into the destination manager. Source rational.h/.cpp uses one global manager,
> so this is an explicit ownership adaptation, not a new source arithmetic method
> or a claim that AST translation is implemented.
>
> `mp_copy.go` adds concrete IntegerManager.CopyFrom and RationalManager.CopyFrom.
> Same-owner calls delegate to the existing source Copy implementation. A different
> source manager supplies indexed live digits; they never become an escaping slice,
> decimal string, hidden buffer, shared cell or foreign destination handle.
> Integer copy retains source sign, small/big tag, live size, source capacity on
> allocation and existing destination capacity when it can be reused, following
> mpz.h set and mpz.cpp big_set. Fallible preparation precedes destination writes.
>
> Rational copy stages numerator and denominator in destination-owned cells, then
> moves the complete pair. It does not normalize: unreduced2/4, negative denominators,
> zero numerators with nonunit denominator and big representations remain intact.
> Partial pair allocation is cleaned in lexical component order; failed publication
> preserves the entire destination. All physical old/new cells and Words are charged
> by the existing numerical service. Completed destination copies outlive source
> reset/deletion/Close independently. No new owning manager header or cache is added.
>
> These are low-level raw-manager APIs. Raw Int/Rational records do not contain
> provenance; callers must supply the genuine owner of each record, as required by
> existing manager operations. They cannot detect all foreign records whose
> owner-local slots/generations happen to coincide. The separately implemented
> rational service validates scalar provenance before invoking this bridge.
> Nil managers receive ErrConfig; nil numerals and closed owners use existing typed
> guards. One identical raw address across distinct managers receives ErrConfig
> because a single owning record cannot belong to both domains. Same-owner identity
> remains the existing checked no-op. No public foreign-handle safety is falsely
> claimed from low-level slot checks alone.
>
> Five tests first produced missing-CopyFrom API RED in an isolated committed module.
> GREEN tests verify source storage shape, reused allocation under FailAfter0,
> independent seeded exact values after source Close, raw rational representations
> in both manager modes, and warm zero-allocation copies. Failure sweeps occupy
> actual free cell slots, then advance every reservation prefix through success
> for small/big integer/rational outputs. Before rendering or cleanup, each failure
> requires exact destination live-cell/Words baselines, unchanged destination raw
> identity and unchanged source raw identity/cells/Words/budget. No Close call can
> mask leaked temporary ownership. Final whole-owner budgets return to zero.
>
> The isolated module passes full native tests, actual checked JS execution of all
> five new names, checked vet and WASI cross-build. Full checked-race module tests passed; the added big-rational warm-copy fixture
> also passed fresh targeted checked-race tests. WASI remains
> compilation evidence only. No Go generics, unsafe, boxed numeral records, production
> math/big arithmetic or additional storage service is introduced. Rational wrapper,
> AST parameters and AST translation remain separate incomplete units.
