> # Numeric display packet
>
> ## Source coverage
>
> The complete selected `_MP_INTERNAL` printing branches were read and translated:
> `mpz_manager::display_smt2(mpz,bool)` maps to IntegerManager
> `FormatSMT2Into` / `SMT2String`; `mpq_manager::display_smt2(mpq,bool)`
> maps to the rational counterparts; `mpq_manager::display_decimal` maps to
> `FormatDecimalInto` / `DecimalString`. The thin `to_rational_string(mpq)`
> and `display_pp(mpq)` wrappers map to `ToRationalString` and
> `FormatPrettyInto`. Existing Integer/Rational `String` / `FormatInto` already
> cover ordinary `to_string` / `display`; the inherited integer overloads are
> available through the rational owner's existing `Integers()` service. There
> is no public global-manager rational wrapper, ostream interface, alternate
> backend, locale/format flag support, or TRACE diagnostic port in this packet.
>
> Integer SMT2 retains the source negative-only Copy/Neg scoped temporary and
> `(- magnitude)` form, including `.0` inside the expression when requested.
> Fractional SMT2 retains `(/ numerator denominator)`, with each operand printed
> using the integer branch. Integral rationals retain the integer representation.
> Decimal printing retains the exact source Copy/Copy, sign/Neg,
> Div/display/Rem, and repeated Mul-by-ten/Div/display/Rem order, with cleanup
> in the source ten/numerator/denominator/digit order. The source development
> assertion tests only that each emitted quotient is below ten; it does not
> require a nonnegative digit. Initialized source RatDiv/Root outputs can have
> negative denominators or remain unreduced. These are accepted and printed
> without normalization: raw 1/-3 produces `0.-3-3-3?` at precision three,
> raw -1/-3 produces `-0.-3-3-3?`, and -1/-1 produces `--1`. SMT2 exposes
> the signed denominator. Unreduced 2/4 remains `(/ 2 4)` in SMT2 and prints
> `0.5` as a decimal. These source-action quirks are explicitly frozen separately
> from the independent mathematical decimal tests for positive denominators. No rounding, zero padding, or blanket
> precision limit is added. A noninteger with precision zero prints the decimal
> point and optionally `?`; exact values terminate immediately, including
> terminating values at UINT_MAX precision. Negative subunit values print `-0`.
>
> ## Ownership and publication
>
> Only the three files in this packet are changed; no existing formatter or
> owner-header edits are required. Static punctuation is copied by scalar index
> into the existing budgeted byte workspace. Scoped numeric temporaries use the
> integer owner's concrete cells and Words, with explicit cleanup on every
> failure. All formatting limbs and bytes use the shared existing owner Budget.
> Workspace growth preserves previously prepared prefixes, including a negative
> fraction numerator while the denominator is formatted. Workspace reuse and
> retention follow the prior formatting storage adaptation; this does not claim
> the C++ stream allocation profile. Complete output is staged before publication,
> so short buffers and predictable allocation errors leave caller bytes untouched.
> This intentionally adapts source partial-stream-output failure behavior to the
> Go caller-buffer contract. Required output length excludes a C NUL; no extra
> byte is written. A String wrapper allocates one final caller-owned Go string;
> its escaped host lifetime is outside the numeric owner Budget, and no hidden
> intermediate string is used. Borrowed numeral inputs remain unchanged.
>
> ## Test evidence
>
> Tests were written first and observed RED because the printing APIs did not
> exist. Nine test functions are now GREEN. Source mpz/mpq/rational test files
> were read: the relevant active decimal output in `src/test/mpq.cpp::tst2`
> prints 1/3 and 1/4 at precision ten. Their exact expectations
> `0.3333333333?` and `0.25` are independently derived, not C++ observations or
> source assertions. No active SMT2 printing assertions occur in those tests.
> Added finite tests cover both manager modes, small and big signed SMT2 operands,
> all numerators -19..19 and denominators 1..19 at precision 0/1/2/3/10 with both
> truncate choices, a test-only big.Rat oracle, integer/terminating/nonterminating
> branches, raw-zero and closed-owner diagnostics, exact caller length/no NUL,
> short buffers, and escaped output lifetime.
>
> Fault sweeps reach both an actual failure and eventual successful completion
> for every operation, both manager modes, and cold/warm formatter states. Each
> prefix checks input identity and unmodified caller output, numeric-cell Live
> immediately before any subsequent formatting or teardown, and Words Live
> accounting for legitimate newly retained formatting refs; Close returns the
> shared Budget to zero. Additional tests cover old-plus-new byte reservation
> refusal, bounded-budget refusal of a UINT_MAX-precision repeating decimal,
> workspace replacement/prefix preservation, zero-allocation warm caller-buffer
> printing, and exactly one allocation for final host strings.
>
> Validation: isolated HEAD:golang plus only these three files passed full native
> and actual g3checked module tests. All nine new tests were registered and passed under actual g3checked JS/wasm
> execution (the initial eight together, then the added noncanonical fixture).
> Checked targeted race/vet and checked WASI cross-build passed. The final
> UINT_MAX precision-bound fixture and added noncanonical source-action fixture
> also passed their affected checked race and actual checked JS reruns. The final

> # Parameters reference and backing owner
>
> Source: all `params_ref` methods in `src/util/params.h/.cpp` and all private
> `params` methods/macros in `params.cpp`, 32-bit unsigned/signed casts. The
> parameter-descriptor implementation is an existing dependency, not duplicated
> or modified by this packet. Normalization remains in `util_param_name.go`.
>
> ## Source method coverage
>
> `ParamsContext.NewValue` supplies the source default/null reference;
> `NewValue` followed by `Assign` supplies its copy constructor. `Assign` performs
> increment-new before decrement-old, including self assignment. `Del` supplies
> reference destruction. `Copy` and `Append` implement sharing for a null
> backing and otherwise initialization followed by ordered-entry merge.
> `init`/`copyCore` preserve new-block publication before ordered detach copying.
> Self copy resolves the source after initialization and traverses actual entry
> identities, retaining rational self-assignment behavior.
>
> `Empty`, `Contains`/`ContainsName`, `Reset`, and
> `ResetKey`/`ResetKeyName` cover every source query/reset overload. Reset and
> validation intentionally never detach shared backing. Six getter groups
> (`GetBool`, `GetUInt`, `GetDouble`, `GetString`, `GetRat`, `GetSymbol`) each
> have Symbol and nullable Name overloads; the five source fallback getter
> families have `Get*FallbackName` overloads. First key **and kind** wins;
> wrong-kind entries do not block later duplicates or fallback. Rational getters
> accept unsigned entries with the source signed-int32 conversion. Returned
> rationals are independent owned copies, including defaults.
>
> Six setter groups (`SetBool`, `SetUInt`, `SetDouble`, `SetString`, `SetRat`,
> `SetSymbol`) each have Symbol and nullable Name overloads. Source initializer
> runs before Name key construction. Existing numeral assignments retain their
> token; replacing another kind publishes the numeral tag and default initialized
> value before assignment. New numerals are initialized and copied before vector
> publication. Numerical symbol values violate source `bare_str`'s precondition
> and receive a typed checked guard before graph mutation; numerical keys remain
> valid. Null symbol values remain valid and display as `null`.
>
> `Validate` applies descriptor module rewriting directly to stored keys, then
> checks source kind rules. Earlier mutations and duplicate keys survive a later
> error. Messages are exact `DefaultException` text, including sorted descriptor
> names transformed only after sorting, defaults whenever present, and descriptor
> nonnull-description preconditions even when descriptions are not printed.
> Validation holds the descriptor owner lock throughout and reads its existing
> payloads directly; it creates no intermediate descriptor-output string.
>
> `Display`, `DisplayKey`/`DisplayKeyName`, `DisplaySMT2` and their caller-buffer
> `FormatInto`/`FormatKeyInto`/`FormatSMT2Into` adapters cover source ostream
> branches. DisplayKeyName interns a temporary symbol even for null backing,
> unlike read getter/contains/reset paths. `DebugString` is the source Z3DEBUG
> `pp` text boundary including its newline, available as an explicit diagnostic
> adapter instead of a process-wide stream side effect.
>
> ## Ownership and storage adaptations
>
> Symbols and numerals borrow explicitly supplied services that must outlive the
> context. Their actual budget can differ from this context's budget. Neither
> borrowed header nor numeral storage is charged fictitiously to context storage.
> All ParamsRef, backing blocks, entry payloads, text refs, and entry allocation
> metadata are pointer-free. No generics, unsafe, raw exported manager borrows,
> per-object slices, or per-entry interface values are used.
>
> A single cold context header owns the concrete block registry, typed pooled
> entry pages, their metadata/directory, Words text pool, and formatting workspace.
> Each actual array and owner is charged exactly, including old/new growth peaks.
> Requested source svector capacity is 2 then `(3n+1)/2`; physical entry blocks
> use geometric classes. Free physical pages remain context-owned until Close;
> Reset frees the logical vector allocation and capacity. This is an allocator
> adaptation, not a claim of identical source allocation timing. Generation and
> reference-count overflow refuse before wrap. NewValue has no backing allocation.
> Raw zero ParamsRef is invalid; the explicit constructor creates an owned null
> token. Shallow token copying is forbidden; Assign is the owning copy operation.
>
> Rational entries retain actual scalar OwnedRational tokens inline rather than
> source separately heap-allocated rational objects. The actual entry width and
> numerical service storage are accounted; no imaginary rational heap-node charge
> is added. Growth transfers tokens and invalidates old slots after publication;
> ResetKey shifts ownership and clears the vacated tail without a second Del.
> Unpublished new values are destroyed on allocation failure. A detach failure
> retains its published partial new block but decrements the old reference even
> on error; source exceptions would skip that decrement and leak. Existing
> RationalService staged allocation semantics are inherited and explicit.
>
> Borrowed source C-string values become owned immutable first-NUL text, preserving
> null versus present-empty. Owned-text replacement prepares its allocation before
> removing the old value, an extra predictable failure adaptation. Symbol values
> remain borrowed scalar symbols. Name reads use `SymbolManager.EqualString` and
> never eager interning. Provenance guards precede source graph actions.
>
> Formatting uses budgeted retained byte storage and stack-bounded numeric
> conversion (`g`, precision 6, classic decimal/scientific spelling, signed zero,
> inf/nan). Locale and custom ostream flags are not emulated. A final Go string
> is caller-owned escaped output; its lifetime is not falsely arena-accounted.
> Caller buffers exclude NUL and stay unchanged on short buffer or error.
> For null **C-string** stream insertion, this adapter models the locally audited
> libstdc++ badbit behavior: Display returns the defined prefix together with
> `ErrParamsStreamFailure`, suppressing subsequent text; FormatInto leaves the
> caller buffer unchanged. libc++ can instead dereference null through
> char_traits::length: this is an explicit libstdc++-mode/Go adaptation, not a
> universal source-language claim. A null module fails only when a matching entry
> actually attempts insertion. Null SYMBOL rendering is a different valid case.
>
> The source process-global `g_empty_params_ref` becomes explicit owner-local null
> values; no process-global symbol/numerical owner is introduced. Cross-context
> ParamsRef sharing is rejected. This utility packet does not claim AST or solver
> consumer behavior is implemented.
>
> ## Tests and verification
>
> No standalone params test or registration exists in `src/test`. Existing solver
> setups using params_ref do not supply isolated params assertions and are not
> counted as ported unit assertions. Eighteen permanent finite tests derive exact
> source action traces and independent scalar/cast expectations: sharing and
> reset, ordered copy/append, duplicate validation prefixes, all getter/setter and
> fallback families, exact messages/displays, nullable inputs, read noninterning,
> capacity progression, generation/provenance, host C-prefix length narrowing,
> self-copy identity, cold headers,
> whole-context accounting, old/new peaks, and warm zero allocations.
>
> Initial observed RED was missing ParamsContext/NewParamsContext/ParamsConfig.
> A later meaningful self-copy RED exposed loss of source entry identity; fixed
> by traversing actual entries and resolving self source after init. Eight
> reservation-prefix operation sweeps continue until success, exercise real cold
> or wide storage growth, and audit live numeric cells, Words text, reference
> roots, and unused entry ownership **before** rendering or teardown. Constructor
> reservation prefixes unwind to the borrowed-owner baseline; every final graph
> Close returns budget usage to zero.
>
> Verification passed on frozen eighteen-test bytes: full native and actual
> checked modules, targeted checked
> race registrations, actual checked-JS eighteen RUN/PASS registrations, vet,
> WASI build and no-generics audit. Parent integration independently passed full
> native, full checked-debug, targeted checked-debug race, vet, WASI build and
> actual checked-debug JS for all eighteen registrations. The Go files matched
> snapshot hashes after these gates. Source inventory/ledger checked separately.

> ## Ownership, failure, and storage adaptations
>
> One SymbolManager is borrowed; it must outlive descriptor owners and must not
> be torn down concurrently with operations. Foreign/marked symbols, numerical
> insertion, duplicate-kind mismatch, missing-null split/display, null description
> display, and invalid index receive typed errors rather than source assertion or
> undefined pointer operations. Numerical query does not intern and returns absent.
> Null is a valid ordinary dictionary key with exact hash **0x9e3779d9**.
> A cold self-identity check rejects shallow-copied owners. Cold mutexes serialize
> an owner; Copy serializes multiowner locking with one cold global mutex. Borrowed
> Budget/callback environments remain external and caller-serialized if shared.
>
> Source info borrows immutable C pointers. The Go ownership adapter copies each
> nonnull C string (through its first NUL) into private arena.Words packed words.
> Nil is absent; empty is a live one-word NUL payload. Entry/name records contain
> only scalar Symbols, cached hash/state, kind, and Words refs/lengths. Metadata is
> recycled on erase; inactive bucket scalar payload is retained like the source.
> Copy directly reads source Words and writes destination Words, without loaded
> intermediate strings. Each destination payload is charged while source payload
> remains live; destination survives source Close while both still borrow the same
> symbol manager. Caller-returned text copies survive erase/close.
>
> Table/header, names capacities, Words owner/descriptors/pages/metadata/directories
> are charged exactly once. New array reserve precedes allocate/copy; old array
> charges release only after publication. Constructor failure unwinds nested
> owners and all earlier charges. Nil Budget permits unlimited storage; explicit
> Text.Descriptors.Budget must equal the owner Budget (or default to it).
> Default table capacity8; configurable power of two. Default text page256 words,
> descriptor page2 are storage adaptations, not source container capacities.
> Source names capacity/history never shrink on erase/reinsert, intentionally;
> metadata page storage independently plateaus with scalar slot generations.
>
> **Source dictionary publication precedes names.push_back.** If names growth
> fails, the live dictionary entry and its metadata remain published while history
> length stays old. Retry duplicate returns and never appends that omitted history
> entry. Metadata adapter failures before dictionary publication release all newly
> live refs; retained Words/table capacities may remain. Copy retains completed
> insert prefixes, including this final published entry without history. Erase
> cleanup reservation failure keeps the completed erasure and old tombstones.
> OutOfMemory's cold diagnostic skips source cleanup when true.
>
> Display charges the actual temporary Symbol vector with source growth and old/new
> peaks; concrete in-place heapsort realizes the standard std::sort ordering/output
> contract without a reflection swapper or second work array. Comparator, name, and
> metadata output read checked bytes directly; only final output storage is
> caller-owned, like the source external ostream. KindInModule charges every
> actual prefix char vector growth (constructor loops push_back, then pushes NUL),
> and explicit Go byte-array/string bridges for suffix/module interning. Prefix
> scratch is destroyed after split returns, before suffix kind/module lookup.
> All such temporary charges release on every exit. Borrowed-manager successful
> intern prefixes persist if a later descriptor operation fails.
>

> # Concrete int32 persistent-array prerequisite
>
> `util_parray.go` translates `src/util/parray.h` for both registered int32
> configurations in `src/test/parray.cpp`. It uses the real ROOT/SET/PUSH_BACK/
> POP_BACK cells, root-preserving inverse trails, materialization and reroot
> algorithms. It does not replace persistence with copied Go slices. There are
> no Go generics, production maps, unsafe casts, boxed values or per-cell Go
> objects. Cells and value blocks use the borrowed `arena.SmallBytes` allocator.
>
> ## Exact source assertion and specialization inventory
>
> | Source test, each preserve-roots policy | ENSURE sites | Executions |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | tst1 | 15 | 15 |
> | tst2 | 4 | 213: two standalone assertions plus loops100 and111 |
> | tst3 | 14 | 128 |
> | both true and false policies | 66 instantiated sites | 712 |
>
> The source fixture ports every active ENSURE and all operations before/between/
> after them. Tst3's guarded Get calls preserve the actual short-circuit routes.
> The initial read-only arithmetic count710 was incorrect: tst2 is1+1+100+111=
> 213. The executable fixture independently counts712 assertions and is named
> `TestPArraySource712Assertions`; no assertion is removed to meet the earlier
> mistaken total.
>
> Both int32 policies suppress value callbacks, preserve roots true/false,
> max-trail8 and factor2. CELL reference counting still occurs in both policies.
> Actual AST expression and dependency arrays use real retain/release callbacks,
> preserve-roots true, max-trail16 and factor2. Subpaving bound arrays suppress
> value callbacks but use preserve-roots true/max-trail16/factor2. All these
> non-int32 specializations remain unported; no fake callback service stands in
> for them.
>
> Registered parray tst5 has zero ENSURE sites but genuine AST initialization,
> 100 distinct variables, Copy, exactly1,000,000 Set updates, two process memory
> high-water prints and explicit Del. It remains OPEN until the actual AST manager,
> expression callbacks and resource/output adaptation exist. Integer plateau
> checks do not claim that source integration route. Disabled `#if0` tst4,
> commented tst4 registration, trace enabling, allocation diagnostics and its old
> AST max-trail8 configuration remain distinguished from current AST code.
> Registered ast.cpp tst5's seven persistent-expression assertions likewise remain
> pending the real AST owner.
>
> ## Source method map
>
> | Source method/action | Concrete counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | constructor; borrowed value manager/allocator | `NewInt32PArrayManager`, no int32 value callbacks; explicit allocator borrow |
> | public `manager()` returning dummy_value_manager<int>& | explicit Go configuration adapter: int32 callback suppression is fixed by the concrete type; no shared mutable dummy-manager object/accessor is exported |
> | private cell ctor/mk/del/inc/dec | encoded RC/kind cells, `mkCell`/`freeCell`/`inc`/`dec`; iterative source chain deletion |
> | capacity/allocate_values/deallocate_values/expand | source-width capacity header; full encoded int32 capacity; exact0→2→3→5→8... growth |
> | root rset/rpush_back/rpop_back | Set/Push/Pop root branches; retained popped slots; value callbacks suppressed |
> | copy_values/get_values | `getValues` root prefix copy at same capacity, source forward replay, retained path scratch |
> | ref default/root/unshared | zero `Int32PArrayRef`; checked private cell kind/RC |
> | mk/del/copy | `Mk`/`Del`/`Copy`; explicit manual token ownership |
> | size/empty/get | `Size`/`Empty`/mutable-pointer `Get`, strict trail threshold |
> | set and source-output overload | `Set`/`SetFrom` |
> | push_back and source-output overload | `PushBack`/`PushBackFrom` |
> | pop_back and source-output overload | `PopBack`/`PopBackFrom` |
> | unshare/unfold/reroot | `Unshare`/`Unfold`/`Reroot`, including finite source PUSH inverse defect |
> | display_info | `DisplayInfo`, scalar identity display adapter and charged lexical formatter |
> | manager destructor implicit scratch cleanup | `Close` owner/scratch refund with explicit no-live-cell contract |
>
> Source shallow ref copies do not retain; ordinary Go record copies are borrowed
> aliases. Use Copy/Del to acquire/release ownership. Source has no whole-manager
> Clone/Swap/Reset/Finalize API. `Stats` and typed errors are Go ownership adapters.
> The source public dummy-manager accessor is adapted away, rather than claimed
> as an implemented mutable callback object. Its int32 inc/dec methods do nothing
> and C::ref_count=false suppresses their use; the concrete configuration retains
> that behavior. No real AST array/value-manager behavior is claimed by the int32
> implementation.
>
> ## Storage, lifetime and physical budget
>
> The cold manager owns its actual reflected header and two retained scalar
> scratch vectors; scratch grows by source vector2→3→5... with old/new overlap
> charged. Its allocator is borrowed, must outlive the manager, and must use the
> same Budget. This is an explicit caller contract because the existing allocator
> has no public Budget identity accessor; no shared API was altered to add one.
>
> Each cell has a fixed explicit24-byte encoding: packed lower30-bit RC/upper2-bit
> kind at0, idx/size at4, int32 element at8, padding at12, scalar link descriptor
> slot/generation at16/20. The descriptor represents a cell link or ROOT value
> block according to kind. No hot pointer is stored. Public references also carry
> scalar manager identity and a per-reference update counter. The counter is not
> shared in the cell. Reshaping roots/trails retains their descriptor generations;
> there is no global epoch invalidation of persistent versions.
>
> The value block begins with target-pointer-width size_t capacity metadata,
> followed by the WHOLE int32 capacity. Logical ROOT size is separate. This
> capacity header is genuinely allocated even when capacity0 during copying an
> empty shared root. Source expand copies every old capacity element and performs
> no value callbacks; root copy allocates the same capacity but copies only the
> logical prefix. Unused newly allocated storage is not exposed as initialized
> source data. Numeric byte encoding is explicit little-endian; these blocks are
> not a reinterpretation of C++ raw memory.
>
> Actual cell bytes, descriptor records/generations/free metadata, value header+
> payload, pool chunks/direct blocks/directories, manager header and scratch
> capacities are charged by their real owners. Source C++ cell pointer layout
> is not claimed equal to the fixed checked encoding. Source large size_t arrays
> beyond the allocator's uint32 byte domain return typed ErrBounds before
> allocation. Tests inspect complete Budget sums using allocator owner, payload,
> metadata and directory bytes, avoiding double-counting DirectBytes (already
> included in PayloadBytes).
>
> Close requires zero live cells and returns ErrPArrayLive without changing owner
> state otherwise. It never closes the borrowed allocator. After explicit Del,
> Close refunds only the manager header/scratch. Pool cleanup remains with the
> allocator owner. Null cells are source-safe no-ops; null refs have size0 and are
> empty; Push initializes them. Invalid null Get/Set/Pop/Unshare/Unfold/Reroot and
> foreign/stale references receive typed adapters for source invalid accesses.
>
> ## Source actions and known finite defect
>
> All cells start RC1. Increment wraps to30bits without destroying on zero;
> dec-zero returns the source-assertion error adapter. Normal deletion processes
> SET/PUSH's stored value (suppressed for int32), ROOT logical values ascending
> (suppressed) and its block, then deallocates the cell, decrements next RC and
> continues only on zero. Future real callback specializations remain required.
>
> Copy retains source before releasing target and resets that caller's update
> counter, including self-Copy. From overloads detect src==out and directly
> mutate, skipping Copy. Get takes a pointer because it can reroot and reset that
> particular reference. Both trail and root update thresholds use strict greater
> than, not greater-or-equal.
>
> Shared root mutation increments its caller update counter before allocating
> its new root. The old block transfers without copying into a new root RC2;
> the older root becomes the inverse operation; its former caller reference is
> released; the caller is published to the new root before the final requested
> Set/Push/Pop action. Nonroot and non-preserving shared-root updates create
> forward trail cells and transfer the existing reference into next without an
> extra retain/release. Materialization replays oldest-to-newest; Unfold releases
> old next before becoming ROOT; Unshare creates a new root and releases the
> old reference. Reroot reverses the collected trail with actual source RC
> publication/destruction order, including reading updated predecessor RC after
> former-root destruction.
>
> **Source finite defect preserved:** Reroot's PUSH_BACK reversal sets old-root
> kind=POP_BACK and idx=sz BEFORE incrementing sz, although Size(POP) returns
> idx-1. An older mathematical size1 becomes source size0; an older size2 becomes
> source size1. Exact fixtures cover forward PUSH with preserve-roots false and
> reverse PUSH produced by Pop with preserve-roots true. These regressions
> explicitly state mathematical versus actual source sizes. The implementation
> does not silently repair this source defect.
>
> The independent mathematical version-array oracle uses materialization before
> inspection to avoid this defective PUSH reroot route. Separate unaffected SET
> reroot fixtures run both policies, POP reroot is checked independently, and
> all source registered Get/Reroot routes remain present. This does not exclude
> false-policy coverage or treat all reroot behavior as correct by assumption.
>
> ## Predictable failure prefixes and explicit unsafe-continuation adapters
>
> Defined prefixes are retained: update counter increments before cell allocation;
> From performs Copy before its operation; first Push can publish an empty ROOT
> before value allocation fails; shared Push can publish inverse trail/new ROOT
> before payload growth fails; scratch preserves successful physical growth
> prefixes. There is no fake whole-operation rollback guarantee.
>
> Two unsafe source exception continuations are explicitly adapted. Mk releases
> its prior reference before replacement allocation; Go clears the destroyed
> output, rather than leaving a dangling descriptor if allocation fails. PUSH
> reroot changes the former ROOT tag before expanding its full payload; source
> failure can leave its values pointer interpreted as a cell link. Go preflights
> that expansion and publishes the valid replacement block before destructive
> retagging. Successful logical source action order and finite inverse-index
> defect are retained. Unpublished int32 materialization cells/blocks receive
> explicit lexical failure cleanup; no source exception-safety guarantee is
> invented for these raw source temporaries.
>
> DisplayInfo uses slot/generation identity spelling instead of machine addresses.
> Its lexical bytes are budgeted with overlap on growth; only final caller output
> is an uncharged string. Predictable format failure returns the already emitted
> prefix and refunds the lexical buffer. Nil Go reference parameters are typed
> errors; source C++ reference parameters cannot represent that call shape.
>
> ## Tests and validation
>
> Fifteen groups cover all712 source assertions, independent bounded version
> oracles, both policies, source RC30 wrap, forward/inverse trail metadata,
> strict trail/update thresholds, retained popped slots, zero-capacity header,
> self-Copy versus self-From, foreign/stale/null refs, borrowed Close lifetime,
> known PUSH defect, unaffected SET/POP reroot, plateau/zero warm Go allocations,
> source publication prefixes, Mk clearing, formatter prefix and bounds. The
> formatter's checked helper tests exact MaxHostInt, addition and doubling overflow
> for32/64-bit hosts without huge allocations and imposes no uint32 output limit.
>
> Failure matrices independently compute reachable unique cells/ROOT blocks and
> expected cell RC from caller references plus graph edges. They compare these
> with live allocation counts and complete physical Budget sums BEFORE any
> Get/String/Del/Close cleanup can hide a temporary leak. Unshare/Unfold/Reroot
> and shared Push exercise all bounded allocation prefixes; both successful and
> failed shapes are checked. Initial isolated tests produced missing-API RED;
> source assertions and independent fixtures drove the implementation. Format
> prefix and nil-reference regressions separately produced behavioral RED then
> GREEN. The earlier arithmetic count correction is not an implementation RED.
>
> Final isolated HEAD `6c30500` plus only the two new Go files passed full
> CGO-disabled native and checked+debug suites, checked+debug targeted race,
> all fifteen named RUN/PASS groups on actual checked+debug JS/wasm,
> checked+debug vet, WASI build and the no-generics audit after the host-bounds
> correction. No WASI runtime
> execution is claimed. Automatic source SASSERT/TRACE diagnostic execution and
> machine-address rendering are distinguished from typed validation/output

>

> # Integer/C-string printf dependency packet
>

> ## Selected implementation and source mapping
>
> | Source | Concrete implementation |
> | --- | --- |
> | warning.cpp:106-113 local svector<char>/initial resize | PrintfFormatter.Format initial logical1024 for PrintfNonWindowsAMD64;128 for PrintfNonWindows32; per-call vector destroyed on every exit |
> | vector.h:60-105 expand_vector and422-435 resize | resize uses capacities2,(3old+1)/2, actual byte arrays and old/new budget peaks; logicalsize separate from physicalcapacity |
> | warning.cpp:114-121 BEGIN/VPRF/AMD64 END | pfRender explicit-argument C integer/string conversion domain; Go diagnostic Begin/Call/End instrumentation only |
> | warning.cpp:123-127 negative result fallback | malformed backend/trailing conversion and signed count overflow give negativecount; AMD64 returns raw first-NUL format after End |
> | warning.cpp:128-133 one-call truncation/ostream | bounded sink counts full output, stores at most logicalsize-1, emits first-NUL byte prefix; no UTF8 repair |
> | warning.cpp:135-142 other-platform retry | NonWindows32 retries at logicalsize2n+1, same source vector expansion; stable explicit argument replay is the Go va_list adapter |

>
> The formatter/default formatted constructor remain **partial**, not generic
> C-printf complete. The supported actual integer/string routes are available;
> warning globals/streams/prefix/flush/warning_displayer and command runtime remain
> separate units. No fake CLI or warning I/O service is introduced.
>
> ## Platform/domain classification
>
> Profiles are explicit and independent of the Go build host: NonWindowsAMD64 is
> Linux/glibc LP64 and C locale, NonWindows32 is ILP32 with the source128 grow loop
> and selected glibc C-locale conversion policy. Windows secure CRT invalid
> parameter installation, previous-handler restoration, and persistent
> _CrtSetReportMode state are **open**; config does not accept a Windows profile.
> Linux BEGIN_ERR_HANDLER/END_ERR_HANDLER are empty macros. Observe events are
> Go-only diagnostics, not claims of actual source callbacks/global CRT effects.
> Observe environment is borrowed, must not reenter owner methods or mutate args,
> and is not charged beyond the actual func field in the owner header.
>
> Supported conversions: d,i,u,o,x,X,s,c and plain %%. Integer flags -, +, space,
> #,0; literal/star widths and literal/star precisions, negative star width meaning
> left alignment, negative precision ignored. String precision counts bytes,
> C strings stop first NUL, char narrows to its byte and may insert NUL while full
> output count continues. hh/h narrow32-promoted values; default32; l/z/t use the
> profile32/64 width; ll/j use64. Explicit arg tags validate count/type domains;
> extra args are ignored. Signed/unsigned corresponding32 values are accepted
> only in representable default-width domains; narrowed hh/h use low bits.
> Unsigned64 values and signed64 values retain their separate tags. Numeric digit
> rendering uses a stack64-byte buffer, not host formatted intermediate strings.
>
> GNU I flag is a no-op alternative-digit selector in the fixed C locale.
> **%I64u means I flag + width64 + unsigned32 in the Linux profile**, not a
> Windows64-bit length. The actual datalog callsites pass uint64_t and have a C
> varargs type mismatch. PrintfUInt64 therefore receives ErrPrintfArgument; an
> explicit caller-chosen PrintfUInt32 conversion demonstrates the observed low32
> LinuxABI diagnostic without defining the original C undefined behavior.
> Those datalog consumers are not yet ported and no complete support is claimed
> for their original mismatched argument. The true Windows I64 length remains open.
> Nullable CString uses the selected glibc behavior: (null), but explicit precision
> 0..5 emits empty and6+ emits the full six-byte label. This is a defined Go/glibc
> profile adapter for source undefined null-%s behavior, not a portable C guarantee.
>
> Legitimate unsupported C domains (f/F/e/E/g/G/a/A, long double, wide lc/ls,
> positional arguments, locale grouping, GNU m, pointer p, count-write n) return
> ErrPrintfUnsupported, never fabricated negative-backend/raw-format fallback.
> Raw Go pointer exposure/count writes are not supported. A future safe p token
> and typed n target adapter needs its own semantics/lifetime/action tests.
> NonWindows32 persistent malformed/count errors receive typed finite failure;
> the source loop would otherwise retry forever. Backend malformed/count errors
> and unsupported/argument adapter failures have distinct diagnostic categories.
>
> ## Budget/lifetime and action prefixes
>
> PrintfFormatter reserves its actual reflect-size cold header at construction,
> self-guards shallow Go copies, and serializes calls with a cold mutex. Borrowed
> Budget is caller-serialized if shared outside this owner. Close releases header
> once; closed/foreign owner calls reject before allocations. Args/string pointers
> are borrowed stable for one synchronous call, never retained by the owner.
>
> Each call allocates the exact source byte-vector capacity sequence, reserves new
> array while old is charged, copies, then releases old. The byte workspace is also
> the bounded formatter output buffer and is fully charged. Final immutable ostream
> text transfers to the caller-owned output boundary, as with other display APIs;
> it is not a retained owner graph. All temporary buffers are destroyed on failure,
> normal return, or observer panic. The owner retains no warmed scratch cache.
> Source cap1065 for logical1024 has peak1775 payload bytes (710+1065); tests show
> owner+1774 fails and owner+1775 succeeds. Logical128 retains cap140, peak233.
>
> Initial growths complete before Begin. Call occurs once for AMD64 even on output
> truncation; End precedes normal/fallback output. NonWindows32 logical sizes are
> 128,257,515,1031,2063,... and capacities140,315,710,1065,2397,... as required.
> A growth failure after a completed Call retains observer prefix with no invented
> End event. Typed unsupported/argument errors are diagnostic Go adapter exits,
> not pretend backend failures. Formatting count is bounded signed32 independently
> of storage. Large padding/precision spans count in O(1) while only bounded bytes
> are written. Overflow includes escaped-percent additions and returns the source
> negative-count fallback on AMD64; no giant host strings or arrays are built.

> ## Exact publication, ownership and domain behavior
>
> Root/square wrappers pass actual output raw identity; they do not hide source
> alias bugs by copying inputs into a new wrapper result. Root's inexact numerator
> publishes while retaining the previous denominator; denominator results are not
> normalized. Integer square output aliases reset to zero; fractional square input
> aliases may attempt source undefined 0/0 normalization, represented by the existing

> -84 yields x=-2,y=3,g=12. Shared x/y gives2 after quotient steps 1,2,3. These are
> independently inferred source-action fixtures, not C++ executions or Bezout
> mathematical expectations for defective alias contexts. LCM's source signed
> shortcuts retain -6 for (-6,1)/(1,-6)/(-6,-6), and -12 for (-6,4)/(6,-4).
>
> All new bitwise wrappers retain actual integer source algorithm, operand copies,
> capacity choices, nonnegative-domain errors, unsigned width and inherited
> width 63 signed-mask adaptation. Rational integer preconditions remain strict;
> unreduced 2/2 is not silently accepted as an integer. Raw rational output numerator
> is computed before denominator reset, preserving aliases and failure publication.
>
> Every service input/scoped destination is validated before numeric action. Scoped
> owner identity/self/closed validation precedes explicit CopyFrom bridges; source
> and destination managers are supplied from the checked owner, not an unlabelled
> raw record. Scoped owners and their managers must remain externally confined for
> the whole call; the service mutex does not make foreign managers or shared Budgets
> concurrently safe. Existing low-level implicit numeric ownership contracts remain
> in force; deliberate misuse of a previously borrowed Scoped.Get raw record is not
> magically detected by coinciding cross-manager handle bits. These APIs return no
> new raw borrow. Independent copies preserve requested source capacity, sign,
> small/big shape, unreduced fractions and signed denominators; no parser or
> normalization stands in for a record copy. Every intermediate is lexical and
> budgeted through existing concrete managers. Named value returns transfer through
> Move. Self/constant projections and to_mpq use independent copies as the explicit
> Go replacement for source const references. Final Go strings belong to callers;
> caller buffers exclude NUL and remain untouched on short-buffer/budget failures.

> # Owner-local rational arithmetic/operator facade
>
> Source: `src/util/rational.h` (Copyright (c) 2006 Microsoft Corporation),
> selected wrapper methods over the synchronized manager. This is a concrete Go
> service adaptation; C++ operators are named methods and every owning value is
> an `OwnedRational` from one `RationalService`. No global numeric manager, foreign
> raw handles, generic Go code, unsafe access, or production `math/big` is added.
>
> ## Completed source routes in this packet
>
> - RR `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`: `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, with the source initial
>   lhs copy, in-place compound operation, and copy of the returned **lvalue** into
>   the value result. The final copy is not elided or replaced by a manager output
>   shortcut. Both int32 operand directions construct an actual rational(int).
> - RR `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`: corresponding `*Assign` methods; int32 `+=`
>   constructs the rational temporary. `AssignInt` likewise constructs then copies.
> - Fresh-result integer `div`, `machine_div`, `%`, `mod`, pair `gcd`; `IDivInto`
>   and `ModInto` retain direct raw output identity, including source alias defects.
> - Prefix/postfix ++/--: local source `mk_q(1)` rational with Add/Sub, not the
>   service cached constant or manager mixed-int Inc/Dec;
>   postfix copies the old value before changing the receiver.
> - Unary minus, abs, member neg/reset; numerator/denominator value extraction;
>   floor/ceil; power/expt (signed exponent casts to source uint32, not reciprocal).
> - Structural equality remains core `Equal`. `NotEqual`, `Less`, `Greater`,
>   `LessEqual`, `GreaterEqual` retain source swapped-LT and negated-LT routes.
>   The four source rational-left int comparisons construct the scalar rational.
> - Predicates, parity, power-of-two query, hash, bitsize/storage_size, 64-bit
>   conversions, inclusive wrapper unsigned/int32 projections, and double query
>   forward to actual manager branches under provenance validation and the lock.
>   `IsBig` is the complement of source small representation, a named Go query.
> - `AddMulAssign`/`SubMulAssign`: coefficient +/-1 receiver Add/Sub branches;
>   otherwise copy **k**, multiply that copy by c in place, then Add/Sub receiver.
>   They do not forward to the manager fused-product helper with different order.
> - `ModHat`: positive-b assertion; fresh Mod, copy r, multiply copy by rational2,
>   strict b<2r test, optional r-=b. Half ties remain positive.
> - `NumBits`: construct two, check source domain, copy operand, repeatedly fresh
>   IDiv followed by assignment Copy; zero returns one. No bitsize shortcut.
>
> Private concrete `facadeValueLocked` and `facadeAssignLocked` helpers require
> an already held service lock; parent `ext_gcd.h` integration can share the
> source value-expression routes without passing foreign raw records.
>
> ## Ownership and domain adaptations
>
> All input provenance is validated before numeric actions, including scalar
> wrappers and multi-operand fused operations. The service mutex covers complete
> source expressions. Every intermediate uses existing budgeted manager storage
> and lexical destruction. Named-local value returns transfer ownership through
> Move; returned compound lvalues use Copy. Errors return an invalid zero token;
> no intermediate owning token survives a failed expression. Numeric scratch may
> retain known owner-managed buffers according to already documented storage
> policies. There is no extra per-value Go allocation or owner pointer.
>
> Source assertion domains become `ErrRationalFacadeDomain` (negative NumBits or
> nonpositive ModHat divisor) and existing `ErrRationalNotInteger`. Existing
> PowerDomainError retains nonterminating uint32 mask behavior; `Expt(-1)` casts
> and fails with that error. Zero^zero remains the source rational result one.
> Source raw signed/unreduced denominators remain visible: 2/4 structurally differs
> from 1/2 while neither is less, numerator-only positivity reports true for
> 1/-3, and multiplication by rational1 retains 1/-3. Direct output-aliased IDiv
> on -26 with divisor7/-7 gives -2/+2; Mod gives zero. These source-action
> fixtures are separate from canonical independent mathematical checks.
>
> ## Tests and completion limits
>
> Tests were written before production; an isolated committed module with only
> new tests failed because RationalService.Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Rem did not exist.

> ## Exact numerical and alias contracts
>
> `Sign` returns source numerator m_val: the entire inline int32 value for small
> numerators, and -1/+1 for big numerators. Source predicates inspect numerator
> sign, even when a raw signed denominator would change the mathematical sign.
> `IsInt` requires a small denominator exactly one; unreduced 2/2 is not an integer
> under this representation test. Source +/-1 predicates require the corresponding
> small numeral representations. Hash ignores the denominator and retains the
> integer source's sign-free big-magnitude hash and unsigned inline casting;
> collisions such as 1/2 and 1/3 are intentional and structural equality resolves
> them. StorageSize is the sum of source live-limb sorting weights, not owner
> bytes or reserved capacities. Bitsize keeps the integer-only branch and otherwise
> sums numerator/denominator sizes with explicit uint32 addition.
>
> The rational accessors enforce their actual source integer-fit assertions;
> negative rational Uint64 gets ErrConversion even though the raw MPZ accessor
> casts an inline negative or returns a big magnitude. IsUnsigned/Unsigned include
> UINT_MAX (<2^32), whereas IntegerManager IsUint32/Uint32 strictly exclude it.
> Rational IsInt32/Int32 include INT_MIN and INT_MAX, whereas the MPZ variants
> exclude both. Naming and comments make these different source contracts explicit.
>
> Float64 performs the source numerator conversion, denominator conversion and
> n/d in order; it preserves the inherited UINT_MAX floating radix, Inf*zero NaN,
> valid numerator Inf/NaN and Inf/Inf. ErrRationalFloatDomain replaces the source
> SASSERT(d>0) for a negative or NaN converted denominator. This is distinct from
> invalid initialization, conversion-fit errors and budget refusal; it does not
> reinterpret or normalize raw negative denominators.
>
> Extraction explicitly copies the selected integer payload, without normalizing
> or borrowing the source lifetime. Rational-output extraction follows Copy then
> reset_denominator. Thin setters likewise publish their integer result and then
> reset denominator; the existing failure-atomic integer preparation is sufficient,
> because a checked denominator reset cannot allocate. Source component and self
> aliases retain this publication order. SwapNumerator exchanges actual ownership
> with no allocation or normalization. Inc/Dec delegate the exact source AddInt
> calls using inline +/-1. Raw 2/-3 increments to -1/-3 and decrements back to
> 2/-3. An internal Numerator(a,&a.den) alias for 0/7 completes the source Copy and
> creates denominator zero; it is not silently repaired or retroactively rejected.
> Subsequent numeral operations diagnose invalid initialization. Such component
> references are private to the numeric package, rather than borrowed public fields.
>

> ## Ownership, synchronization and checked boundaries
>
> `OwnedRational` holds only private `Rational` and scalar uint64 owner ID. Both
> this record and the raw Rational cache backing pass `arena.ValidateRecordType`
> under release and checked layouts. The service owns its manager; no public raw
> numeral or manager borrow escapes. Scalar provenance rejects a foreign value
> even when numerical slots match or both values are inline. Service Close
> invalidates every outstanding value, and a copied value in another service
> remains valid. IDs are monotonic global atomic namespace metadata only; no
> numerical cache/manager/lifetime is global, and overflow never wraps/reuses.
> Only serialized tests restore the namespace counter to exercise exhaustion.
>
> Owning Go token shallow copies remain forbidden by contract, as with primitive
> Int/Rational; no per-value ledger is invented. The cold service self pointer
> rejects reconstructed/shallow copied owner identities. Tests do not copy a
> live mutex as a Go value. All service manager/cache actions take its mutex;
> CopyFrom locks both owners in ID order. An externally shared Budget remains
> owner-confined under the existing Budget contract: separate service locks do
> not make externally concurrent reservations safe.
>
> Signed int32 fraction setters preserve the source valid-input sequence: negate
> numerator then denominator when denominator is negative, before either setter.
> The operation uses widened signed magnitudes for INT_MIN negation (undefined in
> source C++); boundary results are an explicit defined adapter, not an observed
> C++ result. Signed-pair SetFractionSigned stages both widened fields with signed integer
> setters in numerator/denominator order, normalizes, then Move publishes. This
> preserves the signed32 INT_MAX denominator representation; typed64 SetFraction
> retains its distinct unsigned64 denominator shape. Local pair destruction
> provides predictable failure safety. Extremely large power indexes reject uint32 endpoint/length or host
> backing overflow before any cache/charge change.
>
> ## Budget and failure-prefix policy
>
> The actual service header is charged with reflect size, including constants,
> mutex, self identity, cache slice counters, and scalar ID. Manager/nested
> numeric storage uses existing own graph charges; it is not precharged again.
> Borrowed Budget and caller-owned value/output/string storage are external.
> Cache backing is actual `capacity * sizeof(Rational)`. Slice size/capacity
> metadata is already in the service header, so source vector header counters
> are not duplicated. Every expansion reserves the full new array while the
> old array remains charged, then transfers ownership and releases old backing.
> Constructor failures close any constructed child and refund the owner header.
> Close releases cache/header and the complete owned manager graph.
>
> Predictable cache failure preserves successful source prefixes, including
> backing growth before a failed copy. A placement-copy failure does not append a
> live default record. Failed arithmetic/result copy destroys locals immediately.
> A failed request for k can have committed cache[k] before failing the extra
> cache[k+1]; retrying k then returns its cached value without extension, exactly
> as source successful-prefix control flow dictates. Numerical manager staged
> failure adaptations are inherited and explicitly distinct from source fatal
> allocation failure. Successful reservations consume Budget.FailAfter prefixes
> normally; teardown refunds Used charges without resetting the fault counter.
>

> # Actual raw memory allocation paths
>
> This packet implements the real allocate/reallocate/deallocate bodies and
> size/count/peak/watermark configuration/getters from src/util/memory_manager.cpp,
> using the committed utilMemoryAccounting transitions. It owns actual byte
> backings with stored SIZE_T prefixes. It is not the complete process runtime:
> generated initialize/finalize, participating typed-owner allocation hooks,
> multiple shared lanes, process exit/stdout/TRACE and full solver integration
> remain OPEN. Budget.Used is physical Go bookkeeping, never the source getter.
>
> newUtilMemoryRuntime creates an explicitly charged, confined cold owner. It
> borrows its Budget and contains one real accounting lane, a scalar origin, and
> a charged directory of physical allocations. Public block tokens contain only
> origin/slot/generation. Each allocation has its actual data array, including
> four/eight stored extent bytes, and a charged initialized-byte bitset. Slice
> headers belong to the cold allocation directory. No host map, generic, unsafe,
> boxed hot record or per-payload pointer object replaces this storage.
>
> Allocate adds the source SIZE_T prefix with selected unsigned32/64 arithmetic.
> The non-TLS profile changes counters/checks limits before physical storage.
> TLS allocates real data and writes its header before counters/synchronization.
> A TLS limit failure returns the completed owned block along with the source
> error classification: the caller must Deallocate it. Source native throw would
> leave that pointer unpublished; exposing its ownership is an explicit Go
> cleanup adaptation, preserving immediate physical/counter evidence.
>
> Reallocate reads the old stored extent, updates counters before physical work
> in both profiles, allocates new actual backing, copies the surviving bytes and
> initialized bits, then frees the old physical backing and writes the new header.
> The actual Go backend always relocates, a permitted realloc outcome. Successful
> relocation advances the checked pointer generation. Predictable physical
> refusal preserves the old block while retaining counter/OOM prefixes. Exhausted
> checked generations refuse before source actions, an explicit token-domain
> boundary. Old+new data and bitset peaks are charged without inventing source
> allocation-count events for cold metadata or checker bits.
>
> Deallocate reads the actual stored extent, subtracts before free, then performs
> TLS synchronization only after free. It never throws memory/count limits while
> deallocating. Header lifetime guards run at the actual read. Scalar metadata
> State/Stats are diagnostic snapshots; AllocationSize uses the source signed
> clamp and does not flush local counters. MaximumUsed/AllocationCount and strict
> AboveWatermark use the actual source transitions. Setters select signed
> conversion for LP64 and checked valid size_t inputs for the32-bit profile.
>
> Unsigned32 shrinking realloc deltas can add nearly2^32 to signed64 accounting;
> this is preserved. TLS synchronizes strictly above100000 or below-100000, resets
> only local size, and repeatedly contributes cumulative local count. Memory
> limit failure precedes count limit; OOM sets its flag, count failure does not.
> Errors use actual Z3Error classifications101/113. Native exit/diagnostic policy
> is still an OPEN transport boundary, not silently executed by a library test.
>
> Wrapped too-short extents still allocate real bounded physical storage before
> refusing at the unsafe header write. Allocate returns its owned partial token;
> reallocate publishes the new owned binding after freeing the old backing.

> # Resource-limit service
>
> `util/control/rlimit.go` translates `src/util/rlimit.h/.cpp` (Microsoft 2015,
> Nikolaj Bjorner). This is a cold owner service, not a solver or public status API.
> It uses concrete types throughout. Source has no dedicated rlimit assertion
> suite; the new tests are finite source-derived expectations and an independent
> bounded stack oracle. Source consumer tests remain with their unported components.
>
> | Source operations | Go counterparts / evidence |
> | --- | --- |
> | constructor and implicit vector destruction | newUtilReslimit, close; header, limit and child vectors budgeted |
> | inc(), inc(unsigned), count | inc, incOffset, count; inclusive bounds and uint64 wrap |
> | push/pop | push, pop; relative bounds, nested minima, count clamp, local cancel clearing |
> | get_cancel_flag/get_cancel_msg | cancelFlag/cancelMessage; exact source messages, suspension distinction |
> | cancel/inc_cancel/dec_cancel/reset_cancel/set_cancel | atomic uint32 state, process-wide cancellation mutex, recursive propagation |
> | push_child/pop_child | borrowed child stack under the same process-wide mutex |
> | scoped_rlimit | utilLimitScope with explicit deferred close |
> | scoped_suspend_rlimit | utilSuspendLimit with explicit deferred close |
> | scoped_limits | utilChildLimits with counted LIFO detachment |
>
> Counting, push/pop, suspension and destruction require the operation owner's
> confinement. Cancellation and child registration share the source OpenMP critical
> section's process-wide scope; atomic loads/stores replace the C++ volatile flag
> so asynchronous cancellation is race-safe in Go. Child services form an acyclic
> borrow graph, outlive registrations, and must not close while registered. The
> source has the same implicit graph/lifetime precondition. No individual hot
> record contains an interface, closure or mutex. Copying initialized services or
> active scope values is invalid; explicit owner lifetimes replace C++ destructors.
>
> Preserved executable source behavior:
>
> - Counting always increments even when canceled/exhausted/suspended, modulo 2^64.
> - Push computes count+delta, maps zero/wrap to unlimited zero, then applies the
>   literal source minimum. A nested delta=0 can therefore clear an outer bound.
> - Pop clamps count to the departing nonzero bound before restoring its parent.
> - Push/pop clear cancellation only locally; descendants keep their flags.
> - Registration does not inherit a parent's existing flag. The next propagation
>   overwrites every descendant with the parent's counter, including uint32 wrap.
> - get_cancel_flag ignores exhaustion; get_cancel_msg ignores suspension.
> - The suspension destructor sets false rather than restoring a previous value;
>   nested suspension consequently clears the outer one. An explicit test freezes
>   this source defect. Do not silently replace it with nesting depth.
>
> Storage adaptation: constructors charge cold header bytes, and geometric vector
> replacement charges old+new backing capacity before releasing old storage.
> Budget failures preserve limits, cancellation and child publication. Popped
> child pointers are cleared to avoid Go retention beyond the source borrow.
> Close detaches borrowed children without destroying them and releases all owned
> charges. Idempotent explicit scope/owner close prevents repeated deferred cleanup;
> C++ RAII destruction would occur once. Invalid underflow, closed use, nil/self
> children and unrepresentable capacities are development errors. Other cycles
> remain an invalid caller precondition. These changes do not alter valid source
> counting/cancellation semantics. Host runtime OOM recovery is not claimed.
>
> TDD evidence: tests first failed with undefined service/scope constructors and
> methods. Implementation reached GREEN. Tests cover all translated methods,
> 4000 deterministic bounded stack steps, source wrap/suspension quirks, late
> registration, exact messages, failed constructor/push/registration, replacement
> peak budgeting, complete cleanup, warmed zero allocations and four concurrent
> balanced cancelers alongside counting. Native checked race/vet and actual
> js/wasm main-package execution pass. Full integration gates are recorded in
> PORT_PROGRESS.md; WASI compilation is not runtime acceptance.
>
> The general common_msgs class (other strings), cancellation event-handler
> families, timeout/memory services and domain consumer integration remain separate
> source units. This packet supplies resource counting/cancellation only.
>
> ## Concrete cancellation event scope
>
> `util/control/cancel_handler.go` translates `cancel_eh<reslimit>` and the event caller
> IDs from `event_handler.h`. Its cold handler borrows a resource service and uses
> explicit deferred close in place of its destructor. The first invocation fixes
> the caller ID and increments cancellation once; later invocations have no effect.
> Only an invoked handler decrements on close, and the original canceled/caller
> fields remain observable. Nested handlers and external counter reset preserve
> source behavior. Handler invoke/close must be serialized; counter propagation
> retains the resource service's asynchronous safety. No template/generic or
> interface dispatch is introduced. Other event-handler specializations and the
> OS timer/signal dispatch remain separate unported units.
>
> Added finite tests (no dedicated source suite) went RED on missing handler/caller
> symbols before implementation, then GREEN. Tests cover first-caller order, quiet
> handler cleanup, nested propagated cancellation, reset before cleanup, exact enum
> numbers and zero warmed allocations. An isolated prospective-commit tree is used
> for whole-module gates while other agents have intentionally RED tests in progress.

> # Integer and rational root packet
>
> Status: **partial numeric source units**. This packet completes selected internal
> MPZ root/perfect-square methods and MPQ counterparts, without claiming remaining
> numeric methods, alternate GMP backends, public rational wrappers or context
> ownership complete. All source algorithms were read before translation, including
> mpz.h wrappers, both complete mpz.cpp root bodies, mpq.cpp root, mpq.h predicates,
> source normalization, and all active mpz/mpq tests. Copyright notices are retained.
> No production math/big, generics, unsafe, interfaces per limb, new persistent
> manager headers or external C++ fixture/compiler were introduced.
>
> ## Source methods and contracts
>
> | Source method | Go counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | `mpz_manager::root(mpz&,unsigned)` | `IntegerManager.RootInPlace` |
> | `root(mpz const&,unsigned,mpz&)` | `IntegerManager.Root(a,n,out)` |
> | `mpz_manager::is_perfect_square` | `IntegerManager.IsPerfectSquare` |
> | `div_l/div_u` root bound helpers | fixed-width quotient/ceiling blocks in `rootCore` |
> | `mpq_manager::root(mpq const&,unsigned,mpq&)` | `RationalManager.Root` |
> | `mpq_manager::is_perfect_square(mpq const&,mpq&)` | `RationalManager.IsPerfectSquare` |
> | `mpq_manager::is_int_perfect_square` | `RationalManager.IsIntPerfectSquare` |
> | inherited MPQ mpz root/perfect-square forwarding overloads | existing owned `Integers()` service exposes both Integer root forms and square query; no extra overloaded Go forwarding API |
>
> Integer root keeps the exact source log2/mlog2 power-of-two initial bounds,
> unsigned `k+1` arithmetic, lower-equal-upper branch, bisection, truncating
> machine_div2k(mid,1), Power before midpoint termination test, comparison order,
> Swap bound updates, and final upper-bound publication. False results are signed
> ceiling roots: 213^(1/5) publishes3, -213^(1/5) publishes-2. The source Power
> implementation, including its final extra square and classified mask domains,
> is used rather than a separate root algorithm.
>
> Integer perfect-square query preserves the source six temporaries, initial
> hi=a/sq_hi=a*a, source Copy updates, early zero/one branches, bisection using
> Div(mid,2), exact lower square check and false-result upper publication. Negative
> inputs return false and preserve the output. The source output Reset precedes
> rereading a: a nonnegative `a==out` therefore becomes0 and returns true. This
> source-derived alias defect is deliberately retained; independent mathematical
> square tests use a distinct output. Negative aliases remain unchanged.
>
> Rational root keeps `root(num)&&root(den)` short circuit, including successful
> false-result publication. An inexact numerator changes only the output numerator
> and retains the previous output denominator; an inexact denominator publishes
> both computed roots. No normalization is added. Nonalias and alias fixtures
> compare these source output parts, including deliberately unreduced2/4 results.
> Rational square integer branch resets output denominator first. A negative
> integer input thus returns false after changing only that denominator to1;
> a negative fraction leaves all output unchanged. Inexact fraction numerator
> retains the old output denominator; precise numerator/inexact denominator
> publishes both upper bounds, and normalization happens only when both are precise.
> Integer-only square query requires source is_int and otherwise reports its
> assertion domain. Raw Go zero Rational remains invalid; use NewRational.
>
> A correction from the initial read-only alias proposal is explicit: source
> normalize does **not** special-case a zero numerator. Nonnegative fractional
> `IsPerfectSquare(a,a)` resets num and den to0, both integer queries return true,
> then gcd(0,0)=0 leads to source Div(0,0). This is source undefined arithmetic,
> not a finite0/1 result. The adapter reports existing ErrDivideByZero and preserves
> the original fraction on this error. Integer-denominator1 aliases remain the
> finite source0/true result. This inventory is derived from executable source;
> no C++ observed output is claimed for the undefined path.
>
> ## Classified domains and storage adaptation
>
> `RootDomainError` retains Degree and Reason and unwraps to distinct sentinels:
> ErrRootNegativeEven replaces the negative/even source assertion (also negative
> n==0); ErrRootDegreeZero replaces nonzero root degree0 division by zero; and
> ErrRootIntegerRequired replaces the integer-only rational square assertion.
> Integer zero degree0 still returns true before source bound division. Rational
> zero degree0 reaches its nonzero denominator root and reports the degree error.
> The source negative midpoint -1 can inherit PowerDomainError for odd degrees
> >=2^31; it is not silently optimized. Source finite nonnegative zero/one/base2
> fast-path outcomes at huge degrees remain representable and tested. Predictable
> invalid-domain errors leave source/destination values unchanged.
>
> All temporaries are ordinary scalar Int/Rational values whose big payloads live
> in existing IntegerManager cells/Words with the same owner Budget. Deferred
> cleanup follows source local order and also runs on error. There are no per-call
> unbudgeted numeral/digit arrays or new numeric owner objects. Rational methods
> use existing synchronized/local versus unsynchronized/cached normalization
> paths, remaining owner-confined in both modes.
>
> Root output is staged in owned numerals before final Move, including in-place
> calls. Square queries stage output while retaining source negative/alias branches.
> Rational work starts as an explicit Copy of the previous destination and shadows
> input when aliased, preserving exact source rereads and short-circuit values.
> This is an intentional allocation/timing adaptation: old output storage survives
> until publication, copied/staged owners can increase the peak, and source partial
> mutation on an allocation/Power error becomes unchanged caller output. Source
> finite false results are still published. Retained manager scratch may grow on
> failure and remains charged until Close; no claim of identical source physical
> allocation/destructor timing is made. Final Close releases complete owner graphs.
>
> ## TDD and permanent tests
>
> Initial tests were written before implementation and the observed package build
> was RED with missing Root, RootInPlace, IsPerfectSquare and domain error APIs.
> The implemented source algorithms then reached GREEN. The first alias fixture's

>
> Three integer methods x two alias forms x small/big prior-output shapes use bounded fault-prefix sweeps and

> # Actual SAT simplifier source proposal
>
> Read-only proposal at HEAD4b9337e. Only this document is written. No production,

> ## Scope and source registrations
>

> selected LAZY methods and child/iterator actions are available; implicit
> copy/move instantiations, nonlazy profile and STRACE remain separately open.
> All remaining source simplifier methods below are currently unimplemented.
> No directly registered SAT simplifier unit test exists: source-port ENSURE/VERIFY
> count for this unit is zero. `TST(simplifier)` at test/main.cpp:169 refers to the
> Windows-only public Z3 AST simplifier tests, not sat::simplifier, and must not
> be counted as SAT assertions. Actual SAT consumers include `sat_user_scope`
> (TST239), the argument-driven `cnf_backbones` (TST_ARGV247), and solver use by
> actual tactics/SMT integration. `check_assumptions` (TST197) is an SMT-context
> consumer, not a direct SAT simplifier fixture.
>
> The registered user-scope campaign is unbounded. A finite source outer cycle
> has42 executions of one ENSURE site,168 created clauses, seven initial variables
> (0 through6), and original push-three/pop-two actions over seven frames followed
> by seven final pops. The existing uncommitted `sat_solver_user_scope_test.go`
> retains that planned route but its actual runtime/solver APIs do not exist.
> It must not become green using a truth-table production implementation, rebuilt
> formula state in the incremental solver, unknown-only Check, or disabled defaults.
> A test-only bounded CNF oracle remains independent from actual search/model
> reconstruction. The cnf_backbones input-driven unit requires a separate finite
> fixture/source-registration inventory and is not included in the42 claim.
>
> ## Complete default execution path
>
> Constructor binds the actual solver, initializes num_calls0, performs UpdateParams,
> then resets five statistics. Other source scalars are not silently initialized
> before their actual assignment sites. The parent solver constructs its children
> in header order and later calls its own UpdateParams again; the resulting child
> parameter update routes and real current module snapshot calls must remain visible.
>
> Run(learned) returns first for actual solver inconsistency, then only if all three
> subsumption/blocked-elimination/resolution flags are false. Defaults are subsumption
> true, resolution true, elim_vars true, blocked boolean false, blocked_at2.
> Initialize clears need_cleanup, calls real cleaner(true), captures current trail
> size AFTER that cleaner, reinitializes occurrence lists, resets clause/bin/var
> worklists, then resets/resizes visited char storage to2*num_vars. Diagnostic
> check_invariant is conditional source debug code, not a fake true callback.
>
> Run then resets two todos AGAIN, calls cleaner(true) AGAIN, recaptures trail size,
> clears need_cleanup, reinitializes occurrence lists AGAIN, registers learned
> clauses first only when learned=true, then problem clauses. Registration stable
> sorts each actual clause vector by DESCENDING size, preserving equal-size order;
> it skips frozen clauses and inserts only strengthened clauses into sub_todo.
> BCE executes on ordinary calls when enabled OR num_calls==blocked_at. Thus default
> blocked boolean false still reaches BCE on the THIRD ordinary call; learned calls
> do not increment num_calls. Counters and old_num_elim_vars are set after BCE.
> Only then is source scoped_finalize installed. A failure before that guard is
> not an excuse to run the later guarded cleanup as if already installed.
>
> Each loop runs subsume if enabled, returns on conflict, runs elim_vars only for
> ordinary/resolution calls, returns on conflict, stops when subsumption disabled
> or signed sub_counter<0, otherwise repeats while sub_todo is nonempty. Source
> scoped cleanup runs on exits after installation: if need_cleanup, compact watches,
> clean learned clauses then problem clauses; otherwise only remove affected
> learned clauses if vars were eliminated. It checks invariants and then Finalize.
>
> Explicit Finalize order is use_list, sub_todo, sub_bin_todo, elim_todo, visited,
> bs_cs, bs_ls. It does NOT explicitly finalize pos_cls,neg_cls,new_cls there.
> Their ordinary member destructors run in reverse declaration order when the
> whole simplifier dies. Normal completed elim_vars finalizes those three; its
> checkpoint/counter early return skips that explicit finalization. These distinct
> retained storage histories must be reflected in accounting and Close.
>
> ## All algorithm families and finite action obligations
>
> - Clause and literal cleanup overloads differ: clause cleanup scans all literals,
>   copies even true literals, erases false-literal occurrences when live/unfrozen,
>   shrinks and returns satisfaction. Literal-vector cleanup returns immediately
>   at its first true literal WITHOUT final shrink. Preserve both prefixes.
> - Subsumes1 marks all c2 literals, allows at most one complementary missing c1
>   literal, publishes null/single deletion output, then unmarks all c2 literals.
>   Subsumes0 requires direct inclusion. Min-occurrence choice is first strictly
>   smaller count, with source unsigned sums. Approximate subset is only a filter.
> - Collectors use actual compressing occurrence iterators, size/approx filters,
>   signed cost deductions, then paired output pushes. Clause output push can
>   succeed before a literal push fails. BackSubsumption1 handles deletion or
>   literal elimination, converts learned subsumer into problem clause when needed,
>   increments source stats and stops on actual conflict. BackSubsumption0 remains
>   reachable when new-resolvent sub_counter<=0; it is not redundant dead code.
> - PropagateUnit captures old trail size, actual Assign, then ONLY
>   PropagateCore(false), since clause vectors/watches may temporarily be inconsistent.
>   For each new trail literal it inserts false-literal occurrences into sub_todo,
>   advances iterator before mutations, erases satisfied occurrences except current
>   literal, then resets that positive occurrence list. A no-op propagation callback
>   cannot implement this route.
> - ElimLit publishes need_cleanup/stat/elim_todo before source clause elimination,
>   physically erases its occurrence, deducts the remaining count/2, cleans clause,
>   then handles satisfied/empty/unit/binary/long cases in source order. Binary
>   creation precedes bin_todo publication and lazy removal.
> - Binary subsumption starts at one real source RNG draw and rereads CURRENT watch
>   size in its inner indexed loop because backward subsumption can add binaries.
>   It ignores the false return of SubsumeWithBinaries at the caller's source site.
>   Learned-to-problem marking affects reciprocal watch entries.
> - ElimDupBins stable-sorts by the actual bin_lt: binaries first, literal index
>   ascending, nonlearned before learned for identical binary literal, nonbinaries
>   stable. Existing SortByKind is NOT this comparator. Compact both directions,
>   then add eliminated halves/2 to the uint32 statistic.
> - Subsume pops binary todo from the back, updates dummy, then processes clause-set
>   Erase() in the real selected hash physical order. It unmarks strengthened state,
>   deducts counters, conditionally cleans against new trail, handles empty/unit/bin,
>   and performs backward subsumption. Do not substitute a Go map/worklist order.
> - BCE's local heap comparator reads live opposite-literal occurrence count and
>   CURRENT watched-vector length: weight=2*occ(~l)+watches[l].size(). Initial heap
>   bounds128, insert reserve idx+1, decreasing priorities call real heap Decreased
>   or Insert. Its process traverses long occurrences first, collects removals,
>   publishes MC BLOCK_LIT entry on first blocked clause, stores original clauses,
>   updates affected heap priorities, unmarks, then lazily removes collected clauses.
>   Binary phase deletes reciprocal half before current compaction and writes MC.
>   AllTautology filters nonlearned reciprocal binaries and checks complementary
>   literals against actual simplifier marks. External/eliminated vars are excluded.
> - Variable ordering collects eligible vars from real uint_set order, computes
>   source uint32 wrapped 2*pos*neg+pos*bin_neg+neg*bin_pos, resets elim_todo before
>   stable sorting increasing cost, and pushes a separate variable output vector.
> - Resolve marks/pushes c1 except pivot, scans c2 except opposite pivot, detects
>   complementary marks, suppresses only literals marked from c1, and unmarks c1.
>   It DOES NOT mark each appended c2 literal, so duplicate raw c2 literals need
>   exact finite tests rather than an invented global dedup algorithm. Signed
>   elimination counter is charged for both input sizes before each scan.
> - TryEliminate preserves every cutoff, before-literal totals and clause-count
>   range boundary. It first computes all resolvents and refuses if non-tautological
>   count exceeds original clauses. Accepted path creates MC ELIM_VAR and copies
>   originals, marks eliminated, removes binaries and lazy occurrences, resets both
>   occurrence lists, deducts the SAME cost a second time, then recomputes all
>   resolvents. This is source's TWO genuine Resolve campaigns, not an optimization
>   to one replay-less campaign. New resolvents can yield conflict, real unit BCP,
>   binary creation+back-subsumption, or owned new clause→problem vector→occurrences
>   before backward subsumption. No whole-elimination atomic staging.
>
