> # SAT simplifier literal-indexed use lists
>
> Selected source: `src/sat/sat_simplifier.h` use_list, complete bodies at
> `src/sat/sat_simplifier.cpp:29–55`, the selected LAZY_USE_LIST implementation
> in `sat_clause_use_list.h/.cpp`, and actual `vector.h` specializations.
> This packet adds only `sat_solver_clause_use_lists.go` and its test file.
> Standalone cold use-list files remain unchanged.
>
> ## Executable inventory
>
> The source outer methods map to `Init`, `Insert`, `Erase`, `EraseExcept`,
> `Get` (one owning-context adapter for both mutable and const source references),
> `Finalize`, and explicit idempotent Go `Close`.
> The by-value `satClauseUseListView` implements source `size`, `empty`, `insert`,
> `erase`, `erase_not_removed`, `reset`, `check_invariant`, and `mk_iterator` via
> `Size`, `Empty`, `Insert`, `Erase`, `EraseNotRemoved`, `Reset`, `CheckInvariant`,
> and `Begin`. Its by-value iterator implements constructor consume, `at_end`,
> `curr`, `next`, and destructor completion via `Begin`, `AtEnd`, `Current`,
> `Next`, and explicit `Close`. Shallow copying a live iterator is prohibited.
>
> Outer Init destroys the current logical inline elements in ascending order,
> sets outer size zero, computes `2*num_vars` with source uint32 wrap, and performs
> individual source capacity growth steps. Only after all steps succeed does
> resize publish its final size and default construct all new inline elements.
> Thus a later refusal retains completed capacities and the reset prefix. No
> whole-operation rollback, literal deduplication, or all-index prevalidation is
> used. Insert/Erase read clause size once and execute each literal action in
> source order. EraseExcept skips every literal equal to its argument. Repeated
> literals preserve release duplicate insertion and unsigned subtraction; debug
> assertions occur at their actual child action, after earlier completed actions.
>
> Child push constructs the primitive reference before publishing physical size
> and live count. Lazy Erase keeps the primitive vector and decrements only live
> count in release. EraseNotRemoved shifts only the first matching reference, then
> decrements live count even when no match exists in release. CheckInvariant
> executes actual was_removed callbacks in release as well as debug; only its
> final count assertion is debug-only. Child Reset destroys its payload while the
> inline list object remains alive.
>
> Iterator captures physical vector size, not live count, and immediately
> compresses the first surviving current element. Reads and writes resolve the
> CURRENT child payload. Inner growth does not invalidate the inline child
> reference. Current copies a retained raw clause token without an added payload
> callback; the actual later was_removed callback guards the clause lifetime.
> Next increments i and j before consume. AtEnd is only captured i==size and
> performs no owner/lifetime dereference. Destructor completes only while i<size,
> then publishes j via source primitive shrink. It deliberately differs from
> AtEnd when a release caller has advanced beyond the captured end. The bounded
> retained-tail regression first failed against the erroneous != completion loop
> and now exercises the exact less-than condition in both profiles.
>
> ## Actual storage and lifetimes
>
> One self-checked cold owner borrows the real clause allocator and owns one
> concrete arena.Words owner. Clause allocator and its referenced clauses are
> not owned or deleted by lists. A selected owner-local clause allocator must
> outlive actual clause callbacks; foreign allocator tokens are not a substitute
> for an allocator binding. Actual access guards diagnose invalid source domains
> where C++ would read freed/foreign storage.
>
> Each hot inline record is exactly 32 bytes, with no Go pointer or interface:
> 8-byte arena.VectorRef; uint32 physical length, source capacity, live size,
> and initialized primitive-tail length (16 bytes); uint64 alive marker (8 bytes).
> The outer record slice is the single actual fixed-stride inline array. Its slice
> header resides in the charged cold owner; no per-literal cold object is created.
> Each clause token is five uint32 words: owner low/high, slot, generation, kind.
> Words descriptors/pages/directories/free metadata and their headers are actual
> owned charged storage, not invented source heap objects. The pool's rounded
> physical capacity is kept distinct from each child's source requested capacity.
>
> Selected source architecture uses eight-byte pointers: outer element stride16,
> source vector header8, inner pointer stride8. Go charges its ACTUAL owner,
> 32-byte record arrays, encoded payload words, and all Words ownership graph
> bytes. Source uint32 extent checks and actual Go host extent checks are separate;
> a simulated 32-bit-host fixture verifies the actual stride bound without a huge
> allocation. Ordinary growth uses source capacities 2 then (3*c+1)>>1. Old and
> new physical arrays overlap in Budget before old backing is released. Each
> completed step remains published on a later refusal. The source outer
> nontrivial move branch copies only logical constructed elements; ordinary Init
> has already destroyed all elements and has zero live elements to move.
>
> Views encode cold owner, index, and OUTER physical backing identity, not an
> instance-generation epoch. A same-type inline object reconstructed at the same
> retained address can transparently replace the earlier object; old views and
> iterators follow the reconstructed list and current child vector. A destroyed
> slot is rejected until reconstructed. Actual outer growth/free invalidates old
> inline addresses and is diagnosed by the backing identity guard. Child payload
> growth does not change that identity. No unsafe address arithmetic is used.
> Primitive initialized-tail metadata rejects genuinely never-constructed pointer
> slots; initialized retained tail is preserved through child growth/erase and is
> available to defined release operations. Debug current-logical-size assertions
> precede physical bounds guards at the actual source operator[] sites.
>
> Pool storage is a physical adaptation: source child finalize frees its exact
> allocation, whereas this owner releases its descriptor/block and retains reusable
> pool pages until Close. Outer Finalize frees the actual outer backing and destroys
> all logical children but retains its charged cold owner/Words infrastructure.
> Close releases that complete graph and is idempotent. Tests sum every actual
> owner/backing/page/directory/descriptor charge and compare Budget.Used before
> teardown. Constructor failure cleanup restores the borrowed allocator baseline;
> Insert faults preserve earlier literal actions and immediately expose exactly
> those live Words descriptors. Warm cycles allocate zero host objects after
> preparation. These APIs do not promise the C++ allocation profile.
>

> # SAT lazy clause use list — selected implementation
>
> `sat_solver_clause_use_list.go` translates the actual `LAZY_USE_LIST` selected
> by `src/sat/sat_clause_use_list.h/.cpp`, using the committed clause allocator
> and clause-vector owners. No solver, child-solver callback, runtime constructor,
> or Check substitute is introduced. The source headers remain **partial**:
> implicit move APIs, the inactive non-lazy branch, and STRACE integration remain
> open. The full SAT solver and its user-scope consumer are still open.
>
> ## Implemented source surface
>
> | Source | Concrete Go API/action |
> | --- | --- |
> | `clause_use_list()` | `newSATClauseUseList(allocator, budget)` |
> | `size()` / `empty()` | `Size()` / `Empty()` read the independent unsigned live counter |
> | `insert(c)` | `Insert(ref)`: source debug contains/removed assertions, vector push, then counter increment |
> | `erase_not_removed(c)` | `EraseNotRemoved(ref)`: source assertions, physical erase, then decrement |
> | `erase(c)` | `Erase(ref)`: source assertions, counter-only lazy decrement |
> | `reset()` | `Reset()`: vector finalize before publishing counter zero |
> | `check_invariant()` | `CheckInvariant()`: actual removed-flag traversal in **both** builds; final equality assertion only in debug |
> | `mk_iterator()` / iterator constructor | `Begin()`: capture physical vector length, then immediate real `consume()` |
> | `at_end()` | `AtEnd()`: plain `i == capturedSize`, no backing/lifetime dereference |
> | `curr()` | `Current()`: actual current-vector scalar read, no additional removed-flag callback |
> | `next()` | `Next()`: source debug assertions, `i++`, `j++`, then consume |
> | `consume()` | real skip-removed loop; each surviving current reference is written to compacted position j before returning |
> | iterator destructor | explicit `Close()`: finish all remaining Next actions, then vector Shrink(j) |
> | legal implicit copy constructor / assignment | `Clone(budget)` / `Assign(source)` via actual vector copy, followed by live counter copy |
> | implicit list/vector destruction | owner `Close()`: release actual owned vector/header, never delete referenced clauses |
>
> Every source debug assertion site is exercised. Source release bodies are
> preserved: duplicate/removed insertions can execute, missing physical erases
> still decrement, repeated lazy erased-reference decrements wrap unsigned32,
> and invariant equality does not become a new release precondition.
>
> The class has no explicit move declaration; legal implicit move inventory is
> left open until its exact compiler-instantiated layout/copy-forwarder routes
> are separately tested. In particular, the existing ptr_vector move-assignment
> API is a source copy forwarder and is not silently used as underlying vector&&
> transfer. The actual simplifier `use_list::init` resets/destroys the outer list
> elements **before** resizing, so its ordinary growth starts with zero logical
> elements; it does not require relocating live list instances in this packet.
>
> ## Iterator and lifetime contract
>
> The iterator is returned **by value**, with a borrowed stable `*satClauseVector`
> and scalar captured-size/i/j/closed fields. It does not allocate an uncharged
> heap iterator, capture a source backing pointer, pin the original backing,
> cache a current clause reference, or reject vector growth by epoch. Reads and
> writes resolve the vector object's **current** backing on every source action.
> Underlying source operator[] debug guards use the **current** logical size;
> release reads/writes use the existing concrete vector's physical bounds and
> retained scalar slots. Tests demonstrate growth, backing Swap, and public
> implicit list assignment during an active iterator.
>
> Captured size is vector length, not the lazy live counter. Begin already skips
> removed prefixes and publishes the first live scalar to compacted index zero.
> Each Next performs the same immediate publication; Close completes traversal
> even if the caller stops early. Close does not repair the live counter if the
> caller appends while iterating: its captured-end final Shrink can discard that
> appended physical tail while leaving the increased counter, as source does.
>
> Go has no automatic C++ lexical destructor. Callers must explicitly Close a
> successfully constructed iterator at source lifetime end and must not copy a
> live owning iterator. Idempotent Close/closed-state errors are explicit Go
> lifetime adapters. AtEnd is still plain scalar comparison after vector closure;
> actual destructor Shrink then reports the concrete closed-vector error.
>
> Current copies a retained scalar without dereferencing its clause payload.
> An actual subsequent was_removed/other clause access performs the allocator
> generation/lifetime guard. A stale payload encountered by consume or invariant
> traversal reports the actual guard error after prior skips/publications.
> Failed Begin returns the partial scalar iterator alongside its error; Next and
> Close expose their already completed index/write prefixes and do not roll them
> back. An interrupted invalid-payload construction/traversal is not advertised
> as a valid, generally retryable C++ iterator. No clause ownership is lost:
> clauses remain with their actual allocator/caller, and list Close can release
> its own backing independently. No hidden recovery traversal or always-true
> removed callback substitutes for the source.
>
> ## Storage and budget
>
> One cold list header owns one actual `satClauseVector` header/backing. Both
> actual `reflect.TypeOf(...).Size()` headers are charged once; the list header
> contains only cold owner pointers and the scalar live counter. Clause tokens
> in backing remain pointer-free. The vector's real allocator-binding ledger is
> retained/copied as necessary; copied callbacks resolve the actual borrowed
> allocator, including across two real allocator owners. No clause payload or
> source phantom inline header is charged to the list twice.
>
> Underlying vector geometry retains source requested capacity growth and source
> pointer-width limits separately from actual wider Go token byte limits. Full
> old and new backing charges overlap during expansion. A permanent one-byte-
> below-peak fixture refuses capacity2→3 growth with the old vector/counter and
> caller-owned clause unchanged. Reset releases backing before counter zero;
> Close releases only owned headers/backing/bindings. Source unsigned size is
> not normalized, clamped, or recomputed by these lifecycle methods.
>
> Constructors and Clone reserve all actual headers/backing and unwind predictable
> allocation failure without losing caller clause roots. Assign preserves the
> source member order: vector finalization/copy precedes the scalar counter copy.
> Failure can leave an empty destination vector with the previous live counter;
> it does not invent an atomic source assignment. Warm iteration and explicit
> destruction allocate zero heap objects and make no new Budget reservation.
>
> All actual allocator callbacks are the existing Removed/Get/Set operations.
> Payload, owner, epoch-exhaustion and physical-bounds errors are typed safety
> adapters from those concrete owners, observed at actual action boundaries.
> There are no per-element interface boxes, Go generics, unsafe operations,
> mock child solvers, fake counters, or production truth-table algorithms.
>
> ## Source tests and verification
>
> No registered direct `clause_use_list` source test/assertion was found in
> `src/test`; original source assertions claimed here: **zero**. The source
> simplifier remains an actual unported consumer. New tests derive complete

> # Complete standalone SAT solver packet
>
> Status: source inventory and concrete implementation design; solver production is not implemented. The complete standalone source solver is the objective. Existing clause/watch/queue storage tests do not establish search, propagation, conflict analysis, incremental scope, model, or core correctness. No generic Go, unsafe, boxed hot records, fake extension, or replacement DPLL algorithm is permitted.
>
> ## Audited source and evidence
>
> Read the complete `src/sat/sat_solver.h` (578 lines) and `.cpp` (3770 lines), the complete registered `src/test/sat_user_scope.cpp`, configuration and four parameter-generator descriptions, and the complete dependency headers. The method index below records every solver definition, including overloads and helper bodies; inline header bodies are inventoried separately. The complete cleaner, model_converter, SCC, elim_eqs, probing, asymm_branch, MUS, integrity_checker, simplifier, clause_use_list, par, and max_cliques bodies have now also been read. Inactive iff3-finder and external/generated runtime algorithms require their own complete audits before translation; this document does not claim those algorithms have been audited merely from their interfaces or call sites.
>
> `src/test/main.cpp:239` registers `sat_user_scope`. Its source test has ONE textual ENSURE site, inside an infinite campaign. One explicit finite outer cycle executes 42 coherence comparisons: seven repetitions of three pushes/two pops, then seven final pops. It creates 168 three-literal clauses, initially seven variables (variable zero is unused in the formulas), and compares incremental search to a separately reconstructed solver using DEFAULT parameters. A finite-cycle harness is an explicit test termination adaptation, not an assertion-count invention. Both solvers must additionally agree with an independent exhaustive truth-table oracle for the six formula variables, and every returned model must satisfy original active clauses. The oracle is test-only; production retains the real source algorithms.

> `literal(r(6)+1,r(2)==0)` has platform-dependent argument evaluation order. The Go fixture will choose and document one deterministic order and preserve the actual source random_gen recurrence and 15-bit outputs. > ## Concrete API proposal and ownership
>
> Proposed cold `satSolver` owner, public constructor `NewSATSolver(satSolverConfig) (*satSolver,error)` with `{ParamsContext *ParamsContext; Params ParamsRef; RLimit *utilReslimit; Budget *arena.Budget; Runtime *satRuntime; Extension *satExtensionDispatcher}`. The lifetime domain is explicit: parameter and runtime/resource services outlive the solver, ParamsRef is retained through actual shared Assign/Del, and extension is borrowed. Scalar source Boolean/literal/model/result representations remain existing concrete types.
>
> Methods first required by the registered source test: `MkVar(ext,dvar bool)(satBoolVar,error)`, `MkClause([]satLiteral) error` (source mutates its array), `Check([]satLiteral)(lbool,error)`, `UserPush() error`, `UserPop(uint32) error`, `Close() error`. Full surface adds every source method above with typed error returns for allocation, closed/foreign owner, genuine bounds/lifetime/overflow danger and source-debug assertion sites. `Check` returns lUndef only at actual source abort/limit policies; cancellation/max-memory are source solver exceptions, not silently false. Model/core access copies into caller buffers or by-value checked iterators; no arena slice escapes. Source nonlearned Copy is distinct from invented generic Clone/Assign.
>
> A solver cannot store `[]*satWatchList` or a hot `[]satWatchList` containing Go slices. Proposed one cold charged watch-store has pointer-free descriptors (list identity/generation, payload/lifetime refs, logical size/capacity, epoch) and concrete payload pages. The outer source vector owns scalar list descriptors with source 2,3,5,... growth and real move/destructor semantics. Transient by-value views may hold one cold store pointer on the caller stack, never in retained hot records. Full-capacity initialized watch tails and erased-versus-destroyed holes must preserve the frozen watch lifetime contract. Actual backing/descriptor headers/directory/ledger/lifetime bytes and all old+new growth peaks are charged once. Source payload capacity policy and physical arena capacity classes are separately documented; no pointer arithmetic or unsafe codec is introduced.
>
> All variable arrays, scope records, justification arrays, nested occurrence/model/consequence lists, assumptions/sets, clauses/reinit vectors, activity queue, component owners, temporary stable-sort storage, scope guards and parallel graphs are real charged allocations. Borrowed Budget/runtime/callback environment/services are not double charged. Published growth prefixes survive later allocation failure exactly where source bodies publish; no blanket transaction rewinds owner state or Budget failure counter. Unpublished constructor preparations unwind their actual owned graph in lexical/source lifetime order. Cold mutexes/owner IDs reject copied owner values; no per-record closure/interface.
>
> ## Default policies and fidelity traps
>
> Source default phase caching (on400/off100), Luby restart initial100/factor1.5/maxUINTMAX, random frequency .01/seed0, burst100, maximum conflicts UINTMAX, GC glue_psm(initial20000/increment500/smallLBD3/k7), minimization and dynamic subsumption true, core minimization false, one parallel thread, max memory UINTMAX MB. Simplification initial multiplier300, growth1.5/max500000; SCC, probing and asymmetric branching enabled. Simplifier resolution/subsumption and variable elimination enabled, blocked-clause elimination false. Exact parameter definitions and overrides must be tested; optional policies remain part of full scope.
>
> Important observed action order:
>
> - MkVar marks model stale and increments stats BEFORE sequential watch/assignment/justification/decision/level/activity/etc vector publications and queue/todo updates (cpp:135–160).
> - MkClause base propagation may return before binary watches/stat counters; ternary/nary stats precede real clause allocation, attachments precede vector publication (195–370).
> - Propagate increments qhead before watch iteration, publishes replacement clause literals before destination watch Push, and compacts only completed prefix when conflicts/extension outcomes exit (553–710).
> - SimplifyProblem invokes cleaner → SCC → nonlearned/learned simplifier → stable watch sort → probing → asymm → extension, then assumptions; none can be a placeholder (1191–1250).
> - No-extension get_max_lvl returns scope_lvl immediately; conflict analysis cannot replace this with an apparently tighter literal scan (2088+).
> - Pop calls extension before debug bound assertion, shrinks scopes before reinit and uses retained scalar scope fields; unassignment retains justification/level/phase history (2531–2619).
> - UserPop pop-to-base precedes zero-count handling; removes guarded clauses/binaries and shrinks variable arrays in actual source order, then propagates from qhead0 (2620–2751).
> - CollectBinClauses(false) excludes learned; true includes BOTH. FindMutexes true then false deduplicates its pair map (2818+,3119+).
> - WCNF maximum weight+1 wraps uint32; soft literal formatting uses ordinary source variable numbering, unlike DIMACS (2957+). Keep this defined source quirk.
> - Watched external extraction retains the already documented source release value3/debug round-trip assertion behavior; real extension continuation must not silently repair it.
> - Simplifier default elim_blocked_clauses=false still executes blocked-clause elimination when m_num_calls equals default elim_blocked_clauses_at=2, the third nonlearned call. This is an active default dependency, not an optional feature that can be skipped (simplifier.cpp:190–194).
> - Probing cache availability publishes before individual cached literal pushes; operator() calls finalize after each completed run, which frees assigned/to-assert/cached bins (probing.cpp:41–57,243–246,261–265). Preserve this cleanup rather than inventing a permanently retained cache.
> - Integrity checker check_assignment is genuinely return-true; check_learned_clauses counts frozen entries in NONlearned vector before checking learned; selected SASSERT calls run only in debug (integrity_checker.cpp:113–137,225+). Do not silently correct these source bodies.
> - Asymmetric branching catches solver_exception to preserve unvisited clause pointer tail before rethrow and skips final saved-phase assignment on that exception path; scoped detach lifetime still runs (asymm_branch.cpp:82–114).
> - Stats.reset clears16 counters; collect emits15 excluding nonlearned generation; solver reset_statistics does not reset SCC although collection includes it.
> - Source hot integer additions/multiplication/wrapping and signed/float conversion domains require source-defined behavior/debug guards before genuine UB adapters; no universal early bounds narrowing.
>
> ## Full-scope TDD roadmap
>
> 1. Registered finite user-scope cycle FIRST observed compile RED against real missing solver API; permanent independent truth-table/model oracle and charged fixture lifetime. Tests stay RED until genuine default paths work. No reduced solver executable or bypass-default green claim.
> 2. Exact configuration/global module/runtime boundary tests FIRST; real nested vector/watch-store and model-converter/occurrence support lifetimes with failure injection and immediate charge/root checks.
> 3. Full source constructor/Copy/MkVar/MkClause/attach/detach/assignment/propagation algorithms, all clause widths and source watch quirks; bounded propagation closure oracle and publication fault tests.

> ## Concrete ownership and codec
>
> `satSolverWatchListRef` is private scalar owner/slot/generation; list descriptors retain generation/retirement/free links and source length/capacity. Hot descriptors and refs are audited pointer-free. No per-list Go allocation/header or per-record closure/interface, generics, unsafe, or math/big is used. One cold store owns Vectors64 and Words, a scalar descriptor directory and monotonically unique cold owner ID. It rejects copied cold owners and is owner-confined, like Budget; no concurrent-sharing guarantee is invented.
>
> A watch occupies four uint64 words: packed val1/val2, full clause ownerID, packed clause slot/generation, and storageKind. All scalar bits survive roundtrip even when fields are unused. The source two uint32 watch fields remain distinct from widened checked locators; the Go watch codec's physical32 bytes is not claimed equal to C++ watched size8. Source literal packing/debug sites are reused unchanged.
>
> A separate uint32-word bitmap records each slot's initialized lifetime, including noncontiguous Erase→Pop holes and word boundaries. Growth copies all old bytes and bitmap bits, whereas copy construction initializes only logical slots. The four-word extent uses uint64 arithmetic and covers every source geometric watched capacity (source maximum `(UINTMAX-8)/8` ->2147483640 codec words), with checked real host allocation bounds supplied by arena; scalar tests do not allocate multigigabyte memory. The cold directory uses source outer eight-byte watch-list growth progression but charges its actual scalar record width and host byte bounds; it is storage metadata, not a completed outer vector.
>
> Owner headers, both nested arena owner/descriptor graphs, record directory, actual payload/class blocks, page directories, bitmap backing and every old+new overlap are charged exactly once. `Stats().ChargedBytes` reports the real retained graph; immediate failure tests compare it against Budget.Used before teardown. Budget is borrowed, as are clause allocators and output streams. Input slices and final returned stream strings are caller-owned boundaries. Reserve/Release do not rewind the injection attempt controller. No Budget number is substituted for the source global memory manager.
>
> Source one-array expansion is adapted into charged payload-then-bitmap preparation. The source capacity publishes only when both preparations succeed. Earlier actual arena page/directory growth remains owned/charged if the unpublished payload is freed. Source logical capacities are distinct from geometric arena size classes and retained free pages. Within-owner move/swap transfer actual payload ownership without copying; cross-owner owning moves are not exposed, because arena page graphs are common-owner resources. Full solver source uses within-owner watch moves and genuine cross-owner copies. Raw c_ptr/references are represented by scalar access/iterators; mutable slices never escape.

> # Standalone SAT clause storage: coordinator source review
>
> This records the original coordinator source review. Its standalone storage
> packet is now implemented and verified in PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-sat-storage-port-status-md; full SAT
> solver functionality remains open.
> The coordinator read all of sat_clause.h/.cpp, sat_clause_set.h/.cpp,
> sat_watched.h/.cpp, sat_justification.h and sat_var_queue.h in the preserved
> source. The complete solver, propagation, simplification, search, extension
> callbacks and source solver tests remain required by GO_PORT_PLAN.md.
>
> The packet should implement the actual clause allocator and temporary clauses,
> clause wrappers and sets, watched records and owning watch lists, justification
> records, and the activity-backed variable queue. All hot records must be concrete
> and pointer-free. Clause IDs are separate from physical handles and may recycle
> only at the source recycle site. No Go generics, unsafe or boxed hot records.
>
> ## Source details that tests must freeze before translation
>
> - Clause construction copies all literals, sets capacity equal to initial size,
>   initializes removed/used/frozen/reinit/inactivity/glue/psm, and calls
>   mark_strengthened, which recomputes the variable approximation mask. Its source
>   size assertion is greater than one. Shrink retains capacity and recomputes
>   approximation only when size changes. Elim removes the first matching literal
>   and shifts later elements left; it does not swap-remove.
> - check_approx is not a read-only query: it saves the previous approximation,
>   recomputes the real mask, then source-debug asserts may_eq. Preserve this
>   mutation and distinguish release from source-debug execution.
> - Inactivity is an eight-bit field and wraps. Glue and psm saturate at255.
>   Freeze/unfreeze assert learned status and prior frozen status. Models retain
>   true/false/undefined; an undefined literal does not satisfy a clause.
> - Temporary clause Set destroys the previous clause before a larger allocation.
>   Reusing existing capacity updates only size, learned and literal bytes. It does
>   **not** call mark_strengthened or update_approx and does not reset other flags.
>   Preserve stale approximation/flags on reuse; do not silently reconstruct the
>   object on every Set. New temporary clauses use source ID UINT_MAX.
> - bin_clause stores the second literal as `(index << 1) + learned`. Its equality
>   compares the two encoded words directly in both orientations, including the
>   unusual reverse comparison between unshifted and shifted fields. A conventional
>   unordered pair equality would change defined source behavior.
> - The source allocator allocates storage before obtaining a recyclable source
>   ID and constructing the clause. Delete recycles the ID before physical release.
>   Address-segment encoding is a platform storage contract, not a solver algorithm:
>   replace it with explicit stable owner-local offsets/handles and record widths,
>   provenance, reuse generations and limits. Do not reproduce pointer arithmetic
>   or claim source address-segment exhaustion tests apply to the Go layout.
> - Clause-set insert reserves its ID-to-position vector before checking an existing
>   ID, publishes the position before pushing the borrowed clause, and has a source
>   conditional invariant check. Erase uses swap-remove and updates the moved ID.
>   Pop removes the last entry. Sets borrow clauses; they do not own clause cleanup.
>   A post-position-publication push failure needs an explicit defined continuation
>   adapter, not a hidden full-operation rollback claim.
> - Watched ternary construction sorts literal indices and asserts they differ.
>   Binary learned metadata occupies bit2; clause records pack the blocked literal
>   above two tag bits. Preserve source width truncation versus debug round-trip
>   assertions and expose typed guards only where source continuation is undefined.
> - **Source watched external-index defect:** constructor puts the supplied index
>   in m_val1 and EXT_CONSTRAINT(3) in m_val2, but get_ext_constraint_idx returns
>   m_val2. Thus the source constructor round-trip assertion fails for indices other
>   than3 in source-debug, and release access/display returns3. Do not silently fix
>   this defect. Justification's external accessor instead correctly returns m_val1.
> - watched_lt only orders binary before other records and ternary before clause/
>   external; it supplies no ordering within those groups. Clause-watch erase removes
>   the first matching offset and shifts subsequent records left. Ternary erase
>   follows the actual source vector erase action, which must be reread.
> - Justification uses NONE/BINARY/TERNARY/CLAUSE/EXT tags in the low three bits of
>   its second word. Ternary second-literal shift is3, distinct from watched shift2.
>   get_clause_offset/get_ext_justification_idx lack kind assertions in this source;
>   do not fabricate a universal source getter assertion inventory.
> - Variable-queue priority is descending activity with no extra variable-ID tie
>   breaker. It uses the source heap with initial reserve128. MkVar reserves v+1
>   before insert, increased activity performs decreased only if present, unassign
>   inserts only if absent, deletion erases only if present, and reset retains heap
>   storage. Activity must be a real explicitly borrowed concrete uint32 domain,
>   not a fake solver callback or an uncharged copied snapshot.
>
> ## Ownership and verification contract to refine before implementation
>
> Audit the source heap and all vector operations and identify actual test
> registrations and consumers before approving API/storage details. Use actual
> charged cold owners and pages/backings, with old/new overlap and bounded typed
> slot/offset/generation adapters. Copy/move/reset/finalize and all implicit source
> member actions require explicit concrete counterparts. Temporary clauses,
> wrappers/sets/watch lists and clause-vector rendering must use the same real
> clause owner; no parallel simplified clause representation.
>
> Author source assertions and the defect fixtures first and observe missing-real-API
> RED. Add independent bounded literal-array, model and membership/heap oracles,
> source ordering fixtures and immediate ownership/failure-prefix sweeps. Source
> tests that require the real solver remain open until that producer exists; a
> test-only SAT oracle cannot stand in for source solver execution. Preserve exact
> default display bytes while declaring stream-state integrations still open if
> they are not translated. Run frozen full native/checked/debug, race, actual JS,
> vet, WASI compilation and source/no-generics gates before the coherent commit.

>
> ## Selected complete scope and prerequisites
>
> Implemented the executable standalone methods in sat_clause.h/.cpp,
> sat_clause_set.h/.cpp, sat_watched.h/.cpp, sat_justification.h and sat_var_queue.h:
> real clause owner and temporary clause, binary/wrapper scalars and owning vectors,
> borrowed clause set, watched scalars and owning list, justification, and variable
> queue borrowing a real mutable activity vector. Read all these files, sat_types.h,
> heap.h, vector.h, approx_set.h, id_gen.h, small_object_allocator.h/.cpp, the existing
> Go SmallBytes/IDGen/IntHeap/literal/model/approximation implementations and real
> registered heap/sat_user_scope/small allocator tests and SAT consumers.
>
> Available genuine dependencies: satLiteral/satBoolVar/satModel/lbool/satApproxSet;
> arena.SmallBytes with descriptor generations/physical budgets/pooling/direct
> branches; budgeted utilIDGen; source heap algorithms already translated in
> IntHeap (but source action-order difference below prevents blindly wrapping it);
> NumericTextStream for real ostream flags/width/base/numeric emission; exact
> source vector growth/copy capacities. No new solver abstraction is necessary.
>
> Owned files: sat_clause_storage.go/test, sat_clause_set.go/test,
> sat_watched.go/test, sat_justification.go/test, sat_var_queue.go/test and two

> root-owned and will not be edited without coordination.
>
> ## Concrete storage and APIs
>
> Use existing lowercase sat literal/model types and concrete owner-local `sat...`
> names within package g3, with exported method names where useful for inspection.
> No public raw backing slices or Go pointers in retained SAT records.
>
> - satStoredClauseRef: private scalar ownerID uint64 plus storageKind/slot/generation.
>   Existing arena_refs.go satClauseRef (rawRef foundation) is untouched and is NOT
>   the completed clause owner locator; future consumers must adopt this real type.
>   satClauseOffset is a DISTINCT scalar type with the same checked locator fields.
>   Source clause ID is another uint32 scalar stored in clause data, never derived
>   from slot/offset/generation. Zero refs are invalid; physical slot0 remains valid
>   when generation/ownerID are nonzero. OwnerID uses a cold monotonic atomic
>   namespace, never wraps/reuses; self-identity rejects owning Go shallow copies.
> - satClauseAllocatorConfig: one Storage arena.SmallBytesConfig, whose
>   Descriptors.Budget charges the COMPLETE owner graph; source allocation profile
>   default follows the selected Linux g3debug/nondebug profile, with explicit
>   pooled/direct diagnostic overrides only as recorded storage test adapters.
>   Optional borrowed OutOfMemory func()bool feeds existing utilIDGen's real source
>   memory::is_out_of_memory branch. Its cold function field is included in header,
>   its externally owned environment is borrowed, no closure is allocated here.
>   Nil retains existing standalone IDGen's non-OOM contract; no invented global
>   memory-service state or Budget-error-to-global-OOM equivalence.
> - NewSATClauseAllocator(config) → *satClauseAllocator,error; MkClause(literals,
>   learned) → satStoredClauseRef,error; Delete(ref) error; Offset(ref) → scalar offset;
>   GetClause(offset) → scalar ref; IsLive(ref), ID(ref), Size(ref), Capacity(ref),
>   Literal(ref,index), SetLiteral(ref,index,value), AppendLiterals(ref,callerBuffer).
>   Every clause member below is an owner method receiving ref. Close reclaims
>   tracked storage; source has no allocator Reset, so no invented logical-reset
>   algorithm is claimed. IDs recycle ONLY Delete's actual source recycle site.
> - Internal satClauseHotHeader contains uint32 ID/size/capacity/approx/flag lanes;
>   all retained data is pointer-free. The canonical five-word header+literal
>   byte encoding lives in SmallBytes directly, with scalar typed word accessors.
>   No duplicate uncharged literal snapshot or second parallel clause model.
>   Physical byte charges are real allocation lengths and real descriptor/directory
>   metadata, not assumed C++ struct stride. The five-word codec is a Go storage
>   adapter; its selected-baseline size coincidence does not assert ABI equivalence.
>   Object extent is checked uint64 `20+4*n`, including n0 and UINTMAX n
>   (17179869200 bytes). Extents <=UINTMAX use real SmallBytes; larger host64
>   extents use the concrete direct backend in sat_clause_large.go. Actual host
>   byte bounds precede Reserve/make, not an invented 4GB clause limit.
>   The full scalar locator adds storageKind to owner/slot/generation. A wide
>   cold directory is embedded in the charged parent (no second owner header),
>   capacity*actual reflect stride, with exact `5+n` uint32 payload words charged
>   once. Unpublished directory preparations refund on payload failure; fault
>   attempt counters never rewind. Free rows retain generation ledger; exhausted
>   rows retire, independent of source ID recycling. Finite backend fixtures test
>   these real algorithms at 28 bytes; separate huge-count fixtures prove extent
>   and branch arithmetic plus budget refusal without multi-GB allocations.
> - satTmpClause is a cold unique owner with nullable ref. NewSATTmpClause(Budget),
>   Get, Set(literals,learned), SetBinary(l1,l2,learned), SetBinClause(encoded), Close.
>   Reuse the SAME clause codec/access methods through a direct-only storage owner;
>   temporary allocation is source alloc_svect(char,size), not SmallBytes pooled
>   placement. New tmp ID is UINT_MAX; it never calls IDGen.Mk/Recycle. The public
>   allocator rejects releasing another owner's temporary ref. Destruction releases
>   its direct storage; no source rational/resource destructor callback exists.
> - satBinClause: two source encoded uint32 lanes, constructor, Literal1/2, Learned,
>   Equal. satClauseWrapper: scalar clause ref or first literal plus sentinel second
>   literal, Binary, Size, Literal, ContainsLiteral/Var, ClauseRef; binary wrapper
>   allocates no clause. Null second literal makes a source binary wrapper's union
>   unusable as a clause pointer: typed dangling-union guard, no invented tag fix.
> - satClauseVector and satClauseWrapperVector: cold owners, concrete scalar backing,
>   constructors, Push/Get/Set/Pop/ResizeFill/Shrink/Append/AppendTo/Reset/Finalize/Close,
>   Clone/Assign/MoveClone/MoveAssign and cold checked iteration. ClauseVector has
>   source DisplayInto; wrapper scalar has its own display, no invented dedicated
>   source wrapper-vector display overload.
>   Borrow one real allocator; copy raw refs without touching clause data, and
>   preserve defined cross-owner aliasing via cold borrowed allocator bindings if
>   copying different domains is allowed (do not fake owned copies of clauses).
> - satClauseSet: NewSATClauseSet(real allocator,Budget), Contains, Empty, Size,
>   Insert, Erase(ref), Pop() → ref, Reset, Finalize, CheckInvariant and checked
>   bucket-position iteration/AppendTo, Clone/Assign/MoveClone/MoveAssign, Close.
>   Membership follows SOURCE ID, not generation; borrowed clause validity is a
>   separate typed guard before dereferencing. A set is bound to one allocator
>   ID domain; foreign allocators have independent IDs and must not silently share
>   one ID-position vector. Defined source same-ID membership/overwrite quirks
>   remain; source debug invariants diagnose ID aliasing.
> - satWatched: source val1/val2 uint32 lanes plus scalar provenance/generation
>   companions only for clause offsets. Binary/Ternary/Clause/External constructors;
>   all source predicates/getters/setters, MarkNotLearned, Equal/NotEqual and Less.
>   Binary/ternary/external have zero companions and exact two-word scalar equality;
>   clause offsets use full locator identity instead of accidental cross-owner
>   slot equality. This widens hot record size; actual reflect stride is charged.
>   No offset bits are sacrificed to tags: source offset lives in val1, literal/tag
>   packing remains exactly source val2. Raw source equality against invalid/dangling
>   old addresses is not promised as a checked-handle domain operation.
> - satWatchList: charged owner/backing, exact vector lifecycle/copy/move and full
>   scalar access/append/set-end/erase helpers, comparator and DisplayInto(real
>   allocator,real NumericTextStream). EraseClauseWatch first matching clause offset,
>   EraseTernaryWatch constructs source-sorted ternary record then vector.erase.
>   Both shift later entries LEFT and preserve order (neither swap-removes).
> - satJustification: default None, Binary/Ternary/Clause/External factories,
>   Kind/predicates/literal getters, raw ClauseOffset/ExternalIndex, DisplayInto.
>   Clause offset widened as above; scalar assignment/copy only, no owning allocation.
> - satActivityDomain: genuine concrete charged owner of mutable uint32 vector,
>   Push/Resize/Get/Set/Len/Reset/Finalize/Clone/Assign/MoveClone/MoveAssign/Close.
>   Source uint32 activity arithmetic belongs to caller; Set NEVER automatically
>   invokes queue callbacks. Queue borrows this OWNER, so backing growth/assignment
>   reads through current activity storage; no priority snapshot or hidden closure.
> - satVarQueue: constructor(activity,Budget), ActivityIncreased, MkVar, DelVar,
>   UnassignVar, Reset, Empty, NextVar, Clone and MoveClone, Close/Stats plus cold
>   diagnostic Contains/CheckInvariant for tests. Comparator activity[a]>activity[b]
>   has NO variable-ID tiebreaker. New concrete private activity heap holds int32
>   values/indices and borrowed domain pointer. No source copy/move ASSIGN API:
>   comparator reference member deletes those operations, verified below.
>
> Source vector specialization validity matters: watched, bin_clause and
> clause_wrapper have NO default constructor. Their source vector(size) and
> resize(size) default-object forms are ill-formed if instantiated; expose actual
> ResizeFill/size+value/source-array constructors, not fabricated zero records.
> Clause-pointer vector default resize creates null refs; activity default resize
> creates0. Common executable vector operations include Size/Capacity/Empty/Get/
> Set/GetDefault/SetX/Back/Push/Pop/Insert/ReserveFill/ResizeFill/Shrink/SetEnd/Erase
> (first matching, shifts)/Contains/Append/Fill/Reverse/Swap and forward/reverse
> checked iteration, plus constructor/copy/move/reset/finalize routes. Source
> nonempty self Append is nonterminating: typed adapter before actions; empty self
> valid. The implementation is for valid concrete instantiations, not every theoretical
> uninstantiable template method. Cold watch-list owners own only concrete scalar
> record arrays; future solver's outer watch-list collection must use scalar list
> references/common owner metadata, not hot []Go-owner-pointers. That outer solver
> storage is not implemented or claimed by this standalone packet.
>
> The spelling is concrete and source mapping is enumerated below; no arithmetic
> or solver algorithms are represented by standalone storage tests.
> Caller append/output buffers and final strings are caller-owned boundaries.
>
> ## Every clause method and exact lifetime/control flow
>
> sat_clause.cpp:27-42 allocates header/literal capacity exactly initial size;
> initial removed/used/frozen/reinit/inactivity/glue/psm false/zero, learned argument,
> memcpy all literals, mark_strengthened recomputes variable approximation. Source
> approx is unsigned32 mask of variable&31, not literal-index mask. Constructor
> check_approx is inside SASSERT and therefore executed only in source-debug;
> size>1 assertion is LAST after constructor body.
>
> sat_clause.h:58-95: ID/Size; both indexed literal overloads; Learned/UnsetLearned;
> Shrink; Strengthened/MarkStrengthened/UnmarkStrengthened; Elim; Removed/SetRemoved;
> Approx/UpdateApprox/CheckApprox; begin/end via checked scalar iteration;
> ContainsLiteral/Var; SatisfiedBy; Used mark/unmark/query; inactivity inc/reset/query;
> Frozen/Freeze/Unfreeze; static ApproxLiterals; Glue/PSM setters/getters;
> ReinitStack getter/setter. Literal writes MUST NOT implicitly refresh approx or
> strengthened. Shrink recomputes only on a decrease, never changes capacity.
> Elim removes first matching literal and shifts remainder, then decrements size
> and marks/recomputes. Satisfaction reads actual three-valued model and returns
> true only positive=true or negative=false; undefined satisfies neither. Missing
> model index is genuine source OOB and gets a typed guard at actual read.
> Inactivity wraps eight bits; glue/psm saturate255, source flag bits remain distinct.
>
> CheckApprox cpp:55-60 saves old mask, recomputes/mutates real approximation, then
> source-debug asserts equality. Stale mask debug error occurs AFTER the mutation;
> release returns true after mutation. Do not implement a read-only validator.
>
> Tmp Set cpp:105-124 destroys old object and clears pointer BEFORE larger allocate.
> If capacity suffices, only size/learned/literal bytes change: ID/approx/strengthened/
> removed/used/frozen/reinit/inactivity/glue/psm remain stale/preserved. No call to
> mark_strengthened. New temporary uses normal constructor body and UINT_MAX ID.
> Budget failure after old release leaves Get nil; successful capacities retained.
> Source tmp copy is raw-pointer aliasing and double-cleanup-unsafe; user destructor
> suppresses actual implicit move. Allocator implicit shallow copy similarly aliases
> owned SmallBytes chunks/free lists. Neither has a safe source owning Clone contract:
> Go rejects shallow owners by self identity, rather than inventing source deep copy.
>
> Allocator cpp:198-205 allocates actual object bytes BEFORE obtaining source ID,
> then constructs. Delete cpp:208-220 recycles ID BEFORE destructor/storage release;
> if recycle array allocation fails, clause remains live. If true source OOM observer
> skips recycle, physical deletion still occurs. ID generator wraps/reuses according
> to real existing source operations; IDs are never silently retired at generation
> exhaustion. Descriptor generations can retire physical slots independently. Source
> allocator destructor requires caller destruction/deletion of live clauses (solver
> cpp:60-73 does this); Go tracked-owner Close reclaims remaining inert clause storage
> as explicit cleanup adaptation, without fake extension/destructor callbacks.
>
> Clause display cpp:223-238: '(' space-separated literals ')' then x if removed,
> + if strengthened,* if learned. Clause vector emits each clause then LF. Wrapper
> display cpp:259-267 lacks all flag suffixes. Literal output is SOURCE two insertions:
> (sign?"-":"") then unsigned variable. Empty sign CString insertion still consumes
> Width; do not flatten literal into one host string or use dimacs variable+1.
> All renderers use real NumericTextStream actions, preserving flags/base/width/
> alignment/fill and exact default bytes; source intermediate host strings absent.
>
> ## Release/debug domains and packed quirks
>
> Preserve defined release bodies, not blanket stronger preconditions:
>
> - Clause construction zero/one sizes is defined in release; source-debug sz>1
>   fails after body. Preserve allocation/ID/initialized-header prefix at that site
>   with typed assertion diagnostics; expose produced scalar ref where needed.
>   For Tmp new(mem) constructor failure, source pointer assignment has not completed:
>   Get stays nil, allocated storage remains owner-tracked for Close/explicit
>   diagnostic cleanup. Do not pretend that field publication preceded assertion.
> - Elim absent on a NONEMPTY clause is release-defined: no shift, decrements size
>   and drops last literal, then refreshes approximation. Debug error precedes that
>   body mutation. Empty absent Elim would underflow and then scan OOB: typed guard.
> - Shrink greater than size is release no-op/debug error. Invalid learned/frozen
>   state for UnsetLearned/Freeze/Unfreeze performs ordinary release bit write;
>   source-debug diagnoses at actual pre-body assertion. Indexed OOB/dangling refs
>   receive typed guards in all profiles because actual source continuation is UB.
> - BinClause val2=(second.index<<1)+learned, uint32 wrap; no source roundtrip assert.
>   Equal compares BOTH encoded words directly in each orientation. It is not
>   ordinary unordered pair equality. Preserve raw high-bit loss in second literal.
> - Watched ternary sorts indices BEFORE packing, asserts distinct and second-literal
>   roundtrip in debug; val2=TERNARY+(l2.index<<2). Clause constructor blocked literal
>   similarly shifts2 and source-debug roundtrip asserts. RELEASE high two bits
>   truncate; debug diagnosis is source site, not a universal input cap.
>   SetBlockedLiteral/SetClause do NOT have roundtrip assertion even in debug;
>   preserve their uint32 truncation. Binary Learned tests val2>>2==1, not merely
>   bit2!=0; BinaryNonLearned is exact val2==0. MarkNotLearned asserts learned then
>   rewrites binary tag and verifies result.
> - Watched external constructor stores index in val1/tag3 in val2; getter RETURNS
>   val2. Release getter/display therefore return3 for every index. Debug constructor
>   roundtrip fails except supplied3. Do not fix getter to val1. Standalone setter/
>   equality/raw-record tests distinguish external index0/3/UINTMAX and debug errors.
> - Watched Less: binary before nonbinary, ternary before clause/external, false
>   within groups or between clause/external. Source solver.cpp:1251-1255 uses
>   stable_sort, not arbitrary sorting; if exposing standalone SortByKind, use
>   allocation-free concrete STABLE grouping and test within-group order. Do not
>   claim solver::sort_watch_lits ported merely from this storage helper.
> - Justification None/Binary/Clause/External predicates compare exact val2 where
>   source does; Kind masks low3. Ternary val2=TERNARY+(l2.index<<3), truncates top3
>   bits in release AND debug, no constructor roundtrip assertion or sorting.
>   ClauseOffset and ExternalIndex getters have NO kind assertions: preserve raw
>   val1 result with scalar locator companions, which cannot resolve if not a real
>   live clause handle. Only three literal-getter source assertions exist.
>
> Wrong-kind watched/literal justification getters also have SASSERT-only checks:
> preserve their defined scalar release extraction and diagnose in debug, instead
> of making every getter an unconditional ErrKind. A scalar raw word interpretation
> is distinct from an actual invalid clause-pointer dereference, which is genuinely
> undefined and receives an all-profile checked-locator guard.
>
> Use dedicated g3debug profile constants and typed ErrSATAssertion, with optional
> source tag conditions for heap/clause_set CASSERTs. They are selected assertion
> instrumentation adapters, not invented solver callbacks or a fake global debug
> runtime. Validate source-debug and release behaviors separately in permanent
> hermetic tests. No production/tests may depend on C++ compiler/reference source.
>
> ## Set, vectors, activity heap and failed-publication continuations
>
> Source vector:0→2 then(3*old+1)/2; exact source-capacity deep copy, ascending raw
> record copy, Reset retains backing, Finalize releases. Resize expands repeatedly
> BEFORE length/fill publication; retain each successful capacity prefix on failure.
> Cold owners reflect-sized once; actual arrays capacity*reflect stride with full
> old+new overlap, host-byte/source-count checked before Reserve/make. No fictitious

> scalars. Embedded IDGen metadata is charged in owner header, its free array once.

> Concrete methods and explicit thin-route mappings cover the valid vector bodies.
> Source reserve(n) on activity/clause-pointer vectors maps to ReserveFill(n,0) or
> ReserveFill(n,satStoredClauseRef{}); clear() maps to Reset(). Raw c_ptr, iterator
> raw pointer comparisons and mutable reference escape are intentionally replaced
> by checked concrete iterator values/Get/Set, not advertised as raw pointer APIs.
> No completeness of an unrelated obj_hashtable template is claimed: clause_set is
> the actual pair of source vectors, not a hash-table substitution. Watch/bin/wrapper
> source default-size/default-resize instantiations are ill-formed, so are absent.
> Wrapper has no source operator== in C++17; wrapper-vector Contains/Erase(value)
> are likewise ill-formed and absent (scalar wrapper Contains(literal/var) remains).
> Insert(value) is the source push alias; InsertAt and EraseAt are explicit Go
> index adapters. Default-sized activity and pointer-vector construction uses exact
> capacity n, whereas size+value/array constructors use source repeated growth.
> Source fill(size,value) recurses into itself after default resize; FillSize on
> the valid activity/pointer specializations keeps that resize prefix then reports
> ErrSATNonterminating, rather than silently repairing the source overload.
>
> Release clause literal reads/writes past current size but below physical capacity
> remain defined retained-literal accesses; debug diagnoses idx<size at its source
> site. Binary wrapper release indices 2/UINTMAX still extract second; debug errors.
> Scalar svector/ptr-vector retained-capacity access/size writes are preserved,
> while watch-vector access consults explicit initialized-lifetime metadata.
> Source erase(iterator) shifts and decrements WITHOUT a destructor, so its trailing
> initialized watched record remains live and release Get/Set are permitted there.
> Pop/Shrink/SetEnd/Reset destroy only their actual logical ranges; erase→pop can
> leave a dead hole below a still-live erase tail, so a single highwater cannot model
> this. Debug idx<size assertions still occur before lifetime/OOB guards.
> Source UINTMAX SetX performs resize(0) first, then typed guard at endangered
> index write; no early guard hides that completed prefix. Absent Elim on size
> UINTMAX would increment UINTMAX to zero then write index UINTMAX: scalar boundary
> helper guards that actual OOB after debug assertion, distinct from valid last match.
>
> Clause-vector owners retain explicit charged cold allocator binding directories
> for cross-owner copies, with stable scalar origins. Raw copies/MoveClone retain
> closed identities without dereference. Public BindAllocator checks live owner;
> copy adoption checks identity only. Rendering resolves the real borrowed owner
> and returns ErrClosed for dead storage; no owned spelling/clause copy is made.
> Binding allocation prefixes are explicit Go ownership adapters, retained and
> charged immediately; Close releases them. Set intentionally stays in one source
> ID domain, preventing unrelated allocators' colliding IDs from forming a fake set.
>
> Heap contains receives source int32: unsigned event >INTMAX converts to negative
> then would index negative; ActivityIncreased/Del/Unassign/MkVar have typed OOB
> guards, distinct from valid high positive absent-event no-ops. Heap move really
> leaves values size0, so source Empty (size==1) is false after move. Diagnostic Size
> returns0, NextVar guards endangered empty backing, and source Reset recreates
> sentinel via real growth while retaining completed failure prefixes. Reference
> comparator forbids Assign/MoveAssign; permanent reflection/lifecycle checks verify
> this, rather than copying a cold mutex/reference as a Go value.
>
> Each owner and its borrowed activity/Budget are caller-serialized; no global
> solver callback/state or per-record closure exists. Cold self identity rejects
> unsafe shallow owners. Iterator epochs saturate on an operation reaching UINTMAX64
> and reject subsequent structural operations, never wrap to resurrect iterators.
> Source vector expansion checks source byte-domain and actual host-byte bounds;
> Go widened scalar-record strides are charged physically, not assumed C++ stride.
> Pointersegment packing/native address hashes are explicitly replaced by full
> scalar checked locators, not seven fabricated address segments. Optional tag
> CASSERT runtime and TRACE streams are not reconstructed as global solver runtime.

> ## Source audit and selected method mapping
>

> inclusion/typedefs, mpz/mpq constructor/move/swap semantics, vector expansion,
> copy/destruction/reset/push/pop/shrink/resize implementation, and active

>

> predicates) were audited and mapped for these two managers. Arithmetic delegates

>

> | --- | --- |
> | :27 private undefined copy constructor | noncopyable; Go struct-copy use rejected |
> | :29 constructor / :30 destructor | NewScopedIntVector/NewScopedRationalVector / Close |
> | :34 reset | ascending manager.Del for every live element, retain capacity |
> | :42 m() | Manager |
> | :44 push_back | Push grows backing, appends default numeral, then manager.Copy |
> | :49 pop_back | Pop delegates to checked Shrink(size-1) |

> | :62 resize | Resize shrinks first when applicable; grows through source capacities, constructs numeral(0) defaults |
> | inherited indexed access/size/capacity | Read deep caller copy, Set deep manager assignment, Size, Capacity |
>
> Source vector expansion starts cap2, then (3*cap+1)/2 at each step. Int and
> Rational source types have explicit move constructors, so source nontrivial move
> relocation applies: only active elements move, numeric allocation identity stays
> stable, moved-from cell references become empty and m_val survives. The concrete
> code transfers pointer-free scalar records and clears only old cell references;
> it does not delete/re-copy their payloads. No internal vector slice or element
> pointer escapes. Copy-at-read/indexed-deep-set replace raw reference access to
> avoid shallow owning-handle copies; unrestricted inherited raw vector operations
> are not advertised as safe domain APIs.
>
> ## Lifetime, budget and failure policy
>
> Each object borrows one live manager and charges its actual Go owner header to
> that manager's existing Budget. Backing arrays charge actual concrete record size;
> len/cap metadata already resides in the charged header, with no fictitious second
> source counter-header charge. Manager cells/Words charge numeral payloads exactly
> once; borrowed manager/Budget objects are not duplicated. Headers include a cold
> self-identity pointer that rejects shallow Go wrapper/vector struct copies before
> cleanup. Hot Int/Rational backing is pointer-free (reflect audit tests).
> All objects use the existing owner-confinement contract, not per-record locks or
> callbacks. Scalar Get is the source-style borrowed mutable reference to a cold
> inline numeral; it must not be shallow-copied as an owning value and expires at
> Close. Clone/Set/Assign are the deep ownership operations. Foreign scoped owners
> are rejected. Caller read outputs/format strings remain caller-owned.
>
> Close deletes scalar/vector payloads before refunding only its own header/backing;
> it is idempotent. Managers must outlive scoped owners. If that source lifetime
> precondition is violated, methods report ErrClosed; Close refunds independent cold
> storage without deleting already-invalidated numeral cells and reports ErrClosed.
> The manager already destroyed those cells at its own Close. This checked cleanup
> adaptation avoids double deletion and leaked independent owner headers.
>
> The root-approved source action-prefix policies are explicit:
>
> - Failed Push deep-copy leaves the published default0 element (Rational den1).
>   Failed backing growth leaves original length/capacity/payloads.
> - Resize performs each individual source growth reservation. If a later growth
>   fails, successful earlier capacity remains charged while length/values stay
>   unchanged. Default construction happens only after growth completes.
> - Old and newly prepared backing are simultaneously charged before transferring
>   elements and releasing old backing. Exact one-byte-below/at-peak tests pass.
> - Clone constructor failure releases its new header/partial scalar value; manager
>   storage capacity grown earlier may legitimately remain, but immediate live cells
>   and Words payload counts must return to baseline.
>
> Invalid indices, empty Pop, too-large Shrink and invalid input numerals are checked
> before source actions. Budget successful reservation attempts consume FailAfter
> prefixes normally. No transactional controller bypass or hidden generic template
> was added. A test's first fault fixture was corrected when parsing had already
> warmed free cells: the final fixture occupies actual free slots to guarantee the
> next deep copy reserves storage. Constructor peaks are separated from exact vector
> backing peaks with actual charged caller-owned fixture backing, not fake owner
> headers. Warm retained scalar/vector operations measure zero Go allocations.
>

> ## Source rendering and conditional actions
>
> Composite display uses the source iterative frame/index traversal. Empty composites print `)` including nested empty composites. The source top-level atom branch emits `display_atom` then lacks a return and casts the atom as a composite, which is undefined behavior. `Display` preserves the fully defined atom prefix and returns `ErrSexprDisplayContinuation`; no fabricated successful source continuation is claimed. `DisplayAtom` explicitly exposes the private source atom operation safely. Predictable rendering failures return the completed emitted prefix and error.
>
> Numerals use basic `RationalService.FormatInto`, matching source rational `operator<<` calling `to_string`; pretty formatting is not substituted. A short caller staging buffer causes a budgeted growth and a repeated pure preparation via the existing public formatter API; numeric operand copies/arithmetic do not change. No intermediate Go strings are retained or allocated for rendering. Symbols borrow the live SymbolManager byte region under its lock, preserve null `null` and source signed numerical `k!` spelling. Strings stop display at their first NUL, insert backslash only before quote, and preserve backslashes/newlines/other bytes unchanged, as `escaped` defaults require. Their getter preserves the full stored bytes, including embedded NUL and UTF8 continuation bytes.
>
> BV uses the exact function-local `sbuffer<char>` inline sixteen bytes. Heap overflow doubles sixteen→thirty-two→sixty-four with old-plus-new reservation, and is destroyed on success and every failure before the owned val destructor; no digits buffer is cached. A direct 95-byte budget rejects the 32+64 growth peak without mutating the old buffer. Fifteen hex digits plus NUL fit inline with no heap allocation, sixteen plus NUL spill to32, and thirty-two plus NUL spill to64. The production failure fixtures preserve prefix `#x` before any digit emission, and both source inline operation and final caller output allocate only the latter. BV display writes `#`, creates an owned rational copy, writes x/b, performs source Rem and IDiv result creation, Copy assignment and expression destruction, and retains c through digit-buffer push. It runs source hex comparison against rational9, reverses the buffer, pushes its terminating NUL before digit emission, and destroys val afterward. It never truncates values exceeding width. Negative values produce zero padding, width zero selects hex and can produce `#x`, and positive noninteger rem/idiv domains return the existing typed rational error after the completed prefix. Checked capacity arithmetic replaces unrepresentable physical buffers with typed bounds errors.
>
> `g3debug` evaluates source `SASSERT(rational(0)<=c && c<rational(16/2))` after quotient publication and before c-to-digit branching. The lower test short-circuits the upper; the zero temporary survives RHS evaluation, and the RHS temporary is destroyed before zero at the full-expression end. The actual source rational comparisons and owned temporary constructors/destructors are used; false diagnostics return `ErrSexprBVInvariant`. Nondebug builds omit these actions, as the source does. The conditional arithmetic diagnostics are implemented, not left pending.
>
> ## Ownership, storage, and explicit adaptations
>
> Factories return RC0. Composites acquire children in ascending order. `IncRef` retains exact uint32 wrapping: MaxUint32→0 does not delete. A subsequent `DecRef(0)` returns the typed source assertion error. Wrapped-zero records remain generation-valid until a later valid 1→0 deletion or explicit owner teardown. A nonallocating maximum-counter fixture verifies this.
>
> Hot records, child handle pairs, element/iterator tokens and stack frames are pointer-free scalar structs. Cold pages, array directories, owner headers and all cleanup/display/staging/ref-vector backing arrays are charged with exact architecture sizes/capacities and old-plus-new growth peaks. A pre-reserved deletion stack bounded by allocated record capacity makes accepted cleanup of a valid acyclic RC graph allocation-free. Invalid cleanup after counter-overflow corruption can return typed errors; ordinary unsigned semantics are preserved. Record recycling increments generations and retires exhausted slots instead of reusing a public identity.
>
> Record allocation precedes factory value construction, as the source does; failed constructors unwind copied numeral and payload resources and recycle their unpublished record. Physical pooled pages can remain charged after failure for reuse. SymbolManager and RationalService are borrowed and must outlive this manager. All numeral fields own a source Copy; accessors return owning copies rather than exposing mutable source raw borrows. Manager Close destroys every still-live owned numeral once, including RC0 and wrapped-zero records, before releasing physical storage. > # SMT2 symbol utilities and complete escaped byte adapter
>
> The four smt2_util functions and complete escaped byte adapter are implemented
> in util_smt2_util.go/test and escaped/escaped.go/test. Only those four files and this
> assigned status were edited. No central metadata or Git state changed. No Go
> generics, unsafe, cgo or boxed hot records were introduced. Applicable source
> Microsoft2011 notices are retained. Full AST printers remain unported.
>
> ## Complete source surface and concrete names
>
> | Source | Concrete Go API | Exact behavior |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | smt2_util.h:24; .cpp:21-29 | IsSMT2SimpleSymbolChar(byte) bool | ASCII digits/letters and exactly ~!@$%^&*_-+=<>.?/; no whitespace, colon, pipe, backslash or non-ASCII byte |
> | smt2_util.h:25; .cpp:31-51 | IsSMT2QuotedCString(*string) bool | Nullable borrowed C string; stop first NUL; null/empty false; first decimal digit true; special outer-pipe scan; otherwise any non-simple byte true |
> | smt2_util.h:26; .cpp:53-57 | IsSMT2QuotedSymbol(*SymbolManager, Symbol) (bool,error) | Validate live owner/plain token; numerical false; null delegates nullable false; named spelling read directly from owner bytes |
> | smt2_util.h:27; .cpp:59-72 | MkSMT2QuotedSymbol(*SymbolManager, Symbol, *arena.Budget) (string,error) | Assert the source predicate before local buffer construction; open pipe, bytewise prepend backslash before pipe/backslash, close pipe, CStr and final returned text |
> | util.h:379-389; util.cpp:122-136 | Private escapedEnd helper | Null yields empty; first-NUL limit; trim only the maximal suffix of LF bytes, preserving all other bytes |
> | util.h:385-389; util.cpp:138-152 | escaped.Write(io.Writer, *string, bool, uint32) error | Source stream actions: quote emits backslash then quote; every other byte emits unchanged; after each retained LF emit exactly indent spaces |
> | util.h:388 stream insertion | escaped.String(*string, bool, uint32) (string,error) | Standard-library convenience wrapper producing one caller-owned string with a safe allocation bound |
>
> The approved concrete APIs are implemented. ErrSMT2NeedsQuoting rejects an
> invalid mk request before any buffer reservation. Null/numerical inputs return
> false for the predicate but fail this constructor precondition. Marked/foreign,
> stale and closed symbol inputs preserve existing SymbolManager error guards.
> The byte-only pure predicate needs no owner, allocation or Unicode conversion.
>
> ## Source quirks that must survive
>
> The predicate name is not a test for an already quoted string: true means the
> source caller will generate quoting. Null and empty strings are false. A digit
> anywhere after the first byte remains valid, but an initial digit is true even
> when subsequent bytes are simple. This is an exact whitelist, not an SMT-LIB
> keyword/reserved-word validator: names such as true are not specially quoted.
>
> When the C spelling begins and ends with pipe and has length at least2, interior
> backslash immediately followed by backslash/pipe is skipped only when its escaped
> byte is before the closing delimiter (i+2<len). Every other interior pipe or
> backslash makes the predicate true. All other interior bytes, including spaces,
> digits and control bytes, are accepted in this special branch. Thus ||, |a b|,
> and correctly escaped interior delimiters are false. A backslash immediately
> before the closing pipe is true. A single pipe is true. Do not add a generic
> parser, unescape existing names, or strip existing delimiters.
>
> MkSMT2QuotedSymbol always wraps and escapes the full bare spelling, even when
> that spelling already has malformed delimiters; it does not repair/remove them.
> The source uses successive char appends, not one precomputed bulk append. A
> backslash prefix before an offending byte is a completed source action if a
> later append fails. Preserve capacity doubling and CStr boundary growth exactly;
> do not preallocate an exact final buffer or replace it with strings.Builder.
>
> escaped is implemented in src/util/util.h/.cpp, not nonexistent util/escaped.h
> or util/escaped.cpp. It escapes only double quote. Existing backslashes, CR,
> tabs, high-bit bytes and interior newlines are unchanged. With trim=false a final
> LF also gets indent spaces. With trim=true all final LF bytes vanish before
> rendering; final CR is not trimmed. Null and empty have identical empty output
> but remain distinct borrowed input domains. Source indentation is unsigned32;
> Go must check storage arithmetic rather than wrap count/capacity computations.

> ## Physical budgets, prefixes and ownership

> Statistics; both temporary map owners; key buffer including inline16. Every actual
> contribution/map/overflow/binding backing is charged at actual capacity*stride.

> ## Numeric/source undefined-behavior boundary
>
> Source append(unsigned) calls sprintf("%d", unsigned), not %u. Scratch
> .cache/string_buffer_unsigned_probe.c compiled with -Wformat-signedness records
> the type-mismatch warning and AMD64 observed output2147483647, -2147483648, -1

> This is not claimed portable well-defined C high-bit behavior. The parent-approved
> Go adapter explicitly casts uint32→int32 then prints signed decimal for all bits,
> preserving the fork baseline's observed fresh-ID/counter output rather than
> silently replacing it with mathematical unsigned decimal. Permanent boundary
> fixtures cover the complete low/high-bit endpoints independently of the probe.

> Int/long conversions use local [24]byte scratch, include source terminator space,
> and delegate one bulk append. No PrintfFormatter owner/workspace allocation or
> host formatted intermediate string is invented. MinInt32/MinInt64 magnitude
> conversion avoids Go signed negation overflow. LongBits defaults64 (LP64), accepts
> only32/64, and32 rejects values outside signed32 before buffer actions. This
> ABI-range adapter does not claim the rejected value fits a source32-bit long.

> ## Budget, roots, and lifetime behavior
>
> Actual concrete owner reflect-size includes the embedded inline array, mutex,
> self pointer, control scalars, and overflow slice header. It is charged **once**
> at construction. Stats.InlineBytes is informational and already in OwnerBytes;
> no duplicate inline charge/backing allocation exists. Byte arrays are pointer-free,
> and no backing slice/pointer escapes a public method. Overflow capacity doubles,
> reserves full new bytes while old overflow is charged, copies pos bytes, then
> releases old overflow. Embedded initial array remains part of the owner charge
> even after overflow allocation. Owner self-identity rejects shallow copies.
> Cold mutexes serialize an owner; borrowed shared external Budgets still require
> caller serialization across other owners. No owner stores per-record callbacks.
>
> Bulk CString/symbol/buffer appends may publish several successful capacity
> expansions before a later failure. Position and appended bytes stay unchanged
> until all growth completes, preserving source successful allocation prefixes.
> Char append publishes one byte only after its required expansion. Source numeric
> Symbol k! bulk prefix completes before integer suffix append, so suffix failure
> retains k!. Plain symbols read the actual borrowed manager checked bytes directly
> and preserve bulk semantics; no intermediate Symbol.String allocation is used.
> The manager is borrowed only for the synchronous call, not retained in the buffer.
>
> CStr is a mutation: pos==capacity forces one expansion, writes terminator at pos,
> and leaves pos unchanged. Reset keeps all capacity/content; subsequent empty
> CStr writes byte0 at the new pos0. Returned immutable text copies are caller-owned
> output boundary storage and survive reset/close; this replaces source ephemeral
> raw-pointer borrowing. Read exposes only a checked scalar byte within pos.
> Size preserves source unsigned32 cast; Position exposes the widened counter.
> Checked host/uint64 addition and capacity doubling reject unrepresentable Go
> backing sizes rather than wrapping allocation arithmetic.
>
> All9 cross-buffer routes acquire one cold global append mutex then both owner
> mutexes. Source CStr completes first, including source growth and terminator,
> even if the destination's later append reservation fails. A source CStr failure
> leaves destination untouched. Source/destination may have different Budgets.
> Self append works when no heap source pointer is freed, including inline-to-heap
> growth (embedded inline source remains live), full-heap CStr growth before
> append, or a nonfull heap append that fits. A nonfull heap self append requiring
> reallocation would use freed source C storage; ErrStringBufferAlias rejects that
> specific source undefined case before actions. It does not invent snapshot
> semantics for a dangling pointer. Embedded source NUL stops buffer copy at first
> NUL, regardless of source full pos.
