> # Concrete symbol service
>
> The complete selected symbol.h/cpp behavior has a concrete owner service in
> util_symbol.go. Symbol is a pointer-free scalar origin/slot/generation/tag record.
> The source global manager becomes an explicitly constructed SymbolManager which
> may be shared wherever source-wide interning identity is required. Strings from
> separate services belong to separate identity domains and cannot be reinterpreted
> by a foreign service. Numeric/null identities do not own spelling storage.
>
> NewSymbolManager/Close map initialize_symbols/finalize_symbols and the internal
> symbol-table lifetime. Intern, InternNullable and AssignString map the string
> constructor/assignment; NumericalSymbol and raw Symbol{} map numeric/null
> construction. Source equality/inequality use Go's comparable scalar record.
> IsNumerical/Number, private mark/unmark, DummySymbol, String/Display/BareString,
> Hash, Contains, Size, EqualString and Less preserve the source predicates,
> rendering, cached hash, C-string equality and byte order. SymbolToken/FromToken
> replace c_ptr/mk_symbol_from_c_ptr with checked opaque identities, not an ABI.
> BareString represents a nullable pointer through a presence flag and copies its
> text to caller-owned output. Display is the common stream/string-buffer output.
>
> Intern follows source growth-before-duplicate behavior, stores sizeof(size_t)
> bytes of cached hash immediately before the spelling, and includes its NUL.
> The source64 hash prefix has zero high bytes. Region alignment selects the
> logical page/header geometry (4 or 8); numerical symbols retain the full uint32
> AMD64 baseline on every Go target because no integer is packed into an address.
> Source tag0/null, tag1/numerical and mark+2/unmark-2 are explicit. Marked numeric
> values are not numerical. UINT32_MAX renders k!-1, hashes as UINT32_MAX and has
> source size35; numerical size is not rendered text length. Null String is
> <null> while Display is null. Contains(0) includes the spelling terminator.
> Source invalid null/marked data dereferences are explicit precondition errors.
> Less returns false for identical marked/dummy values before any dereference,
> as the source does. Its signed-char comparisons and termination-before-next-byte
> checks are retained, including nonempty-prefix ordering before negative bytes.
>
> Cold owner, region/identity/descriptors, page backing/header/directory, logs and
> hash-table backing are budgeted exactly once. The service has no Reset and
> preserves all strings until Close. Table closes before its spelling region.
> The cold mutex covers intern preparation/allocation/publication and all region
> reads/teardown; hot symbols contain no mutexes, pointers, strings or interfaces.
> The caller owns returned Go strings; no temporary budget reservation claims to
> account for an escaped output's lifetime.
>
> Source get_str inserts its transient query before spelling allocation, then
> replaces the entry pointer. The storage adaptation prepares source growth/probe
> without publishing a caller string, allocates and fills owned region backing,
> then publishes the owned key under the same lock. No query is retained after
> allocation failure. Preparation may retain grown table/descriptor capacity after
> a later failure; assignment publishes only on success. Raw arena refs remain
> owner-local; symbol records and table keys carry unique scalar origin IDs.
>
> All 23 active src/test/symbol.cpp assertions and exact foo boo foo newline were
> ported first and failed RED for missing Symbol APIs, then passed GREEN. Added
> BareString and identical-marked Less cases also went RED before their changes.
> Independent finite raw-byte identity/order checks cover both pointer geometries,
> including signed high bytes, empty strings, and source prefix termination order.
> Tests inspect physical hash prefixes and complete budget graph totals, cover
> NUL truncation, tag/null/numeric quirks, opaque tokens and foreign owners,
> constructor/failure prefixes, publication, close cleanup, source duplicate
> pre-growth failure, warm zero allocations, and concurrent canonical interning.
>
> The string->int map and scoped symbol_table trail algorithms remain separate
> unported components. A source global service should be shared by future solver
> owners when its identity domain is needed; separate services are not implicitly
> merged. Full AST/solver/proof/interpolation behavior remains unimplemented.
>

> # Concrete scoped symbol table
>
> Owned files: util_symbol_table.go, util_symbol_table_test.go and this report.
> No edits to the existing symbol service, global ledger, manifest or git metadata.
> This packet translates the complete source symbol_table<int> successful behavior
> to SymbolInt32Table. Other template payload types remain separate prerequisites;
> it does not complete parser/AST/solver symbol consumers.
>
> ## Source mapping
>
> All src/util/symbol_table.h and src/test/symbol_table.cpp were read, together with
> the applicable full core_hashtable policies and vector storage operations.
>
> | Source | Concrete behavior |
> | --- | --- |
> | symbol_table.h:33-55 key_data constructors | scalar Symbol/int32 entry, default scalar initialization |
> | :57-70 hash/equality | symbol cached-prefix hash read through borrowed manager, comparable scalar identity |
> | :72-106 hash_entry methods | null FREE, DummySymbol DELETED; no stored hash/state field; sentinel changes preserve inactive data |
> | :115-119 reset | Reset clears table, then trail/limits lengths, retaining vector capacity |
> | :121-133 find/contains | Find, FindInto and Contains; miss preserves caller output |
> | :135-137 get_scope_level | ScopeLevel |
> | :139-158 insert | scoped overwrite trails previous pair and bypasses table growth; absent scoped binding trails marked key then normal insertion; unscoped normal insertion |
> | :160-162 begin_scope | BeginScope appends scalar trail limit |
> | :164-182 end_scope | EndScope pops limit before reverse undo; new binding unmarked before erase; old pair inserted before each trail pop |
> | :184-188 append | Append traverses source physical buckets in ascending order and inserts through scoped policy |
> | :190-200 get_range/get_dom | AppendRange/AppendDom preserve caller prefixes and ascending used-bucket order |
> | test/symbol_table.cpp:24-39 | all ten ENSURE assertions preserved |
> | hashtable.h:28,244-255 | default8, power-of-two initial capacity (including1) |
> | :160-220,222-241 | rehash source bucket order, double expansion and same-capacity tombstone cleanup |
> | :286-308 | empty reset no-op; pre-clear FREE overhead decides strict >75% half shrink when capacity>16 |
> | :324-351 | ascending used-bucket iteration |
> | :353-401 | strict 4*(used+deleted)>3*capacity growth before duplicate lookup; linear probing/wrap, last tombstone wins |
> | :481-507 | hash+identity lookup stopping at FREE |
> | :533-580 | erase becomes FREE only when next slot FREE, otherwise DELETED; cleanup only deleted>used AND deleted>64 |
> | vector.h:59-97,215-224,343-365 | trail/limit cap2 then (3*cap+1)/2; reset/pop retain capacity |
>
> Raw source ABI/pointer tags are represented by existing scalar Symbol tokens.
> Source uninitialized inactive int payloads start at zero in Go; retained initialized
> payloads remain unchanged when an entry becomes FREE/DELETED. Scope limits store
> the uint32 bit pattern of the source int-vector/unsigned trail length.
>
> ## Ownership, checked preconditions and budgets
>
> The table borrows one live SymbolManager. The manager and its spelling storage
> are never charged or closed by this table. Explicit common owner domain replaces
> the source global symbol interner. Foreign spelling tokens, dead owners, null and
> Dummy sentinel keys and marked keys are rejected before storage changes. Empty
> EndScope returns ErrSymbolTableScope. Foreign-manager Append is rejected even
> when symbols are numerical. Source self-Append paths that keep the iterator valid
> are supported; an unscoped self-Append requiring rehash returns
> ErrSymbolTablePrecondition before action, guarding source iterator invalidation
> rather than inventing snapshot semantics.
>
> Owner header, actual entry backing, retained trail backing and retained scope
> backing are fully charged. The source vector header counters become owner fields
> already included in the Go header charge; there is no fictitious second charge.
> Constructor failure releases all prepared storage. Close is idempotent, refunds
> the owner's graph and does not require its borrowed manager to remain open.
> Reset/EndScope retain source vector capacity. Returned domain/range buffers belong
> to the caller and do not expose internal arrays; their output allocation is outside
> retained-owner accounting. No Go generics, unsafe, per-entry callbacks, boxing or
> Go pointers appear in hot records. Cold mutexes serialize table operations and
> Append lock ordering; shared Budget access by different owners remains caller
> serialized. Public operations lock the borrowed manager while reading hash bytes.
>
> Insertion prepares trail/table replacements before publication and accounts full
> old+new peaks. Potentially allocating multi-step undo/Append uses charged temporary
> transaction storage and preserves original table/trail/limits on predictable
> failure. Physical copies retain all FREE/DELETED/USED buckets and inactive payloads;
> they are NOT source copy-constructor rehashes. The staged undo pops its limit before
> body replay. Temporary transaction storage is an explicit Go failure-atomicity
> adaptation to source throwing allocations and memory::is_out_of_memory cleanup
> guards. Budget failures return errors instead of exposing partially undone scopes.
> Successful Reserve attempts consume the usual FailAfter prefix even if later
> preparation fails; only Used charges are refunded.
>
> Conservative direct EndScope proof: reverse restoration overwrites extant bindings,
> and erase never increases used+deleted. Initially <=75% occupied and
> deleted+marked-new-records<=64 excludes both growth and tombstone cleanup, so replay
> is failure-free without workspace. Append direct replay similarly bounds maximum
> occupancy by initial used+deleted+missing keys and checks retained trail capacity
> against every possible push. Otherwise it stages. Warm nonrehash scope/lookup and
> Append/self-Append tests measure exactly zero Go allocations, including FailAfter0.
>
> ## TDD and validation
>
> First source assertions and independent tests failed compilation due to absent
> concrete API (RED). After implementation, all source assertions and initial tests
> passed; added source-state/failure coverage before final handoff. Fourteen finite
> tests cover 2000-operation nested snapshot oracle, independent2500-operation bucket
> oracle, collisions/wrap/last tombstones, retained inactive payloads, dynamic cached
> symbol hash prefix, source strict growth/overwrite exception, real >64 tombstone

> ## Real prerequisites and proposed storage gate
>
> Existing exact numerical core algorithms provide Int/IntegerModular owners, Copy/Set/Power/Root/PerfectSquare/Divides, AddMul/SubMul, scalar polynomial Mul/Div, normalize/content, derivative, all GCD/ExtendedGCD/DivRem/ExactDiv and source Power, plus actual resource/cooperation callbacks. Root isolation does not replace factorization. Registered factorization depends on **prime_generator.cpp**, not the already ported active big-prime literal table used by modular GCD.
>
> The coefficient-storage prerequisite is real: Hensel constructs sibling `core_manager` objects over the same underlying integer owner, then passes their raw coefficient buffers among integer/prime/composite-modulus cores. Current `UPolynomialView` and `upolyVectorState` resolve through a manager-local backing directory and origin, so directly using foreign views is rejected. Deep-copying a foreign input, changing an existing core's modulus temporarily, or constructing a fake manager to route reads would add/remove source actions.
>
> **Recommended storage design to approve before coding:** extract the concrete charged backing directory into an owner-local `upolyCoefficientStore`, distinct from each arithmetic core's manager origin, descriptor pages, cached vectors, modulus and scratch. Related real core constructors borrow one actual store plus the same IntegerManager/resource/cooperation owners; public scalar views bind store origin/backing/generation, public polynomial descriptors still bind their own manager origin/slot/generation. Arithmetic uses the receiver's actual modulus/scratch while resolving shared physical coefficient storage. Each core frees only its own lexical/cache/descriptors; shared store retains directory storage until its last real owner closes, without freeing another core's live coefficient roots. Full actual store/directory/header/backing/retain counts are charged once. No mutable global registry or per-coefficient pointers/interfaces.

A separate decision is needed for source-allowed factor Swap across independently constructed storage pools: source swaps data but keeps callback managers. It cannot be implemented as coefficient copies or unconditionally claimed supported. Either approve an actual scalar storage adoption/cohort API covering those owners, with measured/failure-atomic directory-transfer adapter, or explicitly leave that general-domain branch partial. Selected source calls all use related cores sharing one integer owner; this question does not justify replacing/skipping any Berlekamp/Hensel/recombination body. A child retains the directory and child-owned arrays after parent Close. Last release frees the directory only after all owned buffers are destroyed, then closes store; borrowed scalar views become invalid at actual free/closed read. Captured store Stats returns ErrClosed after last release. No bulk freeing child buffers from a parent and no IntegerManager clone/copy. Factor owners borrow their arithmetic core, retain checked physical provenance, and require that core to outlive them (live-factor Close guard is an explicit checked lifetime adapter). Shared physical bytes/roots are attributed once through store Stats; sums across arithmetic-core Stats must not double-count shared arrays. > # Dense upolynomial selected core: implementation held for coordinator review
>
> Source: `src/math/polynomial/upolynomial.h/.cpp`, `util/vector.h`, `util/mpz.h`, `_scoped_numeral_vector`, actual registered `src/test/upolynomial.cpp`. The selected concrete storage/arithmetic/sign-evaluation packet is implemented and frozen after the gates below. This is a selected algorithm/ownership packet in the full upolynomial→algebraic→arithmetic plugin backend; full GCD, factorization, Sturm/isolation/refinement, multivariate conversion and algebraic operations remain OPEN.
>
> ## Selected source surface
>
> Complete actual coefficient-vector storage/lifetime and selected core/derived manager ctor/temp/destructor actions, checkpoint, mode access/configuration, reset/trim/set_size/degree and trim-mutating is_zero/is_const, raw integer and rational coefficient set, in-place/output negation, add/sub/mul, derivative, equality, power, scalar coefficient multiplication, and all three finite-point sign-evaluation overloads plus zero/±infinity. Include source helper bodies and precise aliases. Primitive/content normalization, division/exact division/GCD/monic/factors/sequences and the other transformation/root algorithms are explicitly later packets; do not advertise fake methods for them.
>
> Power is included because actual registered basic `tst1` calls it and it needs only the selected arithmetic: source uses repeated multiplication, not binary exponentiation. General polynomial display and its printer/TRACE events remain OPEN pending a separately audited owned formatter (including source SMT2 single-term fallthrough defect); printing examples is not an assertion port.
>
> ## Concrete public API
>
> `NewUPolynomialManager(UPolynomialConfig{Integer *IntegerManager, Checkpoint func() bool, Cooperation func() error}) (*UPolynomialManager,error)` owns actual source core/derived state and borrows one real IntegerManager and limit service. Checkpoint is required and bound to actual g3 utilReslimit.inc; no nil/default-success substitute. Cooperation is also required: it binds the coordinator's actual source `_NO_OMP_` cooperation service, preserving runtime enable state and call order.
>
> Public polynomial owners are scalar `UPolynomial` tokens with private origin/slot/generation fields. Explicit `NewPolynomial`, `DelPolynomial(*UPolynomial)`, `Copy(dst,src)`, `Swap(a,b)`; size/capacity/degree, source `Reserve`, scoped `Resize`/`Shrink`/`PushCoefficient`/`PopCoefficient` adapters and scalar coefficient read/write actions. No public owning Go slices or raw numeric pointers; `ReadCoefficient(p,i,*Int)` deep-copies through the actual numeral manager, `SetCoefficient` performs actual modular set without automatically trimming. The caller owns read results. `Reset`, `Trim`, `SetSize`, `IsZero`, `IsConst`, `NegInPlace`, `Neg`, `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Derivative`, `Equal`, `Power`, `MulScalar`, plus source mode forwarding `SetZ`, `SetZP`, `SetZPUint64`, `Modular`, `Field`, `NumeralManager`, `IntegerManager` and private borrowed modulus access.
>
> Explicit raw-source array overloads use a scalar `UPolynomialView` (origin, physical backing slot/generation, start/count), obtained by `View` while owning polynomial remains valid. `SetView`, `NegViewInPlace`, `MulScalarView`, `NegView`, `AddViews`, `SubViews`, `MulViews`, `DerivativeView`, `EqualViews`, `PowerView`, and private borrowed actual coefficient access preserve source base-pointer aliases and captured physical lifetime. Read guards are at actual dereferences, not a blanket logical-size restriction; source g3debug subscript assertions versus initialized physical extent are distinct. Relocation/free invalidates views, swap transfers backing ownership without invalidating physical views. Public whole-polynomial methods take source size/base once before operation and reuse these exact algorithms.
>
> `SetInts(p,[]Int)` and `SetRationals(p,[]Rational)` borrow caller arrays only for the call and require the raw common integer owner contract. The latter source copies numerators, only debug-checks integrality, and does not silently multiply denominators or use alternate coefficients. Owned RationalService values need their separate explicit raw-copy boundary later; no illegal shallow owning rational copy.
>
> Derived sign methods: `EvalSignInt(view,*Int)`, `EvalSignRational(view,*Rational)`, `EvalSignBinary(view,*BinaryRational)` and `EvalSignZero/PlusInfinity/MinusInfinity(view)` return `(int,error)`. Inputs must borrow the same real underlying IntegerManager as source's raw numeral pointers. Sign access is source is_zero then is_pos, not a mathematical sign computed by an unrelated manager. No general value-evaluation method is invented: source exposes sign evaluation here.
>
> `Close` requires no live external polynomial owners, refusing before destruction while they exist; no implicit external-reference ownership release or closing the borrowed integer/limit owner. Actual users explicitly close their vectors first. Zero/nil/shallow owner copies are typed rejected domains via charged self metadata. Stats expose actual owner, metadata/page/directory, backing and child-manager bytes without double-counting the borrowed integer graph.
>
> ## Concrete storage and physical budget
>
> Each coefficient is an actual named `Int` record; no token re-encoding, boxed value, per-coefficient pointer, unsafe or generics. Manager-owned scalar vector metadata (size/capacity/initialized/backing ID) lives in concrete typed descriptor pages. External scalar handles select descriptor rows; scratch vector descriptors are embedded in the actual charged cold owner. A cold backing directory owns each actual variable `[]Int` allocation, never exposing a slice as a polynomial. This is the source vector's one owned physical coefficient array, not COW or slice-copy polynomial semantics. The directory holds one slice header per physical array, not one Go object/pointer per coefficient; all directory capacities and row pages are charged, including overlap. Scalar backing IDs/generations model physical pointer validity.
>
> Actual source `mpz` has a user-defined move constructor, so it is NOT trivially copyable. Source `svector<mpz>` growth allocates new capacity, publishes new backing, transfers logical numeral ownership in ascending order, destroys moved-from logical records, then frees old backing. Only logical entries move: initialized inactive capacity is not memcpy-preserved. Preserve old m_val after pointer transfer; stale unused cells are not owning roots. Source resize publishes the new logical size before ascending default construction. Reserve is logical growth, not capacity-only. Capacities are0→2→3→5…, with exact uint32 source multiplication/header arithmetic and selected LP64 sizeof(mpz)=16/header8 bounds independently of actual Go Int stride and host representability. Actual backing/cold headers, rather than fictional source bytes, determine budget charges. Source capacity's real default-initialized prefix is tracked to permit release retained accesses safely and detect uninitialized reads.
>
> Source manager owns16 core vectors: basic1, division2, exact-division1, GCD2, CRA1, modular-GCD6, square-free2, power1. The actual derived manager adds5 more: db, dbab1, dbab2, translation, push. All21 real empty descriptors exist from constructor; pending algorithms are not callable stubs. Core uses the committed real IntegerModularManager; its actual cold child header is charged separately from the parent pointer field once. Parent constructor reservation/source-layout adaptation and child allocation prefixes are documented.
>
> Destruction order matters: derived destructor resets its5 vectors in declaration order, then member destructors free their backings in reverse order. Base destructor resets its16 vectors in explicit source order, then member destructors free their backings in reverse order; its embedded modular manager destructor follows and releases its seven actual numerals. Do not simply iterate all21 vectors in one convenient order. Local scoped evaluation numerals use actual lexical reverse destruction; safe Go failure cleanup is recorded separately from raw MPZ locals lacking destructors.
>
> ## Actual selected algorithms/action order
>
> - Trim scans highest coefficient downward, tests source numeral is_zero, DELs each zero, then publishes shrunk size. `set_size` asserts oldsize>=newsize only in debug, DELs old suffix ascending, shrinks, then trims. `Reset` calls set_size0; it retains vector capacity.
> - Set(Int view) detects nonnull physical base pointer equality first and returns after debug equality-size assertion. Even a zero-count view of a nonempty same-base vector is release no-op, not a reset. Otherwise reserve, copy/normalize each coefficient ascending, then set_size/trim. Rational set reserves first, checks each rational integral in debug, copies its actual numerator, then trims. Numeric failure keeps copied prefix and real expanded size.
> - In-place negation simply negates/normalizes each coefficient ascending, without trimming. Output negation uses basic scratch, copying then negating each coefficient, set_size/trim, then swaps vector ownership. Add/sub reserve max size, operate overlap ascending, copy each remaining left then right tail (right sub tail copied then negated), trim, then swap. Scratch partial failure remains owned; output stays until actual swap. No whole-operation rollback or result slice is invented.
> - Mul resets basic scratch for either zero-size input. Otherwise computes source unsigned size1+size2−1, reserves, RESETs every result coefficient, swaps input order only when first size<second, then performs checkpoint BEFORE each outer row including zero rows. Zero input coefficients skip arithmetic; every nonzero pair executes actual AddMul(result,a,b,result). Trim then swap; partial cancellation/failure leaves scratch coefficient prefixes intact.
> - Derivative writes directly to output (not basic scratch): reserve size−1, for i1…size−1 construct raw local d, modular Set(d,i), Mul(p[i],d,out[i−1]), then set_size/trim. In-place ascending writes do not clobber later reads. Source raw d has no explicit DEL; physically representable selected LP64 vector bounds keep i below INT32_MAX, so it remains inline; no invented destructor action. This invariant requires a scalar source-extent test.
> - Equality first size comparison, then raw numeral EQ ascending, stopping at first mismatch. It does not trim operands or equate differently sized all-zero forms.
> - Power k0 debug-asserts nonempty input, reserve1/set1/set_size; release empty^0 still follows finite source actions. k1/empty input/constant1 branch uses Set. Otherwise Set input into power scratch, then repeat actual Mul(powerScratch,input,powerScratch) for i1…k−1 and swap into output. The `#if 0` binary-power block is inactive and explicitly not ported as the active algorithm.
> - Scalar multiplication zero resets vector; nonzero tests one before ascending Mul and does not trim automatically.
> - Integer sign evaluation: empty0, singleton sign directly; scoped r initialized from last coefficient, Horner descending using Mul for zero coefficient or AddMul(coefficient,r,point,r), final sign, lexical local DEL. No checkpoint exists in this loop.
> - Rational sign evaluation computes numerator-scaled Horner: scoped denominatorPower first, then r, then ak; each nonzero coefficient Mul(a,denPower,ak)/AddMul(ak,r,num,r); every iteration also multiplies denominatorPower by denominator, including final unused multiplication. It returns sign of scaled value, even for noncanonical negative denominators; no RationalManager Horner replacement.
> - Binary sign evaluation scopes r then ak, uses actual borrowed numerator and exponent, k_i uint32 initialized k and increments k_i+=k AFTER each row, including final row. Each nonzero coefficient Mul2k(a,k_i,ak)/AddMul; zero coefficient Mul only. Preserve uint32 wrap, typed actual shift bounds, and source operand/lifetime actions.
> - Zero/infinity signs access first/last coefficient as source; minus infinity flips by degree parity. No trim/default canonicalization is added.

> ## All transform methods used by the source consumers
>
> Provide in-place raw `...ViewInPlace(v,...)` plus the five header-defined translate-to-buffer delegations `...(v,...,out UPolynomial)` that perform Set before transformation. Whole-polynomial convenience wrappers may delegate through actual wholeView; they do not substitute algorithms.
>
> | Source | Concrete method family and exact actions |
> |---|---|
> | translate | `TranslateOne`: sz<=1 shortcut; outer i=1..n checkpoint, ascending k=n-i..n-1 Add |
> | translate_k | `TranslatePowerTwo`: preserve the **actual shadowed inner k**, not the stated mathematical x+2^argument behavior; auxiliary local created after shortcut; Mul2k(p[index+1],index,aux), Add; outer checkpoint. Public argument remains present but ignored by the actual source inner shift |
> | translate_z | `TranslateInteger`: outer checkpoint, ascending AddMul(p[k],c,p[k+1],p[k]); c remains a borrowed scalar reference, not snapshotted |
> | translate_bq | `TranslateBinary`: compose_2kn first; then outer checkpoint; first AddMul, ascending Mul2k/AddMul, final leading Mul2k each iteration; real b.num/b.k reads at the source sites |
> | translate_q | `TranslateRational`: compose_an with raw denominator first; outer checkpoint, first AddMul, inner Mul by denominator then AddMul by numerator, final leading Mul; no normalization/trim added |
> | compose_2n_p_x_div_2 | `ComposeTwoDegreeDivideX`: ascending all-but-leading shifts n..1, no checkpoints/zero skip |
> | compose_2kn_p_x_div_2k | `ComposePowerTwoDegreeDivideX`: k_i=k*sz uint32, subtract k before each coefficient, IsZero then Mul2k; preserve wrapped scalar arithmetic |
> | compose_p_2k_x | `ComposePowerTwoX`: i=1..sz-1 Mul2k then k_i+=k, no zero skip/checkpoint |
> | compose_an_p_x_div_a | `ComposeIntegerDegreeDivideX`: lexical a_i=Copy(a), descending coefficients; skip-zero Mul but always final power Mul, including last unused power update |
> | compose_p_b_x integer | `ComposeIntegerX`: lexical b_i=Copy(b), ascending i=1; skip-zero coefficient Mul, unconditional b_i*=b even after last coefficient |
> | compose_p_b_x binary | `ComposeBinaryX`: local c_i=1, k_i=k*sz; ascending subtract/IsZero/Mul2k/Mul, unconditional power update each coefficient, actual final k_i==0 debug assertion |
> | compose_p_q_x | `ComposeRationalX`: local bc=Power(den,sz-1), ascending skip-zero Mul, except last coefficient Div(bc,den) THEN Mul(bc,num); preserve actual body despite reversed comment |
> | p_minus_x | `PMinusX`: ascending IsZero before parity check, Neg only odd nonzero coefficients |
> | p_1_div_x | `Reciprocal`: source shortcut, source j>=1 assertion, swap actual coefficient ownership until indices meet; no normalization despite introducing leading zeros |

Temporary raw numerals always receive explicit Go failure cleanup (safe exception adapter); output coefficient mutation, metadata and completed callback prefixes remain as source. > ## Concrete storage / lifetime / failure proposal
>
> The source sequence is **flat**, not a vector of owning polynomial objects: one coefficient numeral_vector and two unsigned_vector arrays. Proposed private `upolySequenceState` stores named `coefficients upolyVectorState`, and concrete `begins` and `sizes` uint32 vector states. No per-row pointers/slices/objects, no duplicated owning Int tokens. The existing manager cold backing directory owns the coefficient array; metadata vectors own actual []uint32 backing with capacity/size fields. Each independently follows source2→3→5… growth, uint32 source stride4/header8 arithmetic and separately checked actual host representability. Coefficient growth uses the existing exact nontrivial mpz move route and LP64source16/header8 guard. Charge cold owner header once (actual reflect.Size), every full backing capacity, old+new growth peaks and actual directory overhead. Do not collapse the three source allocations into one pre-reservation.
>
> External `UPolynomialSequence` is one cold owner with self guard and borrowed manager; internal algorithms use lexical state with no fabricated cold heap allocation. Constructor reserves before Go owner allocation. Source implicit owning copies are unsafe in Go: shallow owner copies rejected; no Clone/Assign invented as a source method. Metadata fields remain concrete scalar/slice infrastructure in the cold owner, not boxed hot entries. A source scoped destructor first runs manager Reset, then implicit member vector destruction frees sizes, begins, coefficients in reverse declaration order. Reset retains capacity and destroys flat numerals ascending; explicit Close resets then frees in that exact member order. A lexical local state does the same in deferred source scope cleanup.
>
> Proposed minimal coordinated existing-manager hook (requires approval before code): `liveSequences uint32` tracked at external constructor/Close and checked by manager Close, like its existing live-polynomial precondition. No per-sequence registry or manager pointer in hot records; external sequence must close before borrowed manager/numeric owners. Sequence stats separately report header/metadata/coeff backing and physical numeric roots without double charging manager-directory backing. Whole graph plateau is checked through shared Budget plus manager/sequence ownership attribution. If coordinator prefers no existing-field hook, require an explicit caller close-order contract and document that manager cannot enforce outstanding sequence ownership; do not pretend source reset closes the numeric owner.
>
> Push order is observable: begins.push(coeffsize), sizes.push(count), then each coefficient default push publishes coefficient size BEFORE Copy/Swap. A refusal can leave begins longer than sizes, or a declared row longer than initialized coefficient payload; preserve these real prefixes. Size returns sizes logical length. RowView uses begins and row size and returns a captured scalar coefficient backing/start/count; it must not eagerly reject an oversized declared row. Actual later Read/Eval checks initialized bound/generation. A zero-count stale view performs no read. Metadata reallocation does not invalidate captured coefficient pointers; coefficient reallocation does. Reset preserves physical backing and initialized scalar slots while Del clears owned values; valid retained pointer slots observe actual cleared values. Close/reallocation invalidates generation. Self-input Copy/Move uses source read timing AFTER destination coefficient growth; a captured pointer into freed old backing must fail at that actual read, not be kept alive by a Go slice snapshot. No owning copy of a view or manager-wide preflight.
>
> Builders Reset output first. Pair copies first then second; unary copies p before derivative; Tarski copies a before derivative/mul; Fourier publishes even an empty first row. Sturm has no artificial empty/constant guard: real core signed-remainder debug assertions/defined release shortcuts decide outcome. A refused push retains row metadata/default/coefficient prefix. Cancellation in actual srem retains its source scratch counter/output mutations and already appended rows; lexical r/derivative/product cleanup still releases numerals. Independent failure accounting includes legitimate sequence coefficients and real manager cache roots before any formatting/Del/Close. No all-or-nothing sequence replacement.
>
> Borrowed Int/BinaryRational/Rational arguments are read from actual private numerator/denominator fields in package mpnum, avoiding allocation-adding public owning extraction. Coefficient/numeric owner must be compatible with the real IntegerManager; stale/foreign/closed failures happen at actual numerical reads. DescatesInterval takes an actual borrowed BinaryRationalManager and uses its real Sub/Copy/Neg, with explicit same-integer-owner precondition if required by current manager contract. No fake numeric service or owner-local success callback.

> # Arena foundation packet
>
> This packet implements B7's independent slot/slab/budget storage contracts, not
> the complete C++ region allocator or the complete solver memory subsystem.
>
> ## Source mapping and scope
>
> The slab representation is the intentional Go ownership adaptation specified by
> GO_PORT_PLAN.md B6/B7. It is not a line-for-line translation of region.cpp.
> The source `src/test/region.cpp::tst1` is empty (TODO), so it contains no assertions
> to translate. Source region branches were read, and remain explicitly open:
>
> | Source method/branch | Counterpart or remaining work |
> | --- | --- |
> | region constructor/default-page allocation | Slab constructor defines page policy; scoped region construction remains open |
> | region destructor / debug destructor | Slab.Close drops backing pages and ledger after caller cleanup; region teardown remains open |
> | allocate: in-page, new default page, large dedicated page | Slab.Allocate implements fixed-record growth only; variable payload and dedicated region pages remain open |
> | recycle_curr_page | Slab.TrimFreePages drops wholly dead fixed-record pages, retains generation ledger; region page recycle remains open |
> | reset, release/default-page reuse | Slab.Reset invalidates live records, retains ledger, drops record pages; region reset remains open |
> | push_scope/pop_scope, counted pop_scope | Not implemented; required by arena/region.go and domain cleanup/trail integration |
> | display_mem_stats | Slab.Stats exposes fixed-record capacity, metadata, directory and liveness; source textual region diagnostic remains open |
> | placement new/delete and address alignment | Pointer-free Go typed records replace placement allocation; no unsafe or C layout is required |
> | debug per-object chunks/scopes | Not translated; Go checked/release domain handles are outside this package |
>
> ## API and ownership
>
> - Slots/generations are uint32; slot zero and generation zero are invalid.
> - Concrete slab record audits use ValidateRecordType recursively. Pointers, strings, slices, maps, interfaces,
>   funcs, chans, unsafe.Pointer, and uintptr are rejected, including nested
>   fields and arrays. Arrays/structs of numeric scalars are accepted.
> - Config defaults PageSize to 1024, SlotLimit to MaxUint32; pages must have a
>   power-of-two size. Make-length arithmetic is guarded on 32-bit hosts.
> - Allocate publishes a zero record, stable slot and increasing generation only
>   after predictable budget checks. Read copies records; Write updates them.
>   There are no pointer/slice borrows or callbacks across page growth.
> - Recycle requires domain destruction/cleanup to have run beforehand. It
>   zeros the record, invalidates liveness and links the slot for reuse.
>   MaxUint32 generation permanently retires the slot; it never wraps.
> - TrimFreePages preserves all metadata. Reset invalidates all live records
>   after caller cleanup and drops record pages. Close releases records and
>   metadata and permanently rejects operations. All three are owner operations.
> - A Slab does not run constructors, destructors, source reset hooks, logical
>   reference release, or vector cleanup. Constructed-object pools must preserve
>   their pooled state in a separate domain policy; generic Recycle zeroes records.
> - Budget is single-owner: NewBudget(limit), Reserve, Release, Used, Limit,
>   FailAfter. Nil is unlimited; limit zero allows zero bytes. Injected failures
>   affect reservations, never warmed allocations. Release underflow panics as
>   an ownership invariant violation.
> - Budget charges actual typed backing-array capacity (including unused page
>   slots), scalar metadata, and directory capacity. Directory copying reserves
>   peak old+new capacity before publication. Owners separately account for cold
>   slab/control headers, external scratch and cleanup reserves; these are not
>   slab backing storage. Host runtime allocator overhead/OOM is not recoverable
>   or accounted as exact process memory by this abstraction.
> - Slot-only Read/Write cannot detect a stale slot after reuse. IsLive requires
>   a generation. Public owner/domain validation and checked widened handles
>   remain coordinator/domain responsibilities.
>
> ## Tests and evidence
>
> Tests were written first. `go test ./arena` initially failed to compile with
> undefined NewSlab/Config/errors (RED). Implementation then passed those tests.
> A second RED test exposed missing peak directory accounting; the fix passed.
>
> Independent deterministic state-machine oracle: 4,000 operations, 17-slot
> limit, 2-record pages, live/token/value maps independent of allocator metadata.
> FuzzArenaOps uses at most 512 operations, 7 slots and 2-record pages with the
> same independently recorded token/value expectations. No test reads C++ files,
> uses a reference executable, neighboring repository, network, or Python.
> Source contains no applicable region test assertions beyond its empty TODO.
>
> Verification on go1.26.4-pont-onethread, linux/amd64:
>
> - CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./arena: PASS.
> - CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags=g3checked ./arena: PASS; slab semantics are
>   identical under both tags (domain checked handles remain outside this packet).
> - go vet ./arena: PASS.
> - FuzzArenaOps, 3 seconds, 2 workers: PASS, 3,338 executions, 27 new interesting.
> - CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./arena: PASS.
> - CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build ./arena: PASS.
> - GOARCH=386 go test ./arena: runner failed with `signal: bad system call`;
>   no actual 32-bit execution acceptance is claimed.
> - BenchmarkSlabWarm, 200ms, Ryzen Threadripper 3960X: 25.38 ns/op,
>   0 B/op, 0 allocs/op. This is a warm fixed-record cycle, not a solver benchmark
>   or comparative speedup. AllocsPerRun additionally requires exactly zero
>   allocations for allocate/write/read/recycle inside existing pages.
>
> Subsequent tool cache/temp/artifact locations are golang/.cache. The initial
> RED command used the default Go cache/temp locations before the additional user
> restriction was relayed; it may have produced external compiler cache writes.
> All authored source/status files are inside golang/arena.
>
> ## Remaining requirements
>
> words.go, vectors.go, region.go, marked rollback, payload descriptors/classes,
> large dedicated pages, optional compaction, region/trail domain cleanup and
> source debug/release region conformance are unimplemented. Public owner/domain
> handle checks, actual wasm execution, actual 32-bit execution and integrated
> source destruction/constructed-pool behavior require later packets. No complete
> allocator/full-fork milestone is asserted by this packet.
>
> # Variable payload packet
>
> The later `words.go` and `vectors.go` packet implements B8's non-compacting typed
> payload representation. The earlier statement that those files are unimplemented
> describes the first packet only; marked regions and compaction remain open.
>
> ## Contracts and ownership
>
> VectorRef contains only a descriptor Slot/Generation. Every nonempty/reserved
> vector owns one Slab descriptor and one geometric-class block. Descriptor
> identity remains stable through Reserve/Resize/Append. Payload locations are
> private scalar page/offset/length/capacity fields; no backing slices escape.
> Zero VectorRef denotes an allocation-free empty vector. Allocate(0,nonzero)
> reserves a live descriptor. Free zero succeeds; IsLive zero is false.
>
> VectorConfig.PageSize is a power-of-two element count, default 16384; this is
> 64 KiB for Words (uint32) and 128 KiB for uint64 checked tokens. Descriptors.Budget
> unambiguously charges descriptor slab, payload data, scalar block free links,
> and page-directory capacity. Large classes use a dedicated single-block page.
> Class capacity is the least power of two at least the requested capacity;
> capacities above 2^31 and target-specific oversized make extents fail explicitly.
>
> Read/Write check logical length and generation. Reserve copies logical contents
> then publishes the new location within one owner operation. Resize retains
> capacity when shrinking and clears discarded values; subsequent growth is zero
> initialized. Free always releases the original capacity extent, clears records,
> and invalidates/recycles its descriptor. No element constructors, callbacks,
> destructors, domain handle retains/releases, or ownership transfer are inferred
> from a scalar records. Domain cleanup must precede truncation/free/reset/close.
>
> Failed creation leaves no live descriptor or payload, but may retain newly
> allocated reusable descriptor capacity and generation metadata. Those bytes
> remain charged and visible in Stats, and Close releases them. Failed growth of
> an existing vector preserves identity/content/length/capacity. Directory growth
> charges peak old+new directory bytes; copying also retains the old payload until
> publication. No source addresses, page indices, or empty vector values are
> public identities. Trim drops wholly free payload/descriptor record pages only;
> generation metadata and deterministic page class headers survive. Reset drops
> payloads and invalidates descriptors; Close releases all arrays/metadata.
>
> ## Source mapping
>
> | Source behavior | Storage counterpart / limitation |
> | --- | --- |
> | vector constructor/default empty and buffer empty | Zero VectorRef; no separate empty allocation |
> | vector size/capacity/operator[] and buffer get/set | Len/Cap/Read/Write, explicit bounds errors rather than debug-only unchecked accesses |
> | vector expand_vector and buffer expand | Reserve relocates scalar contents into geometric pooled classes; 1.5x vector growth is intentionally not copied into the storage-class policy |
> | vector/buffer push_back | Append, zero-growth then write |
> | vector resize/shrink, buffer resize/shrink/reset | Resize including zero length preserves reserved extent; owner-local allocator Reset additionally drops payload pages |
> | vector/buffer pop_back/back | Read(last index) followed by Resize(length-1); no standalone source container facade claimed |
> | vector destroy/free_memory/finalize, buffer free_memory/finalize | Free, allocator Trim/Close; domain destructors remain explicit caller obligations |
> | vector copy/move/assignment/swap/iterators and buffer copy/assignment/append/set_end | Not implemented as source container APIs; later util/domain port must provide these behaviors |
> | ptr_scoped_buffer element deletion from src/test/buffer.cpp | Not translated here; pointer ownership conflicts with scalar payload storage and belongs in a domain wrapper |
>
> Finite assertions from `src/test/vector.cpp::tst1` are ported in
> TestSourceVectorTst1: initial emptiness, 1000 ordered pushes and readbacks,
> capacity >= length, forward traversal, reverse back/pop, final empty length.
> Its unbounded billion-element allocation loop becomes a finite budget-error
> regression. This does not claim runtime host OOM recovery. The actual C++ source
> growth policy and owning element destructor behavior remain separate from B8's
> intentional storage-class adaptation.
>
> ## Verification
>
> The new vector tests first produced RED undefined NewVectors/NewWords/VectorRef
> compile failures, then passed after implementation. Tests include 2000 bounded
> state-machine operations with independent Go slice/value models, repeated
> grow/shrink/free plateau, live block non-overlap, payload preservation across
> dedicated large-page growth, reserved-empty semantics, generation rejection,
> failure cleanup, original capacity preservation, peak directory budgets and
> pointer-freedom rejection.
>
> - CGO_ENABLED=0 native and g3checked arena tests: PASS, including uint64 vectors.
> - go vet ./arena: PASS.
> - js/wasm and wasip1/wasm package cross-builds: PASS.
> - GOARCH=386 test binary compilation: PASS. Actual 386 execution remains
>   unverified following the prior host bad-system-call failure.
> - BenchmarkVectorWarm, 200ms, same host/toolchain as first packet:
>   72.60 ns/op, 0 B/op, 0 allocs/op for warm words allocate/write/read/free.
>   AllocsPerRun also verifies exact zero allocations for the bounded warm cycle.
>
> No compaction method is offered. Safe-point relocation, peak old+new payload
> tables and domain raw-offset registration remain deferred together. Region
> marks/rollback, byte/string pools, domain cleanup, source container facades,
> actual wasm execution and full solver integration remain incomplete. No shared
> manifest or previously agreed slab/budget interface was modified by this packet.
>
> # Typed marked-region packet
>
> `region.go` now supplies independent typed marked storage. Earlier references
> to its absence describe preceding packets. This packet does not implement solver
> trail variants or the raw byte/address source allocator layout.
>
> Region32/Region64 own Slab32/Slab64, a scalar RegionRef allocation log and scalar
> serial/length mark records. RegionRef carries Slot/Generation; RegionMark is an
> opaque cold owner identity pointer plus serial token. The mark's owner pointer
> is not stored in hot record or mark backing arrays. Marks are never reused:
> serial exhaustion permanently prevents new marks, even after Reset. Every
> Allocate explicitly writes its initial scalar records. Reads copy values; no raw
> pointer or slice borrow exists. Individual object free is deliberately absent.
>
> Mark/Rollback are strictly nested. Rollback rejects zero, foreign, consumed and
> non-top marks. PopScopes explicitly supports a validated counted pop. Reset
> cleans all records, including base-level allocations, and invalidates all marks.
> Close is idempotent and drops backing arrays and ledger. TrimFreePages returns
> an error so callback reentrancy can be rejected; it drops only fully dead record
> pages while retaining generation metadata and reusable scalar control arrays.
>
> The transient Cleanup32/Cleanup64 parameter is never stored as a trail closure. It runs
> in reverse allocation order; every target record stays live through *all*
> callbacks, after which a separate pass recycles records. This is a documented
> storage cleanup contract, not a claim that source trail objects individually
> remain live after source undo/destruction. Reads/Stats are allowed in callbacks;
> Allocate/Write/Mark/Rollback/PopScopes/Reset/Trim/Close reject reentrant mutation.
> A callback panic preserves allocator records/log/marks and clears the busy flag.
> External callback side effects cannot be rolled back; repeated cleanup after
> panic is not promised safe. A nil cleanup means caller cleanup already ran.
>
> Budget checks reserve peak old+new log/mark backing capacity before copying.
> An injected/limit failure during those growth steps leaves that array and budget
> unchanged. If subsequent slab allocation fails, already prepared reusable log
> capacity may remain retained/charged; no live region record is published.
> Stats separates log/mark bytes and slab capacity/metadata. Cold owner headers,
> caller scratch and source cleanup reserves remain explicit owner responsibilities.
>
> ## Source mapping and inspection
>
> Read source region.h/.cpp/trail.h plus object_allocator.h,
> small_object_allocator.h and both allocator tests before implementation.
> `src/test/region.cpp::tst1` is still only TODO, and no dedicated source trail
> test file exists. `src/test/small_object_allocator.cpp` exercises allocation
> reuse but contains no ENSURE assertions. `src/test/object_allocator.cpp`
> asserts coefficient reset, worker capacity and constructed/destructed balance;
> those belong to its reset-only constructed pool. This region does not substitute
> zero/reconstruction for that pool's reset-only lifecycle or claim its port.
>
> | Executable source behavior | Typed counterpart / limit |
> | --- | --- |
> | region allocate/default pages and debug chunks | Region.Allocate uses stable typed slab records, not source address alignment/chunks |
> | region push_scope mark(page,cursor,previous) | Mark logs typed used length and serial, explicit nesting |
> | region pop_scope and counted pop | Rollback/PopScopes invalidate only suffix allocations, preserving prefix and generation ledger |
> | region reset/recycle/default-page reuse | Reset recycles all typed records while preserving reusable capacity; lazy typed allocation differs from source eagerly keeping one default page |
> | region destructor/display_mem_stats | Close releases all backing metadata; Stats reports typed capacity, not source textual pointer/chunk diagnostics |
> | region large allocation and placement operators | Variable payload extents are Words/Vectors; this Region is fixed-record typed storage, no source address API |
> | undo_trail_stack reverse loop/old_size assertion | Reverse transient cleanup followed by suffix truncation, checked mark lengths; independent scalar undo-state oracle |
> | trail_stack reset base-level undo | Reset includes records before the first scope |
> | trail_stack push_scope/pop_scope | Mark/PopScopes coordinate typed record reclamation only; real domain undo entries and subsystem callbacks remain open |
> | value/reset_flag/restore_size/vector/map/ref/new_obj trail subclasses | Not translated by generic storage; tagged domain dispatch and logical ownership remain higher-layer work |
>

>

> # Concrete constructed scalar pool packet
>
> `pool32.go` supplies the approved **constructed=true scalar policy subset** of
> `src/util/object_allocator.h`. It is not a whole source-template port and does
> not complete `small_object_allocator` or the real rational-cell source tests.
> It introduces no generics, per-record interface/closure, intrusive free-list
> overwrite, unsafe operation, or edits to existing slabs/vectors/regions.
>
> ## Source lifecycle and API
>
> Pool32Config defaults to 8 workers and 1024 scalar records/page, exactly the
> source constants (`object_allocator.h:26`). SlotLimit is a testable physical
> slot limit **per worker region**. Each worker eagerly owns an empty first page;
> filling a page immediately prepares another empty page, including at a configured
> slot limit. A fresh initialized slot invokes the one owner-level Construct
> dispatcher once. A recycled slot invokes neither Construct nor Destroy.
>
> Pool32Policy.Reset is called on Recycle before publishing the ref onto the
> chosen worker's separate LIFO free array. It returns the retained scalar state.
> Nil Reset is the source do-nothing reset policy, so recycled state survives
> unchanged. Nil Construct gives the concrete scalar zero initializer.
> Pool32Policy.Destroy runs once per initialized record on Reset/Close, including
> records on free lists and records retired after generation exhaustion.
> DisableDestructors suppresses Destroy only. No destructor runs on Recycle.
> Reset destroys old objects and creates fresh construction opportunities while
> preserving generations; Close is idempotent and releases all backing storage.
>
> Source destructor traversal is preserved: workers in order, last partially used
> page first, then earlier full pages in allocation order; an eager empty tail page
> has no initialized values to destroy (`object_allocator.h:78`). The source's
> header prose says destructors run only on allocator deletion, but its executable
> region::reset calls free_memory and therefore runs them during Reset too
> (`:118`). The implementation follows the executable path.
>
> Pool32Ref stores original RegionWorker, Slot and Generation. Cross-worker recycle
> puts that ref on the destination worker's free list without changing physical
> ownership. Reallocation increments its generation; old refs never revive after
> reuse or Reset. Exhaustion retires the slot permanently. Its constructed value
> survives retirement until the single applicable Reset/Close destructor.
>
> Allocate/Recycle use worker zero in nonconcurrent mode. AllocateWorker/
> RecycleWorker and the cold Pool32Worker wrapper require concurrent mode.
> ReserveWorkers and Reset reject concurrent mode, matching source assertions.
> Worker wrappers survive reserve and mode toggles. Close works in either mode,
> as the source destructor does. Read/Write/IsLive validate live generation;
> public context-owner validation remains the domain wrapper's responsibility.
>
> A cold owner mutex serializes metadata, dispatch and budget mutation. Worker
> partitions and destination semantics are preserved, but source parallel throughput
> is not claimed. Policy callbacks **must not call methods on the same pool**,
> because that mutex is held; doing so would deadlock. Callbacks must not panic.
> External callback effects are not transactional, and reuse/retry after a panic
> is not supported. This is an explicit caller invariant for the finite dispatcher
> policy. Shared budgets across other owners require external synchronization.
>
> Budget accounts record/ledger pages, worker/page directories, separate free
> arrays and Reset scratch. Page/directory and free-array growth charges old+new
> capacity. Reset preallocates replacement first pages and scratch while old pages
> still exist, failing before destructor effects. Page-boundary growth is checked
> before Construct, and free-array growth before Reset policy effects. This is a
> predictable-limit adaptation: the C++ source runs construction/reset before a
> subsequent vector/page allocation can fail. No exact recovery of host runtime OOM
> is claimed. Failed multi-step preparation may retain reusable charged capacity,
> but never publishes a new constructed record or invokes its Construct callback.
> Cold owner/policy headers and callback-owned allocations are separately budgeted
> by the caller. Generation/tombstone ledgers remain measurable after Reset.
>

> # Concrete SmallBytes release pooled + direct storage packet
>
> Owned files: `small_bytes.go`, `small_bytes_test.go`, this status append. No
> shared slab/vector contract, other package, manifest or git changes. No generics,
> unsafe, per-record interface or escaped byte slices.
>
> `SmallBytesConfig` selects source pointer-width size policy (Alignment4/8,
> explicit default8), source default ChunkSize8192-2*Alignment, and Descriptors
> Config for slot/page/budget controls. Alignment is a size-class policy, not a
> physical Go pointer-alignment promise. Tiny chunks exercise exact boundaries.
> `SmallBytesRef` is a checked pointer-free Slot/Generation descriptor identity;
> internal existing concrete descriptorSlab stores chunk/offset/size/capacity.
>
> | Method/behavior | Source mapping and adaptation |
> | --- | --- |
> | construction | util/small_object_allocator.h:27-38 constants/lists/counters; cpp:28-36 empty initialization |
> | Allocate(0) | cpp:97-98 null; distinguished zero ref, no backing allocation |
> | pooled Allocate | cpp:111-137 ceil(size/Alignment) class, LIFO free list, strict new_curr<end, fresh chunk; fixed scalar links replace intrusive pointer writes |
> | direct Allocate | cpp:104-106 size>=256-Alignment; dedicated pointer-free byte block, no pooled free-list entry |
> | Deallocate(0) | cpp:72-73 no-op; closed Go owner still rejects operations |
> | nonzero Deallocate | cpp:80-93 requested-byte decrement, immediate direct release or class free-list prepend; Go additionally validates exact original requested size and generation |
> | Stats.RequestedBytes | header:48 m_alloc_size / cpp:82,104 requested logical bytes, distinct from aligned free waste and owned backing |
> | Stats.FreeObjects/WastedBytes | cpp:140-166 free list count and aligned class-byte sum; dedicated blocks never counted as pooled waste |
> | Consolidate | cpp:174-245 floor(CHUNK_SIZE/classSize) count gate and per-chunk reclaim/relink; does not move live allocations |
> | Reset/Close pooled | cpp:39-67 pooled chunk traversal and counter/list clearing; generation ledger survives reset |
> | Reset/Close direct | explicit tracked-owner cleanup extension: source direct blocks are separately caller-owned and not traversed by reset/destructor; Go releases all owned direct backing and invalidates refs, after caller logical-object cleanup |
> | Size/Read/Write/IsLive | Go storage access/checked lifetime adaptation; no source public borrow or C++ raw-address alias claim |
>
> Consolidation preserves an awkward exact source behavior: strict endpoint
> allocation usually provides one fewer object for exact-dividing classes, but
> consolidate still requires floor(chunk/class) free objects. Those wholly dead
> chunks remain retained. Likewise incompletely filled free chunks remain retained.
> The new tests deliberately verify this rather than silently improve reclamation.
> Raw-address sorting adapts to deterministic chunk/block conceptual addresses;
> reclaimed chunk indices can be reused, bounding repeated reclaim/grow metadata.
> Reconstructed free-list order follows descending conceptual addresses. Original
> machine address order is not reproducible or asserted. Free byte values are
> unspecified; separate scalar metadata does not promise retained contents.
>
> Budget includes descriptor records/generation metadata/directories, byte payload,
> scalar block metadata, and full actual-capacity chunk directory. Growth reserves
> old+new directory backing and new chunk arrays simultaneously before publication.
> Consolidation uses no allocated scratch. Failed allocate can retain reusable
> charged descriptor capacity/generation history but publishes no live allocation
> and leaves existing content intact. Runtime OOM is not recoverable. Caller
> separately budgets the fixed cold owner header and performs domain destruction.
>

> # Words cross-budget ownership transfer prerequisite
>
> Owned files: Words method/helper, `words_budget_swap_test.go`, this status append.
> `Words.SwapBudgets(other *Words) error` exchanges the two complete owner graphs'
> accounting destinations without moving records, changing refs/free lists or
> running domain cleanup. This is a Go typed-owner budget adaptation needed by
> UIntSetMap cross-budget source swap, not a new source allocator algorithm.
>
> Closed owners reject before actions. Equal Budget pointers (includingnil and
> self-swap) return without reservations. For distinct budgets, both graph sums are
> checked for uint64 overflow before any Reserve; overflow is ErrBounds. Each sum
> includes Words.OwnerBytes, payload, block metadata, payload directory and private
> descriptor OwnerBytes/record bytes/generation metadata/directory. The borrowed
> Budget object and caller/domain roots are not duplicated in the graph charge.
>
> The original outgoing graph stays charged while its destination reserves the
> entire incoming graph. First failure changes nothing. Second failure refunds the
> first prepared Used charge and leaves both owner/config/payload states unchanged.
> A successful Reserve attempt still consumes its ordinary FailAfter prefix even
> when later refunded; no Budget transaction bypass or injector restoration exists.
> After both reservations succeed, original graph charges are released and both
> Words.config.Descriptors.Budget and descriptorSlab.config.Budget are rebound.
> The caller must serialize all affected owners/budgets; an outer table transaction
> can prepare its own distinct charges and refund them if this method fails.
>

> # Concrete variable-byte source region/page foundation
>
> Owned files: `bytes_region.go`, `bytes_region_test.go`, this status append. No
> existing slab/vector contract, domain package, ledger or git changes. This is a
> new concrete BytesRegion for util/region and util/page allocation policy, not a
> SmallBytes substitution or an extension of typed trail callback semantics.
>
> `BytesRegionConfig` selects source pointer width Alignment4/8 (explicit default8),
> PageSize payload bytes (default8192-Alignment, positive aligned multiple), shared
> Descriptors Config/Budget, and DirectOnly diagnostic mode. Checked scalar
> BytesRegionRef contains Slot/Generation. API provides Allocate/Size/Read/Write/
> IsLive, PushScope/PopScope/PopScopes/top-only Rollback, Reset/Close/Stats. There is
> no individual Free, Trim or escaped slice. Caller completes logical-object
> cleanup before scope pop/reset/close; storage performs no domain destruction.
>
> | Method/policy | Source mapping and observable storage action |
> | --- | --- |
> | release constructor | region.cpp:40-46 eagerly creates first default page |
> | release Allocate fit | region.cpp:54-59 strict requested endpoint comparison BEFORE ALIGN; tptr.h:25-31 pointer-width round-up; cursor can land exactly at page end |
> | release small overflow | region.cpp:61-66 obtains new/recycled default, then aligns requested bytes |
> | release big request | region.cpp:68-73 dedicated big payload inserted, immediately followed by fresh/recycled default even without further request |
> | source page headers | page.h:24-35 header width/previous/tag/default end; page.cpp:22-31 allocates payload+pointer-width header; Go allocates those bytes and uses separately charged scalar directory links rather than tagged pointers |
> | default allocation/recycling | page.cpp:41-51 pops free-page head before allocating; :60-67 prepends default free pages, immediately deletes big pages |
> | release PushScope | region.cpp:94-98 snapshots current page/cursor BEFORE allocate(3*pointerWidth) for mark; actual byte/cursor/page action retained even though mark control fields live in scalar Go metadata |
> | release PopScope/PopScopes | region.cpp:100-110 restores saved cursor and recycles pages through saved default page; header counted-pop loop preserved with checked depth adaptation |
> | release Reset | region.cpp:83-91 recycles entire active chain then reuses an existing default page; no new Reserve after successful constructor, tested with FailAfter0 |
> | release Close | region.cpp:49-51 frees active and free pages; Go also closes descriptor/log/scope/identity ownership |
> | diagnostic Allocate/Reset/scopes | region.h:30-79 independent direct chunks without alignment/eager default/in-payload marks, scopes save object count, pop/delete suffix, reset/delete all; vector.h:215-222,389-405 retains scalar directory/log/scope capacity |
> | Read/Write/Size/IsLive/owner identity | Go checked-storage adaptation; no raw pointer ABI or borrowed source-address claim |
>
> Zero-byte release allocation may share the same physical byte offset as another
> allocation; Go returns a distinct live checked descriptor. At an exact endpoint,
> zero request triggers the source new-default branch. Diagnostic zero requests
> are counted live direct objects with zero payload bytes, matching the source
> allocation log rather than a distinguished empty token. Big/direct pages release
> immediately on scope pop/reset. Defaults stay in source LIFO free list, including
> through Reset, and are only finally released at Close.
>
> The private concrete descriptorSlab and scalar allocation log preserve generation
> history across page reuse/reset; exhaustion retires identities. Scalar scope
> metadata retains pre-mark log/page/cursor limits and monotonic serials. Opaque
> cold marks reject foreign/non-top/consumed tokens; stored marks are pointer-free.
> OwnerID() is a stable nonzero scalar origin for borrowed string keys, including
> after rollback/reset/close. A borrowed process-global atomic64 namespace never
> wraps/reuses IDs and rejects exhaustion before constructor publication; failed
> constructors can consume unpublished IDs. Its cold field is included in owner
> header budget; no per-record allocation or second symbol identity namespace.
> Tests that simulate namespace exhaustion restore the test controller serially.
>
> Budget includes cold owner+identity, nested descriptor header/records/generation
> metadata/directories, every byte payload plus its actual source-sized page header,
> full-capacity scalar page directory and allocation/scope logs. Old+new metadata
> arrays and both prepared big/default payloads coexist during growth and are
> charged before publication. MarkPayloadBytes is informational and already within
> page PayloadBytes; never double-count it. Dedicated-page failure cleanup releases
> prepared payloads; reusable prepared metadata/descriptor history can remain
> charged. No new ref/mark, active/free chain mutation or cursor change is published
> on predictable failure. Source C++ may link the big page before a subsequent
> allocation throws; preparing both pages first is an explicit Go failure-safety
> adaptation, not claimed identical exception-state behavior. Runtime OOM recovery
> and caller-held closed tokens/host heap rounding remain outside typed accounting.
>
> Tests first produced RED missing BytesRegion APIs then GREEN. OwnerID dependency
> added RED missing method/namespace then GREEN. Source test/region.cpp contains
> only TODO: no substantive source assertion was invented or claimed inherited.
> Independent release/debug cursor/page model executes 1200 operations per mode,
> with a copied-byte lifetime oracle, nested marks/reset and non-overlap checks.
> Other finite tests verify both pointer widths, default source constants, strict
> fit-before-alignment, zero at endpoint, eager big/default pages, in-region marks
> crossing small/default and tiny big pages, free-page LIFO, generation retirement,
> diagnostic zero objects/capacity retention, first/second page preparation failures,
> constructor/scope fault prefixes, budget graph balance/old+new page-directory peak,
> no-reservation Reset, bulk pop lifetime, invalid scopes/configs, scalar origin
> collisions/stability/exhaustion, bounded reuse plateau and zero warmed allocations.
> The zero-allocation promise is for retained default-page scope churn; source big
> pages and diagnostic payloads allocate fresh backing and are not covered by it.
