> # Dense bit vector: initial utility port
>
> Owned production file: `bit_vector.go`. The only production dependency is the independent utilhash package. Source: `src/util/bit_vector.h`, `src/util/bit_vector.cpp`, Leonardo de Moura, Microsoft 2006. Copyright/license notices are preserved.
>
> | Source operations | Go counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | default/reserve/word constructors | zero value, `New`, `FromWords` |
> | copy constructor, assignment, destructor | `Clone`, `Assign`, Go owner release |
> | expand_to, expand, capacity | private `expandTo`, source growth in `Push`/`Resize`, `CapacityWords` |
> | reset, swap, fill0 | `Reset`, `Swap`, `Fill0` |
> | size, empty, num_words, get_word | `Size`, `Empty`, `NumWords`, `Word` |
> | get, set overloads, unset | `Get`, `Set(index, bool)`, `Unset` |
> | push_back, pop_back, back, shrink | `Push`, `Pop`, `Back`, `Shrink` |
> | resize, reserve, shift_right | `Resize`, `Reserve`, `ShiftRight` |
> | equality/inequality, OR/AND, neg | `Equal`/its negation, `Or`, `And`, `Neg` |
> | display, contains, get_hash | `String`, `Contains`, `Hash` |
> | fr_bit_vector reset/fill0/set/push_back | `FastReset.Reset`, `Fill0`, `Set`, `Push` |
>
> Ownership: words and the fast-reset index vector are owner-local pointer-free uint32 backing slices. Assignment/clone explicitly copy all source capacity words; Go struct assignment is documented as aliasing, and must not substitute for these source operations. Logical Reset retains capacity and clears every capacity word. FastReset.Reset keeps logical size and clears the recorded one-bit indices in insertion order, retaining duplicate entries until reset, just like source. GC replaces physical deallocation; there is no logical reference counting in this source class. Shrink/Pop preserve stale words and resize/bitwise operations use the original masks. Source capacity schedules are retained. Go additionally diagnoses invalid bit indexes, empty pop/back, invalid shrink, and size overflow instead of allowing a corrupted slice/access; num_words rounds via uint64 to avoid source addition overflow on extremely large bit counts.
>
> Source behavior caveats deliberately retained: Contains examines only the receiver's length and requires the other vector's capacity to cover that many words; it ignores excess other bits. Hash hashes only floor(size/8) bytes, so incomplete trailing bits do not participate. The byte representation is the utilhash package's fixed little-endian, signed-char reference baseline. WordBytes preserves source transitions with zero allocation. ShiftRight inserts low zero bits and raises original bit indices; the name comes from source despite the numeric shift direction.
>
> Every assertion in reachable `src/test/bit_vector.cpp` methods is translated: resize crash regressions, all six OR cases, both AND cases, reset/growth for lengths 1–83, and bit-31 equality. The print-only shift sequence has explicit expectations after shifts 16,1,32,42,16,63. Formerly unreachable tst2 and tst1 are also ported; tst1 uses fixed independent PCG choices and a bool-slice oracle instead of platform libc rand. A 5,000-step bounded independent bool-slice state machine covers resize/shrink/pop/push/shift/neg/reset/fill/and/or. Additional cases cover all constructors, capacity growth, clone/assignment independence, display/words, contains, fast reset, source hash byte rounding, empty/longer AND and warmed allocation behavior. Source hash byte fixtures are embedded from `test_vectors/source_hash.json`; their former generator was `hash_reference.cpp` (removed under the pure-Go rule). Tests never require C++ or source files. No permanent fixture is under testdata.
>
> TDD evidence: tests written first failed to compile on missing Vector/FastReset; the source translation then passed. Native CGO-disabled/g3checked tests and vet pass; actual js/wasm tests pass with Node v22.22.2 and the toolchain's official wrapper in a minimal environment; both wasm targets build. Host toolchain is go1.26.4-pont-onethread. WASI execution hits its pre-main runtime failure documented in PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-utilhash-port-status-md; no WASI semantic execution claim is made. Warmed bounded Hash/Or/And/Neg/Reset/Resize collectively allocate zero Go objects (AllocsPerRun test); no unmeasured speed claim.
>
> All methods of the two assigned source classes have counterparts. The following fixed-bit-vector packet is mapped below; sparse bitsets and other source containers remain separate unported components. Contains with insufficient other capacity remains an invalid source precondition, not a supported mathematical subset operation.
>
> ## Fixed bit vector and manager packet
>
> Added `fixed_bit_vector.go` and `fixed_bit_vector_test.go`, translating `src/util/fixed_bit_vector.h/.cpp`, copyright Microsoft 2014, authors Nikolaj Bjorner and Leonardo de Moura. This supersedes the earlier fixed-bit-vector unported status; sparse bitsets and other containers remain separate work.
>
> | Assigned source method | Go counterpart and evidence |
> | --- | --- |
> | fixed_bit_vector constructor/destructor; manager constructor/member allocator destructor | `NewFixedManager`, pointer-free `FixedRef`, `Close`; source bit width, word count, byte count, mask and shared zero-width m_0 are represented |
> | fixed get_word/get/operator[] | manager `Word`/`Get` (owner resolves compact refs) |
> | fixed private set/unset/set(bool) and manager overloads | `Set(ref,index,bool)`, `Unset` |
> | fixed set(other,hi,lo), manager overload | `SetRange`; aligned word path and residual bit path, unaligned bit path, source forward overlapping self-copy order |
> | allocate(), allocate0(), allocate1(), allocate(existing) | `Allocate`, `Allocate0`, `Allocate1`, `Clone` |
> | deallocate(), reset() allocator | `Deallocate`, manager `Reset`, `Close` |
> | copy(), reset(vector), fill0/fill1 | `Copy`/`Assign`, `ResetVector`, `Fill0`/`Fill1` |
> | set_and, set_or, set_neg | `And`, `Or`, `Neg` |
> | num_words, num_bytes, num_bits, get_mask | `NumWords`, `NumBytes`, `NumBits`, `Mask` |
> | last_word, equals, contains | `LastWord`, `Equals`, `Contains`; masked last word retains all source unused high bits in storage |
> | hash, display | `Hash`, `String`; exact floor(numBits/8) bytes with init seed numBits, MSB-first rendering |
> | raw words accessible to source tbv_manager friend | manager-only `WriteWord`; no arena slice borrow escapes |
>
> `FixedRef` is an owner-local arena slot/generation token. There is no cross-owner token detection claim: each call must use the manager that owns its token. Both zero-width Allocate0 and Allocate1 return the same zero ref, representing the constructor-owned source m_0. Deallocate of that root does nothing, manager Reset leaves it available, and Close ends the owner lifetime. The embedded zeroWord field preserves the manager-owned source root budget/storage even though no valid bit addresses it. Nonempty allocation creates a logical vector; Clone copies all storage words, not just active bits. Source Allocate leaves words unspecified; arena allocation supplies zero words, while callers requiring definite source zero/one initialization still use Allocate0/Allocate1. This is an uninitialized-storage adaptation, not a replacement for a source initialization action.
>
> The manager owns an `arena.Words` pool of pointer-free words and descriptors, with explicit source allocation/deallocation actions and generation invalidation. It allocates no per-vector object or per-bit object. Reset releases arena payload pages and invalidates live nonzero handles while preserving the arena generation ledger; Close releases pages/ledger and the manager root charge. Its own header, including the embedded zero-width root, is charged before construction and rolled back on invalid pool configuration. Arena accounting includes backing pages/metadata/directory; the arena API currently excludes its own cold Go allocator owner headers from accounting. That substrate limitation remains recorded rather than using reflection into private arena structures. No manager hash scratch buffer exists: approved `utilhash.WordReader` feeds source word bytes through a checked manager accessor. The accessor's closure and warmed Hash/Neg/Allocate1/Deallocate sequence allocate zero Go objects, verified with AllocsPerRun.
>
> Source allocator replacement: `small_object_allocator` byte chunks, pointer-linked free lists, address-sorted consolidation, debug Valgrind bypass and raw malloc/free are represented here by the agreed typed owner-local pooled arena. The general small_object_allocator implementation, its allocation-size/debug leak diagnostics and consolidation methods are not claimed ported by this packet. One source defect to retain in the inventory: allocator reset/destruction frees small-object chunks but does not track live separately malloc-allocated large blocks; this packet supplies explicit Go owner cleanup and does not reproduce physical leaks. Manager Reset invalidation applies uniformly to owned vectors. Logical operations, masks, initialization calls, deletion calls and traversal ordering follow the source.
>
> All active tests from `src/test/fixed_bit_vector.cpp` were written before implementation and observed RED on missing manager/ref methods: tst1, tst_or, and tst_eq widths 15/16/17/31/32/33/63/64/65. The source tst_and is empty; added independent AND expectations via a bounded 600-step bool-slice oracle at widths 0/1/17/32/33/65/101. Additional tests independently check last-word masks and all word sizes, empty shared-root identity, exact source forward self-alias range semantics, clone/assign independence, stale generations after deallocation/reset, Close, bounds, constructor/failure budget rollback, allocation failure preserving live vectors, and bounded pool reuse. C++ hash expectations in embedded `test_vectors/fixed_hash.json` cover zero width and every floor-byte boundary through width 65; the former source input generator was `fixed_hash_reference.cpp` (since removed), compiled using actual hash.cpp with GCC 13.3.0. Ordinary tests require neither C++ nor repository source.
>
> Final packet validation: CGO-disabled native and g3checked package tests, vet, and actual js/wasm tests pass using the installed go1.26.4-pont-onethread toolchain and Node v22.22.2. wasip1/wasm packages compile. The previously verified custom-Go pre-main WASI seed failure remains an execution limitation; this packet does not modify or bypass the installed runtime. Source-method audit covers all operations of the two assigned fixed-bit-vector classes; general allocator internals remain inventoried separately.
>
> Width bound: fixed-manager constructors reject numBits > UINT32_MAX−31 with arena.ErrBounds before construction/budget changes, because source `(num_bits+31)/32` otherwise wraps to a broken zero-word allocation while reporting a nonzero bit width. A finite metadata-only boundary test covers the highest non-overflowing width (4294967264 bits, 134217727 words) without allocating its payload. This is an explicit invalid-size guard recorded alongside the source overflow defect.
>
> No-generics conversion: constructor header accounting now uses reflect.TypeOf(FixedManager{}) rather than the generic reflect.TypeFor helper. FixedRef/Words APIs retain their concrete signatures while the arena owner replaces its underlying generic storage. No Go generic declarations or instantiations remain in this packet.
> Concrete conversion validation: bitset tests pass against the concrete arena Words implementation on native, checked-tag and actual js/wasm execution; vet and WASI cross-build pass. The existing source assertions, finite masked/hash fixtures, bounded bool-vector oracle and zero-allocation pool checks remain enabled.

> ## uint_set packet
>
> Added `uint_set.go`/`uint_set_test.go`, translating all declared operations in `src/util/uint_set.h`, copyright Microsoft 2006, Leonardo de Moura (2006-12-07). This is the dense unsigned-integer utility set; SAT-local dense-set classes are separate components. Its storage is an owner-local slice of pointer-free uint32 words. No Go generics, interfaces for element storage, unsafe, maps, or production random generator are used.
>
> | Source operation | Go counterpart / contract |
> | --- | --- |
> | default constructor / destructor | zero value `UintSet`, explicit `Close` releases backing storage |
> | copy constructor | `Clone`, source push-back loop preserving logical words and deriving capacity anew |
> | implicit source assignment through unsigned_vector | `Assign`, deep copy with source capacity, self-assignment guard |
> | swap, reset | `Swap`, `Reset` retaining capacity and zero logical length |
> | get_max_elem | `MaxElem`, **exclusive** 32*logical-word-size endpoint, not maximum member and not backing capacity |
> | empty, insert, remove, contains, num_elems | `Empty`, `Insert`, `Remove`, `Contains`, `NumElems` |
> | operator OR/AND | `Union`, `Intersect`; union grows to source.size()+1, intersection shrinks to source logical size |
> | equality/inequality, subset_of | `Equal`/its negation, `SubsetOf`; trailing zero words do not affect equality |
> | begin, end | `Begin`, `End` constructing value iterators |
> | iterator construction, scan_idx, scan_word, scan | `iterator`, `scanIndex`, `scanWord`, `scan`, original word/bit traversal order |
> | iterator dereference/equality/inequality | `Value`, `Equal`/its negation; source compares index only even across different sets |
> | iterator prefix/postfix increment, assignment | `Next`, `PostNext`, `Assign`; postfix returns old iterator value |
> | get_hash, hash/eq functor wrappers | `Hash`, concrete `UintSetHasher`/`UintSetEqual` |
> | ostream display | `String`, original ascending loop and brace/comma format |
> | inherited physical vector capacity inspection | additional `CapacityWords` for storage audit |
>
> Ownership/capacity fidelity: source unsigned_vector growth starts at 2 words, then (3*old+1)>>1 and expands repeatedly until the requested logical word size fits. Go allocation follows that schedule instead of append's unspecified capacity schedule. Reset and intersection retain physical capacity; growth zero-initializes newly logical words, so stale removed/reset members do not return. The source uint_set copy constructor pushes only logical words, while its implicitly generated assignment copies the base vector's capacity; both behaviors and independence are tested separately. Close maps the source backing-store release to Go owner cleanup. Copying a Go UintSet struct is documented as aliasing and must not replace Clone/Assign. Iterators borrow the owner and require no set mutation during traversal. Invalid end increments panic rather than proceeding past the source invariant.
>
> Numerical fidelity: every membership word/mask and hash accumulator is uint32. Source NumElems invokes GCC __builtin_popcount; Go's bits.OnesCount32 is the equivalent platform population-count primitive. Source Hash is h += (i+1)*word[i] modulo 2^32; it does **not** call the generic utilhash string/combine functions, so this packet has no endian/char hashing adaptation. Weighted hash overflow and trailing-zero invariance have exact finite tests. Source get_max_elem overflows when logical length reaches 2^27 words, breaking iterator/display bounds. Insert/Union diagnose such invalid extents before changing/growing storage instead of silently hiding members; the guard and preservation of existing membership/capacity are tested using UINT32_MAX without giant allocation. The source vector's allocation-size/capacity overflow is also diagnosed.
>
> Source tests: `src/test/main.cpp` registers TST(uint_set), `src/test/CMakeLists.txt` includes uint_set.cpp, and **all** tst1/tst2/tst3/tst4/tst5 calls in that file are active. Tests were written first and observed RED on undefined UintSet operations; translation then reached GREEN. tst1's exact assertion categories (count, empty, every membership) use deterministic independent PCG choices with the original 100 repeated bounded domains and fewer than 1000 operations each. tst2 preserves 1000 repetitions for each domain 1/10/31/32/100 and all 100 singleton probes. tst3 translates every assertion at n=12 and n=100, including duplicate insertion, subset direction, copies and singleton-subset equivalence; tst4 covers bit 32. No source uint-set tests are disabled.
>
> `tst5` contains print-only hash observations and a uint_map< unsigned > integration demonstration. Its hash/render observations have embedded finite expectations in `test_vectors/uint_set_prints.json`, independently calculated from source masks and the weighted formula: hash sequence 0,2,6,8198,8214. The value-key copy independence is tested, but the source map insertion, bucket traversal and key/value iteration demonstration remains explicitly **unported map integration**; a UintSet port does not claim a map implementation. No assertion was weakened or dropped to hide that prerequisite. The source key map's iteration order is not replaced by a Go map.
>
> A separate 3,000-step independent bool-array set oracle checks membership, cardinality, empty/equality/subset relations, union/intersection/reset/assignment/swap and complete ascending iteration. Additional deterministic cases cover all iterator operations (including equality across owners with equal index), wrapper functors, source union's extra logical zero word, retained capacity, cloning vs assignment, swap/reset/Close and weighted hash wraparound. Warmed bounded insert/remove/count/hash/union/intersection/iteration allocate zero Go objects. Ordinary tests embed permanent fixtures, never compile C++ or import the repository source, and use no testdata files.
>
> Final packet checks: CGO-disabled native tests, g3checked tests, vet, actual js/wasm execution with Node v22.22.2, and WASI cross-build pass. The installed custom Go runtime's previously documented WASI startup failure remains separate from package execution. Every method in the assigned uint_set header has a counterpart or explicit operator-expression equivalent. Generic source map integration and other unsigned_vector/container operations remain separate production coverage work; they are not claimed complete by this packet.

> Go maps: each 28-byte scalar entry holds state/hash/value plus arena slot,
> generation, **logical word length**, and **source capacity**. Arena payload
> length is the source capacity, so copy assignment at capacity 7/logical length 1
> allocates all seven source words even if the arena capacity class rounds to 8.
> Only active words are copied; source spare words are unspecified and Go supplies
> zero storage. Empty copy-constructed keys use the zero ref and are distinguished
> from FREE entries by the state tag. Weighted hash is h += (i+1)*word[i] modulo
> 2^32; no endian or signed-char adaptation applies to this specialization.
>
> The source uint_set custom copy constructor pushes logical words and derives
> capacity; its user-defined copy constructor/destructor suppress move operations.
> Consequently synthesized `_key_data`/default_hash_entry move assignment calls
> uint_set **copy assignment**, preserving source capacity. An assembly-only audit
> using the original headers verified that call (artifacts under golang/.cache).
> Rehash/Clone allocate distinct USED key payloads while every old USED/FREE/
> DELETED payload remains owned until table destruction. Removal and nonshrinking
> Reset only mark states; even an empty-clean Reset retains FREE payloads.
> Overwriting a slot destroys its former key. Insert/lookup/remove wrappers create
> and destroy all source temporaries; insert-if-absent wrappers preserve both
> copies. Internal intersection uses cloned key_data directly rather than adding
> table2map temporary copies that the source does not make. Swap exchanges table
> and pool ownership without key copies or destruction.
>
> Budget accounting includes map root, scalar arrays, Words/descriptor cold
> headers, payload and all pool metadata/directories, with uint64 charges. This
> depends on the arena owner-header and atomic `Words.SwapBudgets` packets; their
> current implementations also supersede the older fixed-manager paragraph's
> substrate header-accounting limitation. Cross-budget Swap reserves both incoming
> table charges first, then uses the atomic complete-pool graph hook, refunds
> table reservations on pool failure, and exchanges pointers only after success.
> Owner root charges and cold callbacks stay with their owners. Tests exercise
> failure in each destination's table/pool preparation and nil/non-nil budgets.
> Physical arena free pages may cache storage, but descriptor liveness follows
> every source logical deletion. Explicit Close refunds all graph charges.
>
> Typed arena errors replace unchecked source allocation/size failures. Constructor,
> key-copy assignment, table rehash/Clone, and table replacement allocate before
> destroying old storage to preserve existing contents on failure; this adds a
> documented old+new replacement peak where source vector assignment/reset would
> destroy old data first and could leave unsafe state after allocation failure.
> Successful pre-insert rehash remains applied if a later stored-key copy fails;
> multi-entry Assign/Union and Remove with failing cleanup are source-ordered
> partial operations, not transactions. Pool growth may retain reusable physical
> pages after failed operations; tests require no surviving temporary descriptors
> or final budget leaks. uint32 iteration extents and table sizing diagnose overflow.
>
> Tests first obtained RED on the missing concrete API, then GREEN after source
> translation. Additional iterator postfix and cross-budget swap cases were RED
> before their implementations. tst5 has the complete independently computed
> finite stdout expectation: hashes 0/2/6/8198 and bucket-order lines
> `{1, 2, 44} : 1` then `{1, 2, 4, 44} : 3`. No source assertions are disabled in
> that test. A 700-operation independent eight-member mask oracle checks mappings
> and complete iteration; test-only Go maps serve as the mathematical oracle.
> Additional coverage checks strict 3/4 growth before lookup, last tombstone reuse,
> FREE/DELETED retained owners, strict cleanup thresholds and OOM callback, one-step
> reset shrinking and 64-entry finalize, source capacity vs logical/physical size,
> clone/assignment lifetimes, exact wrapper temporary counts, injected constructor/
> insert/lookup/rehash/swap failures, alias guards, stale borrows and caller copies.
> Warmed Find/Insert allocates zero Go objects in AllocsPerRun. Ordinary tests need
> no C++ tools, source headers, testdata, or platform addresses.
>
> Native, g3checked, vet, actual fresh-count js/wasm tests under Node v22.22.2,
> and wasip1/wasm cross-build pass. WASI execution retains the documented installed
> custom-Go runtime pre-main seed limitation; there is no WASI execution claim.

> # Independent finite SAT oracle
>
> This package is test infrastructure, not a translation or replacement of the
> production SAT/SMT solver. It imports no g3 algorithms or representations.
>
> `Literal` is a separate signed one-based representation; `CNF` owns no manager
> state. `Solve` checks all literals and variable bounds before enumerating the
> entire Boolean domain (at most 16 variables, 65,536 assignments). It returns
> exact SAT with a total copied model or exact UNSAT. Malformed/oversized inputs
> return `InputError`; they never produce unknown or a semantic solver result.
> `ValidModel` checks all clauses and assumptions against a total Boolean model.
> Inputs are borrowed without modification/retention; returned models belong to
> the caller. The implementation has no propagation, learning, random generator,
> solver dependency, or hidden mutable global state.
>
> Worst-case work is 2^Variables times input literal occurrences plus assumptions.
> There is no claim of an unbounded SAT oracle, EUF/quantifier/SMT interpretation,
> production assumption handling, production user scopes, unsat cores, proof
> objects, or solver model reconstruction.
>
> ## Source expectations and additions
>
> Read `GO_PORT_PLAN.md` C1/C4, `src/test/check_assumptions.cpp`, and
> `src/test/sat_user_scope.cpp`. Source scenario fixtures are permanently embedded
> under `test_vectors/`; ordinary tests require no source files, compiler, process,
> network, Python, or neighboring checkout.
>
> - `check_assumptions.cpp` actively asserts SAT for `p or q or r` with assumption
>   `not p`. The fixture preserves that expectation; choosing q=true proves SAT.
> - Its final query asserts `not p` and assumes `not q,not r`, but has no result
>   assertion in the source: it is a crash regression. The added explicit UNSAT
>   expectation is independently derived because all disjuncts become false.
> - `sat_user_scope.cpp` compares an incremental solver with a rebuilt solver in
>   an infinite loop. The finite embedded script supplies independent active-CNF
>   expectations for nested pushes/pops, empty frames, and temporary assumptions.
>   Frame management here is a test harness only. No production scope behavior is
>   implemented or validated yet; the oracle is ready for future solver comparison.
> - Added permanent mathematical fixtures cover empty conjunction/disjunction,
>   opposing units, duplicate/complementary literals, binary implications,
>   six-literal clauses, and contradictory assumptions.
> - Added tests exercise all sixteen two-variable truth tables. Clauses are
>   constructed by excluding false assignments; returned witnesses are checked
>   directly against the independent truth-table bits. Tests at the 16-variable
>   bound select the final all-true assignment, then independently contradict it.
>   Invalid input, int32 minimum literal, full-input checking after an empty clause,
>   malformed models, input isolation, and model isolation are checked separately.
>
> ## TDD and validation
>
> Tests and permanent fixtures were authored first. The initial test run failed
> with undefined `Literal`, `CNF`, `Solve`, and `ValidModel` (RED). The subsequent
> enumeration implementation made the tests pass (GREEN). Native package tests
> pass at 100% statement coverage. Race tests pass. Test-binary cross-builds for
> js/wasm and wasip1/wasm pass; this is compilation evidence, not wasm execution.
> All writes, temp files, cache files, and build outputs from this packet are
> under `golang/`; commands use `golang/.cache` for GOCACHE/GOTMPDIR/TMPDIR.

> # Source integer bitwise operations
>
> Source: all four bitwise methods in util/mpz.cpp (the selected _MP_INTERNAL
> 32-bit numerical engine) and their util/mpz.h declarations. The active
> source test is src/test/mpz.cpp::bug4; its alias equality assertion and exact
> printed result are translated. Other MPZ methods and GMP compatibility are not
> claimed by this chunk. No generics, production math/big, unbudgeted numeral
> arrays, unsafe or interfaces were introduced.
>
> ## Algorithm and ownership map
>
> BitwiseOr/BitwiseAnd/BitwiseXor preserve the source small inline arithmetic
> paths and the large-number repeated64-bit chunk algorithm. Each general
> iteration uses Mod by the manager's owned two64 constant, Uint64 conversion,
> the specified machine bit operation, SetUint64, Mul by the multiplier, Add,
> then multiplier Mul and both operand Div calls in source order. The loop
> ends when either copied operand is zero; Or/Xor append either nonzero tail
> through source Mul/Add, while And discards it. Even final unused multiplier
> and division actions are retained. There is no limbwise replacement algorithm.
>
> BitwiseNot preserves the small width<=63 mask branch and general width chunks,
> including copying a large input at width0 and performing final unused multiplier
> and division calls. Explicit unsigned mask arithmetic defines the intended
> source width63 signed-shift result. Width is uint32; no new arbitrary size cap
> is imposed. Source nonnegative assertions become ErrBitwiseDomain before any
> mutation, and existing manager closed/handle errors propagate.
>
> The source's local numerals are concrete stack Int headers with cell/payload
> storage from IntegerManager's existing budgeted owners. Every prepared numeral
> is explicitly Del'ed in source cleanup order. A separate staged result survives
> until final Move; allocation errors leave the destination and aliased operands
> unchanged. This adapts source clear-output-first partial mutation and local
> cleanup on allocation exceptions, without changing any successful arithmetic,
> branch order or alias result. The old destination stays charged while new work
> exists, so the documented failure-atomicity peak is real. Earlier manager scratch
> and pool-page growth may remain retained and charged after failure. Close refunds
> the complete graph; no output/string conversion happens during production bitwise
> operations. The owning manager remains confined/serialized as in the existing
> numerical contract; the source lock variant is not a new implementation here.
>
> ## TDD and validation
>
> The initial four tests failed compilation on missing methods (RED), before
> translation. They then passed (GREEN). A fifth independent aliased-failure test
> was immediately GREEN against the implemented staged contract. Every permanent
> test requires no source checkout or C++ executable.
>
> - Exact active bug4 inputs, equality assertion and independently expected
>   diagnostic4294967295/4294967295 are preserved.
> - Independent math/big oracle checks zeros, inline boundaries, UINT32/UINT64
>   boundaries, long unequal tails and30 seeded192-bit operands. Binary operations
>   cover independent outputs, either input alias and all-input identity. Not
>   covers widths0/1/7/30/31/32/33/62/63/64/65/127/128/129/192/257, both output modes.
> - Each operation reaches both injected failure and successful sweep endpoints,
>   including both operand aliases; failed publication preserves all input/output
>   values and Close refunds every owner. Negative-domain and closed-owner errors
>   preserve output. Warmed all-four-operation runs allocate zero Go objects and
>   succeed under FailAfter0.

> 8a8ae0a plus only the two new Go files. Full native ./..., full g3checked race
> ./..., checked vet and checked WASI compilation passed. Full actual checked
> JS/WASM ./... passed; all six new test names were explicitly checked for both
> RUN and PASS in .cache/bitwise-checked-js-final.log. Source/no-generics audit passes.
> WASI is compilation evidence only; the existing runtime-startup gap remains.
>
> Independent review added immediately-GREEN assertions for live temporary-cell
> counts BEFORE Close on every failure, so manager teardown cannot mask lost
> numerals. A sixth test verifies each small-input fast path releases a preexisting
> big destination under FailAfter0. Final full native and all6 targeted checked race
> and actual checked JS tests pass. No production change was needed by review;
> earlier full-module race/JS gates remain applicable.

> MPZ ignores punctuation throughout. MPQ stops its initial digit scan at the

>
> - Fraction denominator digit scanning skips other punctuation/signs and stops
>   at e/E. Thus 1/-2 is 1/2 and 1/2/3 is 1/23. An e/E after a fraction marker
>   triggers the source mixed-notation exception, including exponent zero.
> - Decimal scanning similarly skips punctuation, so 1.2/3 is 123/100; each ASCII
>   fractional digit multiplies the denominator-of-the-fraction by ten. Whole
>   numerator plus that fraction is formed through the actual rational operations.
> - Scientific sign is recognized only when '-' immediately follows e/E.
>   Nondigits except slash are skipped during exponent accumulation. A slash in
>   the exponent triggers the source mixed-notation exception; a slash in the
>   decimal fractional scan is instead ignored, as above.
> - The exponent accumulator retains unsigned uint64 wrap before its final
>   UINT32_MAX comparison. Exponent 2^64 wraps to zero; 2^64+1 wraps to one.
>   Generic source mask nontermination remains a distinct PowerDomainError.

> # MPQ mixed arithmetic, fused operations, and integer-valued wrappers
>
> Source targets: `src/util/mpq.h` mixed arithmetic / fused overloads and
> integer-valued rational wrappers, including the private mixed `rat_add` and
> `rat_mul` routines. This packet completes these assigned overloads; it does not
> claim the entire mpq.h / rational.h family is complete. Existing mpq.go rational
> Add/Sub/Mul/Div and manager headers were not edited.
>
> ## Exact method map
>
> | Source overload | Concrete Go counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | add(mpq,mpz,mpq), rat_add(mpq,mpz,mpq) | AddInt; integer fast path or one cross-product temporary |
> | mul(mpz,mpq,mpq), rat_mul(mpz,mpq,mpq) | MulInt; integer fast path or copied denominator plus normalize |
> | mul(mpz,mpz,mpq) | MulInts; integer product with denominator1 |
> | div(mpq,mpz,mpq) | DivInt; numerator copy, denominator product, divisor-sign action, normalize |
> | acc_div(mpq,mpz) | AccDiv; denominator product, divisor-sign action, normalize |
> | rat_div(mpz,mpz,mpq) | RatDiv; copy numerator/denominator, normalize, no denominator sign repair |
> | addmul/submul(mpq,mpq,mpq,mpq) | AddMul / SubMul |
> | addmul/submul(mpq,mpz,mpq,mpq) | AddMulInt / SubMulInt |
> | idiv(mpq,mpq,mpq), machine_idiv(mpq,mpq,mpq) | IDiv / MachineIDiv |
> | idiv(mpq,mpq,mpz), machine_idiv(mpq,mpq,mpz) | IDivToInt / MachineIDivToInt |
> | rem/mod(mpq,mpq,mpq) | Rem / Mod |
> | rem/mod(mpq,mpq,mpz) | RemToInt / ModToInt |
>
> The inherited integer-only add/sub/mul/div/machine_div/rem/mod/addmul/submul
> operations already belong to IntegerManager; this packet delegates their
> integer-valued rational wrappers rather than reproducing integer algorithms.
> Increment/decrement forwards, other MPQ predicates/getters, power/root/rounding,
> parsers, display and scoped numeral APIs belong to separate packets.
>
> ## Source branch/action and alias semantics
>
> Fused +/-1 coefficient branches delegate Add/Sub directly, exchanging the
> operation for coefficient-1. Other coefficients compute the product in the
> source rational temporary, then perform the source Add/Sub. The non-GMP source
> small +/-1 predicates are used, including denominator1 for rational
> coefficients. Zero and non-unit coefficients take the full product path.
>
> Synchronized mode uses local integer/rational temporaries and deletes them on
> all returns. Non-synchronized mode reuses the existing addTmp1 and addMulTmp
> manager fields; normalize uses the existing nTmp cache. Existing manager header
> accounting already includes every persistent scratch scalar, so no additional
> owning object or header modification was needed. Locals are concrete scalar
> numerals backed by the same budgeted IntegerManager cells/Words service. No Go
> generics, unsafe, math/big production arithmetic, boxed interfaces, per-numeral
> Go heap owner, or independent resource service is introduced.
>
> Public results are staged until the operation succeeds, following the existing
> mpq.go predictable allocation failure contract. Source arithmetic and observable
> alias actions are preserved rather than treating staging as permission to
> correct source behavior. DivInt reads an output-numerator-aliased divisor after
> the source numerator copy and an output-denominator-aliased divisor sign after
> the product. AccDiv similarly reads an aliased denominator after publication.
> RatDiv rereads its divisor after copying the numerator. Frozen examples include:
>
> - RatDiv(6, output.num initially-9, output) yields1, because the source copies6
>   into the numerator before rereading that divisor.
> - DivInt(2/3, output.num initially-5, output) yields1/3 for the same reason.
> - AccDiv(2/-3, the same denominator) yields2/9; the sign sees the positive
>   product9 rather than the original-3.
> - RatDiv(-5,-5) preserves source representation-1/-1; ordinary RatDiv(6,-9)
>   stores2/-3. RatDiv deliberately differs from sign-repairing SetParts.
>
> Integer-valued wrappers delegate directly to IntegerManager with the actual
> output numerator identity. They preserve its known source divisor/output alias
> quirks: IDiv(-26,7,divisor output) yields-2, IDiv(-26,-7,divisor output) yields2,
> and Mod(-26,+/-7,divisor output) yields0. Denominator is reset to1 after successful
> integer output. The ToInt overloads preserve the same component identity.
>
> Raw uninitialized rationals, stale manager handles, noninteger operands to
> integer-valued wrappers, and zero divisors receive typed errors before unsafe
> source actions. ErrRationalNotInteger replaces the source debug assertion;
> ErrDivideByZero is the established boundary guard. This also rejects a literal
> zero divisor before an output alias could overwrite it. Caller confinement and
> no shallow copying of owned numerals remain existing manager preconditions.
>
> ## Tests-first evidence and independent checks
>
> Tests first failed RED against HEAD:golang with missing IDiv/Mod/AddInt/MulInt/
> DivInt/AccDiv/fused APIs. Shared mpnum had unrelated concurrent display/scoped
> RED tests, so the packet's RED and final gates use a HEAD archive under
> `.cache/release/mpq-ops-red`, overlaid only the assigned ops production/tests.
> No unrelated source files were changed or omitted from that archived baseline.
>
> All24 active ENSURE assertions in src/test/rational.cpp tst9 are preserved:
> eight source signed small/big Euclidean division/modulus fixtures each check
> reconstruction, nonnegative modulus and the strict absolute-divisor bound.
> No missing-overload-specific active assertion appears in src/test/mpq.cpp;
> tst0/inverse aliases and tst1 inherited integer assertions are already covered
> by existing mpq/mpz/parse tests. Other active rational.cpp scenarios, including
> root/modular-inverse and performance cases, are separate source API domains;
> this packet does not count them as ported.
>
> Eight named test groups additionally cover bounded independent math/big.Rat /
> math/big.Int expectations; both synchronization policies; mixed operations with
> in-place output; every fused rational output alias and +/-1/zero/non-unit
> branches; rational/int outputs for integer wrappers; big-limb mixed/fused
> oracles; persistent versus local scratch behavior; frozen source component
> aliases and negative-denominator representation. The initial component-alias
> test was independently RED (RatDiv2/-3 versus source1) before implementing the
> logical source publication identity.
>
> For12 arithmetic categories, FailAfter advances through every failing prefix
> until success. Immediately after a failed operation, **before any String,
> Del or Close**, the test independently enumerates expected caller/base-manager
> cell roots and only explicitly named source cached roots in nonsynch mode.
> It compares exact live numeric-cell counts, then derives expected live Words
> refs solely from these cell payloads and NaturalManager's division/format
> scratch roots. Synchronized failures also require exactly the pre-call live
> cell/Words baseline. Unreachable temporary handles cannot justify their own
> presence, and owner Close cannot mask them. Input/output values are then
> checked, and whole-owner cleanup refunds all budget charges. Large warmed fused
> operations measure zero Go allocations for both source policies.
>
> Native full archived module, native g3checked mpnum, vet, actual fresh checked
> JS/WASM named ops tests and full mpnum suite, race ops tests, and WASI executable
> build passed. Checked race/actual checked JS were repeated after strengthening
> immediate ownership and component-alias audits. WASI semantic execution remains
> blocked by the recorded custom Go runtime pre-main seed/environment issue;
> this status claims executable build only. All edits, caches, archives, compiler
> temporary files and outputs stay under golang. Commit/manifest are coordinator
> owned.

> # Representational adaptations under review
>
> This ledger records translation choices, not permission to replace algorithms.
> See package status files for precise methods and test evidence.
>
> * Storage: Go-managed pointer-free slabs, fixed-width handles and generational
>   public tokens implement the plan's deliberate allocator change. Domain cleanup
>   remains mandatory. Release internal stale-slot reuse detection is unavailable;
>   checked builds retain generations. Scoped region and payload work is pending.
> * Numerics: mpn uses owner-confined reusable scratch in place of an OpenMP lock.
>   Exact source limb algorithms are retained. Invalid shorter-numerator division
>   is rejected by explicit precondition; source mpz handles this before mpn.
>   Signed managers, numeric cells and diagnostics remain unported.
> * Hashing: portable Go reproduces little-endian loads and signed-char tail bytes
>   of the baseline rather than varying hash output with host ABI. Source C++
>   portability to other endianness/char signedness remains an audit item.
> * Diagnostic and platform replacements must be recorded individually before
>   their source units can be marked complete.
>
> ### Explicit source formatter arguments and profiles
>
> PrintfFormatter uses concrete borrowed arguments in place of C va_list and
> implements Linux C-locale integer/C-string profiles. The selected null-%s glibc
> policy and finite failure for the source persistent retry loop are explicit
> adapters. Linux %I64u is width64 plus unsigned32; source uint64 mismatches
> receive a typed error. Other C conversion domains and Windows CRT state remain
> open, so the formatter and formatted exception constructor stay partial.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-printf-port-status-md for source callsites, buffer actions and tests.
>
> ### Parameter references storage and null stream behavior
>
> Parameters borrow explicit symbol/numeric owners and use scalar references,
> pooled concrete entries and owned nullable C text. Reset/Validate mutate shared
> backing as in the source. A failed detach retains its published prefix while
> cleaning the old reference; pooled pages remain physically charged until Close.
> Null C strings model the audited libstdc++ stream badbit prefix with a typed
> error. The source global empty value and debug print become explicit owner-local
> and diagnostic APIs. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-params-ref-port-status-md for remaining adaptations.
>
> ### S-expression undefined display continuation and scalar wrappers
>
> The source atom display falls through to an invalid composite cast; Go returns
> the defined printed prefix plus ErrSexprDisplayContinuation. Empty composites
> retain the source closing-parenthesis-only rendering. Scalar handles/snapshots
> replace raw borrows; owner Close destroys outstanding owned numerals. Vector
> null callbacks become no-ops, nonempty self-append rejects unbounded source
> growth, and capacity preflight avoids leaked increments. BV source debug
> short-circuit temporaries and inline16/doubling temporary storage are preserved.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-sexpr-port-status-md for detailed lifetimes, guards and source mappings.
>
>
> ### Concrete string-buffer ownership and numeric boundaries
>
> StringBuffer32/64/128 embed physically charged inline arrays and charge doubled
> overflow with old/new overlap. Scalar reads and caller-owned CStr text replace raw
> borrows; CStr still writes its terminator and grows at the exact source boundary.
> Bulk append preserves successful capacity prefixes before copying bytes or
> publishing position, and cross-buffer insertion completes source CStr first.
> The heap self-append path that would use freed source storage gets a typed guard;
> valid inline and full-heap paths retain source actions. Cold locking and owner
> identity checks are explicit Go lifetime adapters.
>
> Source sprintf("%d", unsigned) has a high-bit type-mismatch undefined domain.
> The approved adapter interprets uint32 bits as signed32, preserving observed
> AMD64 outputs; this is not claimed as portable C semantics. Stack24-byte numeric
> conversion avoids invented formatter allocations. LongBits32 rejects values
> outside source signed32 range. Arbitrary initial sizes and Windows secure-CRT
> runtime/error profiles remain open. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-string-buffer-port-status-md.
>
> ### Integer inverse domain adapter
>
> The source integer Inv body contains only SASSERT(false); release C++ otherwise
> leaves its operand unchanged. Go returns ErrIntegerInvUnsupported after its
> existing ownership checks, preserving the operand and budget. This explicitly
> checked unsupported domain is not an inverse algorithm or a release no-op
> equivalence claim. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-mpz-facade-extra-port-status-md.
>
> ### Recycled source ID reservation
>
> The embedded cold ID generator charges its actual separate backing arrays; its
> header is charged by the enclosing owner. Recycle reports fallible reservation,
> and an explicit preflight method prepares physical capacity without changing
> logical IDs, retaining successful growth prefixes. Reset retains capacity and
> cleanup refunds it. This supports future explicit AST reclamation but does not
> implement the AST consumer or full process memory service. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-id-port-status-md.
>
> ### Concrete chained storage and quota transfer
>
> Scalar cell links replace source pointers; owner and complete backing arrays are
> charged with actual layout. Rehash retains the source attempted-copy UsedSlots
> prefix on later failure. Finalize charges old/new overlap and preserves old
> storage on predictable failure, adapting source delete-before-init. Swap retains
> hash functors and transfers only positive cross-budget capacity delta; it adds
> no fictitious same-budget reservation. Cold epoch-checked views replace raw
> borrows. Automatic Z3DEBUG visited-set diagnostics and AST structural/identity
> specializations remain open. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-chain-table-port-status-md.
>
> ### SMT2 symbol quoting and complete escaped byte output
>
> Nullable Go C-string inputs and checked scalar symbols replace raw borrows.
> Quoting reads symbol bytes directly while holding the manager lock around only
> an unpublished private buffer, avoiding inversion with shared-buffer symbol
> insertion. Complete temporary owner/inline/overflow and old/new storage is charged;
> only the one final immutable text is caller-owned. Source predicate quirks,
> char append order and CStr mutation remain unchanged.
>
> Escaped ostream byte emission becomes append into concrete StringBuffer64.
> Quote-prefix and indentation failure prefixes remain published; all uint32
> indent values are valid subject to actual host-int representability and budget.
> A convenience output wrapper cleans its temporary prefix on error. External
> custom ostream state, badbit and exception behavior remain open, separate from
> complete byte rendering. No AST printer scaffold is introduced.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-smt2-util-port-status-md.
>
> ### Concrete family registry ownership
>
> The source symbol table and names vector have real nested cold/storage charges.
> Counter increment, table insertion and names append keep their source publication
> order and defined failure gaps. Signed next++ overflow is a typed bounds domain.
> Caller enumeration buffers and scalar Symbols replace source vector output/raw
> name references. Borrowed symbols outlive the registry; Close refunds owned
> storage independently. This helper supplies no simulated AST manager or plugins.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-family-port-status-md.
>
> ### Standalone sort-size scalar default and finite guard
>
> Private sort-size kind encoding makes Go zero value infinite as the source
> constructor requires. Nonfinite size is canonical zero instead of copying source
> unspecified default bits. The finite Size precondition is checked in every Go
> profile, replacing invalid release reads with a typed error. Actual borrowed
> RationalService IsUint64 then Uint64 calls preserve source classification;
> negative, fractional and too-large inputs become very-big without an invented
> cardinality domain check. No mutable owner/header or fake AST manager is added.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-sort-size-port-status-md.
>
> ### Persistent-array ownership and unsafe source continuations
>
> Actual SmallBytes owns encoded scalar cells/value blocks with source capacity
> headers; a separate cold manager owns only its header and retained scratch.
> Mk clears its destroyed caller output on replacement failure. PUSH reroot
> preflights growth before the source unsafe union retag; all defined publication
> prefixes remain. The finite PUSH inverse index defect is retained explicitly.
> Scalar identities replace machine addresses in budgeted prefix rendering with
> host-int bounds. Int32 suppressed callbacks expose no invented value service;
> actual AST/dependency/bound callbacks and diagnostics remain open.
> See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-parray-port-status-md.
>
> ### Integer allocation and publication prefixes
>
> Selected internal MPZ setters and Div/Mod now preserve source old-free, sign,
> result transfer and sequential quotient/remainder publication order. One charged
> retired descriptor represents a failed replacement without changing Int layout;
> reads reject it, while owner-qualified Del/Reset clear it and release live
> companions. Missing scratch is guarded at its next actual access and is not
> automatically repaired. Wrapped finite allocations occur before the guarded
> undersized span access. These Go continuations do not claim C++ exception
> recovery. Source small-object allocator topology, global memory events and
> higher-level staged wrappers remain open. See PORT_PROGRESS.md#audit-mpz-source-publication-port-status-md.

> # Source hashes and RNG: initial utility port
>
> The former root `random.go` now lives in `util/random`; root retains `hash.go`. Neither imports solver or numeric/arena packages. `LICENSE.txt` remains the repository license.
>
> | Source operation | Go counterpart | Coverage |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | `hash.h`: `hash_u`, `hash_ull` | `Uint`, `Uint64` | finite source constants including zero, high bit, maximal values |
> | `combine_hash`, `hash_u_u` | `Combine`, `UintPair` | combine source constant; pair composition |
> | `mix`, `mk_mix` | private `mix`, `Mix` | source mix constant and string/composite use |
> | `hash.cpp`: `string_hash`, `read_unsigned` | `String`, internal `hashBytes`, `WordBytes`, `WordReader` | embedded fixture lengths 0–25 including every residual length and high-bit bytes |
> | `get_composite_hash` | `Composite` | arities 1–10; independent exact child callback visit order |
> | `util.h`: `random_gen` constructor, `set_seed`, both calls, `max_value` | zero value/`z3rand.New`, `SetSeed`, `Next`, `Bounded`, `z3rand.Max` | source constants for seeds zero and UINT_MAX, reseed, bound and max |
> | `util.h`: `shuffle` | `ShuffleUint32`, `ShuffleInt32` | source permutation of five elements with seed zero |
>
> `src/test/random.cpp` only prints its seed-zero stream under TRACE and asserts nothing. The port adds exact finite expectations rather than passing a vacuous test. There is no standalone `src/test/hash.cpp` in this checkout. Golden values in `test_vectors/source_hash_random.json` were collected from the actual source headers and `hash.cpp` with GCC 13.3.0, not from the Go implementation. The former `test_vectors/reference.cpp` input generator has been removed under the pure-Go rule; ordinary tests embed the retained JSON and neither compile C++ nor access repository source.
>
> Representation decisions: all source unsigned arithmetic is fixed-width uint32 (uint64 in hash_ull); overflow wraps. Source string_hash uses machine-endian memcpy loads and implementation-defined char signedness. The fixture baseline is little-endian and signed-char (this source on Linux/amd64); the Go port fixes those semantics on all targets including wasm. This is a recorded adaptation, not a replacement hash. `WordBytes` feeds the same hash state transitions using an allocation-free word/byte accessor for the bit-vector hash. Inputs must fit source uint32 lengths. `Bounded(0)` and zero-child Composite are invalid preconditions and panic in Go; they do not invent a valid result. Random state belongs to its caller, with no global RNG or math/rand substitution.
>

> ## Concrete u_map<unsigned> packet
>
> Added `uint_map.go` and `uint_map_test.go`, translating the **u_map<unsigned>** instantiation of `src/util/map.h` and its `core_hashtable<default_map_entry<...>>` substrate in `src/util/hashtable.h`. Copyright Microsoft 2006, Leonardo de Moura. This is distinct from `src/util/uint_map.h`'s direct-index unsigned→T* vector and from the local UintSet-key `uint_map<unsigned>` defined inside `src/test/uint_set.cpp`. >
> | Source operation in this instantiation | Concrete Go counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | table2map/u_map construction; core default constructor | `NewUintMap(UintMapConfig)` creates 8 FREE entries and charges owner/header plus table |
> | core copy constructor; copy_table/move_table | `Clone`, `copyUintMapTable` scans old buckets ascending and reprobes cached hashes |
> | core destructor, physical delete_table | `Close`, backing-table charge release and Go owner cleanup |
> | core alloc_table, expand_table | `allocateTable`, `rehash` to doubled capacity, source pre-lookup load predicate |
> | remove_deleted_entries and memory::is_out_of_memory | same-capacity `rehash`, cold owner `OutOfMemory` callback (nil means false) |
> | table2map reset/finalize | `Reset`, `Finalize`, exact source early returns and capacity predicates |
> | empty/size/capacity | `Empty`, `Size`, `Capacity`; `Deleted` adds observable audit count |
> | insert and INSERT_LOOP_BODY | `Insert`, internal `insert(overwrite=true)` |
> | insert_if_not_there_core and source overloads | `InsertIfNotThereCore`, internal `insert(overwrite=false)` |
> | insert_if_not_there / insert_if_not_there2 | `InsertIfNotThere`, `InsertIfNotThere2`, returned cold entry ref supports reading/writing value |
> | find_core, find(k,out), find(k), operator[] | `FindCore`, `Find`/`FindInto`, `MustFind`; mutable value via `UintMapEntryRef.SetValue` |
> | get(k,default), contains, find_iterator | `Get`, `Contains`, `FindIterator` |
> | remove/erase and REMOVE_LOOP_BODY | `Remove`, `Erase` |
> | begin/end and iterator used-slot scan | `Begin`, `End`, iterator `scan` traverses ascending physical buckets |
> | iterator dereference/arrow, prefix/postfix increment and equality | `Entry`/`Ref`, `Next`/`PostNext`, `Equal`/its negation |
> | core copy assignment, union/intersection | `Assign`, `Union`, `Intersect`; source reset+insert order, source self guards and clone-before-removal preserved |
> | swap | `Swap`; backing array/counters exchanged, owner resources/callbacks retained |
> | get_num_collision | `CollisionCount` returns zero: HASHTABLE_STATISTICS is disabled in this source baseline |
> | Z3DEBUG check_invariant | `CheckInvariant` counts USED/DELETED entries against source counters |
> | default_hash_entry data/hash/state operations | scalar `uintMapEntry` fields and FREE/DELETED/USED transitions; no entry ownership callbacks for uint32 data |
>
> Algorithm fidelity: keys/values/hash/state/counters are uint32. The hot array contains exactly four scalar uint32 fields per entry (16 bytes), with no per-entry pointers, interfaces, generics or unsafe. Zero and UINT32_MAX keys/values remain legal. Lookup and mutation probe linearly from key&(capacity−1) and wrap once. Insertion remembers the **last** deleted slot encountered and uses it only on reaching a FREE slot; existing-key Insert overwrites only its value, while insert-if-absent retains it. Expansion runs before lookup when (size+deleted)*4 > capacity*3, so an existing-key update/duplicate can expand. Cached hashes are preserved across ascending-bucket rehash. Remove uses FREE only if the next wrapped bucket is FREE; otherwise it makes a tombstone and attempts same-capacity cleanup only when deleted>size AND deleted>64. An out-of-memory callback suppresses that cleanup, matching the source branch.
>
> Reset counts buckets already FREE before clearing, **not** tombstones. It halves once only if capacity>16 and free*4>capacity*3; an already empty clean reset returns immediately. Finalize allocates 64 buckets when current capacity>64, otherwise follows Reset. Clone rehashes at source capacity and removes tombstones; Assign calls destination Reset then source bucket-order Insert rather than copying storage. Union overwrites shared-key values in source bucket order; intersection retains destination values for shared keys and removes keys absent from the source through a temporary clone. All thresholds, equal-boundary cases, source growth-before-duplicate behavior, wrapped probes, tombstone selection and resulting bucket order have exact finite tests.
>
> Budget/ownership adaptations: UintMap imports only the independent arena Budget/error contract. Construction charges its cold owner header, then the 8-entry array; failed construction rolls back charges. Reallocation reserves the full new array while the old array remains charged, so peak old+new memory is bounded before mutation/publication. Close releases both charges. Failed expansion/Clone leave the source intact. Source Remove logically deletes before cleanup; a cleanup allocation error therefore returns an error with that removal completed and a still-valid tombstoned table, covered explicitly. Reset/Finalize allocate before releasing/clearing old storage; their failures are intentionally atomic instead of reproducing source post-delete allocation failure corruption. Cross-budget Swap reserves incoming ownership charges before releasing outgoing charges and rolls back failed transfer; its source-independent resource callback/header stay with each owner. Primitive values need no logical retain/free; future domain wrappers storing handles must perform their source logical reference actions outside this utility.
>
> Cold `UintMapEntryRef` and iterator wrappers contain owner/table epoch/bucket, never a raw backing-array pointer. Structural membership mutation/reset/swap/reallocation invalidates these checked nonowning snapshots; value overwrite updates the existing bucket without invalidation. This is explicitly stricter than raw C++ pointer borrow lifetimes. Source mutable value references are represented by `SetValue`; callers cannot silently mutate a key while retaining its old cached hash. Missing required-key lookup and invalid/closed snapshots fail explicitly. Scalar table backing and epochs are owner-local; concurrent use requires owner synchronization. Array lengths/byte charges are checked in uint64 against platform int bounds. Capacity growth beyond the source's safe uint32 load-predicate range (2^30 buckets) is diagnosed before overflow/allocation; byte arithmetic does not wrap. Epoch rollover is diagnosed instead of validating an old snapshot.
>
> TDD/source tests: before production translation, the complete initial test packet failed RED on missing UintMap operations, then reached GREEN. `src/test/map.cpp` is active and tests a **string-key** map; its assertion categories (insert, contains, find_iterator, value/size, remove) are ported here with concrete unsigned keys as clearly labeled u_map specialization coverage. The actual string-key/hash/equality variant remains unported, not silently replaced. `src/test/hashtable.cpp` registers tst_hashtable but its body is empty on this Linux baseline; the _WINDOWS-only int_set assertions have additional portable concrete-map membership/cardinality/copy coverage. The original sentinel-based int_set and hash 3*x variant remain separate coverage work. No source cases were mislabeled active or falsely claimed as that different specialization.
>
> Independent tests include a 6,000-operation finite Go-map oracle (Go maps are test-only), exact manually derived collision/probe/bucket cases, threshold equality boundaries, zero/full-width keys and values, deletion cleanup/OOM skip, same-capacity rehash order, reset/finalize/clone/swap/assignment/union/intersection, cold reference/iterator invalidation, constructor failure rollback, old+new allocation-peak refusal, source partial deletion before failed cleanup, atomic sparse reset/finalize failure, cross-budget transfer rollback and release accounting. Warmed scalar update/lookup/value-ref/iteration operations allocate zero Go objects. All tests are hermetic and need no C++ source/compiler, network or sibling checkout.

> Assigned variant audit: all table2map/u_map operations and applicable core algorithms have counterparts. General core dump requires streamable data; source `_key_data<unsigned,unsigned>` has no ostream operator, so that latent method is not callable for this instantiation and no invented Go rendering format was added. Other hash/equality/storage specializations, optional enabled HASHTABLE_STATISTICS accounting, generic streamable-table dump, direct-index uint_map<T*>, and UintSet-key map demo integration remain explicitly unported separate components. This is a concrete source specialization, not a completed generic hash-table/map subsystem.

>

> `src/util/str_hashtable.h`'s `ptr_hashtable<char,str_hash_proc,str_eq_proc>` and
> its applicable core_hashtable/ptr_hash_entry algorithms. Copyright Microsoft
> 2006, Leonardo de Moura. This packet supplies the owner-bound string set needed
> by the symbol interner; it does **not** claim the full arbitrary-pointer source
> container, the separate string→int map, symbol service, or scoped symbol bindings.
>
> | Assigned source operation | Owner-bound counterpart / remaining scope |

> | alloc_table/delete_table, copy_table/move_table/expand_table/cleanup | `allocateTable`, table charge release, `copyStrTable`, `rehash`, `prepareInsert`; no byte copies/releases |
> | insert const/rvalue; insert-if-absent core/ref/entry | `Insert`, `InsertIfNotThereCore`, `InsertIfNotThere`, `InsertIfNotThere2`; scalar borrow copying requires no spelling allocation |

> | remove/erase, reset/finalize | `Remove`/`Erase`, `Reset`/`Finalize`; pointer sentinel transitions drop the table reference without freeing bytes |
> | empty/size/capacity, invariant/collision count | matching concrete methods; source disabled collision statistics returnzero |
> | dump ostream of char pointers | `Dump`, exact bracket/space byte rendering in ascending buckets |

>
> Storage/lifetime: a cold table binds one borrowed `*arena.BytesRegion`. Each
> 32-byte pointer-free entry stores hash/state and a `StrKey` containing region
> slot/generation, byte offset, C-string logical length and uint64 origin identity.
> No per-spelling object, Go string, Go map, interface, generic declaration, raw
> pointer or unsafe storage occurs in hot records. `BytesRegion.OwnerID` is stable
> through reset/rollback/Close and prevents a foreign StrKey with numerically equal
> slot/generation/offset from accessing the wrong region. Same-region clones and
> independently constructed tables accept each other's keys. Raw BytesRegionRef
> arguments to CString retain the arena's explicit owner-local token precondition;
> the returned opaque StrKey carries the origin and is checked at table boundaries.
>
> CString scans within the allocation to its first NUL; empty strings require a
> live terminating byte. Explicit offset permits borrowing a spelling after its
> source hash prefix. Input bytes must remain immutable and live while borrowed;
> region rollback/reset/Close makes affected key accesses return typed invalid-slot
> or closed errors. Table destruction, removal, reset, rehash and clone never call
> region Allocate/Write/Free/Close. Source ptr_hash_entry removal overwrites its
> pointer with FREE/DELETED sentinels; the table's key descriptor is cleared on
> those transitions, while the region allocation remains owned independently.
> Clone preserves the exact borrowed descriptor, not a newly allocated spelling.
>
> Hash seed is17 and uses the existing validated Jenkins core via WordReader,
> assembling little-endian source word loads from byte reads and signed-char tails.
> The first NUL and every suffix byte are excluded, unlike utilhash.String's
> explicit-length behavior. strcmp equality is raw unsigned-byte identity; no
> Unicode normalization, rune conversion or case folding is applied. Cached
> uint32 hashes are copied during rehash/clone, never recalculated for placement.
> Entry SetKey models the symbol interner replacing its temporary source pointer
> with an owned pointer, and checks equal spelling/hash so no invalid cached hash
> can be silently introduced. It preserves the entry borrow; structural membership
> changes, reallocation/reset/swap invalidate cold owner/epoch/slot refs and cursors.
>
> Exact table behavior remains source linear probing with wrapped ascending slots,
> last-tombstone reuse only after finding FREE, strict `(size+deleted)*4 > cap*3`
> growth before even duplicate lookup, FREE removal only when the next wrapped
> bucket is FREE, and cleanup only when deleted>size and deleted>64. The cold
> OutOfMemory callback suppresses cleanup. Reset counts only buckets already FREE
> before clearing, halves at most once when cap>16 and free*4>cap*3, and returns
> early for empty-clean tables. Finalize uses64 only above64. Stats reports only
> table owner/header and array charges; the borrowed region reports its graph
> separately. Array reservations bound old+new allocation peaks. Cross-budget Swap
> pre-reserves both incoming arrays, rolls back if the second reserve fails, and
> exchanges binding/table/counters only after success, with exhausted epochs checked
> upfront. It neither transfers region budget charges nor assumes region ownership.
>
> Allocation adaptations: failed constructor/rehash/Clone leave no table charge
> leak; failed expansion leaves membership and refs intact. Reset/finalize reserve
> a replacement before destroying old data, so predictable failures preserve the
> old table rather than the source unsafe post-delete failure. Remove occurs
> before cleanup allocation, so failed cleanup returns an error with removal and
> tombstones retained, matching source action order. Multi-entry operations remain
> source-ordered partial updates rather than transactions. Capacity beyond the
> safe source uint32 load-predicate range and platform slice bounds is diagnosed.
>
> PrepareFindCString performs source growth-before-duplicate lookup using a
> transient Go string prefix; no query string is retained in entries. A missing
> query leaves no pending borrowed entry: the caller allocates an owner spelling
> and publishes it with InsertIfNotThereCore. This allows safe failure before
> publication instead of the source interner's dangling temporary after region
> allocation failure. Source serialized owner access must encompass that sequence.
> It returns only an epoch-checked cold ref on hits, never a mutable table pointer.
>
> Remaining source gap: arbitrary pointer spellings can originate in several
> independent owners, whereas this concrete table has one region binding. The
> full source multi-origin Assign/Union/Intersect are **not ported**; future work
> requires a concrete cold owner directory and scalar origin records, not silent
> foreign-ref reinterpretation. Swap already supports different bound regions.
> Table byte-pool mutation/marking ownership is caller-owned; spelling regions
> must outlive all borrowing tables. Optional enabled HASHTABLE_STATISTICS counters
> and arbitrary-address/C API pointer compatibility remain separate adaptations.

> # Concrete borrowed CString → int32 map
>
> Target: `src/util/map.h` specialization
> `map<char const*, int, str_hash_proc, str_eq_proc>`, using
> `default_map_entry` / `default_hash_entry<_key_data<...>>` and the applicable
> `core_hashtable` algorithms in `src/util/hashtable.h`. The spellings use
> `str_hash_proc` / `str_eq_proc` from `src/util/str_hashtable.h`.
>
> This specialization is implemented; the entire generic `map.h` family remains
> partial. Numeric maps, pointer identity maps, other key/value domains, and
> scoped symbol maps are distinct packets. No Go generics, production Go maps,
> unsafe, interface boxing, or pointers inside the hot entries are introduced.
>
> ## Source API inventory
>
> | Source API | Concrete counterpart |
> | --- | --- |
> | `_key_data` key / value constructors, entry hash and equality functors | scalar `strInt32Entry` with `StrKey` / `int32`; Hash / Equal and shared CString byte readers |
> | `default_map_entry` / `default_hash_entry` get/set data, cached hash, state predicates and transitions | explicit `hash,state,key,value`; entry Value / SetValue, Key / SetKey / SetKeyFrom, Hash; transitions retain complete dead/free payload |
> | `table2map` / `map` constructor, core constructor/destructor | NewStrInt32Map / Close; default capacity8, optional source-core power-of-two capacity |
> | implicit copy constructor, core copy_table | Clone; ascending source buckets into fresh slots using cached hash; skips dead/free payloads |
> | implicit assignment / core operator= | Assign; Reset then Union; ascending source bucket order and partial insertion failure prefixes |
> | reset, finalize, empty, size, capacity | Reset / Finalize / Empty / Size / Capacity |
> | insert | Insert / InsertFrom; duplicate replaces both borrowed pointer and scalar value |
> | insert_if_not_there_core / insert_if_not_there / insert_if_not_there2 | corresponding InsertIfNotThereCore / InsertIfNotThere / InsertIfNotThere2 and explicit foreign From variants; checked entry refs replace source pointers / data borrows |
> | find_core, find output overload, get fallback | FindCore / FindFrom; Find / FindFromValue / FindInto / FindIntoFrom; Get |
> | find reference overloads, const/nonconst operator[] | FindCore entry Value / SetValue; caller checks presence (source requires key present) |
> | find_iterator, begin/end, iterator dereference/member access, prefix/postfix increment and equality | FindIterator / FindIteratorFrom / Begin / End; iterator Ref / Key / Value / Next / PostNext / Equal / AtEnd; mutable entry through Ref |
> | contains, remove, erase | Contains / ContainsFrom / Remove / RemoveFrom / Erase / EraseFrom |
> | expand_table, move_table, remove_deleted_entries | growth / cached-hash ascending rehash; strict tombstone cleanup and borrowed OOM callback |
> | swap | Swap; table, directory, primary binding and membership travel together; owner/header/resource configuration stay with owner |
> | core operator\|=, operator&= | Union / Intersect; intersection clones destination, queries other without adopting foreign queries, removes only absent keys, preserves values |
> | check_invariant, get_num_collision | CheckInvariant / CollisionCount (zero in source-default statistics-disabled build) |
>
> Core `dump` is not a valid instantiated operation for this map: `_key_data`
> has no C++ stream insertion overload, and table2map does not forward `dump`.
> The optional `HASHTABLE_STATISTICS` instrumentation is not enabled by the source
> configuration and is not implemented. Arbitrary raw key mutation via source
> entry references can corrupt hashing; the checked key setter accepts only
> hash/equality-preserving replacement. Scalar values remain fully mutable.
>
> ## Source semantics and ownership
>
> Seed17 CString hashing uses the established little-endian / signed-char hash
> baseline, stops at the first NUL, and compares unsigned bytes for equality.
> Spelling bytes are immutable borrowed regions. `StrKey` carries a scalar unique
> region identity and owner-local allocation/generation/offset/prefix length;
> entry arrays hold no region pointers. Primary owner binding is implicit; sorted
> cold `strOwner` directory binds retained secondary origins. Queries with an
> explicit foreign owner adopt nothing. Duplicate insert-if-absent retains the
> old key and value and adopts nothing. Equal Insert replaces the complete pair.
>
> Unlike ptr-based StrHashtable, default hash entries preserve **both key and
> value** when marked FREE or DELETED. Reset without replacement preserves those
> payloads; rehash, shrinking reset, finalize replacement and clone copy only
> USED entries. Regions and their bytes are never copied, freed or closed by map
> operations. Bound owner metadata remains until Close, including after removal
> and reset; this is checked-borrow bookkeeping, not source spelling ownership.
> Callers serialize owners and ensure retained spellings remain live/immutable.
> Region rollback/reset/close invalidates affected checked key reads. A scalar
> value read does not dereference the borrowed key, matching source behavior.
>
> Linear probing wraps bucket order, remembers the **last** tombstone before
> FREE, and grows strictly above75% before duplicate detection. Removal marks
> FREE iff the following wrapped slot is FREE; otherwise DELETED. Cleanup occurs
> only with deleted>size and deleted>64, unless the OOM callback suppresses it.
> Reset counts preexisting FREE slots and shrinks once only above75% overhead
> with capacity>16; finalize caps large tables to64. Rehash/clone use cached hash,
> not fresh spelling hash. Assignment/union/intersection preserve source ordering
> and already-published prefixes on failure.
>
> Root object, full physical entry arrays and full physical cold directory arrays
> are budgeted. Replacement arrays coexist with the old arrays while copying.
> Directory growth reserves the incoming complete backing array before releasing
> old bytes. Swap pre-reserves both complete incoming table+directory graphs and
> rolls back the first reservation if the second fails. Clone unwinds every
> failed published prefix. Predictable reset/finalize allocation failure is
> staged before clearing entries, strengthening the source allocation exception
> contract; cleanup failure retains the preceding source removal. Epoch exhaustion
> is preflighted before structural mutation/adoption. Existing-key overwrite and
> scalar mutation need no structural epoch. Close always releases at epoch max.
> Checked owner/epoch refs replace raw pointer/reference lifetimes.
>
> FindCString / PrepareFindCString are transient string boundary adapters, not
> stored string keys. The latter follows source growth-before-duplicate and
> preflights a missing insertion epoch before a caller allocates spelling bytes.
> Raw arena allocation refs are owner-local; callers use BorrowCString with the
> matching owner to form a key. `InitialCapacity` exposes the underlying source
> core constructor; source `map` itself always starts at8.
>

Explicit activity bits and encoded link indices replace tagged addresses and pointers. The map starts with eight buckets/two cellar cells, displaces heads into sequential cellar cells, copies ascending source buckets/head-first chains when expanding, doubles cellar again if copy overflows, grows before duplicate lookup, and erases by replacing heads or recycling cellar links. New entries retain key then value; same-value insertion retains activity and ownership; replacements increment incoming value, decrement old value, then publish and clear activity. Find marks unused entries accessed and decrements unused exactly once. Eviction skips used queue entries, deletes the oldest unused map entry, releases key then value, and compresses only after the source threshold. Reset retires live entries in source bucket/chain order, conditionally reinitializes the table and retains queue capacity; Cleanup always finalizes/reinitializes the table and frees queue storage. Null values support the original proof-cache entry semantics. Size/capacity/empty and the source's always-true invariant method are exposed. Reached Go failures retain explicit incoming/evicted roots for Close; full ownership/failure campaigns remain deferred.

Preserved a source bookkeeping quirk rather than repairing its algorithm: replacement of an accessed entry clears its activity bit without incrementing unused or appending the key. Subsequent native Find therefore underflows zero toUINTMAX; the debug path reports the original reached unused>0 assertion after setting the bit. Original CheckInvariant does not detect this. Tests explicitly record both behaviors.

### util files: stack.cpp and stack.h

Ported the low-level LIFO byte allocator as exported Stack and StackRef APIs. Stack owns an arena BytesRegion and gives every allocation a nested rollback mark, preserving strict last-in-first-out reclamation, aligned default-page growth, immediate large-allocation release, zero-size allocation identity, reset and top access. Default pages are held on the region's explicit free-page list until Close and reused deterministically; no sync.Pool or garbage-collector-dependent retention is involved.

Checked StackRef values replace raw void pointers and bind every allocation to its original owner and lifetime. Read, Write and Size provide bounded byte access. DeallocateRef implements top-checked placement deletion, while non-generic DeallocateValue invokes a borrowed destructor callback before reclaiming the top allocation. Explicit Close replaces the C++ destructor and copied owners are rejected.

Four focused tests cover small, large and zero-size allocation; LIFO top restoration; stale, foreign and copied-owner rejection; bounds; page recycling and large-page release; typed destructor order; reset; close and empty operations. Focused native and g3debug checks pass (0.004s/0.006s). Util vet, ledger and diff validation pass; inventory is now 2102 units, 677 APIs: 91 ported, 276 partial, 1726 unported, plus separately classified platform replacements. The 23:35 UTC full-suite checkpoint remains current.

### util files: statistics.cpp and statistics.h

Completed the remaining `get_memory_statistics` implementation as exported GetMemoryStatistics. It reads Go's documented runtime.MemStats counters: HeapAlloc for current heap-object bytes, HeapSys for the standard library's estimate of the largest heap size, and Mallocs for the cumulative heap-object allocation count. Memory values retain the source's truncation to hundredths of a mebibyte, and allocation counts use the uint32 statistics domain when representable or the double domain otherwise.

The existing concrete Statistics implementation continues to cover contribution storage, append-copy/reset, typed indexed access, aggregation, the three rendering modes, source formatting quirks and resource-limit statistics. A deterministic snapshot test covers exact conversion, both allocation-count domains and source storage ordering; the same test exercises the real Go runtime path and verifies all three exported keys.
